output: Prescription Drug Monitoring Act of 2016 This bill requires a state that receives grant funds under the prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) or the controlled substance monitoring program to comply with specified requirements, including: (1) a requirement to consult the PDMP before prescribing a controlled substance; (2) notification of a practitioner when patterns indicative of controlled substance misuse are detected; (3) reporting of prescriptions by dispensers; and (4) making data contained in the PDMP available to other states.  Beginning two years after the bill's enactment, each state that receives grant funds under the PDMP or the controlled substance monitoring program must make the data contained in the PDMP available to other states through the data-sharing single technology solution established by the bill. The bill directs the Department of Justice to award a grant to an eligible entity to establish and maintain an inter-state data-sharing single hub to facilitate the sharing of PDMP data among states and the accessing of such data by practitioners.

Promoting Financial Literacy and Economic Opportunity Act of 2015  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for 20% of the amount paid to carry out programs that promote economic and financial literacy. The credit is allowed to up to 20 organizations at any time. The bill requires that at least 20% of the credit be paid for direct activities and 75% be paid for subgrants.

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require an accrediting agency or association to apply procedures throughout the accrediting process, including evaluation, interim sanction, and withdrawal or termination of accreditation proceedings, that comply with due process, including the right to specified procedures. 
Requires an agency or association that conducts an assessment of an institution's governing board to:  (1) assess the institution's board in the same manner as it assesses the institution; and (2) apply the accreditation standard, to the greatest extent possible, to any State-appointed receiver, special trustee, or similar interim governing authority until such time as the governing authority is returned to the regular governing board.  Prohibits an agency or association from terminating accreditation solely on the ground that the institution is under interim management of a State-appointed receiver, special trustee, or similar governing authority unless:  (1) the agency or association determines that there are other deficiencies at the institution that provide grounds for termination; and (2) after providing due process required by this Act, the interim governing authority has not corrected such deficiencies within a reasonable period of time. 
Requires an agency or association, and any officer or subdivision of such agency or association that makes accreditation recommendations to its decision-making board, to

Contributions Legally Interdicted from Noncitizens to Our Nonprofits Act of 2016 or the CLINTON Act of 2016 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit a federal official organization (an organization controlled, funded, or managed by a federal employee or officials) from accepting or soliciting contributions from persons connected to a foreign government.  A federal official organization shall not be treated as knowingly or willingly accepting such contribution if the organization returns the contribution to the person within 30 days after learning that the person is connected to a foreign government.  A federal official organization shall not be treated as knowing or willingly accepting any contribution from any person connected to a foreign government if the organization accepts the contribution and learns that the person is connected to a foreign government within 30 days after acceptance.  The bill imposes a tax on any federal official organization which knowingly or willingly accepts any contribution from any person connected to a foreign government.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income all excess campaign contributions received by a House of Representatives campaign committee.  Exempts such committee from the limitations on the amount of certain tax-exempt income and the amount of income subject to the lowest unit rate for broadcast advertising.  Exempts a House of Representatives campaign committee from the requirement to pay third-class mail fees unless it certifies that it has not obtained any excess campaign contributions for the current election cycle.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) provide for the treatment of bonds issued to finance electric output facilities as private activity bonds or industrial development bonds, without regard to any permissible competitive actions taken by the issuer; and (2) include any bond issued as part of an issue any of the proceeds of which are to be used for electric output facilities other than small distribution property as a private activity bond, including a bond issued to refund a pre-effective date electric output facility bond if the weighted average maturity of the issue of which the refunding bond is a part does not exceed 120 percent of the average reasonably expected economic life of the facilities being financed with the net proceeds of such issue. 
Revises the limitation on the amount which a taxpayer may pay into the Nuclear Decommissioning Costs Fund.

United States-Afghanistan Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) Act of 2011 - Directs the President to seek to negotiate and enter into a bilateral status of forces agreement with the government of Afghanistan.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the President should submit such agreement to the Senate for ratification as a treaty, or the President should request statutory authorization for such agreement by Congress.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish the Return of Talent Program to permit certain aliens who are citizens of countries in which U.S. Armed Forces are engaged in combat or peacekeeping operations or who are citizens of countries where authorization for United Nations peacekeeping operations was initiated during the preceding 10 years to temporarily return to their country of citizenship in order to make a material contribution to it if the country is engaged in post-conflict reconstruction activities.

Strategic Withdrawal of Agencies for Meaningful Placement Act of 2018 or SWAMP Act This bill directs the General Services Administration (GSA) to establish a competitive relocation process for the headquarters of executive agencies located in the Washington metropolitan area.

Minority Business Development Improvements Act of 2010 - Requires the Director of the Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) to establish the Minority Business Development Program to assist qualified minority businesses.

Defines a "qualified minority business" as any entity that: (1) meets certain ownership and control requirements; (2) has a net worth not greater than $2 million; (3) operates in a sector of industry having a North American Industry Classification System code; and (4) submits required reports.

Authorizes the Director to: (1) provide technical assistance to such businesses with regard to writing business plans, marketing, management, and securing sufficient financing; and (2) enter into agreements with the federal government and any department, agency, or officer thereof having procurement powers to provide for the fulfillment of procurement contracts and opportunities for such businesses with regard to such contracts.

Authorizes the Director to terminate a qualified minority business from the Program for any violation of this Act by that business, including: (1) conduct by a principal of the qualified minority business that indicates a lack of business integrity; (2) willful failure to comply with applicable labor standards and obligations; (3) consistent failure to tender adequate performance with regard to Program contracts; (4) failure to obtain

Directs the Secretary of Labor to make a grant to an eligible public university to establish the Center for the Study of Women and Workplace Policy. Requires the Center to: (1) compile and analyze available data and data sets on the difference between the earnings of men and women, including the Panel Study of Income Dynamic housed at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor; (2) identify factors which affect differences in earnings; (3) disseminate its findings annually to the public; (4) maintain a website to serve as a clearinghouse for the data and findings of relevant recent studies; and (5) publish one best practices guide for businesses and one for families, containing information about workplace equity, retaining women in the workplace, and promoting a family-friendly workplace.

Small Business Access to Capital Act of 2009 - Amends the Small Business Act to increase the maximum loan amount for small business lenders to small businesses that receive loans in amounts equal to 75% (currently, 85%) of the total amount of debt outstanding. Increases from $1.5 million to $4.5 million (currently, $2 million) the maximum amount of a small business loan that may be guaranteed by the Secretary of the Treasury.

Allows a project that does not involve the expansion of a small business concern to include the refinancing of existing indebtedness if: (1) the amount of the financing is not more than 80% of the value of the collateral for the financing; (2) the small business concern has been in operation for all of the two-year period ending on the date of the financing; (3) the existing indebtedness was not incurred during the two-year period ending on the date of the financing; (4) the existing indebtedness is not subject to a federal agency guarantee; and (5) the borrower agrees to pay a fee in an amount equal to the anticipated additional cost.

Allows the approval of a financing regardless of whether the project meets job creation goals.

Amends the Small Business Act

Census Improvement Act - Prohibits participation in the Planning Partnership Program for the 2010 census of population from being allowed in the case of: (1) an organization which has been indicted for a violation under federal or state law relating to an election for federal or state office; or (2) an organization which employs applicable individuals.

Defines "applicable individual" as an individual who: (1) is employed by the organization in a permanent or temporary capacity, (2) is contracted or retained by the organization, or (3) is acting on behalf of, or with the express or apparent authority of, the organization. Includes the District of Columbia within the meaning of "state" for purposes of this Act.

Prohibits any bill or joint resolution containing a provision which would have the effect of repealing, suspending, or otherwise limiting the application of provisions relating to confidentiality of certain information from being considered as passed or agreed to by either chamber of Congress, unless so passed or agreed to by a vote of not less than two-thirds of the Members of such chamber.

Directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review and report to Congress on the questions proposed to be included in the 2010 census of population and the American Community

Electronic Campaign Disclosure Act of 1998 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to revise requirements for electronic filing of Federal election Commission (Commission) reports. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) establish a public Internet site for such reports by direct posting or by electronic transmission; and (2) permit each person required to file a report to do so by such method as it deems appropriate. 
Requires the Commission to provide for one or more methods (other than requiring a signature on the report being filed) for verification of such reports. 
Requires the Commission to make software to carry out the requirements of this Act available to the public. 
Requires a political committee which is required to file Commission reports electronically during an election cycle to file with the Commission a report listing each contribution of $100 or more received by the committee during the cycle after the date on which such requirement first applies to the committee as if:  (1) the reference to $1,000 were a reference to $100; (2) the reference to 20th day were a reference to 90th day; and (3) the reference in the second sentence to 48 hours were a reference to

Requires the Chief of Staff of the Air Force to administer the Civil Air Patrol, under the direction of the Secretary of the Air Force.  Directs the Secretary to appoint a National Board of Directors.  Provides for the appointment of members of the National Board of Directors by the Chief of Staff.  Provides that the appointment or assignment of members of the armed forces or civilian employees under this Act is not precluded by any law or regulation prohibiting active duty members of the armed forces or civilian employees from participating in the management of non-Federal entities.  Subjects the use of Civil Air Patrol employees and volunteer members to the Executive Director and National Board of Directors' needs.  Subjects all funds provided to the Patrol to the Federal Grant and Cooperative Agreement Act and Federal regulations governing the provision of appropriated funds to private, nonprofit organizations.

Children's Bicycle Helmet Safety Act of 1993 - Authorizes the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to make grants to States, State political subdivisions, and nonprofit organizations for programs that require or encourage individuals under the age of 16 to wear approved bicycle helmets. 
Authorizes a grant to be used to:  (1) enforce a law that requires such individuals to wear helmets while riding on bicycles; (2) assist such individuals to acquire helmets; (3) develop and administer a program to educate such individuals on the importance of wearing helmets to improve bicycle safety; or (4) carry out any combination of the activities. 
Sets forth standards for such helmets. 
Declares that until the final standard takes effect, a bicycle helmet that does not conform to an interim standard shall be considered in violation of a consumer product safety standard promulgated under the Consumer Product Safety Act.  Declares that the final standard shall be considered a consumer product safety standard promulgated under such Act. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Electronic Employment Verification Reauthorization Act of 2008 - Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to make permanent the pilot programs for electronic verification of employment eligibility (E-Verify) for aliens coming to work for U.S. employers. Requires participation by U.S. contractors in such programs.

Requires employers that verify the employment eligibility of existing employees to do so within 10 days after notifying the Secretary of Homeland Security of their election.

Authorizes the Secretary to require participation by employers that have engaged in material violations of the prohibition against hiring aliens from certain noncitian refugee and other unauthorized countries.

Requires each employer participating in the E-Verify Program to reverify the work authorization of any individual not later than three days after the expiration of such authorization.

Directs the Director of United States Citizenship and Immigration Services to establish a small business demonstration program that assists small businesses in verifying the employment eligibility of their newly hired employees.

Requires the Director to submit a monthly report to the Assistant Secretary of Immigration and Customs Enforcement that includes for each person who receives final nonconfirmation through the E-Verify Program: (1) the name and contact information for the individual's current employer; and (2) any other critical information that the Assistant Secretary determines

Selected Reserve Home Loan Equity Act - Amends Federal law to make permanent the authority of the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make home loans to qualifying members of the Selected Reserve for the purchase or construction of a dwelling. (Currently, such authority terminates on September 30, 2009.)

Revises the loan fee schedule for such veterans to include those active duty veterans. (Currently, such veterans are excluded from the loan fee schedule.)

New Aid for Trustworthy, Affordable Drugs Act (NAFTA Drugs Act) - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to seek to enter into agreements with other North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) countries to harmonize regulatory requirements for drugs such that drugs approved for commercial distribution in any NAFTA country may be imported or exported into any NAFTA country.

Older and Disabled Americans Criminal Protection Act of 1998 - Authorizes a shared housing (a residential arrangement involving at least two persons who share a dwelling unit and receive care or other services for the benefit of one or more elderly or disabled persons) referral agency to request the Attorney General to conduct a search and exchange of criminal history records regarding any applicant for participation in a shared housing arrangement as a service provider resident. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) the use of such information; and (2) fees. 
Establishes criminal penalties for the knowing use of such information for other than housing determinations. 
Provides that an agency that reasonably relies upon such information shall not be liable for damages based on such information's inaccuracy.

Amends Federal law to allow a fish and wildlife officer of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service of the Department of the Interior to retire from the Civil Service Retirement System with full retirement pay.

Assault Weapons Prohibition Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit the transfer or possession of an assault weapon. 
Defines an assault weapon as:  (1) specified firearms and their functional equivalents; (2) a firearm or part or combination of parts designed to facilitate the attachment of a silencer, bayonet, grenade launcher, flash suppressor, or folding stock to a firearm; (3) any detachable magazine, drum, belt, feed strip, or similar device which has a capacity of, or can be readily restored or converted to accept, ten or more rounds of ammunition; and (4) any combination of parts designed to assemble such a firearm or device. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to recommend modifications to such definition. 
Increases penalties for the possession of an assault weapon. 
Directs the Attorney General to:  (1) investigate and study the effect of this Act on violent and drug-related crime; and (2) evaluate the recreational and other noncriminal uses of assault weapons.

Open Our Democracy Act of 2014 - Provides for the election of Members of the House of Representatives through open primaries and general elections in the state in which the candidate seeks election.  Requires each state to hold a single open primary election and a single general election for each office of Member of the House of Representatives.  Allows each state to choose any candidate in the primary election who receives the greatest number of votes in the general election.  Provides for the election of Members of the House of Representatives through open primaries and general elections in the state in which the candidate seeks election.  Requires each state to hold a general election for each office of Member of the House of Representatives in the state under which: (1) each candidate for such office, regardless of the candidate's political party preference, shall appear on a single ballot; and (2) each voter in the state who is eligible to vote in federal elections in the congressional district involved may cast a ballot in the election, regardless of the voter's political party preference.  Provides for the election of Members of the House of Representatives through open primaries and general elections in the state in which the candidate seeks election.  Requires each state to hold a general election for each office of Member of the House of Representatives in the state

Natural Gas Reserve Act of 2001 - Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to authorize the Secretary of Energy to establish, maintain, and operate a Natural Gas Reserve. Declares that the Reserve is not a component of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.Authorizes the Secretary to: (1) purchase, contract for, lease, or otherwise acquire storage and related facilities and storage services; (2) use, lease, maintain, sell, or otherwise dispose of such storage and related facilities; (3) acquire natural gas for storage in the Reserve; (4) store natural gas in facilities not owned by the United States; and (5) sell, exchange, or otherwise dispose of natural gas from the Reserve, including to maintain the quality or quantity of the natural gas in the Reserve or to maintain the operational capability of the Reserve.Requires the Secretary to determine procedures governing the release of natural gas from the Reserve.Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to establish the Natural Gas Reserve Account.

Hospital Price Disclosure Act of 2005 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers, based on national data, to report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services the frequency with which they perform or administer certain procedures or drugs, as well as the average and median price charged by the hospital or center for such procedures or drugs. Requires the Secretary to: (1) post such information on the Department of Health and Human Services' (HHS) public Internet site; and (2) classify different procedures and assign items and services to those procedures. Sets forth provisions regarding: (1) the computation of an average and median price; (2) penalties for violations; and (3) non-preemption of state laws.

Requires the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to modify the rules authorizing the operation of low-power FM radio stations to prescribe minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels (as well as for co-channels and first- and second-adjacent channels) and prohibit any applicant from obtaining a low-power FM license if the applicant has engaged in any manner in the unlicensed operation of any station in violation of specified provisions of the Communications Act of 1934. Prohibits the FCC from: (1) eliminating or reducing the minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels; or (2) extending the eligibility for application for low-power FM stations beyond the organizations and entities as proposed in MM Docket No. 99-25, except as expressly authorized by Act of Congress enacted after the date of enactment of this Act. Makes any license that was issued by the FCC to a low-power FM station prior to the date on which the FCC modifies its rules and that does not comply with such modifications invalid.
Requires the FCC to conduct an experimental program to test whether low-power FM radio stations will result in harmful interference to existing FM radio stations if such stations are not subject to the minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels. Directs

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow the proceeds of qualified zone academy bonds to be used for acquiring the land on which a qualifying facility is to be constructed.  Repeals the limitation on the tax-exempt credit allowed for the issuance of such bonds.  Allows a credit to be stripped (i.e., separated) from the ownership of a bond and the entitlement to the credit with respect to such bond.  Revises the formula for the allocation of credit authority among States.

Turkish Human Rights Act - Prohibits assistance under the economic support fund of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 for the Government of Turkey unless the Secretary of State determines that there has been significant progress in the following areas:  (1) human rights monitoring and reporting by domestic and international human rights monitoring organizations without fear of reprisal or prosecution; (2) cessation of efforts to deny the recognition of the civil, cultural, and human rights of its Kurdish citizens, military operations against Kurdish civilians, and peaceful resolution of the Kurdish issue; (3) demilitarization of Cyprus and withdrawal of Turkish military forces from Cyprus; (4) cessation of the blockade of U.S. and international assistance to Armenia; and (5) cessation of restrictions on Christian churches and schools and sufficient protection against violence and harassment in such churches and schools.

Environmental Finance Act of 1995 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish an Environmental Financial Advisory Board to provide expert advice on issues affecting the costs and financing of environmental activities at the Federal, State, and local levels. 
Directs the Administrator to establish and support an Environmental Finance Center in an institution of higher education in each of the regions of the EPA.  Authorizes the Center to:  (1) provide training of State and local officials; (2) publish materials relating to financing of environmental infrastructure; (3) conduct conferences and advisory panels on specific financial issues relating to environmental programs and projects; (4) establish information services; (5) generate case studies and reports; (6) develop surveys of financial issues and needs of State and local governments; (7) identify financial programs and alternative financial mechanisms for training purposes; (8) hold public meetings; and (9) collaborate with another Center. 
Authorizes appropriations.

High School Sports Information Collection Act of 2009 - Amends the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002 to direct the Statistics Commissioner for Education to collect, annually, for the immediately preceding academic year, from each coeducational secondary school that receives federal financial assistance that has an athletic program, certain information about teams and athletes, including gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as other team and athlete information.

Requires such schools to: (1) make such information available to students and potential students, upon request, and to the public, by October 15 of each school year; and (2) ensure that all students at the school are informed of their right to request such information.

Generating American Income and Infrastructure Now Act - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to sell, under terms established by the Secretary of the Treasury, distressed notes and other obligations held by the Department of Agriculture (USDA). Requires that of the proceeds from such sales: (1) 50% shall be deposited in an account specifically designated for carrying out infrastructure projects in low-income communities; and (2) 50% shall be retained in the Treasury for purposes of deficit reduction.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to establish a fair market valuation for the sale of such notes or obligations.

Requires the sale of such notes or obligations to be made on a nonrecourse basis. (This means that the borrower and any subsequent purchaser of such notes or obligations sold on a nonrecourse basis shall be relieved of any responsibilities that might have been imposed had the borrower remained indebted to the Secretary of Agriculture.)

National Youth Summer Jobs Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to local governments for providing job placement during the summer for out-of-school youths.

Defines "eligible youth" as an individual who has attained age 14 but not age 22.

Allows local governments that operate existing youth summer jobs programs to use a grant to expand such programs by providing under such program job training and support services, including health and nutrition referrals, housing referrals, financial literacy, and instruction on basic daily living skills.

Medicare Pharmacist Services Coverage Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for Medicare coverage of pharmacist services.

Reducing Barriers to Veterans' Benefits Act - Amends Federal veterans' benefits provisions to provide for presumptive service connection for hearing loss associated with a particular military occupational specialty or combat service, notwithstanding that there is no record of evidence of such hearing loss or tinnitus, as the case may be, during the period of such service.

Directs the Secretary of the military department, with respect to such a veteran, to: (1) issue proposed regulations setting forth the Secretary's determination; or (2) publish the determination in the Federal Register and submit a report to the congressional veterans' committees.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to ensure, under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of Defense, that a member of the Armed Forces receives an audiometric test at the 8000 Hz frequency (or other test that the Secretary determines has the ability to discover potential future hearing loss) to evaluate the hearing of the member during the 90-day period before the date on which the member is discharged, separated, or retired.

Coal Cleanup Taxpayer Protection Act - Amends the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to approve as part of a State or Federal program an alternative system that will: (1) achieve the objectives and purposes of the bonding program under such Act; and (2) result in no greater risk of financial liability to the Federal or State Government than the bonding program under such Act.

Prohibits the Secretary from accepting the bond of the applicant himself (self-bond) but allows the Secretary to accept a separate surety or collateral bond.

Requires the Secretary to notify all State regulatory authorities that allow applicants to self-bond that the approved regulatory programs of such authority must be amended to: (1) remove the authority for applicants to self-bond; and (2) require coal mining operations covered by a self-bond accepted by the State regulatory authority prior to enactment of this Act to replace the self-bond with another form of bond acceptable under such Act by not later than the earlier of the date of renewal of the permit or the date of any major permit modification.

Requires the Secretary to issue rules establishing limitations on surety bonds accepted to minimize the risk of financial liability to the Federal or State Government, including rules regarding

United Nations Oil-for-Food Accountability Act of 2004 - Requires that, until the President submits to Congress a certification that satisfies specified requirements, amounts shall be withheld from amounts appropriated for contributions to international organizations as follows: (1) 10 percent of the amount available for U.S. assessed contributions to the regular budget of the United Nations (UN) for FY 2005; and (2) 20 percent of the amount available for U.S. assessed contributions for FY 2006.

TANF Recipients' Lifeline Act - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to repeal the five-year limit on TANF benefits.Amends the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 to provide benefits under TANF to qualified aliens.Directs States to use bilingual personnel and printed material in the administration of TANF in those portions of the political subdivisions in the State in which a substantial number of TANF recipients speak a language other than English.Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to reduce by two percent the amount of a State's TANF grant for the immediately succeeding fiscal year for any State that has failed to use bilingual personnel and printed material in the administration of its TANF program. Extends the period of block grants for TANF to FY 2005.

Stop Assistance to Counterfeiters Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to prohibit providing U.S. assistance to a person seeking such assistance until such person certifies to the President that: (1) such assistance will not be used to intentionally traffic in goods or services that contain counterfeit marks; (2) such assistance will not be used by any person that has had an administrative or judicial determination issued against the person for infringement, counterfeiting, or piracy of intellectual property in the United States or a foreign country; (3) any material or product, including a material or product in electronic form, that was developed using such assistance will not be imported into the United States in violation of federal copyright law or the Tariff Act of 1930; and (4) if such assistance will be used for a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, or other agreement that includes use of any intellectual property, provides evidence of the right to use the intellectual property, including a written license agreement for the use of the intellectual property, the date of the first commercial use of the intellectual property, and any registration for the use of such government.

Requires such certification to be submitted to the President by a person seeking U.S. assistance prior to the provision of

Developing Resources Immediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2008 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2008 - Terminates all provisions of existing federal law prohibiting the spending of appropriated funds to conduct oil and natural gas leasing and preleasing activities for any area of the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS).

Revokes all withdrawals of federal submerged lands of the OCS from leasing, including withdrawals by the President under the authority of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act (OCSLA).

Revokes all authorities given to the President with respect to the leasing of federal submerged lands of the OCS, given under OCSLA, except in the interest of national security.

Authorizes the governor of a state to petition the Secretary of the Interior for authorization to conduct oil and natural gas exploration and extraction activities in any area that is at least 50 miles beyond the state's coastal zone.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to deposit into a Clean and Alternative Energy Fund in the Treasury, for each applicable fiscal year, 25% of qualified revenues from such rentals, royalties, bonus bids, and other sums due and payable to the United States from leases entered into under this Act for natural gas exploration and extraction activities

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to classify certain electric utility transmission and distribution plant land and qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property as 20-year property for depreciation recovery purposes. Defines "qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" as any roof system: (1) placed in service above conditioned or semi-heated space on an eligible commercial building during the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on December 31, 2013; (2) which has a slope equal to or less than 2:12; (3) which replaces an existing roof system; and (4) which includes insulation which meets or exceeds the minimum prescriptive requirements in tables A-1 to A-9 in the Normative Appendix A of ASHRAE Standard 189.1-2009, and in the case of an eligible commercial building located in a climate zone other than climate zone 6, 7, or 8, a primary roof covering which has a cool roof surface.

Federal Propaganda Prohibition Act of 2005 - Requires an executive agency to notify each of the following congressional committees within 30 days of entering into a contract for public relations, media relations, advertising, or public opinion research services: (1) the Committee on Government Reform of the House of Representatives; (2) the Committee on Governmental Affairs and Homeland Security of the Senate; (3) the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives; (4) the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and (5) each authorizing committee of the House and Senate with jurisdiction over the executive agency submitting the notification.

Requires such an agency that provided such a notification to submit to each such committee a copy of the contract, any modifications, and any materials produced.

Prohibits a U.S. officer or employee from making or authorizing a U.S. expenditure or obligation for publicity or propaganda purposes unless authorized by law. Subjects violators to appropriate administrative discipline, including suspension from duty without pay or removal from office, and criminal penalties, including imprisonment. Requires each executive agency advertisement or other communication to prominently inform the target audience that such communication is paid for by that agency.

Confederate Commemorative Works Inventory and Joint Resource Study Act - Directs the Secretaries of the Interior, Defense, and Veterans Affairs to conduct inventories of Confederate commemorative works under their respective administrative jurisdictions and submit the inventories to the Director of the National Park Service (NPS).  Requires the Director, using the inventories, to conduct a special resource study that:  (1) examines works, commemorating and interpreting the Civil War, the commemoration thereof, the soldiers, people on the home front and battle lines, and the related locations in the United States from 1861 through 1865; and (2) identifies, based on extensive research, a historical assessment of each inventoried Confederate commemorative work, an evaluation of the suitability and feasibility of retaining the work, the identification of properties that could meet criteria for listing in the National Register of Historic Places or criteria for designation as National Historic Landmarks, an evaluation of relevant historical research on education about, interpretation of, and public awareness of the work.

Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard Deadline Harmonization Act of 2015 This bill requires the governor of each state to designate all areas of the state as attainment, nonattainment, or unclassifiable with respect to the national ambient air quality standards for ozone published in the Federal Register on October 26, 2015, as well as any areas that have not been designated as attainment or nonattainment. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) must promulgate final designations for all areas in all states with respect to such standards, including any modifications to the areas designated as attainment or nonattainment. Each state must submit the plan required by the Clean Air Act for the 2015 ozone standards. The 2015 ozone standards shall not apply to the review and disposition of a preconstruction permit application if: (1) the EPA or the state, local, or tribal permitting authority determines the application to be complete on or before the date of promulgation of final designations, or (2) the EPA or the state, local, or tribal permitting authority publishes a public notice of a preliminary determination or draft permit for the application before 60 days after the date of promulgation of final designations

Endangered Species Community Advisory Board Act of 1995 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish an Endangered Species Community Advisory Board in connection with the designation of an area as either critical habitat or as a National Wildlife Refuge. 
Requires the Secretary to make funds available to facilitate the participation of private individuals on such boards to ensure public input in the designation process.  Permits such private individuals to use such funds only to:  (1) obtain technical assistance of experts in interpreting scientific data, material, and issues regarding protection of endangered species; and (2) educate the local community in understanding such data, material, and issues. 
Requires the Secretary, before designating any area as either critical habitat or as a National Wildlife Refuge, to:  (1) consult with and seek the advice and recommendations of the board regarding such issues; and (2) publish board recommendations within 180 days after the date the Secretary initiates consultation. 
Requires each such board to:  (1) monitor and periodically report to the Secretary on progress made in the conservation and recovery of species for which that critical habitat or Refuge was designated; and (2) periodically review and report to the

Freedom to Mourn in Peace Act of 2011 - Amends federal law to prohibit any person from carrying out: (1) a demonstration on the property where a funeral for a veteran is held unless the demonstration has been approved by the cemetery superintendent or the owner of the property on which the funeral is held; or (2) a part of such a demonstration that takes place within 150 feet of a road, pathway, or other route of ingress to or egress from such cemetery or other property and includes any individual willfully making or assisting in making of any noise or diversion that disturbs or tends to disturb the peace or good order of the funeral, or that is within 1,000 feet of such cemetery or other property and impedes access to or egress from such cemetery or other property, if there is visible at each place at the applicable distance a sign which clearly and conspicuously states that a funeral will be held on such cemetery or other property and so states the time interval during which the funeral will be held.

Defines "demonstration" to include: (1) picketing or similar conduct; (2) any oration, speech, use of sound amplification equipment or device, or similar conduct that is not

Helping to Encourage Real Opportunities (HERO) for At-Risk Youth Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the work opportunity tax credit, to: (1) allow an employer to claim the credit for regularly attending secondary school during the summer for up to 20 hours per week during any period between September 16 and April 30, and (2) allow an employer to claim the credit for an at-risk youth.  An at-risk youth is an individual who is: (1) between ages 16 and 25 on the hiring date, (2) not regularly attending any secondary, technical, or post-secondary school during the six-month period preceding the hiring date, (3) not regularly employed during such six-month period, and (4) not readily employable because of lacking a sufficient number of basic skills.  The bill extends the eligibility of the work opportunity tax credit through 2019.

Save America's Utility Infrastructure and Secure America Now Act of 2008 - Amends the Federal Power Act to revise the authority and enforcement powers of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) with respect to standards for the reliability of electric power systems. Extends the authority of the Commission to issue regulations that require electric power substations to operate without interruption in a manner that ensures the reliability of electric power to the public when disturbances (other than planned maintenance) last longer than five days. Directs the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Office of the Infrastructure Protection, to conduct a study to examine gaps in emergency planning preparedness and management as related to vulnerable populations.

Small Company Capital Formation Act of 2011 - Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to direct the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to add a class of securities to the securities exempted pursuant to such Act in accordance with the following terms and conditions: (1) the aggregate offering amount of all securities offered and sold within the prior 12-month period in reliance on such exemption shall not exceed $50 million; (2) such securities may be offered and sold publicly; (3) such securities shall not be restricted securities; (4) the civil liability provision in the Act shall apply to any person offering or selling such securities; (5) the SEC shall require the issuer to file audited financial statements with the SEC annually; (6) the SEC may require an issuer of a class of securities exempted under this Act to make available to investors and file with the SEC periodic disclosures regarding the issuer's business operations, financial condition, corporate governance principles, use of investor funds, and other appropriate matters; and (7) the SEC may provide for the suspension and termination of such a requirement with respect to that issuer.

Exempts only the following types of securities from the requirements of the Act: equity securities, debt securities, and

Federal Election Integrity Act of 2004 - Amends the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to require an applicant for voter registration to provide a photographic copy of any document which provides proof that the applicant is a U.S. citizen, in accordance with guidelines established by the Election Administration Commission.

Amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to require voters to provide a current and valid photo identification when voting in person or by mail.

Child Care Lending Pilot Act of 2003 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make loans to small, non-profit child care businesses to assist, in addition to other eligible small business concerns, such businesses, provided that: (1) the loan will be used for a sound business purpose that has been approved by the SBA; and (2) each such business receiving financial assistance meets all of the same eligibility requirements applicable to for-profit businesses under the Act, except for status as a for-profit business.

Flexible Refinancing for American Families Act of 2012 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to each carry out a program to provide for the refinancing of qualified mortgages on single-family housing owned by such enterprise through a refinancing mortgage having a 50-year term, and for the purchase of and securitization of such refinancing mortgages.

Requires such program to: (1) require such refinancing of a qualified mortgage upon the mortgagor's request and the mortgagor's determination that the mortgage is a qualified mortgage; and (2) provide for the payment of a fee to the servicer of $1,000 for each qualified mortgage of an enterprise that the servicer refinances through a refinancing mortgage pursuant to this Act.

Prohibits the mortgagor from requiring an appraisal of the property subject to the refinancing mortgage.

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA), beginning with FY2010, to make new discretionary budget authority available for the fiscal year involved and for the subsequent fiscal year in amounts first available after the end of such fiscal year. Specifies the medical care accounts of the VA to which such new budget authority shall apply.

Directs the Comptroller General to study the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the Enrollee Health Care Projection Model, or its equivalent, as utilized for the purpose of estimating and projecting VA health care expenditures with respect to the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.

(Sec. 1) This bill directs the Comptroller General to study and report to the Senate and House Communications and Transportation and Energy and Commerce Committees on the filing requirements for eligible telecommunications carriers or service providers that receive universal service support under the Communications Act of 1934 for the provision of universal service fund program services.  The Comptroller General must report on: (1) the filing requirements, including any filings required by the Universal Service Administrative Company; (2) the financial impact of those filing requirements on such carriers; and (3) recommendations on how to consolidate redundant filing requirements.  The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) must initiate a rulemaking to consolidate redundant filing requirements and seek comment on the report's recommendations.

Hunt Unrestricted on National Treasures Act or the HUNT Act - Requires each head of a federal public land management agency to make available on the agency's website a report that includes: (1) a list of the location and acreage of federal public land on which the public is allowed, under federal or state law, to hunt, fish, or use the land for other recreational purposes to which there is no public access or egress or to which public access or egress to the legal boundaries of the land is significantly restricted; (2) with respect to such land, a list of the locations and acreage on the land that the head of the agency determines have significant potential for use for hunting, fishing, and other recreational purposes; and (3) a plan developed by the agency that identifies how public access and egress could reasonably be provided to the legal boundaries of the land in a manner that minimizes the impact on wildlife habitat and water quality, specifies the actions recommended to secure the access and egress, and is consistent with the travel management plan in effect on the land.

Requires each agency head to make available on the website of such agency a list of roads or trails that provide the primary public access and egress to the legal boundaries of contiguous parcels of

Clean Alternatives for Energy Independence Act of 2005 - Amends the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to repeal the tax incentives for small refiner cooperatives and natural gas distribution lines and gathering lines.

Increases the residential fuel cell tax credit to $1,000.

Increases the tax credit for new qualified fuel cell motor vehicles and expands the eligibility of vehicles for such credit.

Increases the tax credit for alternative motor vehicle refueling property.

Fixed Asset Relief Act of 2015 Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase from 50% to 100% the rate of bonus depreciation for certain business equipment, (2) make such depreciation rate permanent, (3) allow a tax deduction for the depreciation of computer software, water utility property, or qualified leasehold improvement property, and (4) allow such a deduction for alternative depreciation purposes for certain other business equipment.

Amends the Siletz Tribe Indian Restoration Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to accept title to any additional number of acres of real property located within the boundaries of the original 1855 Siletz Coast Reservation (comprised of land within the political boundaries of Benton, Douglas, Lane, Lincoln, Tillamook, and Yamhill Counties in Oregon) if that real property is transferred to the United States by or on behalf of the tribe.

Requires that any real property taken into trust under this Act be considered and evaluated as an on-reservation acquisition under regulations governing acquisitions of tribal property and become part of the reservation of the tribe.

Requires approval from the appropriate county boards of county commissioners or other county executives of the counties in which the real property is located before the county can take into trust real property that is owned by the tribe. Allows revocation of such approval by a county executive.

Prohibits any real property taken into trust under this Act from being eligible, or used, for any gaming activity carried out under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

.  Measuring the Economic Impact of Broadband Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Department of Commerce to conduct an assessment and analysis regarding the contribution of the digital economy to the U.S. economy biennially.  The assessment and analysis shall consider: (1) the impact of the deployment and adoption of digital-enabling infrastructure and broadband; (2) e-commerce and platform-enabled peer-to-peer commerce; and (3) the production and consumption of digital media, including free media.

Increasing Medical Oversight in the Department of Veterans Affairs Act of 2014 - Establishes in the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) an Office of the Medical Inspector to: (1) review the quality of health care provided to veterans by the VA and through contracts with non-VA health care providers, (2) review VA offices and facilities and the performance of the VA in providing such care, (3) investigate any systemic issues that arise within the VA's Veterans Health Administration (VHA), (4) establish temporary investigative teams to carry out such reviews and investigations in response to specific incidents or inquiries, (5) recommend policies to promote economy and efficiency in the administration of VHA programs and operations and to prevent and detect criminal activity, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, and (6) carry out any other tasks required of the Office by the VA or the VA's Under Secretary for Health.  Requires the Medical Inspector to: (1) report on any problems or deficiencies encountered in VHA programs and operations, including any recommendations for corrective actions, and (2) make such reports available to the public on the VA's Internet website.

Rehab and Ahmed Amer Foster Care Improvement Act of 2012 - Amends part E (Foster Care and Adoption Assistance) of title IV of the Social Security Act to require a state to follow certain procedures in placing a child removed from the custody of his or her parents into foster care.

National Strategic Gasoline Reserve for Purposes of National Security Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to: (1) establish a Strategic Gasoline Reserve system with a total capacity of 10 million barrels of regular unleaded gasoline; (2) determine strategic locations for at least three and no more than five Gasoline Reserve sites, each located in a different geographical region of the United States; (3) confer with the Secretary of Transportation and the Secretary of Homeland Security with respect to physical structures' security, transportation security, and operational security; (4) transmit to Congress, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the governor of each state in which a Gasoline Reserve will be sited a plan for the transportation of the contents of the Gasoline Reserve to wholesale or retail markets in the event of an emergency sale; (5) complete the process of filling the Gasoline Reserve to a minimum of 90% within two years of submitting a transportation plan to Congress; (6) conduct an annual review of the gasoline supply to ensure that the reserves do not exceed their shelf life; (7) have in place within two years of enactment of this Act a plan for assuring that the inventory is sold and replaced in a manner that assures the

Skill Game Protection Act - Amends the Wire Act to exclude from the definition of "bets or wagers" for purposes of such Act any operating, or participation in, poker, chess, bridge, mahjong, or any other game where success is predominantly determined by a player's skill, to the extent that: (1) the game provides for competition only between and among participants, and not against the person operating the game; and (2) the operator is in compliance with regulations.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, before the end of the 180-day period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, to prescribe regulations requiring each person who operates a game of skill on the Internet to maintain: (1) safeguards to ensure that the individual participant depositing funds is 18 years of age or older; (2) safeguards to ensure that the individual participant is physically located in a jurisdiction that does not bar participation in the particular Internet games of skill in which the individual participates; (3) mechanisms to ensure that all taxes relating to Internet games of skill due to Federal and State governments and to Indian tribes from individual participants are collected; (4) safeguards to combat fraud and money laundering; (5) safeguards to combat compulsive participation in

Spearfish Canyon and Bismarck Lake Land Exchange Act This bill requires the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to convey to the state of South Dakota 4 parcels of land comprising approximately 1,954 acres in the Black Hills National Forest in South Dakota that are currently non-federal land if South Dakota conveys to USDA all right, title, and interest of South Dakota in and to those parcels.  USDA and South Dakota shall: (1) select an appraiser to conduct appraisals of the parcels; and (2) complete any environmental analysis required under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 with respect to the land exchange.  The non-federal land acquired by USDA shall be: (1) added to, and administered as part of, the Black Hills National Forest; and (2) managed in accordance with the laws applicable to the National Forest System.  If the non-federal land exchanged under this bill is subject to a lease, permit, or contract for the grazing of domestic livestock in effect on the date of acquisition of the non-federal land, USDA shall allow the grazing to continue subject to the related terms and conditions of user agreements.  The federal land acquired by the state shall be managed by the

Troubled Asset Relief Program Enhancement Act - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to require the Secretary of the Treasury to take specified actions to increase oversight of the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) to ensure that the Secretary's authority to make and enforce TARP-related requirements is publically accountable.

Requires the Comptroller General (GAO) to have access, upon request, to any information, data, schedules, books, accounts, financial records, reports, files, electronic communications, or other papers, things, or property belonging to or in use by any entity established by the Secretary of the Treasury under TARP, or any entity participating in a TARP program, including the exercise of such authority. Requires each contract, term sheet, or other agreement between the Secretary or TARP and an entity participating in a TARP program to provide for access by the Comptroller General.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from publicly disclosing proprietary or trade secret information obtained under this Act.

American Livestock Protection and Ranching Opportunity Act of 2014 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) the overwhelming majority of U.S. consumers want to know where the meat is born, raised, and slaughtered; (2) country-of-origin labeling provides information that consumers have a right to know; and (3) country-of-origin labeling facilitates supply chain information critical for food safety. Amends the Animal Health Protection Act to prohibit the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) from allowing the importation of fresh meat or meat products from a country until USDA certifies that the country is free of foot-and-mouth disease without vaccination. Establishes in the Department of Agriculture a livestock disease initiative to provide competitive matching grants to eligible entities for research and development relating to bovine brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, and other zoonotic diseases in livestock. Amends the Agricultural Act of 2014 to: (1) make livestock producers in the Greater Yellowstone Designated Surveillance Area (GYSDSA) eligible for assistance for grazing losses due to brucellosis, and (2) modify livestock indemnity payment rates. Authorizes the Secretary to provide a price adjustment in the monthly feed cost for high-value forage.

Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance Adjustment Act of 2002 - Amends Federal provisions concerning educational assistance to: (1) increase the rate of survivors' and dependents' educational assistance; (2) increase the rate of correspondence courses; (3) increase the rate of special restorative training; and (4) increase the rate of apprenticeship training.Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to modify the duration of educational assistance from 45 to 36 months in the case of a person who first files a claim for such assistance after enactment of this Act. Increases the aggregate annual amount available for State approving agencies for administrative expenses from $13 million to $18 million.

Strengthening Entrepreneurs' Economic Development Act of 2013 - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to: (1) establish and carry out a loan program for small businesses (with fewer than 20 employees) that are eligible for SBA assistance for state and local development projects; and (2) establish a process for small businesses to submit applications to secure such loans. Limits each loan to $150,000 and requires repayment within six years. Prohibits prepayment penalties. Sets forth loan interest rates and borrower fees. Directs the Administrator to: (1) establish a process for lenders to obtain loan applications submitted for such loans, and (2) offer to sell such loans through a semiannual public solicitation of offers to purchase. Amends the Small Business Act to direct the Administrator to assess and retain a fee for each high-dollar loan (exceeding $2 million) approved for state and local development projects.

Affordable Housing Preservation and Revitalization Act of 2009 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to transfer, at the time of a qualified sale or exchange, funds in the residual receipts account of an eligible multifamily housing property to a preservation entity.

Defines "residual receipts" as: (1) funds generated by a property in excess of the amount needed for operating expenses, operating reserve requirements, and allowable distributions to project owners; and (2) includes any other funds that the Secretary, in his or her discretion, designates as residual receipts.

Requires a preservation entity that acquires an eligible multifamily housing property through a qualified sale to use the funds in the transferred residual receipts account, or for its benefit, to: (1) pay for rehabilitation costs approved by the housing agency; (2) deposit funds into the replacement reserve account of the property; (3) pay for social and other services that directly benefit the tenants of such property, but in any year such payments may not exceed 10% of the balance of the property's residual receipts account at the end of the prior fiscal year; (4) pay for costs associated with the property's

District of Columbia Government Improvement and Efficiency Act of 1996 - Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act to reduce the number of members of the Board of Trustees of the American University from 45 to 25. 
Amends the Service Contract Act of 1965 to remove the District of Columbia from the list of places eligible for service contracts under such Act. 
Authorizes the Mayor of the District of Columbia and the Director of the Bureau of Prisons to enter into an agreement waiving certain requirements of the Act with respect to District of Columbia convicts in any Federal penitentiary, so long as the Director provides notice of the intent to enter into the agreement to specified congressional committees. 
Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act to exempt from Council review certain preconstruction, design, or construction contracts. 
Amends the District of Columbia Government Comprehensive Merit Personnel Act of 1978 to authorize the Director of Personnel to waive the requirement that the compensation of Office of the Inspector General employees be paid by the Government in the amount determined by the Inspector General. 
Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act to make the

Children's Express Lane to Health Coverage Act of 2003 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to allow a State Medicaid program to provide that financial eligibility requirements for medical assistance are met for an individual who is under age 21 by using a determination (made within a reasonable period) of the individual's family or household income or resources, notwithstanding any differences in budget unit, disregard, deeming, or other methodology, by a Federal or State agency (or a public or private entity making such determination on behalf of such agency) specified by the plan, including but not limited to the agencies administering the Food Stamp Act of 1977, the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act, and the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, provided that such agency has fiscal liabilities or responsibilities affected or potentially affected by such determinations and provided that all information furnished by such agency is used solely for purposes of determining eligibility for medical assistance under the State plan or for child health assistance under SSA title XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program).

State Prescription Drug Discount Act of 2002 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require manufacturers of drugs covered by a State prescription drug discount program to enter into agreements with States to make rebate payments for drugs covered by such program in the same amounts as are paid by the manufacturer to the State for such drugs under a rebate agreement.Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide for enhanced rebates for State Medicaid programs.

Minuteman Missile National Historic Site Establishment Act of 1998 - Establishes the Minuteman Missile National Historic Site in South Dakota as a unit of the National Park System.  Requires the Secretary of the Interior to prepare a general management plan for the Site, including an evaluation of an appropriate location for a visitor facility and administrative site within the areas depicted as "Support Facility Study Area--Alternative A" or "Support Facility Study Area--Alternative B" on the map of the Site. 
Authorizes appropriations. 
Directs the Secretary of the Air Force to transfer to the Secretary any funds specifically appropriated to the Air Force for the maintenance, protection, or preservation of the facilities described in this Act.  Requires the Secretary to use such funds to establish, operate, and maintain the Site.

Title II:  Controlling Outlays Under Medicare Program
 - Establishes a limit on total outlays to be made under the Medicare program for the fiscal year. 
Amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act) to provide for sequestration of any budgetary excess in the Medicare program if Congress has not enacted a joint resolution to save Medicare by a specified percentage by the first day of the fiscal year. 
Provides for reductions in Medicare outlays through sequestration.

Theodore Roosevelt Wildlife Legacy Act of 1997 - Sets forth the mission and purposes of the National Wildlife Refuge System.  Lists priority uses of the System. 
Directs the Secretary of the Interior, in administering the System, to ensure that:  (1) the mission and purposes of the System and the uses of the refuges are carried out; (2) opportunities for the public uses of the System receive priority attention in planning and management; (3) the System is planned to contribute to the conservation of U.S. ecosystems; and (4) fish, wildlife, and plant status and trends are monitored. 
Prohibits the Secretary from initiating or permitting a new use or expanding, renewing, or extending an existing allowed use of a refuge unless the Secretary determines that the use is compatible with the primary purposes of the refuge and the mission and purposes of the System.  Requires the Secretary to:  (1) identify, prior to acquisition, existing compatible priority public uses on lands added to the System; and (2) prepare a conservation plan for a refuge not later than two years after the Secretary has determined that sufficient land has been acquired to warrant comprehensive planning.
Government Shutdown Prevention Act - Provides for continuing appropriations (at the beginning of a fiscal year) in the absence of regular appropriations.

Investment Tax Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a deduction, in computing the alternative minimum taxable income, for depreciation of certain property placed in service in a taxable year beginning after December 31, 1992.  Repeals special depreciation rules applicable under the adjusted current earnings provisions of the minimum tax.

Deter Revolving-door Appointments In our Nation; Stop Washington Appointees from becoming Manipulative Petitioners Act or the DRAIN the SWAMP Act - Amends the federal criminal code to impose a five-year ban on a former political appointee serving as a registered lobbyist. Defines "political appointee" as an individual employed in a position: (1) described in the Executive Schedule; (2) a limited term, emergency, or noncareer appointee in the Senior Executive Service; or (3) of a confidential or policy-determining character under certain federal regulations. Authorizes the Director of the Office of Government Ethics to waive such ban if it would create an undue hardship in obtaining qualified personnel and granting such waiver would not create the potential for use of undue influence or unfair advantage.

Amends the Foreign Agents Registration Act of 1938 to prohibit a former political appointee from registering as an agent of a foreign principal.

Requires dealers and manufacturers to disclose to new automobile consumers, in a clear and conspicuous written format, the presence and location of, as well as the type of information recorded by and how such information is recorded, and the fact that such information may also be used in a law enforcement proceeding. Requires such information to be disclosed in the owner's manual.

Declares that any event data recorder in the vehicle and any data recorded on any event data recorder in the vehicle shall be considered the property of the owner of the vehicle. Prohibits the retrieval of recorded data by a person other than the owner, except under specified circumstances.

Prohibits manufacturers from selling, importing, or delivering into interstate commerce, or offering for sale, an automobile equipped with an event data recorder unless such recorder includes a function whereby the consumer has the option to enable or disable the recording function of such recorder. Requires that once disabled, such function shall not resume functioning until the consumer elects to re-enable it.

Treats violations of this Act as unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Stabilize Medicaid and CHIP Coverage Act This bill amends titles XIX (Medicaid) and XXI (Children's Health Insurance Program) (CHIP) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid or CHIP plan to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for benefits under such plan shall remain eligible and enrolled for such benefits through the end of the month in which the 12-month period (beginning on the date of determination of eligibility) ends.

National Milestones to Measure Progress in Ending the Opioid Epidemic Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop national indicators to measure success in curtailing the opioid epidemic, with the goal of significantly reversing the toll of opioid misuse and opioid-related morbidity and mortality within five years. HHS may extend the timeline for meeting the goal if the indicators or metrics will not be met within that timeframe. HHS must report annually to Congress on the national milestones and provide an update on the progress of federal agencies in achieving the goals detailed in the milestones.

Deems the full equalization of allotments within the meaning of the Agua Caliente Equalization Act of 1959 to have been completed. 
Deems to have expired the entitlement of holders of equalized allotments to distribution of net revenues from parcel B. 
Amends the Act to remove the restriction that the mineral springs of the Band be used for equalization purposes only.  Makes the amendment applicable as if enacted on March 31, 1983.  Requires any per capita distribution of tribal revenues of the Band made after the date of enactment of this Act to be made to all members of the Band in equal amounts.

Special Needs Trust Fairness and Medicaid Improvement Act (Sec. 2) This bill allows a Medicaid supplemental needs trust to pay the entire cost of the care provided by the trust to an individual who is the individual's next of kin. (Sec. 3) Medicaid continues to cover tobacco cessation services for pregnant women through the first year after giving birth. (Sec. 4) The bill eliminates federal financial participation with respect to Medicaid expenditures for agents used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth, except where medically necessary. (Sec. 5) The bill makes available for the Medicaid Improvement Fund additional funding for FY2021 and FY2022.

Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to provide that a member of a reserve component of the Armed Forces who is ordered to report for military service for a period of more than 90 days and who, on the date of such order, is a lessee of real property that is occupied by the member or dependents as their primary residence shall not be required to pay rent under that lease for any period of such service during which the member is assigned to duty at a location sufficiently distant from such property that the member is unable to reside there. Provides that a member of a reserve component who is ordered to report for military service for a period of more than 90 days and who, on the date of such order, resides at real property that is occupied by the member or dependents as their primary residence is: (1) owned by the member; and (2) secured by a mortgage. Provides that any payment not made by reason of this Act shall be deferred and shall be appended, on a month-for-month basis, to the end of the term of the mortgage, in the same amount as originally due.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that a lessor shall be allowed a refundable tax credit for the reserve component rent relief credit.

Patent and Trademark Office Authorization Act of 2002 - Authorizes appropriations to the United States Patent and Trademark Office for FY 2003 through 2008 based on certain fees estimated by the Secretary of Commerce.Authorizes the Director of the Office to develop an electronic system for the filing and processing of patent and trademark applications that is user friendly and that includes the necessary infrastructure to: (1) allow examiners and applicants to send all communications electronically; and (2) allow the Office to process, maintain, and search electronically the contents and history of each application.Establishes conditions under which the Secretary of Commerce shall report to specified congressional committees on the progress made in implementing the 21st Century Strategic Plan issued on June 3, 2002, and any amendments made to the plan.Directs the Secretary to submit to such committees annual reports on the determination of the existence of a substantial new question of patentability in reexamination proceedings.Directs the Secretary to permit a third-party requester to: (1) appeal with respect to any final decision favorable to the patentability of any original or proposed amended or new claim of the patent; and (2) be a party to any appeal taken by the patent owner.

Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2011, the duty on certain three-ring binders that are wholly or predominantly covered with polyester fabric.

Wholesale Motor Fuel Fairness and Competition Restoration Act - Prohibits an owner or operator of a terminal facility from selling motor fuel from the terminal facility to a distributor or retailer at a price in excess of the price it charges any other distributor or retailer, including one it owns or with which it is affiliated. Makes such prohibition inapplicable to sales made pursuant to the terms of a franchise or sales contract entered into before October 17, 2000. Authorizes the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to assess a civil penalty, not to exceed $1 million, for each such violation. Provides for criminal penalties for violations. Requires FTC regulations concerning disclosure of wholesale motor fuel pricing policies to establish procedures for determining the price an owner or operator of a terminal facility charges a distributor or retailer which it owns or with which it is affiliated. Requires FTC dissemination of information acquired pursuant such regulations to the public. 
Directs FTC to study and report to Congress on whether ownership or operation by a refiner of a facility for the retail sale of motor fuel has anticompetitive effects on the price of motor fuel.

Foreign Medical School Accountability Fairness Act of 2013 - Amends title I (General Provisions) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to repeal the grandfather clause with respect to loans to foreign graduate medical schools. (The grandfather clause prohibits a foreign graduate medical school from receiving a loan if, in the preceding two years, at least 60% of the students enrolled and 60% of the graduates were persons ineligible for loans under the Federal Family Education Loan program, and at least 75% of the students or graduates who were nationals of the United States or of the countries of the European Union, Japan, or Australia taking the medical licensing examinations administered by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates received a failing score in the preceding two years.) Terminates the authority of such schools to participate in the loan programs after July 1, 2014.

Disclosure; and Encouragement of Verification, Innovation, Cleaning, and Efficiency Act of 2017 or the DEVICE Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require a device manufacturer to give the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) notice of any change to the design of a medical device, or reprocessing instructions for a device, that is marketed in interstate commerce. The bill also requires the FDA to approve any communication to foreign health care providers that relates to a change to the recommended reprocessing protocols, if any, for a device, or a safety concern about the device. The bill defines "reusable device" as a device that is intended to be used more than once and must be sanitized to ensure that it is safe and effective for such intended use. The FDA must publish a list of types of rapid assessment tests for which reports must include specified validation data.
