ESA Improvement Act of 2014 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to exclude from the National Invasive Species Council (NICS) list any population of a species in a state that has approved a state protective action for such population. Directs the Secretary to: (1) notify each state in which a population of the species occurs of the opportunity to submit to the Secretary a proposed state protective action for the species in such state, and (2) provide guidance to the state regarding such preparation. Requires the Secretary to approve or disapprove a proposed state protective action by not later than 45 days after its submission. Allows a proposed action to be resubmitted before the end of the 45-day period, and the Secretary to issue a final decision regarding the proposed action. Prohibits the Secretary from adding a population of a species to a list before a final determination is made regarding approval of each state protective action for such population. Treats an approved state protective action as a cooperative agreement entered into pursuant to the Act. Directs the Secretary to review every five years the implementation and effectiveness of the approved state protective action, and if necessary, provide guidance on revisions that are required to

Requires a vessel that is exempted from such standards to: (1) notify prospective passengers and crew members in writing that the vessel does not comply with applicable fire safety standards due primarily to the wooden construction of passenger berthing areas; (2) display prominently throughout the vessel, including in each state room, a notice that the vessel fails to comply with safety rules and regulations of the U.S. Coast Guard; (3) disclaim liability to a passenger or crew member for death, injury, or any other loss caused by fire due to the negligence of the owner or managing operator; (4) acquire liability insurance in an amount to be prescribed by the Federal Maritime Commission; (5) make annual structural alteration to not less than 10% of the areas

Health Care for Young Adults Act of 2005 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to provide for Medicaid coverage of young adults up to age 23.

Amends SSA title XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program) (SCHIP) to provide for SCHIP coverage of young adults up to age 23.

Authorizes appropriations for FY2006-FY2009 to States to provide additional allotments for coverage of optional young adults.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide for grants to States to implement expansions of eligibility for children and young adults under their State Medicaid and SCHIP plans.

Lower Colorado River Multi-Species Conservation Program Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to manage and implement the Lower Colorado River Multi-Species Conservation Program (LCR MSCP) in accordance with the Program Documents.

Authorizes the Secretary to enter into an agreement with the States of Arizona, California, and Nevada for the use of water from the Lower Colorado River for habitat creation and maintenance in accordance with the Program Documents.

Rocky Mountain National Park Wilderness Act of 1997 - Designates specified lands in Rocky Mountain National Park, Colorado, as wilderness and components of the National Wilderness Preservation System, and shall be known as the Rocky Mountain National Park Wilderness.  Includes within such Wilderness the lands within the Indian Peaks Wilderness that were transferred to Rocky Mountain National Park. 
Reserves water within the Wilderness.

Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to: (1) enhance and expand research and surveillance infrastructure to study the epidemiology of congenital heart disease (CHD) from birth to adulthood; (2) plan and implement a public outreach and education campaign regarding CHD across the lifespan; and (3) award grants to eligible entities to carry out a cohort study to improve understanding of the epidemiology of CHD across the lifespan, and an awareness campaign regarding CHD.  The bill authorizes the CDC to expand, intensify, and coordinate research and related activities of the Institute of Medicine on CHD.

Small Business Lending to Entrepreneurs for Growth in Underserved Populations Act of 2011 or the Small Business Leg-Up Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to transfer all unobligated funds in the Small Business Lending Fund to the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund.

Amends the Riegle Community Development and Regulatory Improvement Act of 1994 to direct the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to carry out a small business capital investment program to make capital investments in eligible community development financial institutions in order to increase the availability of credit for small businesses. Defines "eligible" as a community development financial institution with assets of $10 billion or less, as reported in audited financial statements.

Interstate Transport Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill allows a person who is not otherwise prohibited by any federal law from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a knife to transport a knife from any place where the person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport the knife to any other place where the person may lawfully do so if: (1) the knife is not directly accessible from the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle or is contained in a locked container other than the glove compartment or console in the case of motor vehicle transport, and (2) in the case of transport by other means, the knife is contained in a locked container.  This bill shall not apply to the transport of a knife or tool in the cabin of a passenger aircraft subject to the rules and regulations of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).  A person who is transporting a knife in compliance with this bill may not be arrested for violation of any state or local law related to the possession, transport, or carrying of a knife, unless there is probable cause to believe that the person is not in compliance.

Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to grant an easement or right-of-way on the outer Continental Shelf or specified activities formerly authorized (the Deepwater Port Act of 1974 and the Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Act of 1980) when such activities: (1) support exploration, development, production, transportation, or storage of oil, natural gas, or other minerals; (2) produce or support production, transportation, or transmission of energy from sources other than oil and gas; or (3) use facilities currently or previously used for activities authorized under such Acts.

Requires the Secretary to establish reasonable forms of annual or one-time payments for any such easement or right-of-way, including fees, rentals, or cash bonus payments.

Requires the Secretary to consult with the Secretary of Defense concerning issues related to national security and navigational obstruction.

Authorizes the Secretary to issue an easement or right-of-way for energy and related purposes as described above either competitively or non-competitively, subject to specified factors.

Directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress on the results of: (1) an independent safety assessment of the design, construction, maintenance, and operational safety performance of the systems at the Indian Point Energy Center, Units 2 and 3, located in Westchester County, New York; and (2) a comprehensive evaluation of the radiological emergency plan for such units, conducted by the NRC and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including a response to each of the criticisms of the plan contained in the Review of Emergency Preparedness of Areas Adjacent to Indian Point and Millstone, published by James Lee Witt Associates on January 10, 2003.

Alaska Native Veterans Land Allotment Equity Act - Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to make eligible for allotments under such Act any person who is a veteran who served between August 5, 1964, and May 7, 1975, or who would otherwise have been eligible for an allotment on land withdrawn from the United States by the Native Corporation of Alaska. Allows such a person who qualifies to select an alternative allotment from land located within the boundaries of such land withdrawn, and which is not selected or relinquished by the Native Corporation as an heir to the individual applying for an allotment on behalf of the estate of the individual.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) approve any application for an allotment filed within three years after the Secretary determines that such application is appropriate; and (2) issue a certificate of allotment under any term, condition, or restriction as the Secretary determines to be appropriate. Requires the Secretary to notify any person or entity that has an interest in such land that is potentially adverse to the interest of the applicant of the right to initiate a private contest of the allotment or to file a protest against the allotment. Clean Water Compliance and Ratepayer Affordability Act of 2015 This bill requires the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to carry out a pilot program to work with and facilitate the efforts of municipalities to develop and implement integrated plans to meet their wastewater and stormwater obligations under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (commonly known as the Clean Water Act) in a cost-effective and flexible manner and consistent with the Integrated Municipal Stormwater and Wastewater Approach Framework issued by EPA in May 2012.  The EPA shall select at least 15 municipalities to participate in the program each fiscal year. A municipality shall be eligible to participate if it: (1) is a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permit holder or designee, or (2) is operating under an administrative order, administrative consent agreement, or judicial consent decree to comply with the requirements of the Clean Water Act. In approving the integrated plan of a municipality under the pilot program, the EPA shall: (1) account for the municipality's financial capability to adequately address the requirements of the Clean Water Act that apply to the municipality, (2) prioritize the obligations of the municipality under the Clean Water Act according to the most cost-effective and environmentally beneficial outcomes, (3)

National Heroes Credit Protection Act - Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to authorize a member of a reserve component who serves on active duty outside the continental United States in support of a contingency operation to request that a consumer reporting agency include a military service deployment explanation with respect to a qualifying account in the file of that member at the agency.

Requires a consumer reporting agency, upon receiving such a request, to: (1) include such explanation in the file of the requesting member; (2) provide the explanation to each person who requests the credit score or consumer report of the member; (3) develop and maintain procedures for the referral to other such agencies of any such explanation; and (4) notify the member in writing that the inclusion of any explanation or notation could potentially negatively affect the member's credit rating and may not mitigate a low credit score.

Requires a reseller to include in any report of the reseller on a servicemember any military service deployment explanation placed in the member's file by another consumer reporting agency.

Requires any prospective user of a consumer credit report containing such an explanation to acknowledge it.

EINSTEIN Act of 2015 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to deploy, operate, and maintain technologies to protect federal agency information and federal civilian information systems. DHS may access information traveling to or from or stored on a federal civilian information system, enter into contracts or other agreements with private entities to deploy, operate, and maintain such technologies, and retain, use, and disclose information obtained through such activities to protect federal agency information and federal civilian information systems from cybersecurity risks only to investigate, prosecute, disrupt, or otherwise respond to specified violations of federal law, threats to life and limb, or attempts to commit such violations.  Contracts or other agreements regarding such activities must include appropriate provisions barring: (1) the disclosure of information to any entity other than the DHS or a federal agency disclosing information in accordance with this Act that can be used to identify specific persons and is reasonably believed to be unrelated to a cybersecurity risk; and (2) the use of any information to which such private entity gains access for any purpose other than to protect federal agency information and federal civilian information systems against cybersecurity risks or to administer any such contract or other agreement.

Medicare Drug Formulary Protection Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to prohibit the Medicare prescription drug plan (PDP) sponsor from removing a covered part D (generic) drug from the plan formulary or imposing a restriction or limitation on coverage of such a drug other than at the beginning of each plan year, except as the Secretary of Health and Human Services may permit to take into account new therapeutic uses and newly covered part D drugs.

Makes exceptions for a covered part D drug that: (1) is a brand name drug for which there is a generic drug approved that is placed on the market during the period in which there are limitations on removal or change in the formulary; (2) is a brand name drug that goes off-patent during such period; (3) is a drug for which the Commissioner of Food and Drugs issues a clinical warning that imposes a restriction or limitation on the drug during such period; or (4) has been determined to be ineffective during such period.

Requires the PDP sponsor to provide notice (such as through a preferred status or usage restriction) of any removal or change under this Act to the Secretary, affected enrollees, physicians, pharmacies, and pharmacists.

Rail Merger Reform and Customer Protection Act - Amends Federal transportation law to revise the antitrust permitting process for rail carriers and rail transportation by requiring the Surface Transportation Board (STP) to find that a proposed rail carrier merger will not reduce transportation alternatives available to current railroad customers and will not provide additional transportation alternative options for railroad customers, will not increase competition among rail carriers, and will not improve service to customers. Prohibits the Board from approving or authorizing any transaction unless the Attorney General agrees with the Board's findings.

Subjects rail carriers and rail transportation to the jurisdiction of the Board as well as the antitrust laws.

Prescribes guidelines for the application of the antitrust laws.

Exempts from the Sherman Act's antitrust prohibitions any rate agreements between rail carriers that are in effect as of the date of the enactment of this Act and that carry out the agreement (currently, such agreements are exempted from the Sherman Act's antitrust prohibitions if the agreement is made pursuant to a court order or the Sherman Act's antitrust prohibitions would not apply to the agreement).

Declares that nothing in the Sherman Act is amended by this Act.

Prohibits a person proceeding against a rail carrier from proceeding against the same rail carrier under Federal or State law,

Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial 1-Cent Coin Redesign Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, during 2009, to issue one-cent coins with the reverse side bearing four different designs representing different aspects of the life of Abraham Lincoln.

Energy Efficient Buildings Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to establish a pilot program to award competitive grants to businesses and organizations for new construction or major renovations of energy efficient buildings to demonstrate innovative energy efficiency technologies, especially those sponsored by the Department of Energy.

Requires the Secretary to give due consideration to proposals for buildings that are likely to serve low and moderate income populations.

Authorizes appropriations for FY2008-FY2012.

Prosperous and Secure Neighbor Alliance Act of 2007 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to require the President, acting through the Director of Foreign Assistance, to provide assistance to improve security and promote economic development in Mexico by: (1) training Mexican law enforcement personnel to combat illicit drugs and drug-related violence; (2) providing technology to assist such personnel; (3) strengthening the Mexican judicial branch; and (4) supporting anti-corruption programs in Mexico.

Directs the President to evaluate the results of such programs, and to report on them to Congress.

Authorizes appropriations for FY2008-FY2012.

Expresses the sense of Congress that certain amounts of assistance should be made available for each of specified activities related to combating illicit drugs and drug-related violence in Mexico and the United States.

Social Security Lock-Box Act of 2005 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to make it out of order in the House of Representatives or the Senate to consider any concurrent budget resolution, amendment, or conference report that would set forth totals for any fiscal year with respect to the Social Security Trust Funds that are less than the totals of such funds for that fiscal year as calculated in accordance with a current services baseline. Makes such point of order inapplicable if a violation of such point would result from an assumption in the resolution, amendment, or conference report of an increase in outlays or a decrease in revenues and disbursements relative to the baseline underlying that resolution for social security reform legislation for any such fiscal year.

Makes it out of order in the House of Representatives or the Senate to consider any bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report if the enactment of such legislation or resolution, the adoption and enactment of such amendment, or the enactment of such legislation in the form recommended in that conference report would cause the totals for any fiscal year covered by the most recently agreed to concurrent budget resolution to be less than the totals of the Social Security Trust Funds for that fiscal year as calculated in accordance with the current services baseline. Economic Recovery Through Responsible Homeownership Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individual taxpayers who purchase a residence in the United States in 2009 or 2010 a refundable tax credit for up to $10,000 of the purchase price if the down payment is at least 15%. Sets a $5,000 credit for a down payment of at least 10% and a $2,000 credit for a down payment of at least 5%. Exempts any taxpayer from such credit if the residence is financed by the proceeds of a tax-exempt mortgage or the taxpayer is a nonresident alien.

Creating Opportunities for Rural Economic Expansion Act or the CORE Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a new market tax credit for investments in a qualified active low-income community business located in a low-income community which is contiguous to a county that was one of the 30 counties with the biggest employment decrease among coal operators or that contains at least 1 low-income community.  The bill also allows a recapture of previously earned tax credit amounts for such investments.

Requires an end-use certificate that meets specified requirements to be included in the documentation covering the entry of any foreign commodity.  Requires a consignee of any imported foreign commodity to submit to the Secretary of Agriculture a quarterly report that certifies:  (1) what quantity of the foreign commodity was used by the consignee during the quarter; and (2) that the commodity was used for the purpose stated in the end-use certificate. 
Directs the Secretary to prescribe such requirements as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this Act.  Provides for:  (1) customs and civil penalties for end-use certificates required by this Act; and (2) the Commissioner of Customs to permit entry of a foreign commodity unless the importer presents an end-use certificate.

Higher Education Accrediting Agency Responsibility Act of 2002 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to repeal the mandate for the National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity. Revises the title of the Act to: (1) make the purpose of accreditation in the Act's purview the same as that of the Department of Education; and (2) make the title of the Department's report on accreditation the same as that of the Act's report to the Congress. Repeals the title of the Act on the subject of accrediting agencies. Revises the definition of "institutional quality and integrity" to include the quality and integrity of historically black colleges and universities (HBCUs). Repeals the title of the Act on the subject of distance education demonstration programs. Repeals the title of the Act on the subject of program participation agreements. Repeals the title of the Act on the subject of accrediting agency recognition. Repeals the title of the Act on the subject of eligibility and certification procedures.

Debt Relief and IMF Reform Act of 1999 - Amends the Bretton Woods Agreements Act to condition the approval of any proposal by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to sell or otherwise convert or liquidate gold on specified congressional conditions, including:  (1) cancellation of all debts owed to the IMF by Haiti and the heavily indebted poor countries; (2) the Secretary of the Treasury's demonstration to the Congress that there is no other feasible way to finance such debt cancellation; (3) the IMF's operational budget, with any information that could disrupt financial markets or affect adversely the national security of any country redacted, and the publicly available financial statements of the IMF are reorganized and restated in a manner consistent with the IMF's code of good practices and the principles of transparency and accountability; (4) the Congress's joint resolution certifying that the IMF is in full compliance with certain conditions imposed by the Foreign Operations, Export Financing, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 1999; (5) the proposal to sell all gold held by the IMF on the effective date of the Second Amendment to the Articles of Agreement of the IMF; (6) the interest accruing on any investment of the residual proceeds to the

Directs the Election Assistance Commission to establish a program to make backup paper ballots available in case of voting system or equipment failure or other emergency situations in the administration of the regularly scheduled general election for federal office held in November 2008.

Requires the Commission to make such a grant to each participating state and each unit of local government if the state or local government submits an application at such time and in such manner as the Commission shall require, and includes in the application: (1) a certification that the state or local government has established a program to make backup paper ballots available in such cases; (2) a statement of the reasonable costs the state or local government expects to incur in carrying out its program; (3) a certification that the state or local government will repay the Commission any amount by which the payment made under this Act exceeds the actual costs incurred in carrying out its program; and (4) such other information and certifications as the Commission may require.

Sets forth requirements for a program to make backup paper ballots available in such cases, including: (1) notification of individuals who are waiting at a polling place on election day to cast a ballot in the election if the voting equipment at the polling place malfunctions and cannot be used to cast ballots or if some other

Clean Slate for Kids Online Act of 2018 This bill amends the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 to make it unlawful for an operator of a website or online service directed to children, or any operator that has actual knowledge that it is collecting personal information from a child, to fail to delete personal information collected from a child if a request for deletion is made pursuant to this Act. The Federal Communications Commission must promulgate regulations that require the operator of any website or online service directed to children, or any operator that has actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child, to:  provide notice on the website of how an individual over the age of 13, or a legal guardian of such individual, can request that the operator delete all personal information in the possession of the operator that was collected from or about the individual when the individual was a child, and promptly delete all such personal information when a request is made by an individual over the age of 13 or by the legal guardian of such individual acting with the knowledge and consent of the individual; provide written confirmation of deletion after the deletion has occurred to an individual or legal guardian of such individual who has requested such deletion; and  except personal information collected from or about a

Access to Inpatient Rehabilitation Therapy Act of 2017 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to include recreational therapy services among the therapeutic modalities that constitute an intensive rehabilitation therapy program in determining whether inpatient services in an inpatient rehabilitation facility are reasonable and necessary.

America's Cup Act of 2011 - Authorizes an eligible competing or supporting vessel operating only in preparation for, or in connection with, the 34th America's Cup to position competing vessels and transport individuals and equipment and supplies utilized for the staging, operations, or broadcast of the competition from and around U.S. ports.

Prohibits a vessel from operating unless it has received an Eligibility Certification from the Administrator of the Maritime Administration of the Department of Transportation (DOT). Subjects a vessel participating in the 34th America's Cup as a competing or supporting vessel that has not received an Eligibility Certification or is not in compliance with certain requirements to the applicable penalties for noncompliance.

Authorizes the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating to issue a certificate of documentation with a coastwise endorsement for each of the following vessels: (1) LNG GEMINI, (2) LNG LEO, and (3) LNG VIRGO.

Portable Fuel Container Safety Act of 2017 This bill requires the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to promulgate a final rule for flame mitigation devices in portable fuel containers that impedes the propagation of flame into the container, except when the CPSC determines that: (1) there is a voluntary standard for flame mitigation devices in portable fuel containers that impedes the propagation of flame into the container, and (2) the voluntary standard is in effect within 18 months and is developed by an organization that the CPSC determines has met the intent of this bill. The CPSC must: (1) undertake a campaign to educate consumers about the dangers associated with using or storing portable fuel containers for flammable liquids near an open flame or any other ignition source, and (2) submit a summary of actions taken in such campaign to Congress. The bill amends the Children's Gasoline Burn Prevention Act to include in the definition of "gasoline" for purposes of such Act the following: "any receptacle for gasoline, kerosene, or diesel fuel, including any spout, retrofit spout, cap, and other closure mechanism and component of such receptacle, produced or distributed for sale to or use by consumers for transport of, or ref

Social Security Preservation through Individual Choice Enhancement Act - Amends the Tax Relief, Unemployment Insurance Reauthorization, and Job Creation Act of 2010 to allow an individual to make a tax holiday election for a calendar year (or taxable year beginning in such calendar year) in the payroll tax holiday period beginning in or after 2012. Allows such election to be made before July 1 of the calendar year for which such remuneration is received. Allows an individual to revoke an election to have such effect if made before July 1 of the calendar year. Prescribes special rules for making such an election and revoking it. Allows an individual to elect to take an employee payroll tax cut. Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) of the Social Security Act to increase by one month the retirement age for each calendar year beginning with or after 2012 for which the payroll tax cut election applies.

Directs the Secretary of the Air Force to carry out a demonstration program to assess the feasibility and advisability of permitting individuals with auditory impairments (including deafness) to access as officers of the Air Force. Requires the program to include at least 15 but no more than 20 individuals. Requires the program participants to be individuals who are deaf and individuals who have a range of other auditory impairments. Requires the Secretary to: (1) publicize the program nationally, including to individuals who have auditory impairments and would be otherwise qualified for officer training; (2) create a process whereby interested individuals can apply for the program; and (3) select program participants from among applicants based on certain criteria. Requires the participants to undergo the Basic Officer Training course or the Commissioned Officer Training course at Maxwell Air Force Base, Alabama. Requires the Secretary to designate a special advisor to the program to act as a resource for program participants and as a liaison between program participants and those providing officer training.
Protect Children from Video Game Sex and Violence Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit the sale or rental of adult video games to minors. Sets forth penalties for violations.

ED 1.0 Act - Establishes within the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) a pilot program under which the Administrator shall award four matching grants to eligible educational institutions to develop digital and wireless networks for online educational programs of study within the institutions. Requires the Administrator to give priority to institutions that serve counties in which: (1) 50% of the residents are members of a racial or ethnic minority; (2) less than 18% of the residents have obtained a baccalaureate degree or a higher education; (3) the unemployment rate is 7% or greater; (4) 19% or more of the residents live in poverty; (5) the population is growing at a negative rate; or (6) the median family income is $32,000.

Allows grant funds to be used to: (1) acquire equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware, software, digital network technology, wireless technology, or wireless infrastructure; (2) develop and provide educational services, including faculty development; or (3) develop strategic plans for information technology investments.

Hospital Price Reporting and Disclosure Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require a hospital and an ambulatory surgical center to report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services certain data, including the frequency with which each service and drug was performed or administered, the total number of times each service was performed or the drug was administered, and the average and median charge by the hospital for each service or drug.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) select the 25 most frequently performed services in a hospital inpatient setting, the 25 most frequently performed services in a hospital outpatient setting, the 25 most frequently performed services in an ambulatory surgical center setting, and the 50 most frequently administered drugs in a hospital inpatient setting; and (2) periodically update such selection.

Authorizes the Secretary to impose a civil penalty of up to $10,000 for each knowing violation of the reporting requirements.

Nuclear Innovation Act This bill requires the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out a program to enhance the nation's capabilities to develop new reactor technologies through high-performance computation modeling and simulation techniques.  DOE must coordinate with relevant federal agencies through the National Strategic Computing Initiative while taking into account:   utilizing expertise from the private sector, universities, and National Laboratories to develop computational software and capabilities that prospective users may access to accelerate research and development of advanced fission reactor systems, nuclear fusion systems, and reactor systems for space exploration; developing computational tools to simulate and predict nuclear phenomena that may be validated through physical experimentation; increasing the utility of DOE's research infrastructure by coordinating with the Advanced Scientific Computing Research program within the Office of Science; leveraging experience from the Energy Innovation Hub for Modeling and Simulation; and ensuring that new experimental and computational tools are accessible to relevant research communities.  DOE must consider support for additional research activities to maximize the utility of its research facilities, including physical processes to simulate degradation of materials and behavior of fuel forms and for validation of computational tools.  DOE must carry out a program to enable the testing and demonstration of reactor concepts to be proposed and funded by the private sector. Oregon Coastal Land Conveyance Act - Declares that all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to approximately 14,804 acres of federal land (the land to be conveyed), including any improvements located on it, appurtenances to it, and minerals on or in it, shall be held in trust by the United States for the benefit of the Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua, and Siuslaw Indians and shall be part of their reservation.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) complete a survey of the boundary lines to establish the boundaries of the land taken into trust, and (2) file a map and legal description of the land with the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the House Committee on Natural Resources.

Applies federal law relating to the export of unprocessed logs harvested from federal land to any unprocessed logs that are harvested from the federal land.

Prohibits gaming on the land taken into trust.

Department of Environmental Protection Act - Redesignates the Environmental Protection Agency as the Department of Environmental Protection.

Fighting Medicare Payment Fraud Act of 2009 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services, upon a determination that there is a likelihood of fraud, waste, or abuse involving a particular category of service providers or suppliers, categories of service providers or suppliers in a certain geographic area, or individual service providers or suppliers, to extend the number of calendar days in which Medicare claims must be paid to up to 365 days with respect to claims submitted by such categories or suppliers, or such time as is necessary to ensure that the claims with respect to individual providers of services or suppliers are clean claims. Requires the Secretary to engage in heightened scrutiny of claims during such extended period of time.

Directs the Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services to report to the Secretary recommendations with respect to the application of this Act.

Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Modernization Act of 2008 - Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to require the President, acting through the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), to: (1) modernize the integrated public alert and warning system to ensure that the President can alert and warn governmental authorities and the civilian population in areas endangered by disasters; and (2) implement such system.

Small Business, Family Farms, and Constitutional Protection Act - Prohibits the use of federal funds to: (1) propose or issue rules, regulations, decrees, or orders or to use funds for programs designed to implement the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change before the date on which the Senate gives its advice and consent to ratification of such Protocol; or (2) advocate, develop, or implement a program providing regulatory credits for early voluntary greenhouse gas emission reductions before such date.

The bill requires the chairperson of the Committee, instead of just one of the members, to be the head of the agency to which the President has delegated primary responsibility for government-wide coordination of the authorities in the Act. The bill also requires the chairperson to appoint one person to coordinate all of the Committee's activities. The bill requires the Committee to issue a report each year by March 31. The bill requires the chairperson to: (1) be a full-time employee of the federal government, (2) report to the chairperson, and (3) carry out activities relating to the Committee that the chairperson may determine appropriate.  The bill requires the chairperson to: (1) review the contingency planning by the President for events that might require the use of the priorities and allocations authorities, and (2) make recommendations for legislation actions to support the effective use of such authorities. The bill requires the Committee to: (1) issue a report that describes the use of such authorities, (2) annually review and update any final rules related to such authorities, and (3) make up

Preventing Iran's Access to United States Dollars Act of 2016 This bill prohibits the President from issuing any license under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act that permits a person to: (1) conduct an offshore U.S. dollar clearing system for transactions involving the government of Iran or an Iranian person, or (2) provide U.S. dollars for any offshore U.S. dollar clearing system conducted or overseen by a foreign government or a foreign financial institution for transactions involving the government of Iran or an Iranian person.  The Department of the Treasury shall report to Congress at least every 90 days on any identified financial institution that: (1) operates an offshore U.S. dollar clearing system that conducts transactions involving the government of Iran or an Iranian person, or (2) participates in such an transaction through a system described above.  The President shall block and prohibit transactions in all property and property interests of such financial institution if any such property and property interests are in the United States, come within the United States, or are or come within the possession or control of a U.S. person.  The bill amends the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 to consider property that comes within the possession or control of a U.S. person

Biased IRS Audit Systems Prevention Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to: (1) provide taxpayers sufficient information regarding the reason a tax return has been selected for an audit by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and (2) preserve and make available for review by an applicable oversight entity any information or criteria used in selecting a tax return for auditing. Prohibits the IRS from conducting any audit, investigation, or examination of a taxpayer primarily for the purpose of research. Directs the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to repurpose resources for the National Research Program to combating tax refund fraud and identity theft.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to issue a final rule relating to ergonomics. Requires such rule to: (1) address work-related musculoskeletal disorders and workplace ergonomic hazards; (2) not apply to musculoskeletal disorders that are not related to work; (3) set forth in clear terms the circumstances under which an employer is required to take action to address ergonomic hazards and the measures required of an employer; (4) emphasize the prevention of injuries before they occur; and (5) cover all industries where workers are exposed to workplace ergonomic hazards and there are economically and technologically feasible measures to control such hazards. Requires the Secretary to consider existing standards on ergonomics or preventing work-related musculoskeletal disorders established by national consensus or recognized private standard setting organizations, states, and other countries.

Broadband Regulatory Parity Act of 2002 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to direct the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to prescribe regulations to ensure that: (1) all broadband services (any service that is used to provide access to the Internet) and all broadband access services (a service that combines computer processing, information storage, protocol conversion, and wire routing with transmission to enable users to access Internet content and services) are subject to the same regulatory requirements, or no regulatory requirements; and (2) such requirements are implemented without increasing the regulatory requirements applicable to any provider of broadband services, or broadband access services, on any such service or on any facilities or equipment used to provide such service. Prohibits the jurisdiction of any State with respect to broadband services and broadband access services, and the facilities and equipment used to provide such services. Requires each incumbent local exchange carrier to provide all Internet service providers with the telecommunications necessary for such provider to provide broadband access service to its subscribers. Requires such telecommunications to be offered on rates, terms, and conditions that are just and reasonable.

Military Savings Act of 2012 - Directs the Undersecretary of Defense (DOD) to carry out a five-year pilot program at at least 10 military installations to develop innovative consumer financial products that encourage savings and wealth-creation among active-duty servicemembers. Permits such products to seek to: (1) increase the rate of savings among active-duty servicemembers by providing automatic deposit of special pay and allowances received by a servicemember, including on account of deployment; (2) reduce the need for high-cost short-term lending services by providing alternatives, such as financial institutions providing an option for servicemembers to receive advances on salary payments, where servicemembers receive pay in more frequent installments and where interest or fees on such advances do not exceed the federal minimum interest rate and adhere to the Affordable Small Dollar Lending Guidelines of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC); and (3) address obstacles to traditional consumer banking and lending for servicemembers with limited credit history. Requires the pilot program to be carried out in such a way that it does not exacerbate the incidence of credit overextension among servicemembers.

Directs the Secretary to ensure that the lands and interests exchanged are equalized by the payment of money to the Secretary or to the Corporation as appropriate in accordance with the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976. 
Requires the Secretary to require the Corporation to make direct payments to Nevada and the Southern Nevada Water Authority equal to five percent and ten percent of the fair market value of the Federal lands conveyed, respectively, and to use such payments only in the general education program of the State and for water treatment and transmission facility infrastructure in Clark County, Nevada. 
Allows the Secretary to make such minor corrections in the maps as may be agreed upon by the Secretary and the Corporation, after notifying the Senate and House Committees on Energy and Natural Resources and on Resources of any such minor corrections.

National Cheese Exchange Oversight and Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends the Commodity Exchange Act to direct the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to regulate a concentrated cash market until it is no longer functioning as a reference price for a majority of commercial transactions off the cash market for the commodity being traded. 
Requires the CFTC to:  (1) require a concentrated cash market to submit for Commission approval a set of rules governing its operation; and (2) promptly review submitted rules and notify the market of the result of the review. 
Prohibits a concentrated cash market from changing approved operating rules unless the proposed change is also submitted for review and the Commission approves the change. 
Allows the National Cheese Exchange, and other concentrated cash markets, to operate only in accordance with rules approved by the Commission.

Critical Infrastructure Protection Act or CIPA (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to include in national planning frameworks the threat of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) events and conduct outreach to educate owners and operators of critical infrastructure, emergency planners, and emergency response providers at all levels of government of the threat of EMP events.  In furtherance of domestic preparedness and response, DHS, acting through the Under Secretary for Science and Technology, shall conduct research and development to mitigate the consequences of EMP events. The scope of such research and development shall include: (1) an objective scientific analysis of the risks to critical infrastructures from a range of EMP events, (2) determination of the critical national security assets and vital civic utilities and infrastructures that are at risk from EMP events, (3) an evaluation of emergency planning and response technologies that would address the findings and recommendations of experts, (4) an analysis of technology options that are available to improve the resiliency of critical infrastructure to EMP, and (5) the restoration and recovery capabilities of critical infrastructure under differing levels of damage and disruption from various EMP events. Amends part A (Aid to Families with Dependent Children) (AFDC) of title IV of the Social Security Act to require States, if they are operating a general welfare assistance program for able-bodied residents without dependents, to reduce by 50 percent their AFDC payments for a calendar quarter in which more than 20 percent of their local governments are operating such a program.  Requires States to reduce by 50 percent the payments to State offices administering the AFDC program located within the jurisdiction of such local governments.  Requires States to reduce by 50 percent the payments to any State office administering the AFDC program which is not located within the jurisdiction of any such local government. 
Sets forth participation rate requirements for such workfare programs. 
Directs the Secretary to review State and local participation rates and report to the Congress on any recommendations with respect to such requirements.

Securing Affordable Vocational and Collegiate Education (SAVE) Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a deduction for payments to any qualified State tuition program for the benefit of any designated beneficiary.  Limits the deduction to $5,000 ($10,000 in the case of a joint return).  Excludes from gross income for income tax purposes any amounts paid to a qualified State tuition program for education expenses.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a 50 cents per tire excise tax on the manufacture or importation of tires.  Establishes the Waste Tire Recycling, Abatement, and Disposal Trust Fund in the Treasury.  Transfers tax revenues to such Fund.  Authorizes appropriations to the Fund for expenditures under the Solid Waste Disposal Act.

Border Smog Reduction Act of 1998 - Amends the Clean Air Act to prohibit noncommercial motor vehicles entered from a foreign country bordering the United States and contiguous to an ozone nonattainment area more than twice in a single calendar-month period, if State law has requirements for the inspection and maintenance of such vehicles under the applicable implementation plan in the nonattainment area.  Provides for civil penalties for violations.  Exempts States that elect to be exempt from the prohibition.  Exempts States, and the President may implement an alternative approach, if:  (1) the Governor submits to the President a written description of an alternative approach to facilitate the compliance, by some or all foreign-registered motor vehicles, with the motor vehicle inspection and maintenance requirements that are related to emissions of air pollutants and applicable to motor vehicles of the same types and model years as the foreign-registered motor vehicles; and (2) the President approves the alternative approach as facilitating compliance with such requirements. 
Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to specified congressional committees on the impact of the amendment on air quality in ozone nonattainment areas.

Treat and Reduce Obesity Act of 2017 This bill authorizes the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to cover intensive behavioral therapy for obesity furnished by: (1) a physician who is not a qualified primary care physician, (2) any other appropriate health care provider, (3) an evidence-based, community-based lifestyle counseling program approved by CMS, or (4) an appropriate health care provider or program that communicates with the referring physician or primary care practitioner regarding recommendations or treatment plans.  The CMS must exclude from Medicare part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) coverage of obesity medication.

Requires a State, to be eligible for such a grant, to provide assurances to the Attorney General that the State: (1) has in effect laws that penalize computer crime; (2) has assessed its and local resource needs, including criminal justice resources; and (3) has a plan for coordinating its programs under this Act with other federally funded technical assistant and training programs, including directly funded local programs such as the Local Law Enforcement Block Grant program. Anti-terrorism Information Sharing Is Strength Act - Amends the USA PATRIOT Act to expand the definition of "terrorist activity" to include specified unlawful activities. Includes within the definition of "unlawful activity" any activity that may involve terrorist acts, money laundering activities, or a specified unlawful activity.

Expresses the sense of Congress that, in furtherance of efforts to stop the financing of terror and other forms of illicit financing through increased sharing of information, and consistent with the need to prevent inappropriate dissemination of such information: (1) federal law enforcement agencies and regulators should share information about terrorist acts, money laundering activities, and other specified unlawful activities to the fullest extent possible and in a timely fashion; and (2) financial institutions, including nonbank financial institutions, should share information about such acts and activities with each other to the fullest extent possible and in a timely fashion.

Expands the duty of a financial institution to make a disclosure to a person to include any duty or requirement of such institution to demonstrate to a person that a disclosure is made in good faith.

Amends the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995 to include within the definition of "lobbying activities" those paid communications campaigns to influence the general public to lobby Congress.  Requires a lobbying firm that receives an aggregate of $100,000 or more in income from a client for such activities in any quarterly period to register with the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives.  Requires such a firm to file a separate good faith estimate of the total amount of income relating specifically to such campaigns, if such income from the client exceeds $50,000 during the quarterly filing period.

Direct Check for Education Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make multiyear awards to local educational agencies (LEAs) for kindergarten through grade 12 (K-12) students to support programs or activities that the LEAs deem appropriate.  Authorizes appropriations for FY 2000 through 2004. 
Sets forth:  (1) a formula for determining the amount to be awarded to an LEA by the Secretary; and (2) requirements for a census to determine the average daily attendance of K-12 students served by an LEA. 
Provides for:  (1) disbursement of funds awarded to LEAs; and (2) penalties for knowingly submitting false information for the purpose of gaining additional funds. 
Authorizes the Secretary to conduct audits of LEA expenditures to ensure that funds are used in accordance with this Act.

Indian Employment and Training Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends the Indian Employment, Training and Related Services Demonstration Act of 1992 to authorize a tribal government to waive any statutory requirement under the Act. 
Authorizes a tribal government to use a percentage of the funds made available under the Act for the creation of employment opportunities, including providing private sector training placement.  Sets the percentage at the greater of the rate of unemployment in the area subject to the tribal government's jurisdiction or ten percent. 
Directs the Secretary of the Interior to ensure an orderly transition with respect to the administration of the demonstration project in such manner as to eliminate any potential adverse effects of the project on any Indian tribe that:  (1) has entered into a self-determination contract; or (2) receives funds under the Act. 
Authorizes the assignment of Federal personnel and resources to State Indian economic development programs. 
Requires the head of each Federal agency that otherwise has jurisdiction over a program integrated under the demonstration project to permit a tribal government to establish a consolidated advisory committee to carry out the duties of each advisory committee that would otherwise be required under applicable law.

Junior Duck Stamp Conservation and Design Program Act of 1994 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to carry out a Junior Duck Stamp Conservation and Design Program to provide environmental education opportunities for school children and increase the capacity for educational programs relating to conservation and education. 
Directs the Secretary to seek to conduct the Program in all 50 States. 
Authorizes the Secretary to:  (1) conduct a competition to solicit designs relating to conservation of migratory birds from elementary and secondary school students; and (2) license and market such designs, which shall be known as Junior Duck Stamps.  Makes proceeds from such licensing and marketing available for:  (1) awards and scholarships to individuals who submit designs that are selected in a competition or that are otherwise determined to be superior; (2) awards to schools and other participants in such a competition to further education activities related to the conservation education goals of the Program; and (3) expenses for licensing and marketing.  Prohibits use of such proceeds for administrative expenses of the Program. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Russian Weapons Embargo Act of 2014 - Prohibits the head of an executive agency from entering into a contract, subcontract, memorandum of understanding, cooperative agreement, loan, or loan agreement with, or making a grant to, or providing a loan or loan agreement to, Rosoboronexport, any subsidiary or affiliate of Rosoboronexport, or any entity that has a business relationship with Rosoboronexport or any subsidiary or affiliate of Rosoboronexport related to the design, manufacture, or sale of military equipment.  Directs the head of each executive agency to immediately terminate any such contract, subcontract, memorandum of understanding, cooperative agreement, loan, or loan agreement.  Authorizes the President to waive the applicability of this Act if the President certifies in writing to the appropriate congressional committees that, to the best of the President's knowledge: (1) Rosoboronexport has ceased the transfer of lethal military equipment to, and the maintenance of existing lethal military equipment for, the government of the Syrian Arab Republic; (2) the armed forces of the Russian Federation have withdrawn from Crimea (other than military forces present on military bases subject to agreements in force between the government of the Russian Federation and the government of Ukraine); and (3)

Transparency in Judgment Payments Act of 2011 - Amends federal judicial code provisions to require the Secretary of the Treasury to publish electronically, within 30 days after the payment of a final judgment, award, or compromise settlement, the following information about a claim for damages or other relief in a civil action: (1) the agency responsible for the payment; (2) a citation to the provision of law under which the claim was made; (3) the amount to be paid; (4) the amount of any interest to be paid; (5) the amount of any attorney fees to be paid; and (6) for any case filed in a court: (1) the case number for the case that resulted in the judgment, award, or settlement; and (2) the court in which the case was filed. Requires the Secretary to submit quarterly reports to specified congressional committees describing published information and confidential appendixes containing the identities of the plaintiff, counsel for the plaintiff, and the defendant for each case described.

Directs each federal agency to submit annual reports to specified congressional committees describing: (1) civil actions filed or pending against the agency or any agency employee, and (2) settlements entered by or final judgments against the agency or any agency

Building Bridges and Transforming Resentment and Unfairness to Support and Trust for Municipal Law Enforcement Act of 2014 or the Build TRUST Act of 2014 - Reduces the amount of federal grant funding that local governments are allowed to receive for law enforcement programs and activities if they use a disproportionate amount of funds to collect fines and other fees related to violations of traffic laws.  Exempts local governments that: (1) serve a population of less than 15,000 people, or (2) have received a waiver from the Attorney General.  Authorizes the Attorney General to grant a waiver to a local government for good cause shown if the local government: (1) is subject to a consent decree or Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) or an investigation by the Special Litigation Section of the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice (DOJ) for excessive use of force, false arrests, improper searches and seizures, failures to discipline officers sufficiently, or failure to supervise officers; (2) has taken affirmative action to ensure that adequate practices and procedures are in place to increase public trust and confidence in the impartial and equitable administration of justice; and (3) has a legislative body and executive departments that are

Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2009, the duty on certain items, including: (1) front panels for cathode-ray television picture tubes with a viewable diagonal measurement of 80.01 cm, an outer panel radius of less than 500 cm, and an aspect ratio of 4:3; (2) front panels for cathode-ray television picture tubes with a viewable diagonal measurement of 90.17 cm, an outer panel radius of less than 500 cm, and an aspect ratio of 4:3; (3) front panels for cathode-ray television picture tubes with a viewable diagonal measurement of 76.00 cm, an outer panel radius of greater than 500 cm, and an aspect ratio of 16:9; (4) 32V funnel for use with curved screen panels and with Pure Flat (PF) panels; (5) funnels for cathode-ray television picture tubes with an outside diagonal measurement of 94.12 cm and an aspect ratio of 4:3; (6) funnels for cathode-ray television picture tubes

Fort Sumner Project Title Conveyance Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the Fort Sumner Irrigation District, located in De Baca County, New Mexico, all works, land, and facilities of the Fort Sumner reclamation project in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Transfer Agreement.

Requires the Secretary to assure compliance with all applicable requirements under: (1) the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA); and (2) the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (ESA). Modifies NEPA to provide that, effective on the date of the conveyance: (1) the United States shall have no further interest in, and shall not be liable for, damages arising out of any act, omission, or occurrence relating to the conveyed property, except for damages caused by acts committed by the United States or its employees, agents, or contractors before the date of the conveyance; and (2) the United States and the District shall have no obligations under the contract for the forbearance of exercising priority water rights numbered 08-WC-40-292 and dated August 21, 2009 (Forbearance Agreement).

Voluntary Adoption Protection Act - Amends the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 to provide that, with respect to a child custody proceeding, an involuntary removal of a child from the Indian community means the absence of a written consent by a parent or legal guardian (other than a tribal court) of the child. 
Provides that this Act shall not be the basis for determining jurisdiction over any child custody proceeding involving an Indian child if a parent or legal guardian (other than a tribal court) consents to a voluntary child custody proceeding.

Gila Bend Indian Reservation Lands Replacement Clarification Act - Amends the Gila Bend Indian Reservation Lands Replacement Act to prohibit class II or class III gaming activities on specified lands located north of latitude 33 degrees, 4 minutes north if such lands are located in Arizona.

Campus Fire Safety Right to Know Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require each eligible institution participating in any program under title IV (Student Assistance) to: (1) prepare, publish, and distribute, through publications or mailings, an annual fire safety report containing specified information regarding the campus fire safety practices and standards of that institution; and (2) make timely reports to the campus community on fires that are reported to local fire departments and the incidence of false fire alarms on campus. Requires each institution to: (1) make a log recording all such fires and false fire alarms; and (2) submit annually to the Secretary of Education a copy of the statistics concerning campus fires and false fire alarms. Requires the Secretary to: (1) review such statistics; (2) make copies available to the public; and (3) identify exemplary fire safety policies, procedures, and practices and disseminate information concerning those policies, procedures, and practices that have proven effective in the reduction of campus fires.

Provides for automatic continuing appropriations (at a rate of operations not exceeding those provided for under the regular appropriation Act for the preceding fiscal year) in the absence of regular appropriations for a fiscal year.

Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to require the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to establish an emergency preparedness demonstration program to research and promote the capacity of disadvantaged communities to carry out programs to provide data, information, and awareness education by providing grants to or executing contracts or cooperative agreements with eligible nonprofit organizations to establish and conduct such programs.

Allows an eligible nonprofit organization to use a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement awarded under this Act to: (1) conduct research into the status of emergency preparedness and disaster response awareness in households of disadvantaged individuals located in urban and rural communities, particularly in those States and regions most impacted by natural and man-made disasters and emergencies; and (2) develop and promote awareness of emergency preparedness education programs within disadvantaged communities.

Makes eligible for such a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement an organization that is a nonprofit organization that is tax-exempt under the Internal Revenue Code and whose primary mission is to provide services to disadvantaged communities, and that can demonstrate a partnership with a disadvantaged business enterprise, including enterprises located in a HUBZone (historically underutilized business zone).

Territorial Economic Growth and Recovery Act of 2016 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the tax cap for distilled spirit taxes. The bill also directs the Department of the Treasury to pay to each U.S. possession a mirror code tax system, which is a system in which a tax credit is allowed for income tax liability determined by reference to U.S. income tax laws.  The bill requires Treasury to pay to each U.S. possession: (1) a mirror code tax system for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2015, and (2) an estimated tax credit for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2015, if the possession does not have a mirror code tax system.  The bill eliminates the earned income tax credit for U.S. possessions.
