Urban Recovery and Growth Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend the tax incentives for issuance of economic development extension bonds for specified cities.

National Spaceport Act - Establishes within the Department of Transportation a National Spaceport Office.  Directs the Office to administer the application and assistance program for spaceport development and to establish appropriate procedures for the competitive awarding of grants and the transfer of excess Federal property to spaceports. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for tax-exempt bond financing for spaceports. 
Subjects the activities of the National Spaceport Office and of spaceports to specified regulatory exemptions. 
Authorizes appropriations. 
Terminates the Office on October 1, 2000.

Delphi Pensions Restoration Act of 2012 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to require that proceeds from the sale of troubled assets purchased under such Act, or from the sale, exercise, or surrender of warrants or senior debt instruments acquired under such Act, be paid into the general fund of the Treasury for reduction of the public debt.

Requires that proceeds from the sale or transfer, after the enactment of this Act, of any stock, warrant, or financial instrument acquired by the Secretary in connection with providing financial assistance to the General Motors Corporation (GM) under such Act be transferred to the Delphi Retired Employees Fund.

Establishes in the Treasury a Delphi Retired Employees Fund to be used by the Secretary in making payments to eligible separated employees of the Delphi Corporation.

Defines an "eligible separated employee" as any individual who: (1) is separated from employment with Delphi before the enactment of this Act; (2) was a participant in a defined benefit plan terminated before the enactment of this Act; and (3) is not covered by any agreement between the GM Corporation and participants in a defined benefit plan under which the GM Corporation provides to the covered participants a payment of nonforfeitable benefits in an

Veterans Traumatic Brain Injury Treatment Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish a program to screen veterans who are eligible for hospital care, medical services, and nursing home care for symptoms of traumatic brain injury.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) develop and carry out a comprehensive program of long-term care for post-acute traumatic brain injury rehabilitation that includes residential, community, and home-based components utilizing interdisciplinary treatment teams; (2) establish a traumatic brain injury transition office at each Department of Veterans Affairs polytrauma network site to coordinate the provision of health-care and services to veterans who suffer from moderate to severe traumatic brain injuries and need health-care and services not immediately offered by the Department; and (3) establish and maintain the Traumatic Brain Injury Veterans Health Registry.

Energy Development Program Implementation Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to develop: (1) strategic plans for the energy development program consistent with title V of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Act of 1978; and (2) implementation plans for such program.

Requires the Secretary to submit the strategic and implementation plans to the appropriate congressional committees for review. Requires the Secretary to implement the plans.

Directs the Secretary to report annually to the appropriate congressional committees on the plans.

Requires the Secretary to report to the appropriate congressional committees on the feasibility of expanding cooperative activities established pursuant to the Alternative Energy Corps program into an international cooperative effort.

High School Data Transparency Act of 2011 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to collect, annually, for the immediately preceding academic year, from each coeducational secondary school that receives federal financial assistance that has an interscholastic athletic program, certain information regarding gender and race or ethnicity disparities in participation and success in athletic programs.

Requires such schools to: (1) make such information available to students and potential students, upon request, and to the public, by October 15 for the previous school year; and (2) ensure that all students at the school are informed of their right to request such information.

Recapture Excess Profits and Invest in Roads (REPAIR) Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax of 25% on the windfall profit of any producer or refiner of crude oil for taxable years beginning 2008 or 2009. Defines "windfall profit" as the excess of the adjusted taxable income of the applicable taxpayer for the taxable year over the "reasonably inflated average profit" for such taxable year.

Medicare Fracture Prevention and Osteoporosis Testing Act of 2007 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a national minimum payment amount for CPT codes (Current Procedural Terminology) relating to dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and vertebral fracture assessment (VFA), and any successor to such codes.

Directs the Secretary to enter into an arrangement with the Institute of Medicine of the National Academies to study and report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Congress on: (1) the ramifications of Medicare reimbursement reductions for DXA and VFA on beneficiary access to bone mass measurement benefits in general and in rural and minority communities specifically; and (2) methods to increase use of bone mass measurement by Medicare beneficiaries.

Directs the Secretary of Transportation, on October 1, 2011, and each ensuing fiscal year, to withhold from amounts apportioned to a state under the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration Act of 2004 certain funds for that state if the state does not enact and enforce a law that prohibits operating a motor vehicle while using a wireless communications device (such as a cell phone or portable electronic device) while in motion or part of traffic. Exempts from such prohibition: (1) use of a wireless communications device solely in a voice-activated or other hands-free mode, for making a cellular phone call, for obtaining emergency assistance to report a traffic accident or medical emergency or to prevent a crime, in the belief that a person's life or safety is in immediate danger, in an authorized emergency vehicle while in the performance of official duties, when a motor vehicle is stopped and the driver has the transmission in neutral or park, and (2) in other circumstances as identified by the Secretary by regulation in which the use of a wireless communications device does not adversely affect safety.

Sets forth a withholding schedule for a state that is subject to a penalty for noncompliance.

Stop Illegal Reentry Act or Kate's Law - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to impose criminal penalties on aliens who have been denied U.S. entry, excluded, deported, or removed, or who departed the United States while an order of exclusion, deportation, or removal is outstanding, and who thereafter enter, attempt to enter, or are found in the United States without the consent of the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) or with prior permission to reenter.

Imposes a fine and/or 10-year prison term for such aliens who: (1) were convicted before such removal or departure of three or more misdemeanors involving drugs, crimes against persons, or both, or a felony (other than an aggravated felony); (2) were excluded from the United States because they were excludable under the Immigration and Nationality Act or the Immigration and Freedom Act of 1996, and who thereafter, without DHS permission, enter, attempt to enter, or are found in the United States; (3) were removed from the United States because of unlawful reentry, and who thereafter, without DHS permission, enter, attempt to enter, or are found in the United States; or (4) were denied admission, excluded, deported, or

Good Samaritan Charitable Physicians' Services Act of 2018  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for the cost of qualified charity care furnished by a taxpayer as a direct primary care physician. The bill also amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a physician from being liable in a civil action for harm caused by an act or omission if such act or omission: (1) occurs in the course of furnishing qualified charity care, and (2) was not grossly negligent.

Homebuyer Tax Credit Improvement Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make the first-time homebuyer tax credit inapplicable to taxpayers under 18 years old as of the purchase date; (2) require taxpayers filing the credit return to attach to the return a properly executed copy of the settlement statement used to purchase the residence; (3) make the credit inapplicable to spouses of taxpayers under 18 years old; and (4) make certain errors with respect to the eligibility for the credit treated as mathematical or clerical.

Requires tax return preparers to file tax returns on magnetic media.

Fair International Labor Standards in Trade and Investment Act of 2001 - Declares that the policy objectives of Congress with respect to international labor issues are: (1) fundamental economic, political, social, technological, and cross-cultural changes are proceeding in ways that accelerate global integration and interdependence; (2) the U.S. national interest is served by more open markets, expanding trade, and investment liberalization within the community of nations, balanced by increased respect and enforcement of universal human rights; (3) the American people believe that more open international trade, investment, and market access are not ends in themselves, but means for attaining greater economic justice, social responsibility, and sustainable development; (4) U.S. international economic policy should emphasize the four principal goals of the international economic policy of the United States: (A) the achievement of steadily increasing purchasing power throughout the global economy in tandem with expanding global productive capacity that leads to the elimination of abusive child labor, rising living standards in developing and developed national economies, and the acceleration of broad-based consumer markets within all trading nations; (B) the discouragement of economic development by any nation based on the commercial exploitation of child labor and the systematic denial of internationally recognized worker rights and core labor standards, in order to

Patient Access to Disposable Medical Technology Act of 2015 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for the coverage of certain "substitute disposable medical technologies" under Medicare. (Currently, Medicare only covers durable medical equipment.) "Substitute disposable medical technologies" are medical equipment that: (1) is primarily and customarily used to serve a medical purpose, (2) would otherwise be covered as durable medical equipment, and (3) the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services determines substitutes for durable medical equipment.

Gulf Security and Iran Sanctions Enforcement Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) require a lessee of an oil and gas lease on the Outer Continental Shelf to make a certification that it does not engage in any activity for which sanctions may be imposed under the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996, and authorizes the Secretary to cancel the lease if the person fails to make such a certification or makes a false certification; and (2) require such a lessee to disclose to the Secretary any participation in any energy-related joint venture, investment, or partnership located outside Iran that involves property and interests blocked pursuant to certain executive orders.

Authorizes the Secretary to waive such requirements on a case-by-case basis if it is in the national interest.

Terminates this Act 30 days after the President certifies to Congress that the government of Iran: (1) has permanently ceased providing support for acts of international terrorism and no longer satisfies the requirements for designation as a state sponsor of terrorism; and (2) poses no significant threat to U.S. national security, interests, or allies.

Encroachment on Military Bases Prevention Act - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from designating as a critical habitat any lands or other geographical areas owned or controlled by the Department of Defense (DOD), or designated for DOD use, that are subject to an integrated natural resources management plan prepared under the Sikes Act if the Secretary determines that such plan addresses special management considerations or protection.

Requires the Secretary to provide written notice to the Secretary of Defense of the exact military lands to be covered by a special resource study that will include, or will be expanded to include, military lands. Directs the Secretary of Defense to evaluate the existing environmental protections for the military lands and the importance of the military lands to military readiness and preparedness. Authorizes the Secretary of Defense to require the Secretary of the Interior to exclude all or a portion of the military lands from the study if the Secretary of Defense determines that: (1) the environmental protections for the military lands are sufficient; and (2) inclusion of the military lands in the National Park System could adversely impact military readiness and preparedness. Requires the Secretary of Defense to make such a determination before the end of the 90-day period beginning on the date on

Statewide PTV Access Act of 2009 - Amends the Federal Communications Act of 1934 to allow a statutory license provided for in the case of commercial noncommercial educational television (PTV) stations to be applied to the secondary transmission of any noncommercial educational broadcast station in a state-wide network to any subscriber outside that station's local market and not served by a noncommercial educational television broadcast station within that state.

Defines "state-wide network of noncommercial educational broadcast stations" as a network of three or more noncommercial educational broadcast stations that are licensed to a single State, political, educational, or special purpose subdivision of a State, or a single public agency.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to authorize a satellite carrier to retransmit the secondary signal of a part of a network of noncommercial educational broadcast stations located outside the station's local market to its subscribers if: (1) such station is a part of such a network; and (2) the satellite carrier retransmits the secondary signal of such station only to its subscribers.

Authorizes a satellite carrier to carry the signals of such a network to all subscribers outside a designated market area if such network consists of three or more noncommercial educational broadcast stations and the

Highway Fairness and Reform Act of 2009 - Amends federal highway provisions to require the Secretary of Transportation to carry out a direct federal-aid highway program beginning with FY2011. Authorizes a state governor or chief executive officer to elect to have the state waive its right to receive amounts apportioned or allocated to it under the federal-aid highway program for the fiscal year to which the election relates and receive instead the amount determined below for that fiscal year. Requires the Secretary to accept an election if the Secretary determines that the state: (1) has an interstate maintenance program and agrees to maintain the interstate in accordance with that program; (2) submits a plan describing the purposes, projects, and uses to which amounts received under the program will be put and which programmatic requirements of federal highway provisions the state elects to continue; (3) agrees to obligate or expend amounts received under the program exclusively for projects that would be eligible for funding under provisions for state aid to transportation for intermodal surface transportation efficiency projects and provisions for state aid to transportation for intermodal surface transportation reliability projects if the state were not participating in the program; and (4) agrees to report annually to the Secretary on the use of amounts received under the program and

Third Higher Education Extension Act of 2007 - Amends the Higher Education Extension Act of 2005 to extend the loan guarantee program through March 31, 2008.

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to revise requirements for loan guarantee eligibility for lenders that are not-for-profit entities. Makes a lender eligible for such a guarantee only if it is not owned or controlled by a for-profit entity.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2014 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require each energy manager, as part of the certification system, to provide an explanation regarding any life-cycle cost-effective measures that have not been implemented in federal buildings. Requires the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to include in the annual report on energy conservation performance contracts and utility energy service contracts information on: (1) the status of each agency's energy savings performance contracts and utility energy service contracts, the investment value of such contracts, the guaranteed energy savings for the previous year as compared to the actual energy savings for the previous year, the plan for entering into such contracts in the coming year, and information explaining why any previously submitted plans for such contracts were not implemented.  Revises the definition of "energy manager" to include retrofit activities, or energy consuming devices and required support structures.  Authorizes a federal agency to sell or transfer energy savings and apply the proceeds to fund a contract.

Childrens' Internet Protection Act - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to make elementary and secondary schools and libraries that fail to provide the required certification to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for universal service assistance under the Federal Communications Commission's mandate to filter or block material deemed to be harmful to minors on computers used by the public (including minors) ineligible for such assistance. Sets forth requirements for such certification, including that the school or library shall notify the FCC within 10 days after ceasing to use the filtering or blocking technology.

Directs the Secretary of the military department concerned, in the case of a member of the Armed Forces with a combat-related disability who is entitled to military retired pay, to permit the member to elect to have used in computing such retired pay a retired pay base equal to $2,917, which represents the average monthly salary for high school graduates in the United States, as determined by the Census Bureau for 2006, in lieu of the retired pay base of the member computed under provisions relating to regular military retired pay or to those provisions relating to veterans' retired pay.

Directs the Secretary concerned, in the case of a member with a combat-related disability who is entitled to monthly military retired pay, to permit the member to elect to have used in computing such retired pay a monthly compensation equal to $2,917, which represents the average monthly salary for high school graduates in the United States, as determined by the Census Bureau for 2006, in lieu of the monthly compensation rate in effect under provisions relating to regular military retired pay or to those provisions relating to veterans' retired pay.

Directs the Secretary concerned, in the case of a veteran with a covered service-connected disability rated as total, to permit the veteran to elect to receive

Autofill Act of 2015 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to direct the Department of the Treasury to establish a program under which taxpayers may download forms relating to the individual income tax returns that are populated with tax return information reported to Treasury under the Social Security Act.  The bill requires the Secretary of the Treasury to: (1) establish standards for data download to tax preparation software, and (2) provide a demonstration server for downloading the partially populated printable document file.  The bill also requires the Secretary to provide on the Secretary's website a secure function that allows a taxpayer to download, as both a printable document file and in a form suitable for input to automatic tax preparation software, the 1040, 1040A, and 1040EZ forms that are populated with tax return information with respect to the taxpayer that is reported under the Social Security Act.

Intergovernmental Law Enforcement Information Sharing Act of 2001 - Amends Federal law to require the Attorney General to: (1) carry out security clearance investigations for the persons identified in this Act, and to grant appropriate clearances to all such persons who qualify for clearances under applicable laws and executive orders; and (2) ensure that information systems are configured to allow efficient and effective sharing of information among appropriate Federal, State, territorial, and local officials and agencies.Requires the Attorney General to study and report to specified congressional committees on methods to enhance the sharing of sensitive Federal law enforcement information with State, territorial, and local law enforcement officials.Requires State, territorial, and local law enforcement agencies to participate in the study.

Mobile Workforce State Income Tax Fairness and Simplification Act - Prohibits the wages or other remuneration earned by an employee who performs employment duties in more than one state from being subject to income tax in any state other than: (1) the state of the employee's residence; and (2) the state within which the employee is present and performing employment duties for more than 30 days during the calendar year.

Allows an employer, for purposes of determining an employee's state income tax withholding and information return obligations, to rely on an employee's determination of the time expected to be spent by such employee in the states in which the employee will perform duties, absent actual knowledge of fraud by the employee in making the estimate or collusion between the employer and the employee to evade tax.

SIG TARP Small Business Awareness Act of 2009 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to direct the Special Inspector General for the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) to: (1) examine how smaller financial institutions are being affected by TARP expenditures and by the considerations and determinations of the Secretary of the Treasury and the regulators of such smaller financial institutions, with respect to capital adequacy and troubled assets; and (2) examine the effects the provision of financial assistance under TARP has had on small businesses.

Requires the Special Inspector General to include in each quarterly report to Congress information on the activities of the Secretary and any financial institutions receiving TARP financial assistance to include, and utilize, minorities and women, and minority- and women-owned businesses.

King Cove Road Land Exchange Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the state of Alaska approximately 131 acres of federal land in the Wilderness of the Izembek National Wildlife Refuge in the state of Alaska if Alaska offers to convey to the Secretary approximately 43,093 acres of non-federal land in the Refuge. Requires the federal land to be conveyed to Alaska for: (1) designating a road corridor through the Refuge, and (2) constructing a single-lane gravel road along the road corridor.  Requires the value of the exchanged land to be equal, as determined by appraisals.  Requires the land exchange to be completed within 180 days after the enactment of this Act.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) reduce estate and gift tax rates to 30 percent; (2) increase the exclusion equivalent of the unified credit to $10 million; and (3) increase the annual gift tax exclusion to $50,000.
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through June 30, 1999, the duty on certain HIV drug substances.

Veterans Serving Veterans Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the VA Choice and Quality Employment Act to require the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to maintain a single searchable database, to be known as the Departments of Defense and Veterans Affairs Recruitment Database, that contains information about VA positions that require intermediate care services. The database shall include, with respect to each qualified member of the Armed Forces, the following information:  the name and contact information of the qualified member, the date on which the qualified member is expected to be discharged and released from active duty, and each military occupational specialty currently or previously assigned to the qualified member.  The VA shall hire qualified members of the Armed Forces who apply for vacant positions listed in the database without regard to the provisions of the Armed Forces Recruiting and Promotion Act.  The VA may authorize a relocation bonus to any qualified member who has accepted a position listed in the database. (Sec. 3) The VA shall implement a program to train and certify covered veterans to work as intermediate care technicians in the VA. The VA shall establish centers at VA medical facilities selected by the VA for the purposes of carrying out the program.  "Covered veteran" means a veteran whom the VA determines served as

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the exclusion from gross income for gain from the sale of certain small business stock from 50 to 75 percent and extend the holding period for such gain from five to three years. Makes such exclusion available to corporations.  Makes the stock of larger businesses eligible for such exclusion.  Repeals the minimum tax preference for such gain. 
Increases from $50 to $300 million the amount of small business stock which may be excluded from gross income without regard to the 75 percent exclusion limitation.  Makes such exclusion available to corporations.  Makes the stock of larger businesses eligible for such exclusion.  Repeals the minimum tax preference for such gain. 
Increases from $100,000 to $200,000 the maximum incentive stock option price before the option is considered to be a poison option and such option is excluded from the alternative minimum tax.

Highway Infrastructure Privatization Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to make qualified highway infrastructure projects eligible for tax-exempt financing. Directs the Secretary of Transportation to select up to 15 projects to be pilot projects eligible for such financing. Sets forth eligibility criteria, including that no project may be selected unless it: (1) serves the general public; (2) is necessary to evaluate the potential of the private sector's participation in the provision of U.S. highway infrastructure; (3) is located on publicly owned rights-of-way; (4) is publicly owned or the ownership of the highway constructed or reconstructed reverts to the public; and (5) is consistent with a transportation plan. Limits the aggregate face amount of tax-exempt financing to $15 billion. Allows the Secretary to reallocate unused portions of such amount among the remaining eligible pilot projects. Exempts such bonds from general state volume caps.

National Telecommuting and Air Quality Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Environmental Policy Institute for the development of a design for a pilot program to encourage telecommuting as a means of improving air quality. 
Directs the Secretary to ensure that the design developed includes recommendations for carrying out the proposed pilot program in each of the following geographic areas:  (1) the greater metropolitan region of the District of Columbia (including areas in the States of Maryland and Virginia); (2) the greater metropolitan region of Los Angeles, in California; and (3) three additional areas to be selected by the Secretary. 
Requires the Secretary to require that, in carrying out such geographic area requirement, the grantee consult with local governments and business organizations in the geographic area. 
Directs the Secretary to require that, in developing the design, the grantee study and report to the Congress and to the Secretary the potential significance of the proposed pilot program as an incentive for expanding telecommuting and reducing vehicle-miles-traveled in the geographic areas for which the design is developed, and the extent to which the program would have positive effects on:  (1) national, State, and local transportation and infrastructure policies; (2) energy conservation and consumption;

Cyber Preparedness Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to share information relating to cybersecurity risks with state, local, and regional fusion centers.  Fusion centers are centers that collect, analyze, and disseminate information related to homeland security matters.  Fusion centers must incorporate information relating to cybersecurity risks that is gathered by state, local, and regional fusion centers into DHS's own information relating to cybersecurity risks.  The bill also requires the national cybersecurity and communications integration center to assist fusion centers in using information relating to cybersecurity risks to develop a comprehensive and accurate threat picture.  (Sec. 3) DHS must include the enhancement of cybersecurity within the funding authorized for homeland security grants.  (Sec. 4) The bill expresses the sense of Congress that DHS should share actionable information related to cyber threats in an unclassified form with state, local, and private sector stakeholders.

Veterans' Access to Child Care Act (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide child care assistance to a veteran who: (1) is the primary caretaker of a child or children, and (2) is receiving regular mental health care services, intensive mental health care services, or other intensive health care services.  The child care assistance may include:  a stipend for child care offered by a licensed child care center modeled after the Department of Veterans Affairs Child Care Subsidy Program, direct provision of child care at a VA facility, a payment to a private child care agency, or a collaboration with a facility or program of another federal department or agency.  In the case of a stipend provided under this Act, the bill requires the child care assistance to cover the full cost.  (Sec. 3) The bill extends through FY2026 the reduction in the amount of VA pension benefits for certain veterans covered by Medicaid plans for services provided by nursing facilities.  (Sec. 4) The bill extends through December 31, 2024, the requirement for collection of VA housing loan fees.

Federal Agency Anti-Lobbying Act - Amends Federal law to prohibit the use of funds made available to any Federal agency by appropriation for any activity (including the preparation, publication, distribution, or use of any kit, pamphlet, booklet, public presentation, news release, radio, television, or film presentation, video, or other written or oral statement) that is intended to promote public support or opposition to any legislative proposal (including the confirmation of the nomination of a public official or the ratification of a treaty) on which congressional action is not complete, unless such activity has been specifically authorized by an Act of Congress. Makes an exception for the President or Vice President, for communication with Members of Congress, and for communication with the American public on the views of the President for or against any pending legislative proposal.
Public Good IRA Rollover Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from inclusion in gross income distributions from individual retirement accounts for certain charitable purposes.

Solar Stimulus for Job Creation and Energy Independence Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow a refundable energy tax credit for property used to manufacture solar energy property; (2) exclude from the definition of "subsidized energy financing" loans for solar energy property; (3) exclude from the definition of "private activity bond test" loans for solar energy property; and (4) allow the government to contract for renewable energy for a period of not more than 25 years.

Workforce Training Enhancement Act of 2016 This bill amends the Trade Act of 1974 to authorize a state to reimburse the costs of providing training to a worker after a petition for trade adjustment assistance is filed if the worker is covered by a certification for eligibility under the trade adjustment assistance program and the training commences after the date on which the total or partial separations of the group of workers covered by the certification for eligibility began or threatened to begin.

Right of Passage Community Service Act - Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a community-based Right of Passage after-school and summer service corps program that offers young people the opportunity to: (1) perform service in their communities; (2) participate in activities that would provide training in certain critical skills; (3) engage in service-learning curricula linked to academic goals; and (4) work with older AmeriCorps members who can organize service projects and act as mentors.

Requires an individual to be considered to be a participant in such a program if the individual: (1) satisfies certain requirements; and (2) is between the ages of 12 and 16, inclusive at the time the individual begins the term of service.

Requires an individual participating in such a program to agree to participate in it for at least 160 hours during a period of at least two months and not more than one year.

Requires an individual who participates in such a program upon completion of the required 160 hours of service to receive a $500 education award.

Health Care Liability Reform Act - Authorizes punitive damages to be awarded against a manufacturer or product seller in a civil action if the claimant establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the harm suffered was the result of conduct manifesting actual malice. 
Prohibits the manufacturer of a prescription drug or device and a health care provider from being subject to punitive damages with respect to harm caused by a drug or device if the drug or device was approved under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act unless:  (1) the manufacturer withholds from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) information which is relevant to the performance of the drug or device and causally related to the harm suffered by the plaintiff; or (2) the health care provider withholds from a patient information which is relevant to the performance of the drug or device and causally related to the harm suffered by the plaintiff. 
Limits the amount of punitive damages that may be awarded for a claim in any civil action to three times the amount awarded to the claimant for the economic injury on which such claim is based, or $250,000, whichever is greater. 
Provides that, in any action, the liability of each manufacturer or product seller of the product involved in such action shall be

Work Force Enhancement for Technology Transfer Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce, through the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to direct Regional Centers for the Transfer of Manufacturing Technology and, when established, Manufacturing Outreach Centers to assist managers and other workers in U.S. manufacturing firms in effectively utilizing and operating advanced and modern technologies by:  (1) making available assessments of the needs of such firms for worker training in the effective utilization and operation of such technologies, and information on commercially and publicly provided worker training services in the effective utilization and operation of such technologies; and (2) making available to such firms accessible and affordable training services for the effective utilization and operation of such technologies when such training is not available from commercially or other publicly provided training services. 
Directs the Secretary, through the Director, to assist such managers and workers in effectively utilizing and operating advanced and modern technologies by:  (1) establishing and managing a clearinghouse for information on the best available training material and services for the effective utilization and operation of such technologies; (2) encouraging U.S. providers of advanced and modern technologies for manufacturing firms to develop training material specifically designed for such managers and workers; and (3) establishing such managers and workers as an important criterion in the assessment of advanced and

Securing Protections for the Injured from Limitations on Liability Act - Amends the Death on the High Seas Act to provide for fair compensation for the decedent's pain and suffering, including loss of care, comfort, and companionship (nonpecuniary loss).

Amends the Jones Act to provide for recovery for loss of care, comfort, and companionship for a seaman who dies of a work-related injury.

Repeals provisions in the Bankruptcy Abuse Prevention and Consumer Protection Act that limit the rights of creditors in bankruptcy cases.

Authorizes the trustee of a bankruptcy case to sell or lease, other than in the ordinary course of business, significant property of the estate of a debtor liable under any law for a claim for wrongful death, personal injury, or property damage arising from an incident that gives rise to liability under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 if certain conditions are met, including creditors holding at least two-thirds in amount, and more than one-half in number, of all such claims not paid by the debtor's consent.

Authorizes the debtor to sell or lease, other than in the ordinary course of business, significant property of the estate if certain conditions are met, including creditors holding at least two-thirds in amount, and more than

Unemployment Assistance Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income any qualified unemployment distribution from a tax-favored account, as long as such distribution is made during a period of unemployment which does not exceed two years and is used for qualified living expenses, qualified health care expenses, or qualified education or job training expenses.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on imported crude oil and refined petroleum products if the average international price of crude oil for any four-week period is less than $24.  Defines "average international price" as the average of the weighted average price per barrel of crude oil for each week in such period, as estimated and published in the Weekly Petroleum Status Report prepared by the Secretary of Energy or his delegate.  Exempts from such tax: (1) crude oil condensates and natural gasoline; and (2) domestic crude oil.

Psychological Kevlar Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to: (1) develop and implement a plan to incorporate evidence-based preventive and early-intervention measures, practices, or procedures that reduce the likelihood that military personnel in combat will develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or other stress-related psychopathologies into basic and pre-deployment training, combat theater operations, and post-deployment service; (2) conduct and fund research to develop such plan; (3) develop and implement a training program to educate and promote understanding and awareness among commissioned officers, non-commissioned officers, and front-line medical professionals about the signs and risks of combat stress as well as the signs and risks of stress-related psychopathology; (4) educate members of the Armed Forces and their families to recognize signs of combat stress, provide members pre-deployment combat stress management training, and increase outreach and access to members and their families about programs and treatment options that mitigate the negative impact of combat stress on the returning member; and (5) work with the Department of Veterans Affairs and the National Institutes of Health to research and implement best practices for information dissemination to military personnel and their families.

Directs the Secretary to establish: (1) a working

Amends the Agricultural Act of 1949 to permit the haying and grazing of reduced acreage, acreage devoted to a conservation use, and acreage diverted from production under a land diversion program, except during any consecutive five-month period that is established by the State committee for a State for a State, or during the five-month period that begins April 1 and ends October 31 of a year for any producer who elects to pay a fee equal to: (1) the grazing fee in effect as established by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) in the case of grazing, or (2) a haying fee established by BLM that is comparable to the grazing fee. Prohibits the Secretary of Agriculture from excluding irrigated or irrigable acreage not planted to alfalfa when exercising the authority of the Secretary under this Act.

Artists' Contribution to American Heritage Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a fair market value deduction for the charitable contribution of literary, musical, artistic, or scholarly compositions or similar property, or the copyright created by the taxpayer, if such property was created and donated no sooner than 18 months prior to the donation and is used for a tax-exempt purpose.

Superfund Research, Development, and Demonstration Act of 1999 - Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 to authorize appropriations for FY 2000 through 2004 for the Superfund Innovative Treatment and Evaluation (SITE) program. 
Authorizes the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to enter into agreements with persons, public entities (including the Departments of Defense and Energy), and nonprofit private entities to arrange for the use of other sites appropriate for carrying out hazardous substances research, testing, evaluation, development, and demonstration projects. 
Requires the Administrator to strive to enter into agreements with the Departments of Defense and Energy and other Federal agencies to ensure the effective transfer to such agencies of technologies potentially applicable to remediation or containment of hazardous substances at sites owned or operated by such agencies. 
Revises responsibilities of the University Hazardous Substance Research Centers. 
Directs the Administrator to maintain funding for each hazardous substance research center at a level not less than that funded in FY 1999 until such time as the Administrator completes the next competitive selection process for the centers.

Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act) Suspension of FY2013 Budget Sequestration Under the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act This bill cancels the sequestration of budgetary resources for FY2013 under the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act.  The bill requires the flexible sequestration of budgetary resources for FY2013 to be implemented as determined by the head of the agency with spending authority over such account.  The bill authorizes the Department of Defense (DOD) to take appropriate actions in the management of current multiyear DOD contracts to minimize the effects of discretionary spending reductions required under the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act.  The bill makes certain shipbuilding and conversion funds available for shipbuilding cost increases.

African Free Trade Initiative Act - Amends the African Growth and Opportunity Act to direct the President to develop a plan for negotiating and entering into one or more free trade agreements with all sub-Saharan African countries, identifying the 15 countries or groups of countries that are most ready for such agreement with the United States.

Requires the plan to include: (1) the steps such sub-Saharan African country needs to be equipped and ready to enter into such an agreement with the United States, including the development of a bilateral investment treaty; (2) milestones for accomplishing each step, with the goal of establishing a free trade agreement with each sub-Saharan African country not later than 10 years after enactment of this Act; (3) the resources required to assist each sub-Saharan African country in accomplishing each milestone; (4) the extent to which steps may be accomplished through regional or subregional organizations in sub-Saharan Africa; and (5) procedures to ensure adequate consultation with Congress and the private sector during negotiations.

Directs the President to report to Congress on the plan.

Requires the U.S. Trade Representative and Administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) to consult and coordinate with the Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation regarding countries that have entered

Diamond-Blackfan Anemia Research and Care Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), in coordination with the Directors of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, and the Office of Rare Diseases, to expand and intensify research and related activities of NIH with regard to Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

Requires the Director to make grants to, or enter into contracts with, public or private entities to support a comprehensive research initiative to study, develop better treatments for, and ultimately find a cure for Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to maintain and expand the Diamond-Blackfan Anemia Registry. Requires the Secretary to establish a comprehensive clinical care center for Diamond-Blackfan anemia, where a majority of the patients with the disease are examined, treated, and tracked through the Registry, by experts in the disease.

Modifies the circumstances under which persons convicted of committing capital offenses may be interred in national cemeteries and denied interment in military cemeteries and funeral honors. 
Requires the Secretary of the Army to remove the remains of Russell Wayne Wagner from Arlington National Cemetery.

Economic Fairness for Seniors Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the monthly Medicare part B premium for 2010 to be the monthly Medicare part B premium for 2009.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Tax Act of 2009 to extend for calendar years 2009 and 2010: (1) the Medicare prescription drug benefit; (2) the Medicare beneficiary's self-coverage option; (3) the Medicare supplemental health insurance (Medicare SCHIP) benefit; and (4) certain economic recovery payments to individuals who are retired or disabled as a result of a foreclosure or other bankruptcy.

Directs the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) to study whether a consumer price index for elderly consumers (CPI-E) more accurately reflects the true costs of inflation for elderly Americans than the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W), and if the elderly are being financially disadvantaged by the use of the CPI-W in the determination of current benefit levels. Directs the BLS to report to Congress on the results of such study and, if appropriate, the creation of a CPI-E.

Amends the

Colombian Temporary Protected Status Act of 2002 - Expresses the sense of Congress that, in view of the recent escalation of the current civil war in Colombia, Colombia qualifies for designation under the Immigration and Nationality Act pursuant to which Colombian nationals would be eligible for temporary protected status (TPS) in the United States. 
Designates Colombia as a TPS-eligible country for purposes of the Act.  Requires an initial one-year designation period. 
Sets forth TPS-eligibility requirements for Colombians.  Directs the Attorney General to give prior consent to travel abroad to an alien granted TPS pursuant to this Act if the alien establishes that emergency and extenuating circumstances beyond the control of the alien require the alien to depart for a brief, temporary trip abroad.  Treats an alien returning to the United States in accordance with such an authorization the same as any other returning alien provided TPS under the Act.

Authorizes the Chief of the National Guard Bureau to establish and operate up to five National Guard counterdrug schools in California, Florida, Iowa, Mississippi, and Pennsylvania.  Requires annual reports from the Secretary of Defense to the Congress on the activities of such schools.  Authorizes appropriations.
Amends the Carl D. Perkins Vocational and Technical Education Act of 1998 to revise the Indian student count formula.

Veterans TRICARE Choice Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a veteran enrolled in the TRICARE program to make a health care coverage election that makes such veteran ineligible for TRICARE health care coverage.

American Worker Mobility Act of 2014 - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to grant a relocation subsidy to an individual who: (1) is totally unemployed and has been totally unemployed for at least 26 consecutive weeks, (2) has exhausted all rights to regular compensation under state or federal law, (3) has not received a relocation subsidy in the two-year period preceding the application date, and (4) is able to work, available to work, and actively seeking work.  Prohibits the Secretary from granting a relocation subsidy to an eligible individual unless the Secretary determines that: (1) the subsidy will assist the individual in relocating within the United States, at least 60 miles from the individual's current residence, for the purpose of attaining employment; (2) the individual applied for the subsidy not later than January 1, 2019; and (3) the individual has obtained a bona fide offer of suitable employment affording a reasonable expectation of long-term duration in the area in which the individual wishes to relocate or wishes to relocate to an area that has an unemployment rate that is at least 2% less than the unemployment rate of the area of the individual's initial residence.  Limits the amount of a

Native American Commercial Driving Training and Technical Assistance Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to provide competitive grants to tribal colleges and universities to support programs providing training and certificates leading to the licensing of Native Americans with respect to commercial vehicle driving. Requires the Secretary, in providing such grants, to give priority to grant applications that: (1) propose training that exceeds proposed minimum standards for training tractor-trailer drivers of the Department of Transportation; (2) propose training that exceeds the entry level truck driver certification standards set by the Professional Truck Driver Institute; and (3) propose an education partnership with a private trucking firm, trucking association, or similar entity in order to ensure the effectiveness of the grant program.

Prescription Drug Labeling Promotion Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a working group to develop and promulgate guidance on best practices for pharmacies to ensure that blind and visually impaired individuals have safe, consistent, reliable, and independent access to the information in the labeling of prescription drugs.

Requires the working group to consider: (1) the use of Braille, auditory means, and enhanced visual means of prescription drug labeling; (2) whether there are technical, financial, manpower, or other factors unique to pharmacies with 20 or fewer retail locations which may impact their ability to implement the best practices; and (3) other appropriate factors.

Directs the Commissioner of Food and Drugs (FDA) to conduct an informational and educational program to inform the public and pharmacists about the guidance and practices.

Directs the Comptroller General to review the guidance, the extent to which pharmacies are complying with such best practices, and the extent to which barriers to accessible prescription drug labeling for blind and visually impaired individuals continue.

Religious Liberty and Charitable Donation Protection Act of 1997 - Amends Federal bankruptcy law to prohibit the court from taking into consideration whether a debtor has made, or continues to make, charitable contributions to a qualified religious or charitable entity or organization in making a determination as to whether to dismiss a case under the bankruptcy code.

Federal Credit Cost Reduction Act of 1994 - Amends the Federal Credit Reform Act of 1990 to include administrative costs in the computation of direct loan and loan guarantee costs. 
Amends Federal law to provide for a separate listing of administrative costs for direct loans and loan guarantees originating before the enactment of this Act. 
Sets forth Federal credit subsidy rates.  Prohibits the consideration of budget resolutions that would allow the maximum permissible subsidy rate to be breached.

Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to set forth a time frame for determinations by the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) in investigations initiated pursuant to the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) involving rights under TRIPS or the General Agreement on Tariffs (GATT 1994) relating to products subject to intellectual property protection.

Amends the Andean Trade Preference Act and the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act to require the USTR to ensure a timely review and disposition of requests received from an interested party that the President reconsider the status of a country as a beneficiary country under such Acts.

Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to require a foreign country, in order to be eligible as a CBTPA beneficiary country, to comply with TRIPS obligations.

Amends the Andean Trade Preference Act and the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act to require a foreign country, in order to be eligible as an ATPDEA beneficiary country, to comply with TRIPS obligations.
Syrian War Criminality Accountability Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of State to report to Congress on war crimes and crimes against humanity in Syria.

Veterans Life Insurance Opportunity Act of 1998 - Makes eligible for the Veterans' Group Life Insurance program any person whose Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance (SGLI) was continued in force after termination or discharge from military service under the law as in effect prior to the date on which the Veterans' Group Life Insurance program became effective.  Makes such program five years in effect, less the time elapsed between the termination of the applicant's SGLI and the effective date on which the program became effective. 
Authorizes:  (1) any person who did not convert SGLI coverage to VGLI coverage within the period after separation from service to apply for (within 20 months after the end of such period of separation) VGLI coverage in an amount equal to the amount of the insured's SGLI; and (2) any person who did not convert SGLI coverage to VGLI coverage and whose SGLI coverage terminated during the five-year period after the end of a service or travel period to apply for (within 90 days after enactment of this Act) VGLI coverage in an amount equal to the amount of the insured's SGLI. 
Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide

Mortgage Insurance Fairness Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for mortgage insurance premiums. Reduces the amount of such deduction for taxpayers with adjusted gross incomes exeeding $100,000. Allows a tax deduction for mortgage insurance premiums paid by individuals who receive payments from a trade or business in connection with mortgage insurance.

International Rule of Law and Antiterrorism Act of 2003 - Directs the President to: (1) direct the U.S. Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use U.S. influence to establish negotiations with the United Nations and U.N. member states to establish a professional United Nations civilian police corps (UNCPC); (2) direct the Secretary of State to request that the United Nations Secretariat prepare a report concerning the establishment of a professional United Nations civilian police corps; and (3) direct the Secretary to work with the United Nations Secretariat and other U.N. member states to establish standards and training programs for international civilian police.Requires the President to report to specified congressional committees on the progress of negotiations to establish a professional United Nations civilian police corps.

Protecting Seniors' Medicare Choices from Obamacare Act of 2014 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to eliminate the premium assistance maximum benefit amount (FMAP) for Medicaid enhanced Medicare (Medicare Advantage) plans for individuals incarcerated in a public institution.  Establishes a Medicare Advantage Stabilization Program under which the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) shall provide a PMPM (Plan Year Maximum Premium) stabilization funding amount to each eligible Medicare Advantage plan for plan year 2015 to address the beneficiary plan inadequacies applicable to such plan.

Hygiene Assistance for Families of Infants and Toddlers Act of 2017 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make grants to states, Indian tribes or tribal organizations, or nonprofit organizations to conduct demonstration projects that implement and evaluate strategies to help families with eligible children to address the diapering needs of such children. HHS must use grant funds to: (1) fund diaper distribution demonstration projects that will reduce the substantial cost of diapers and diapering supplies by making them available to low-income families; (2) evaluate the effects of such demonstration projects on mitigating health risks that can arise when low-income families do not have an adequate supply of diapers for infants and toddlers; and (3) integrate the diaper distribution demonstration projects with other assistance programs serving families with eligible children. HHS must report on the effectiveness of the projects.

Block Access to North Korea Act of 2016 or the BANK Act of 2016 This bill expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) providers of specialized financial messaging services are a critical link to the international financial system, and (2) directly providing specialized financial messaging services to, or enabling or facilitating access to such services for, any financial institution is inconsistent with the United Nations Security Council Resolution 2094 regarding sanctions against North Korean financial institutions. The President shall impose sanctions pursuant to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act with respect to a person if, 90 days after enactment of this Act, the person continues to knowingly and directly provide specialized financial messaging services to, or knowingly enable or facilitate access to such services for:   the Central Bank of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (Korea);  a financial institution that facilitates any transaction or transactions or provides significant financial services for nuclear development or proliferation for or on behalf of North Korea; or  a person identified on the list of specially designated nationals and blocked persons maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the Department of the Treasury by reason of assisting the nuclear development or proliferation efforts of North Korea.  The President may waive the requirement to impose sanctions with respect to a person if:

Requires the Director of Central Intelligence to complete a specified survey and issue a report to Congress respecting the results of such survey.
Requires the Director of Intelligence to issue specified guidelines to the Congress respecting the implementation of such survey.
Requires the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the Director of Central Intelligence to establish procedures to restrict access to intelligence information in the data system under circumstances in which such information is not to be disclosed directly to Government officials.

Mary Jo Lawyer Spano Mesothelioma Patient Registry Act of 2015 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry to develop a patient registry to collect data on mesothelioma, including information on the incidence and prevalence of the disease in the United States. The agency must use the registry to:   enhance and expand infrastructure and activities for tracking the epidemiology of mesothelioma patients;   collect, consolidate, and report on health information on mesothelioma patients;   describe the incidence and prevalence of mesothelioma in the United States;   facilitate research on mesothelioma;   examine factors that may be associated with mesothelioma;   outline key demographic factors associated with mesothelioma; and   make information available to the public to facilitate and enhance research on, and the prevention and treatment of, mesothelioma.

Makes funds appropriated to the Department of Defense (DOD) available for the payment of costs incurred by the National Guard in conducting international military-to-civilian contacts, civilian-to-civilian contacts, and comparable activities to: (1) support the objectives of the commander of the combatant command for the theater of operations in which such contacts and activities are conducted; (2) build international civil-military partnerships and capacity; (3) strengthen cooperation between the departments and agencies of the United States and foreign governments; (4) facilitate intergovernmental collaboration between the U.S. government and foreign governments; and (5) facilitate and enhance the exchange of information between the U.S. government and foreign governments on matters relating to defense and security.

Bars the availability of such funds for contacts and activities: (1) conducted in a foreign country unless jointly approved by the commander of the combatant command concerned and the chief of mission concerned; or (2) performed by a member of the National Guard in a foreign country unless the member is on active duty in the Armed Forces at the time of such participation.

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2013 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to provide that any unsecured claim of a governmental unit against the debtor or the estate that arises before the filing of the petition, or that arises after the filing of the petition and before the debtor's discharge as a result of the sale, transfer, exchange, or other disposition of any property used in the debtor's farming operation shall: (1) be treated as an unsecured claim arising before the date on which the petition is filed; (2) not be entitled to priority under the bankruptcy laws of the United States; (3) be provided for under a plan; and (4) be discharged in accordance with the bankruptcy laws of the United States.  Allows a governmental unit to file a proof of claim for such a claim that arises after the filing of the petition.  Requires a debtor that files a tax return after the filing of the petition for a period in which a claim arises, and the claim relates to the tax return, to serve notice of the claim on the governmental unit charged with the responsibility for the collection of the tax at the address and in the manner designated by the unit.  Permits a governmental unit that has received notice of a claim to file a

Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to revise the requirements for a space to be benchmarked and disclosed under the Energy Star program for leasing buildings without Energy Star labels. Requires that the space: (1) be renovated for all energy efficiency and conservation improvements that would be cost-effective over the lease's life; and (2) be benchmarked under a nationally recognized, online, free benchmarking program, with public disclosure, unless the space is a space for which owners cannot access whole building utility consumption data.

Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE), in coordination with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), to study the impact of: (1) state and local performance benchmarking and disclosure policies, and any associated building efficiency policies, for commercial and multifamily buildings; and (2) programs and systems in which utilities provide aggregated information regarding whole building energy consumption and usage information to owners of multitenant commercial, residential, and mixed-use buildings.

Directs the Secretary to maintain and make public energy-related information on commercial and multifamily buildings, including: (1) data provided under federal, state, local, and other laws or programs regarding building benchmarking and energy information disclosure; (2) information on buildings that have

Encouraging Mortgage Modifications Act of 2008 - Amends the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act of 1974 to require a servicer of pooled qualified residential mortgages to act in the best interests of all investors and parties having a direct or indirect interest in the pooled loans or securitization vehicle, if the servicer agrees to or implements a qualified loan modification or workout plan for a qualified residential mortgage, or if, and only if, such efforts are unsuccessful or infeasible, takes other reasonable loss mitigation actions, including accepting partial payments or short sale of the property.

Prohibits a servicer from being liable for entering into a qualified loan modification or workout plan under any federal, state, or local law or regulation for any action filed by or on behalf of any person: (1) based on the person's ownership of any interest in a residential mortgage, a pool of residential mortgage loans, or a securitization vehicle, that distributes payments out of the principal, interest, or other payment on loans in the pool; (2) based on the person's obligation to make payments determined in reference to any loan or interest referred to in clause 1; or (3) based on the person's obligation to insure any loan or any

District of Columbia College Access Improvement Act of 2002 - Amends the District of Columbia College Access Act of 1999 to revise eligibility requirements for public and private elementary and secondary school programs for eligible individuals who were residents of the District of Columbia for at least 12 consecutive months before the commencement of their studies at an institution of higher education. Includes among such requirements that an individual: (1) be enrolled at an institution of higher education within 3 years after graduating from a secondary school or receiving the equivalent diploma; (2) have been domiciled in the District of Columbia for at least five consecutive years at the date of application; or (3) graduated from a secondary school or received the equivalent diploma on or after January 1, 1998.Provides for the continued authorization of appropriations for such programs.

American Heroes Act - Allows each State to provide one statue of an individual representing that State which shall be displayed in the Capitol Visitor Center. Requires the statues to be depictions of individuals who participated in the life of the State in ways that will inspire young Americans to embrace the ideals of the United States as reflected in the Constitution.

Requires the Clerk of the House of Representatives and the Secretary of the Senate to jointly assign to one of their employees the post of the American Hero Administrator, with such term as agreed upon by the Clerk and the Secretary.

Requires the American Hero Administrator to prepare guidelines establishing the size, weight, and other necessary restrictions to be placed on the statues to be displayed in the Capitol Visitor Center.

Requires a State, in order for a statue provided by that State to be placed in the Capitol Visitor Center, to establish an American Hero Commission to select the individual to represent that State.

Fair Wage Act  This bill amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to increase the federal minimum wage to: (1) $8.00 an hour, beginning 30 days after the date of enactment of this bill or January 1, 2017, whichever date is earlier; (2) $9.00 an hour, beginning one year after the earlier of such dates; (3) $10.00 an hour, beginning two years after such date; (4) $11.00 an hour, beginning three years after such date; (5) $12.00 an hour, beginning four years after such date; (6) $13.00 an hour, beginning five years after such date; (7) $14.00 an hour, beginning six years after such date; and (8) $15.00 an hour, beginning seven years after such date, and annually thereafter.  The bill also requires the Department of Labor to publish a notice in the Federal Register and on its website 60 days before any increase in the minimum wage. Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer who is a qualified mentor (i.e., an individual who attained age 21 before the beginning of the taxable year) a tax credit of $1,000 for each qualifying mentored individual by the taxpayer. Defines "qualified mentor" as an individual who: (1) has attained age 18 as of the close of the taxable year but did not attain age 22 during the taxable year; (2) was placed by an authorized placement agency or by court order after attaining age 18; and (3) has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than half of the taxable year.

National Guard Investigations Transparency and Improvement Act of 2014 - Places the duties of the Office of Complex Administrative Investigations (OCAI) within the Office of the Chief of the National Guard Bureau (Chief of Guard). Requires the Chief of Guard to treat any final report of OCAI as if such report were the report of an Inspector General of the Department of Defense (DOD) or a military department on such matter. Requires the Chief of Guard to submit annual reports to Congress on investigations undertaken by OCAI during the preceding year.

Directs the Customs Service to reliquidate certain entries, in accordance with the final decision of the International Trade Administration of the Department of Commerce and the final results of the administrative reviews, for entries made on or after December 1, 1993, and before April 1, 2001.

Home Health Care Planning Improvement Act of 2007 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise requirements for the provision of home health services by clinical nurse specialists, certified nurse-midwives, and physician assistants.

Revises requirements for the provision of home health services by physicians.

This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the tax credit for production from advanced nuclear power facilities, to: (1) allocate such credit among facilities placed in service in different orders of time, and (2) transfer such credit to a public entity that elects to apply it to all of the credit received from a project partner.

Strengthening Community Safety Act of 2010 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to make grants to eligible first responder agencies for the additional costs incurred as a direct result of one or more of their employees who are reservists being placed on active duty.

Defines "eligible first responder agency" as an agency for which the cost of operating has increased by not less than 5% as a direct result of such an employee being placed on active duty.

Prohibits the use of grants for costs relating to an employee being placed on active duty if federal funds are used for the pay or benefits of the employee.

Authorizes grant use for: (1) pay and benefits for an individual hired to replace such an employee; (2) overtime expenses for an employee who performs tasks that would have been performed by an employee placed on active duty; and (3) the cost of equipment, maintenance, or other activities the eligible first responder agency was unable to acquire or perform because of the cost of replacing an employee placed on active duty, or the need for which was caused by an employee being placed on active duty.
