Temporary IRA Distribution Suspension Act of 2008 - Suspends, for calendar 2008 and 2009, the requirement that individual taxpayers who are beneficiaries of a qualified retirement annuity pay the beginning date of the tax year for distributions from such an annuity.

Gas Pump Access Act of 2016 This bill requires it to be considered discrimination for a gas station or convenience store to fail to clearly display at each self-service gas pump a decal that: (1) is at least 15 square inches in size, has a blue background, includes the telephone number of the gas station or convenience store at which such pump is located and the words "Call for Assistance" in printed white text, and includes the International Symbol of Accessibility; and (2) is at least 15 square inches in size, has a blue background, includes the telephone number of the gas station or convenience store at which such pump is located and the words "Call for Assistance" in printed white text, and includes the International Symbol of Accessibility, if the phone connected to such number is not operational and answered directly by an employee of the gas station retailer during the hours the gas station retailer is open for business to the public. It shall be considered discrimination for a gas station or convenience store that is open for business to the public with two or more attendants on duty to fail to provide gas pumping assistance to a qualified individual with a disability who makes a request for such assistance. It shall not be considered discrimination for a gas station or convenience store that

Intellectual Property Assembly of the Americas - Establishes a meeting of the Congress and representative parliamentary groups from other countries in the Americas to:  (1) discuss common problems and interests in intellectual and industrial property; and (2) promote such national and multilateral measures as may further common interests in intellectual and industrial property. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Federal Employees' Compensation Reform Act of 2011 - Terminates the payment of Federal employees' compensation under the Federal Employees' Retirement System (FERS) and the Social Security Act (SSA) at the same time that an employee attains retirement age and is eligible for an annuity under FERS or SSA, as appropriate.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to provide notice of this Act to the employee, the employee's employing agency, and the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).

Requires the employing agency to file an application for an annuity with OPM.

Caribbean National Forest Wild and Scenic Rivers Act of 2002 - Amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate specified rivers within the Caribbean National Forests of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico as components of the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System.

Import Control and Safe Handling of Spent Nuclear Fuel Act of 1995 - Prohibits the import into the United States of spent nuclear fuel unless:  (1) the Congress has approved a repository for the storage or disposal of all spent nuclear fuel generated by commercial nuclear reactors in the United States and from atomic energy defense activities; (2) the appropriate Federal agency has licensed such repository; and (3) the repository is operating. 
Makes such prohibition inapplicable to imports from a country that:  (1) is not a country authorized to possess nuclear weapons under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and is known or suspected to be producing or developing nuclear weapons; and (2) the President notifies specified congressional intelligence committees at least 30 days in advance of the arrival of the imported fuel into U.S. customs territory. 
Makes such prohibition inapplicable to samples of spent nuclear fuel imported for testing and evaluation for national security purposes. 
Authorizes any port authority to establish reasonable guidelines to ensure that the unloading, transfer, and shipment of spent nuclear fuel at or through a port under its jurisdiction is conducted in a manner that protects the public health and safety and the environment at, and in the vicinity of, such

Colonias Improvement Act of 2014 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), in consultation with the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA), to issue a proposed rule containing a definition of the term "colonia" that: (1) is the same for each covered program, to the extent consistent with specified provisions of this Act; (2) is limited to a community that is located within 75 miles of the border between the United States and Mexico, or that has applied for or received funding under a covered program before the enactment of this Act; (3) reflects and preserves the historic, geographic, and cultural character of the communities served by the covered programs; and (4) may be used to determine whether an applicant qualifies for assistance under any covered program.  Directs the Administrator to ensure that the final rule takes effect not later than one year after the enactment of this Act.  Requires the Administrator, HUD, and USDA to establish and regularly update a webpage that: (1) serves as a clearinghouse for information relating to the covered programs; and (2) includes links to information specific to each state in which a covered program operates, including local contact information.

Health Care Consumer Protection Act of 1995 - Requires an insurer providing health insurance coverage under a health plan to provide annual notice to each current enrollee regarding the extent of coverage of the plan.  Requires such notice to be in writing and to include a copy of the contract between the insurer and enrollee, in addition to information regarding the terms and conditions of the policy and the rights and obligations of the parties. 
Requires an insurer to provide notice to each potential enrollee regarding the extent of coverage of the plan upon request. 
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to promulgate regulations to ensure that an insurer provides such notice. 
Sets forth a process for the Secretary to enforce penalties for entities that offer a health plan that violates this Act. 
Prohibits an insurer from including provisions in a health plan to hold itself harmless for any liability. 
Bars a State from establishing or enforcing standards for insurers or health insurance coverage with respect to the subject matter of this Act that are weaker than the standards established under this Act.

Small Business Reform Act of 2010 or the Not Too Small to Succeed in Business Act of 2010 - Amends the Small Business Act to extend the period of eligibility for small business program assistance for seven years (currently, five years) for: (1) newly-established small businesses; (2) small businesses that have been in operation for less than 10 years; and (3) small businesses that have been in operation for at least 10 years and have not been in business for less than 5 years.

Allows a small business that completed a 9-year period of participation in the program and that is otherwise eligible to participate in such program during the two-year period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act.

Increases the net worth and adjusted gross income limitations for program participants.

Education in Vocational Technology Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Education to make grants to States to:  (1) improve the quality of instruction or training in, or develop instruction and training in, manufacturing and other occupational technologies; and (2) assist local educational agencies in purchasing State-of-the-art equipment for technical vocational education. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Nuclear Policy and Posture Review Act of 2007 - Directs the President to conduct a nuclear policy review to consider a range of options on the role of nuclear weapons in U.S. security policy.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct a comprehensive review of the nuclear posture of the United States to clarify U.S. nuclear deterrence policy and strategy.

Weekends Without Hunger Act - Amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to establish a program to provide commodities, on a competitive basis, to nonprofit institutions (including schools, food banks, and homeless shelters) to provide nutritious food to at-risk children on weekends and during extended school holidays during the school year.

Requires the Secretary to give priority to institutions that: (1) have on-going programs and experience serving populations with significant proportions of at-risk school children; (2) have a good record of experience in food delivery and food safety systems; (3) maintain high quality control, accountability, and recordkeeping standards; (4) provide children with readily consumable food of high nutrient content and quality; (5) demonstrate cost efficiencies and the potential for obtaining supplemental funding from non-federal sources to carry out projects; and (6) demonstrate the ability to continue projects for the full approved term of the pilot project period.

Pharmaceutical Supply and Value Enhancement Act or the Pharmaceutical SAVE Act - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), upon determining that there is a prescription drug shortage, to: (1) authorize temporary importation of such drug for a period of up to three years if the drug is subject to certain requirements; and (2) treat a noncompetitive market as creating a drug shortage.

Continuity of Electric Capacity Resources Act - Amends the Federal Power Act to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to require each transmission organization with a tariff on file with FERC to notify FERC of its intent to procure electric capacity resources. Requires the transmission organization to submit to FERC a report that: (1) identifies electric capacity resources that are available to the transmission organization; (2) describes the fuel sources and operational characteristics of each such resource; (3) evaluates the financial health, viability, and projected remaining years of service of the available resources; (4) identifies over the short- and long-term periods in the planning cycle of the transmission organization, announced and projected retirements of the available resources, the projected future needs of the transmission organization for electric capacity resources, and the availability of transmission facilities and transmission support services necessary to provide for the transmission organization reasonable assurances of essential reliability services; and (5) assesses the current and projected status of the reliability of the elements of the bulk-power system under the control of the transmission organization, over the short- and long-term periods in the planning cycle of the transmission organization. Requires the transmission organization that submitted the report to file with FERC one or more tariff amendments that would achieve specified objectives with respect to

Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit Expansion Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the passive activity tax credit for rental real estate activities (the rehabilitation credit).  Reduces such credit for taxpayers with adjusted gross incomes over $100,000.  Eliminates the phaseout of such credit for low-income housing tax credits. 
Allows the rehabilitation credit to offset a portion of the alternative minimum tax.

Prohibits the use of funds appropriated or otherwise available to the Department of Defense (DOD) for the procurement of specified covered items (including food, clothing, tents, or natural fiber products, specialty metals, or hand or measuring tools) that are not grown, reprocessed, reused, or produced in the United States, except as provided for in this Act.  Authorizes the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary of the military department concerned to waive such requirement if:  (1) satisfactory quality and sufficient quantity of any such article or item cannot be procured at U.S. market prices; (2) 30 days have elapsed since the Secretary has notified the congressional defense committees; and (3) the Secretary has notified such committees.  Makes such waiver applicable to procurements outside the United States in support of combat operations, procurements by vessels in foreign waters, and emergency procurements or procurements of perishable foods by establishments located outside the United States for their personnel.  Makes an exception for specialty metals or chemical warfare protective clothing that is necessary:  (1) to comply with agreements with foreign governments requiring the United States to purchase supplies from foreign sources to offset U.S. sales under approved programs serving defense requirements; or (2) in furtherance

Preservation of Access to Osteoporosis Testing for Medicare Beneficiary Act of 2011 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend the minimum payment amount for osteoporosis testing to: (1) Medicare beneficiaries for 2010, 2011, and 2012; and (2) Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries for 2011, 2012, and 2013.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a tax credit for a specified amount based on the fuel efficiency of a motor vehicle.  Limits the amount of such credit based upon the taxpayer's adjusted gross income. 
Terminates the alternative motor vehicle tax credit.

Cameron Gulbransen Kids and Cars Safety Act of 2003 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to evaluate: (1) devices and technologies intended to reduce the incidence of child injury and child death occurring outside of parked motor vehicles in nontraffic, noncrash events, including backing-over incidents, that are caused by such vehicles, and determining which of those methods is the most effective; and (2) currently available technology to prevent injury and death of children left unattended inside of parked motor vehicles, including injury or death due to hyperthermia, power windows, or power sunroofs.Requires the Secretary to: (1) establish a database of (or modify an existing database to include), and collect data regarding, the numbers and types of injuries and deaths in nontraffic, noncrash events involving motor vehicles; (2) evaluate the available technologies for detecting and preventing collisions with individuals and objects behind a motor vehicle; (3) prescribe motor vehicle safety standards that require the installation, as standard equipment on a new motor vehicle, of devices for detecting, and providing to operators of such a vehicle a warning of, individuals and objects behind the motor vehicle, and establish requirements for the performance of such devices; and (4) prescribe motor vehicle safety standards for

Amends the Civil Rights of Institutionalized Persons Act to provide that a claim against a Federal prisoner for deprivation of rights shall be submitted in forma pauperis (i.e., in the lowest form of civil procedure) only if the prisoner has attained the age of 18 years.  Provides that a stay of the action for a specified period shall be ordered if the court does not dismiss a claim within a specified time frame. 
Amends the Federal criminal code to:  (1) provide that a multiple in forma pauperis claim shall be resolved within the preceding five years; and (2) provide that a party to an action in forma pauperis shall not be required to prove or stipulate that the multiple claim is in fact made. 
Provides that a stay of the action shall be ordered if the court determines that the prisoner is in danger of immediate harm. 
Provides that, if the court determines that the multiple claim is in fact made, the court shall proceed with the action except to the extent the court is notified by the parties that it has been resolved.

Tackling Excessive Standardized Testing Act of 2015 or the TEST Act of 2015 Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to revise the requirements for administering state academic assessments in mathematics and reading or language arts for students in grades 3 through 8.  Requires that students who are at the 15th percentile or above for mathematics or who are at the 15th percentile or above for reading or language arts, or whose achievement levels fall between these percentiles, for the preceding school year in each of grades 4, 6, and 8, be allowed, for the school year following the administration of such assessments, to administer the academic assessments in mathematics in each of grades 4 and 8, and in reading or language arts in each of grades 3 and 7.  Requires that students who are at the 15th percentile or above for mathematics or who are at the 15th percentile or above for reading or language arts, or whose achievement levels fall between these percentiles, for the preceding school year in each of grades 3, 5, and 7, be allowed, for the school year following the administration of such assessments, to administer

DHS FOIA Efficiency Act of 2015 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Chief Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Officer of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to: (1) finalize and issue an updated regulation implementing FOIA provisions, (2) identify the total annual cost to DHS of implementing FOIA, (3) develop guidance on reporting standards related to the costs of processing FOIA requests, (4) identify unnecessary and duplicative actions taken by DHS in the course of processing FOIA requests and eliminate such actions, (5) develop a plan to automate the processing of such requests, and (6) develop a plan to automate the processing of such requests and update guidance to the heads of DHS components on reducing the backlog in processing such requests.  (Sec. 3) Upon completion of the plan to automate the processing of requests, the Chief FOIA Officer shall provide the plan to the heads of DHS components and seek written feedback on the extent to which the component will adopt the plan, the associated costs, and the projected timelines.

Cocopah Lands Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to take specified lands in Yuma County, Arizona, into trust for the Cocopah Indian Tribe of Arizona, if the Tribe transfers title to such lands to the Secretary and there are no adverse legal claims to such land, including outstanding liens, mortgages, or taxes owed.

Considers such land to be part of the Tribe's initial reservation.

Provides that for the purposes of the delivery of federal services to enrolled members of the Tribe, the Tribe's service area shall be Yuma County, Arizona.

Prohibits the use of such trust land for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

Plan B for Plan B Act of 2005 - Directs the Commissioner of Food and Drugs to approve or disapprove the supplemental new drug application for Plan B (emergency contraception containing 0.75 mg levonorgestrel) as amended by the formal response to the non-approvable letter dated May 6, 2004, from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to Barr Pharmaceuticals to switch Plan B from prescription-only to nonprescription status for women of all ages.

Uterine Fibroid Research and Education Act of 2003 - Requires the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand, intensify, and coordinate programs for the conduct and support of uterine fibroids research.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop and disseminate to the public information regarding uterine fibroids, including information on: (1) the incidence and prevalence of uterine fibroids; (2) the elevated risk for minority women; and (3) the availability of a range of treatment options for symptomatic uterine fibroids.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Administrator of the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), to develop and disseminate to health care providers information on uterine fibroids, including information on the elevated risk for minority women and the range of available options for the treatment of symptomatic uterine fibroids.

Directs the Attorney General to prescribe regulations governing the storage by State and local law enforcement agencies of explosive materials that have been shipped or transported in interstate or foreign commerce.  Authorizes the Attorney General to enter during business hours any place where such an agency stores or keeps explosive materials that have been so transported, for the purpose of inspecting and determining whether the materials are being stored or kept in compliance with such regulations. 
Authorizes the Attorney General to reduce by 10 percent the funds that an agency would otherwise receive, or would otherwise be allocated, under any Department of Justice grant program if the agency fails to comply with this Act or any related regulation.  Requires any funds that are not allocated to an agency that is not reduced by reason of this Act to be reallocated to other agencies that are not reduced by reason of this Act. 
Authorizes the Attorney General to make matching grants to State and local law enforcement agencies for the cost of complying with such regulations.  Authorizes appropriations.

Bond Transparency Act of 2014 - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require a broker, dealer, or municipal securities dealer that effects a riskless principal transaction to disclose to the customer, in writing, at or before the time of completion of the transaction the amount of the difference between: (1) the customer's purchase price and the broker's, dealer's or municipal securities dealer's purchase price; or (2) the customer's sale price and the broker's, dealer's or municipal securities dealer's sale price. Defines "riskless principal transaction" as: (1) a transaction in which a broker, dealer, or municipal securities dealer receives a customer order to buy or sell any municipal securities and, after receiving the customer order, buys the municipal securities from, or sells the securities to, another person, while acting as principal for its own account, to complete the customer order; and (2) any other transaction the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) identifies by rule as a riskless principal transaction.

Equity in Public Education Act of 1996 - Directs the Secretary of Education to provide for reimbursement to eligible States for certain educational costs incurred by local educational agencies in providing a free public education to eligible illegal alien students.

Responsible Stem Cell Research Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a National Stem Cell Donor Bank to: (1) seek and preserve donations of qualifying human stem cells; and (2) make such donated cells available for biomedical research and for therapeutic purposes.Requires the Secretary, acting through the Director of the National Institutes of Health, to conduct and support research that uses qualifying human stem cells. Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to treat U.S. cruise industry income as effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United States. Defines "U.S. cruise industry income" as income attributable to any covered passenger cruise, including income directly or indirectly attributable to the carriage of passengers and any on-board or off-board activities incidental to such covered passenger cruise. Excludes from such definition any voyage: (1) on any vessel owned or operated by the United States, a state, or any subdivision thereof; (2) which occurs exclusively on the inland waterways of the United States; or (3) in which a vessel in the usual course of employment proceeds, without an intervening foreign port of call from one port or place in the United States to the same port or place or to another port or place in the United States.

Exempts from the definition of "U.S. cruise industry income" any U.S. source gross transportation income which is U.S. cruise industry income.

Exempts nonresident aliens and foreign corporations from the tax exemption for income from sources outside the United States for purposes of the U.S. tax system. Declares that no tax exemption or reduced tax rate shall be permitted under any treaty of the United States with respect to U

Incentives for our Nation's Veterans in Energy Sustainability Technologies or the INVEST Act This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a work opportunity tax credit for hiring veterans in the field of renewable energy. The bill defines "veteran" as a certified veteran who: (1) has received a credential or certification from the Department of Defense in a field of renewable energy or with respect to advanced manufacturing, machinist or welding, or engineering; (2) has completed a vocational degree in a field of renewable energy during the one-year period ending on the hiring date; or (3) has completed a LEED certification with the United States Green Building Council.  The bill also requires the Department of the Treasury to pay to each possession of the United States with a mirror code tax system (a possession that uses the same income tax system as the United States, but without the income tax credit for the first $10,000 of income earned by residents of such possession) the amount of the loss that would have occurred if a mirror code tax system had been in effect in such possession.  The bill reduces the amount of any credit (or other tax benefit) allowed to a qualified veteran against income taxes imposed by a possession of the United States by reason

Global Nuclear Security Initiative Act of 2002 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the Secretary of Energy should develop a comprehensive program of activities to encourage all countries with nuclear materials to adhere to, or to adopt standards equivalent to, the International Atomic Energy Agency standard on The Physical Protection of Nuclear Material and Nuclear Facilities (INFCIRC/225/Rev.4), relating to the security of stockpiles of highly-enriched uranium (HEU) and plutonium (Pu). Directs that such program be developed in consultation with the Russian Federation, other Group of 8 countries, and other U.S. allies.Requires the Secretary, acting through the Administrator for Nuclear Security, to require the Office of International Materials Protection, Control, and Accounting of the Department of Energy to conduct a study to determine the feasibility and advisability of developing a program to secure radiological materials outside the United States that pose a threat to U.S. national security.Directs the Secretary to study the feasibility and advisability of various actions to reduce the risks associated with terrorist attacks on nuclear power plants outside the United States.Amends the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Materials to express the sense of Congress that the President should encourage amendment of such Convention to: (1) apply to

Student Health Insurance Portability Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Public Health Service Act, as amended by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, to apply the health insurance portability and protection provisions to coverage offered in connection with a college-sponsored health plan.

Federal Bureau of Investigation First Amendment Protection Act of 1993 - Prohibits the Federal Bureau of Investigation (Bureau) from initiating or conducting any investigation that may involve the collection of information about the exercise by a U.S. person of first amendment rights, except in accordance with this Act. 
Directs the Attorney General to issue publicly available guidelines for such investigations. 
Prohibits the Bureau from initiating such an investigation unless the Director finds in writing that:  (1) specific and articulable facts indicate that the subject has engaged in a Federal criminal offense; and (2) the investigation is warranted. 
Sets forth a special rule if the investigation is directed at an organization exercising its rights under the first amendment. 
Requires the Bureau to:  (1) seek to gather only relevant information; (2) employ the least intrusive techniques; and (3) follow procedures to minimize the acquisition, retention, or dissemination of information relating to the exercise of first amendment rights or individual privacy. 
Prohibits the Bureau from disseminating or using any record resulting from such an investigation, except that the person to whom such record relates may examine it. 
Requires the Bureau's Assistant Director to review each open investigation covered by this Act at least once every

Taxpayer Savings and Employee Notification Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) include in gross income for a taxable year the income on a nonqualified company-owned life insurance contract; (2) exclude from gross income certain benefits payable to an employee upon retirement or death; (3) require the issuer of such contracts to make information returns and reports to the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary's beneficiaries, and other specified persons; and (4) use the increase in Federal receipts resulting from the amendments made by this Act to reduce the public debt.Directs the entity purchasing a nonqualified company-owned life insurance contract to provide the employee purchaser with a written disclosure of such contract.

Local Food for Healthy Families Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to establish the Local Food for Healthy Families Program to make matching grants to certain entities to carry out projects to provide incentives to low-income families receiving supplemental nutrition assistance program (SNAP, formerly the food stamp program) benefits to purchase fruits and vegetables.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the limitation on the amount of the deduction for travel expenses of spouses, parents, and children.

Brownfields Housing and Community Renewal Development Act - Amends the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to establish a program to make grants to assist in carrying out redevelopment activities for brownfield sites and abandoned, idled, and underutilized industrial, commercial, or housing structures located in brownfield sites.

Gives grant priority to proposals that ensure that the grant will be used for two or more of the following objectives: (1) to benefit low and moderate income communities; (2) to increase affordable housing opportunities; (3) to address imminent threats or urgent community needs; and (4) to provide open spaces or parks.

Stop Iran From Smuggling Weapons to Terrorists Act This bill authorizes the Department of Defense (DOD) to provide training to Israel, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Kuwait, and Qatar that have maritime security missions and training to increase maritime security and domain awareness of foreign countries bordering the Persian Gulf, the Arabian Sea, or the Mediterranean Sea in order to deter and counter illicit smuggling and related maritime activity by Iran, including illicit Iranian weapons shipments.  The bill designates such training as the Counter Iran Maritime Initiative.  DOD shall provide notice to Congress of such training.

Business Checking Freedom Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act to authorize any depository institution to permit the owner of any interest- or dividend-paying account to make up to 24 transfers per month (or such greater number as determined by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) for any purpose to another account of the owner in the same institution. Considers such an account offered pursuant to this Act a transaction account for purposes of the Federal Reserve Act (the Act).

Amends the Federal Reserve Act to authorize: (1) a Federal reserve bank to receive at least once a quarter payment of up to $250,000 of its reserve base; and (2) any depository institution to receive up to $250,000 of any member bank's reserve base.

Revises the definition of "depository institution" to include any trust company, corporation organized under the Uniform Commercial Code or having an agreement with the Board, or any branch or agency of a foreign bank.

Authorizes pass-through reserves for member banks.

Revises the definition of "reserve base" to include the amount of any reserve held by a Federal reserve bank in excess of the amount of any reserve required to be held

Taiwan Airpower Modernization Act of 2011 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) Taiwan must be a capable, independent, and peaceful nation, and (2) the sale of F-16C/D multirole fighter aircraft to Taiwan would have significant economic benefits to the United States.

Directs the President to carry out the sale of no fewer than 66 F-16C/D multirole fighter aircraft to Taiwan.

Citizen Empowerment Act of 2015  Requires executive agency employees who are conducting an in-person or a telephonic interaction with an individual, relating to a possible or alleged violation of any federal statute or regulation that could result in the imposition of a fine, forfeiture of property, civil monetary penalty, or criminal penalty against, or the collection of an unpaid tax, fine, or penalty from, such individual or a business owned or operated by such individual, to allow such individual to make an audio recording of such interaction at the individual's expense and with the individual's equipment.  Allows federal agency employees to record such interaction if they: (1) inform the individual prior to or at the initiation of the interaction, and (2) provide the individual with a transcript or copy of such recording upon request and with the individual's reimbursement.  Requires executive agency employees, before or at an initial in-person or telephonic interview, to audit and notify the individual of such individual's rights under this Act.  Permits an individual who is permitted to represent before an executive agency an individual permitted to make an audio recording under this Act to: (1) make such recording as if the person were such individual, and (2) receive a transcript or copy of

Hunt Unrestricted on National Treasures Act or the HUNT Act - Requires each head of a federal public land management agency to make available to the public on the agency's website: (1) a report that includes a list of the location and acreage of lands more than 640 acres in size under the agency's jurisdiction on which the public is allowed to hunt, fish, or use such lands for other recreational purposes, as well as a list of the lands that the agency determines have significant potential for use for hunting, fishing, and other recreational purposes; and (2) a plan that identifies how public access and egress could reasonably be provided to the legal boundaries of such lands in a manner that minimizes the impact on wildlife habitat and water quality, specifies the actions recommended to secure such access and egress, and is consistent with the travel management plan in effect on such lands.

Requires each agency to make available on the website a list of roads or trails that provide the primary public access and egress to the legal boundaries of contiguous parcels of land equal to more than 640 acres in size under the agency's jurisdiction on which the public is allowed to hunt, fish, or to use such lands for other recreational purposes.

Amends the Land and

Domestic Violence Courts Assistance Act - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to direct the Attorney General to award grants to states for the provision of resources to establish and maintain a court system dedicated to the adjudication of domestic violence cases.

Amends the State Justice Institute Act of 1984 to direct the State Justice Institute to implement and evaluate court-based approaches to adjudicating domestic violence cases in state courts.

Senior Citizens' Freedom to Work Act - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to increase the amount of outside income which beneficiaries who have attained retirement age may earn during taxable years before 2003 without incurring a reduction in benefits. Provides for a cost-of-living adjustment in such increased amount after 2002. 
Amends title II to require the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund to pay an increase in interest rate for each fiscal year beginning after 1995 and before 2002 on obligations issued after September 30, 1995, and before October 1, 2002. 
Requires each nonexempt account within the discretionary spending category for FY 1996 through 2002 to be reduced, if necessary, by the uniform percentage necessary to offset the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund shortfall resulting from the amendments made by this Act.

Environmental Protection Encouragement Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to elect to expense the cost of certain environmental improvement property.  Defines such property as tangible, depreciable U.S. property used for:  (1) source reduction; (2) solid waste minimization; (3) waste conversion or recycling; (4) reduction of environmental hazards; (5) compliance with environmental permits, rules, and similar requirements; (6) prevention, containment, or control of unplanned releases; or (7) the manufacture, distribution, and sale of alternate fuels and blending stocks or fuel additives for reformulated fuels.

Amends the Federal criminal code to permit a person who is not prohibited from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a firearm or ammunition to transport such items (with exceptions) from any place where the person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport them to any other such place if, during the transportation: (1) a firearm is unloaded and is not directly accessible from the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle, or is in a locked container or secured by a secure gun storage or safety device, if the transportation is by motor vehicle; or (2) ammunition, a magazine, or a feeding device is not directly accessible from the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle, or is in a locked container, if the transportation is by motor vehicle. Permits such person to stay in temporary lodging overnight, stop for food, fuel, vehicle maintenance, an emergency, medical treatment, and any other activity incidental to the transport, but disallows such person from transporting: (1) with intent to commit a crime punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year that involves the use or threatened use of force against another; or (2) with knowledge, or reasonable cause to believe, that such a crime is to be committed in the course of, or arising from, the transportation. Natural Disaster Mitigation Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individual taxpayers a nonrefundable tax credit for 25% of the cost of natural disaster mitigation property expenditures for a principal residence. Limits the amount of such credit to $5,000 (half such amount in the case of a married individual filing a separate return).

Essential Oral Health Care Act of 2009 - Amends title V (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to award grants to eligible entities to purchase portable or mobile dental equipment and to pay operational costs for the provision of free dental services to underserved populations.

Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require an increase in the federal medical assistance percentage (FMAP) for dental and oral health services for individuals covered by a state Medicaid plan to ensure adequate provider participation and access for such individuals.

Requires the Administrator for Nuclear Security to: (1) conduct an inventory of, and report to the congressional defense committees on, Restricted Data at each national security laboratory; and (2) ensure that, after October 1, 2002, each lock used to secure such a vault is an electronic lock meeting specified standards.

SCHIP Improvement Act of 1999 - Amends the National School Lunch Act to authorize the Secretary of Agriculture to identify children eligible for State nutrition services and administration plans under titles XIX (Medicaid) and XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program) (SCHIP) of the Social Security Act. 
Amends the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 to direct the Secretary to establish a demonstration project in not more than 40 local agencies in not fewer than two States under which costs of nutrition services and administration shall include the costs of identification of children eligible for benefits under, and enrollment of children in, such plans. 
Amends the National School Lunch Act to direct the Secretary to make grants to States to carry out State plans to involve eligible entities in the identification of children eligible for benefits under, and enrollment of children in, such plans.  Requires the authorized uses of grant funds to include carrying out the demonstration project. 
Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to provide specified funds for FY 2000 through 2003.
Coastal Restoration Tax Credit Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for up to $2 million of expenses incurred in restoring and protecting coastal lands.

Iranian Nuclear Trade Prohibition Act of 2005 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the countries of the world should choose between trading with state sponsors of terrorism or maintaining good trade relations with the United States.

Amends the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 to direct the President to prohibit the United States, or any U.S. entity, from purchasing nuclear fuel assemblies from any person or government entity, or any entity affiliated with such person or entity, that sells nuclear fuel assemblies to Iran. Authorizes the President to waive such prohibition if: (1) the waiver is in the national security interest of the United States; and (2) the President notifies the required congressional committees at least seven days before the waiver takes effect.

Youth Opioid Use Treatment Help Act of 2017 or the YOUTH Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to states, political subdivisions, Indian tribes, professional family medicine provider organizations, professional pediatric provider organizations, professional addiction medicine provider organizations, hospitals, institutions of higher education, or other appropriate public or nonprofit institutions to establish demonstration programs to:   expand access to medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorders among adolescents and young adults;   identify and test solutions for overcoming barriers to implementation of such treatment; or   create and distribute resources on medication-assisted treatment training and implementation for providers of health care to children, adolescents, and young adults.

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out major medical facility projects in FY2010 in specified locations in California, Colorado, Kentucky, and Pennsylvania; in Atlanta, Georgia, and Huntsville, Alabama; and in various locations in Texas, including McAllen, Texas. Authorizes the Secretary to carry out specified fiscal year 2010 major medical facility leases in locations in South Carolina, Georgia, California, Alabama, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, and Texas.

Cut Taxes for the Middle Class Act of 2014 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2014: (1) the tax deduction for state and local sales taxes; (2) the above-the-line tax deduction for qualified tuition and related expenses; (3) the tax deduction for certain expenses of elementary and secondary school teachers; (4) the exclusion from gross income for determining the area median gross income for the low-income housing tax credit and for qualified residential rental project exempt facility bonds; (5) the employer tax credit for employees who are active duty members of the uniformed services; and (6) the work opportunity tax credit and the new markets tax credit through 2014.

National Security Whistleblower Protection Act of 2016 This bill amends the Freedom of Information Act to require the Office of Inspector General of the Department of Defense (DOD) to report to Congress on the suspension or revocation of access to classified information by DOD employees.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to promulgate regulations to protect the privacy of customers of telecommunications services, including broadband Internet access service and interconnected VoIP (voice over Internet protocol) service.

Requires the FCC to: (1) require a telecommunications carrier to notify a customer about the collection, use, and sharing of his or her customer proprietary information, including by specifying how and for what purposes the carrier uses and shares customer proprietary information and identifying the types of entities with which the carrier shares customer proprietary information; (2) require a telecommunications carrier to provide such notification at the point of sale, before the purchase of service, and to update the customer when the carrier makes a material change to a privacy policy; (3) require a telecommunications carrier to obtain opt-in approval from a customer to use and share his or her sensitive customer proprietary information; (4) implement strong protection for de-identified customary proprietary information, to prevent re-identifying such information; (5) prohibit a telecommunications carrier from refusing to serve a customer who doesn't consent to the use and sharing of his or her customer proprietary information for commercial purposes (commonly known as "take-it-or-leave-it offers"); and (6)

Rocky Flats Environmental Technology Site Act of 2005 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to purchase essential mineral rights at the Rocky Flats Environmental Technology Site, Colorado, at fair market value, unless: (1) the owner is unwilling to sell the right at such value; (2) the Secretary purchases the right at fair market value; and (3) the Trustees enter into a natural resources damage settlement that includes a covenant not to sue.

Authorizes the Secretary to satisfy any natural resource damage liability obligation to the Trustees by paying the fair market value of the essential mineral right owned by an unwilling seller as part of a settlement of a natural resource damage claim to the Trustees.

Declares that any claim for damage to a natural resource under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) shall be considered to be satisfied by: (1) the Secretary purchasing an essential mineral right; or (2) the Secretary paying the Trustees the fair market value of the essential mineral right owned by an unwilling seller.

Exempts a purchase of an essential mineral right under this Act from the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969.

Mortgage and Rental Disaster Relief Act of 2007 - Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to authorize the President to provide assistance, on a temporary basis, in the form of mortgage or rental payments to or on behalf of individuals and households: (1) who, as a result of financial hardship caused by a major disaster, have received written notice of dispossession or eviction from a residence because of foreclosure of any mortgage or lien, cancellation of any contract of sale, or termination of any lease entered into before the major disaster; and (2) whose adjusted gross income was not more than $75,000 (adjusted for inflation, for areas with a high cost of living). Limits such assistance to 18 months.

Requires an individual or household seeking such assistance to submit an application in the manner and accompanied by information as the President shall establish, including a requirement that such an individual or household sign a statement indicating that he or she meets the eligibility requirements of this Act. Requires an individual or household without access to records necessary to demonstrate eligibility to submit such records within six months after application.

Directs the Attorney General to establish and implement a program to identify, from among the individuals who are incarcerated in local governmental facilities prior to arraignment on criminal charges, those individuals who are within one or more of the following classes of deportable aliens:  (1) aliens unlawfully present in the United States; and (2) certain aliens and nationals of such countries as are listed in the Immigration and Naturalization Act (and in the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996). 
Directs the Attorney General to select for participation in the program each local political subdivision in which at least 10 but no more than 50 aliens are unlawfully present, and in which at least 20 percent of the political subdivisions are not contiguous to a land border, that:  (1) are requesting such selection; (2) are owned by the local government; and (3) incarcerate or process individuals prior to their arraignment on criminal charges. 
Requires the Attorney General to complete a study and report to the Congress on the logistical and technological feasibility of implementing the program in a greater number of locations through the assignment of a single Immigration and Naturalization Service employee to more than one incarceration facility and the development of a system

Veterans Education Equity Act of 2011 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to revise the formula for determining the actual net cost for tuition and fees for individuals entitled to post-9/11 educational assistance who are pursuing programs of education at institutions of higher learning.

Wireless Microphone Users Interference Protection Act of 2013 - Directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to: (1) expand the eligibility of wireless microphone users for licenses under the service regulation for amateur radio operators, and (2) establish two safe haven channels for exclusive use by such users.  Directs the FCC to authorize the owners and operators of wireless microphones to have access to the TV bands databases for the purpose of protecting wireless microphone operations from interference.

Military Spouses Residency Relief Act - Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to provide that a person who is absent from a State because the person is accompanying the person's spouse who is absent from that same State in compliance with military or naval orders shall not, solely by reason of that absence: (1) be deemed to have lost a residence or domicile in that State, without regard to whether or not the person intends to return to that State; (2) be deemed to have acquired a residence or domicile in any other State; or (3) be deemed to have become a resident in or a resident of any other State.

Provides that a spouse of a servicemember shall neither lose nor acquire a residence or domicile for purposes of taxation with respect to the person, personal property, or income of the spouse by reason of being absent or present in any tax jurisdiction of the United States solely to be with the servicemember in compliance with military orders if the residence or domicile, as the case may be, is the same for the servicemember and the spouse.

Declares that income for services performed by the spouse of a servicemember shall not be deemed to be income for services performed or from sources within a tax jurisdiction of the United States if the

Otay Mountain Wilderness Act of 1998 - Designates specified public lands in the California Desert District of the Bureau of Land Management as the Otay Mountain Wilderness. 
Declares that all the public lands not designated wilderness within the boundaries of the Southern Otay Mountain Wilderness Study Area and the Western Otay Mountain Wilderness Study Area managed by the Bureau and reported to the Congress in 1991 have been adequately studied for wilderness designation pursuant to the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 and are no longer subject to the requirements pertaining to the management of wilderness study areas in a manner that does not impair the suitability of such areas for preservation as wilderness. 
Declares that nothing in this Act may be construed to preclude Federal, State, and local agencies from conducting within the Wilderness:  (1) drug interdiction and border operations; and (2) wildland fire management operations, including prescribed burns. 
Declares that any lands within the boundaries of the Wilderness Area acquired by the United States after the date of enactment of this Act shall become part of the Wilderness Area and shall be managed in accordance with this Act and other laws applicable to such a wilderness. 
Declares that the designation of the Wilderness Area by this Act does not

Childcare Accountability and Responsibility Act of 2009 or the CARE for Kids Act of 2009 - Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to require a criminal background check for a child care staff member of a child care provider in any state that receives funds under such Act.

Requires such background check to include searches of: (1) the National Sex Offender Registry; (2) the National Crime Information Center; (3) the state criminal registry or repository in the state in which the child care staff member resides and each state where such staff member previously resided; (4) state-based abuse and neglect registries and databases; and (5) the Integrated Automated Fingerprint Identification System of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

Requires a child care provider to submit a request for such a background check to the appropriate state agency designated by the state for each child care staff member: (1) before its submission of an application for a state child care license, except that this provision shall not apply to any additional applications submitted within a five-year period after such request for a criminal background check and such submission of an application is made by the child care provider; (2) for each child care staff member before

Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to implement a structured risk-benefit assessment framework in the new drug approval process to facilitate the balanced consideration of benefits and risks and to develop and implement a consistent and systematic approach to the discussion of, regulatory decision making with respect to, and the communication of, the benefits and risks of new drugs.

Requires the Secretary to establish processes under which: (1) an entity seeking to develop patient experience data may submit to the Secretary initial research concepts for feedback from the Secretary and related data and guidance documents; (2) the Secretary may request such an entity to submit such documents, data, and summaries and analyses; and (3) patient experience data may be developed and used to enhance the structured risk-benefit assessment framework.

Defines "patient experience data" as data collected by patients, parents, caregivers, patient advocacy organizations, disease research foundations, medical researchers, and research sponsors or other parties intended to facilitate or enhance the Secretary's risk-benefit assessments.

Medicaid Fraud Recovery Act of 2008 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to: (1) authorize a county or other local government to establish a local fraud investigative unit to investigate and prosecute provider and recipient fraud under Medicaid within the jurisdiction of such local government; and (2) require a state to provide for payment, on a pass-through basis, to the local government of the federal financial participation received by the state which is attributable to expenses of such unit.

Requires a state, in the case of establishment of such a unit in a state, to provide for: (1) recognition of such unit and permit its operations; (2) data sharing with such unit; (3) payment of the local government of the federal financial participation received by the state which is attributable to expenses of such unit; and (4) payment of a bounty to the local government if funds under the Medicaid plan are recouped and an investigation by such local unit led the recoupment of funds.

Requires a state to provide to a local fraud investigative unit a statement that: (1) explains the reasons for a refusal to prosecute a case referred to it by such unit; and (2) identifies which entity is more appropriate to handle the

Transfers administrative jurisdiction over certain lands in New Mexico and Washington from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Air Force and the Secretary of the Army, respectively. Withdraws the mineral estate of such lands from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws and the geothermal leasing laws, but not the Materials Act of 1947 and the Mineral Leasing Act. Authorizes the Secretary of the Air Force (Secretary) and the Secretary of the Army (Secretary) to use, without application to the Secretary, the sand, gravel, or similar mineral material resources on such lands when required for construction needs on the Melrose Air Force Range, New Mexico, and the Yakima Training Center, Washington.

Accuracy in Medicare Physician Payment Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish and appoint an expert outside advisory panel to provide oversight to the processes relating to valuation of physicians' services.

Head Start Assessment Act of 2003 - Prohibits the Secretary of Health and Human Services from proceeding with the full-scale implementation of the Head Start National Reporting System on Child Outcomes until the Secretary certifies to Congress that: (1) congressional oversight hearings on the development and implementation of the System have been concluded; (2) public forums in different regions of the United States, and provided an opportunity for written public comments, on early childhood assessment proposals; (3) a study on early childhood assessments, focusing on improving accountability, instruction, and the delivery of services, has been submitted to Congress; and (4) without reducing the number of students served by Head Start, sufficient funds are available to develop and implement any new Head Start assessments, and deliver necessary additional technical assistance and professional development required to successfully implement them.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified postsecondary education expenses paid by the taxpayer during the taxable year.  Limits the aggregate payments during the taxable year for such expenses of each individual to $10,000 and the amount allowed for the taxable year for the taxpayer to $20,000.

Purchase Card Waste Elimination Act of 2006 - Directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidelines to assist the heads of executive agencies in improving the management of the use of the Governmentwide commercial purchase card for making micropurchases. Directs the Administrator of General Services to: (1) continue efforts to improve reporting by financial institutions that issue the Governmentwide commercial purchase card so that the General Services Administration (GSA) has the data needed to identify opportunities for achieving savings; and (2) pursue point-of-sale discounts with major vendors accepting the purchase card so that any Federal Government purchaser using the purchase card can benefit from such point-of-sale discounts. Requires the senior procurement executive for each executive agency to report to the Director periodically on agency actions taken pursuant to the guidelines.Directs the GSA Administrator, in conjunction with the Internal Revenue Service and the Financial Management Service, to develop procedures to subject purchase card payments to GSA federal contractors to the Federal Payment Levy program. Requires the Administrator to report annually to Congress on all first class and business class travel by GSA employees.

Alisa's Law of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to withhold specified graduated percentages of a state's apportionment of certain federal-aid highway funds for FY2015-FY2017 if the state has not enacted and is not enforcing a law requiring the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual who is convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence.

Foreign Investment Transparency and Security Act of 2006 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to prohibit a foreign government controlled entity from acquiring, owning, controlling, or managing any critical infrastructure of the United States through the establishment or operation of a foreign owned general business corporation if the general business corporation does not meet specified requirements, including having a board of directors, the majority of which is composed of U.S. citizens, a chief security officer who is a U.S. citizen responsible for safety and security issues related to the critical infrastructure, and records related to operations, personnel, and security of the United States general business corporation in the United States.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security, in coordination with the Secretary of the Treasury, to promulgate regulations to carry out this Act.

Directs the Secretary to report to Congress on the processes and policies for implementation of a scanning system for 100% of the inbound maritime containers.

Bond Financing Renewal Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase from $10 to $20 million the maximum amount of qualified small issue bonds that may be issued for the use by related principal users of a manufacturing facility; and (2) allow the deduction of acquisition interest expenses for financial institutions for such small issue bonds.

Freedom and Human Rights for the Enclaved People of Cyprus Act - Directs the President to: (1) inform the United Nations, foreign governments, and U.S. government agencies of the restrictions on the enclaved people of Cyprus; (2) enlist the United Nations and foreign governments in efforts to end restrictions; (3) establish U.S. government programs of assistance to the enclaved people of Cyprus; (4) use funds allocated for a fiscal year to the government or ethnic community participating directly or indirectly in imposition of restrictions to assist such people; and (5) establish a foreign assistance program for the enclaved people of Cyprus in the absence of such funds. Directs the President to: (1) notify in writing each fiscal year the head of the government of any foreign country that is participating in the restrictions on freedom and human rights of the enclaved people of Cyprus of the opposition by the United States to that government's participation in such restrictions; and (2) urge the head of such government to cease participation and work to eliminate such restrictions.  Directs the Secretary of State to include a report on the enclaved people of Cyprus as part of the annual Department of State's Country Reports on Human Rights Practices.  Directs the

Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to revise provisions regarding the revision of joint budget resolutions by the two Houses of Congress and the President. 
Makes it out of order in both Houses to consider any joint budget resolution or amendment thereto or conference report thereon.  Makes such a resolution or amendment or conference report inadmissible in both Houses as a budget resolution or conference report on a budget resolution. 
Makes the joint budget resolution considered as enforceable upon enactment or 15 days following presentment to the President, whichever occurs earlier.

Meat Promotion Act of 2005 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a voluntary program of country of origin labeling for covered meat products (ground beef, ground pork, ground lamb, and fresh muscle cuts of beef, pork, and lamb).

Prohibits a participant from labeling a covered meat product as having the United States as the country of origin unless the covered meat product is derived exclusively from: (1) an animal born, raised, and slaughtered in the United States; or (2) an animal born and raised in Alaska or Hawaii transported for a period not to exceed 60 days outside of those States and slaughtered in the United States.

Authorizes the Secretary to assess civil penalties for participants that knowingly violate program terms.

Agricultural Credit Act of 2001 - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to revise the definition of "debt forgiveness" with respect to farm and ranch loans to include: (1) consolidation, rescheduling, rereamortization, or deferral of a loan; (2) a write-down during the lifetime of the borrower due to a financial problem relating to a natural disaster or a medical condition of the borrower or an immediate family member; or (3) any write-down provided as part of a resolution of a discrimination complaint against the Secretary of Agriculture.Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to make socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers eligible for specified types of farm loans.Directs the Secretary to allow operating loans and guaranteed operating loans to be made or guaranteed to borrowers who are operating in an area which has been affected by a natural disaster or a major disaster or emergency designated by the President under the Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act or has suffered from an economic emergency.Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to revise the percentage of recapture for certain shared appreciation arrangements.

PTSD/TBI Guaranteed Review For Heroes Act - Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish within the Office of the Secretary of Defense a special review board to review the discharge or dismissal (other than a discharge or dismissal by sentence of a general court-martial) of a former member of the Armed Forces who was deployed in support of a contingency operation and who was discharged or dismissed under a general or other than honorable condition, and who has been diagnosed by a health care professional with post-traumatic stress disorder or a traumatic brain injury. Authorizes the special review board, upon request, to review such discharge or dismissal. Allows the special review board to change the discharge or dismissal of such an individual to honorable if the individual's request is denied or the board does not change the discharge or dismissal. Directs the Secretary concerned to correct the military records of such an individual in accordance with a change made by the special review board.

Requires a physician, clinical psychologist, psychiatrist, or other appropriate health care professional who determines that a member who was deployed in support of a contingency operation has (or may have) post-traumatic stress disorder or a traumatic brain injury to refer the member for evaluation by a physical evaluation board. Prohibits the separation of such a member from the Armed Forces until the

Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit a person from holding a gun show unless:  (1) the person is licensed; and (2) at least 30 days have elapsed since the person, using a prescribed form, has notified the Secretary of the Treasury and the chief law enforcement officer of the postal address and the dates and times at which the gun show is to be held. 
Requires a person desiring to be licensed to submit to the Secretary an application which:  (1) contains a certification by the applicant that the applicant meets certain requirements, including that any gun show to be conducted under the license is not prohibited by State or local law and will be conducted in accordance with State and local law; (2) contains a photograph and fingerprints of the applicant; and (3) is in such form as the Secretary shall by regulation prescribe. 
Directs the Secretary to issue to the applicant a license which, upon approval and payment of an established fee, entitles the licensee to hold gun shows in interstate or foreign commerce during the three-year period that begins with the date the license is issued. 
Requires the Secretary to approve or deny an application submitted within 60 days after the Secretary receives the application.  Permits an applicant to bring an action

Obamacare Marriage Penalty Elimination Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the marriage penalty in the health insurance premium tax credit.  The bill also amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to eliminate the 400% limitation on the credit eligibility percentage for individuals with joint tax returns.

Canyon Mountain Land Conveyance Act of 2013 - Declares that all U.S. rights, title, and interest to approximately 17,826 acres of federal land, including improvements, appurtenances, and minerals, shall be held in trust by the United States for the benefit of the Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Indian Tribe and shall be part of the Tribe's reservation.  Directs the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) complete a survey of the boundary lines to establish the boundaries of the land taken into trust, and (2) file a map and legal description of the federal land with the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the House Committee on Natural Resources.  Prohibits the use of the federal land for any gaming activity.  Requires any commercial forestry activity that is carried out on the federal land to be managed in accordance with all applicable federal laws.  Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) and the Secretary to identify: (1) any land owned by the Oregon and California Railroad that is conveyed under this Act, and (2) public domain land that is approximately equal in acreage and condition and located in the planning area. Election Jamming Prevention Act of 2006 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the use of any means, including any device, to prevent or obstruct the broadcast or exchange of election-related information. Defines "election-related information" to include information related to: (1) the endorsement, support, promotion of, or opposition to any clearly identified candidate or slate of candidates for the office of President, Vice President, presidential elector, Member of the Senate, Member of the House of Representatives, Delegate or Commissioner from a territory or possession; (2) the time, place, or manner for the election of such offices; or (3) the facilitation of transport to or from polling places for any such election.

Grants any person aggrieved by a violation of such prohibition the right to bring a civil action for injunctive or declarative relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, including an application in a U.S. district court.

Healthy Maternity and Obstetric Medicine Act or the Healthy MOM Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require a group health plan to provide a special enrollment period for pregnant women, beginning on the date on which the pregnancy is reported to the health insurance issuer. The bill amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require a state health insurance exchange to provide a special enrollment period for pregnant women, beginning on the date on which the pregnancy is reported to the exchange. The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to require a group health plan to permit an employee who is eligible, but not enrolled, for coverage under the plan to enroll for coverage under the plan upon pregnancy, with the special enrollment period beginning on the date on which the pregnancy is reported to the group health plan. The Office of Personnel Management must issue regulations to ensure that pregnancy is considered a change in family status and a qualifying life event for an individual who is eligible to enroll, but is not enrolled, in a federal employee health benefit plan.

Continuity of Congress Act of 2003 - Authorizes a State legislature to fill vacancies in the House of Representatives or the Senate following a catastrophic incident by filling the vacancies with laws providing for: (1) special elections; (2) appointments by the governor or legislature of the State; and (3) appointments pursuant to a list of successors created by the incumbent member of the house of Representatives. Allows a member that has been incapacitated to reclaim his or her office at any time after such member determines that he or she is no longer incapacitated. Requires the executive authority of the relevant State to issue writs of election, which shall be held within 120 days after any such vacancy occurs. Deems a general election occurring within such 120 day period to satisfy this Act's requirements. Provides for determining that one-fourth of the members of the House of Representatives or the Senate have been killed or incapacitated if: (1) the Speaker of the House (or that person's designee) or the Majority Leader of the Senate makes a joint declaration with the leader of the minority party in the House (or that person's designee) or the Minority Leader of the Senate (or that person's designee) that one-fourth of

Earmark Reform and Federal Spending Transparency and Accountability Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit earmark beneficiary contributions aggregating more than $5,000 to any requesting candidate during the period beginning on January 1 of an odd-numbered year and ending on December 31 of the next even-numbered year.

Prohibits an employee of the personal staff of a Member of Congress from attending a political fund raiser held on behalf of the Member of Congress for whom they are employed, except that a Member of Congress may designate one employee to be exempt from such prohibition.

Requires the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House to post on their respective websites a link to the earmark database maintained by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).

Requires the head of each federal department and agency to post on their website a link to a searchable database that lists each expenditure made by the agency with respect to such expenditure.

Supporting Emergency Responders Volunteer Efforts Act of 2009 or the SERVE Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer who is a bona fide volunteer member of a qualified volunteer emergency response organization a refundable tax credit for $1,000. Defines "bona fide volunteer member" as an individual who receives, for a taxable year, compensation in the form of: (1) reasonable expenses reimbursement or a reasonable allowance; or (2) reasonable benefits (including length of service awards), and nominal fees for such services, paid by eligible employers in connection with the performance of such services by volunteers. Limits the amount of such compensation to the annual limitation, which is the product of the federal minimum wage and 2,080 hours. Requires such individual to have served as a volunteer for more than 6 months and to provide more than 40 hours of such service.

Fuel-Efficient Fleets Act of 2006 - Requires each passenger automobile purchased, or leased for at least 60 consecutive days, by an executive agency after the enactment of this Act to achieve a minimum fuel economy as specified for each vehicle type. Provides for a phase-in period for such vehicles.

Directs the Secretary of Energy to evaluate the fuel economy standards based on relevant technological advances during the previous year. Authorizes the Secretary to increase fuel economy standards if it determines that significant technological improvements make it feasible to achieve higher fuel economy.

Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to award grants to assist states to purchase vans, trucks, sport utility vehicles, minivans, or passenger automobiles that meet the fuel economy requirements for new federal fleet vehicles. Requires such grants to be used to purchase such vehicles.

Requires an executive agency that purchases or leases passenger automobiles to give a preference, when purchasing models, to automobiles that are assembled in the United States from components, of which not less than 50% were manufactured in the United States.

Taxation of Minor Children Simplifcation Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for the tax imposed on unearned income of minor children to be the sum of: (1) a tax computed at the rates and in the same manner as if such unearned income had not been taxed as if parent's income; and (2) the excess (if any) of the tax on total taxable income over the tax on taxable income reduced by net unearned income.

Expands the parental election to allow a parent to claim the income of a child on the parent's return.

Strengthening Child Welfare Response to Trafficking Act of 2014 - Amends the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to identify and assess reports involving children who are sex trafficking victims. Requires the Secretary to identify and assess reports involving children who are victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons. Requires the Secretary to: (1) identify and assess reports involving children who are sex trafficking victims, and (2) identify and assess reports involving children who are victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons. Requires the Secretary to identify and assess the needs of children who are sex trafficking victims and the needs of children who are victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons.
