Health Care COBRA Offset Tax Savings Act of 2005 or the Health Care COSTS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individuals who are eligible for COBRA continuation coverage under a group health plan and whose modified adjusted gross income does not exceed certain limits a refundable tax credit for 50 percent of the amount of the premium that would be required to be paid by such individual for COBRA continuation coverage.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to provide alternative COBRA continuation coverage notice to individuals who become entitled to elect COBRA continuation coverage after enactment of this Act.

Enhanced Emergency and Enforcement Authority Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 to require the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to issue emergency orders to prohibit securities activities or compliance with securities laws by: (1) investors, issuers, brokers or dealers, transfer agents, investment advisers, or other market participants; and (2) investors, issuers, brokers or dealers, transfer agents, investment advisers, or other market participants, if they fail to comply with securities laws in a timely, orderly, or efficient manner.

Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to authorize the use of subpoena in certain actions instituted by the SEC in a U.S. district court for any judicial district.
Safe Medications for the Elderly Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of certain pharmaceutical care services furnished by a pharmacist.

This bill designates the Department of Veterans Affairs health care system in Lexington, Kentucky, as the "Lexington VA Health Care System."  The Troy Bowling Campus of the Department of Veterans Affairs is designated as the "Troy Bowling Campus." The Franklin R. Sousley Campus of the Department of Veterans Affairs is designated as the "Franklin R. Sousley Campus."

Elgin Stafford Mental Illness Information Disclosure Act of 2012 or Elgin's Law - Requires a health care professional to disclose to a parent (if any) of an individual who is being treated for mental illness, as may be useful for the appropriate involvement of the parent with respect to the treatment, but exempts in exceptional circumstances where the involvement of the parent would be counter-productive to the treatment.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to post information on the requirements of this Act on HHS websites to inform the public and health care professionals.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of the cost of installing qualified hydrogen-powered vehicle refueling property. Terminates such credit after 2013.

Excludes from gross income for income tax purposes income attributable to the sale of hydrogen fuel sold at retail for use in a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle. Terminates such exclusion after 2013.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2013 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require each energy manager, as part of the certification system, to provide reasons for not implementing any life cycle cost-effective measures for federal agencies to implement energy-saving or conservation measures identified in the agency's energy management program. Requires each federal agency: (1) to use the benchmarking systems selected or developed for the agency to track energy savings realized by the agency through the implementation of such measures, and (2) to submit information regarding such savings to the Department of Energy (DOE) for publication on a public website. Requires each federal agency to consider using energy savings performance contracts or utility energy service contracts to implement such measures. Sets the goal of the federal government, in the implementation of such measures, to enter into energy savings performance contracts or utility energy service contracts equal to $1 billion in each year during the five-year period beginning on January 1, 2014.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2015 This bill requires a state to enact and enforce a law that requires the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence. The bill also provides for a phased-in reduction in the period of noncompliance with such requirements.

Small Business Expansion and Job Creation Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) extend through 2010 the increased limitation on the expensing of certain depreciable business assets; (2) extend through 2010 the current year tax allowance for business property and other property used in a trade or business; and (3) allow a special tax deduction for business-related property placed in service in 2010.

Home-Assembled Firearms Restriction Act of 2015 This bill prohibits the sale of, and advertising for the sale of, a firearm receiver casting or receiver blank that: (1) at the point of sale does not meet the definition of a firearm in the federal criminal code, and (2) can be completed by a consumer after purchase to the point at which it functions as a firearm frame or receiver for a semiautomatic assault weapon or machine gun.  It also prohibits the sale of an assault weapon parts kit or a machinegun parts kit. The Consumer Product Safety Commission shall consult with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives regarding enforcement strategies. A violation of this bill shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Academic, Social, and Emotional Learning Act of 2011 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to require the Secretary of Education to make specified funds available for training and recruiting teachers and principals.

Requires such funds to be used to train teachers and principals in practices that have demonstrated effectiveness in improving student achievement, attainment, and behavior through addressing the social and emotional development needs of students, such as through social and emotional learning programming.

Defines "social and emotional learning" as the process through which children and adults acquire the knowledge, attitudes, and skills associated with the core areas of social and emotional competency, including: (1) self-awareness and self-management to achieve school and life success; (2) social awareness and interpersonal skills to establish and maintain positive relationships; and (3) decisionmaking skills and responsible behaviors in personal, academic, and community contexts.

Amends Federal law to extend the probationary period for Federal employees, with respect to positions: (1) requiring formal training, to two years beginning on the date that such training is completed; (2) requiring a license, to two years beginning on the date that such license is granted; and (3) not covered by the above requirements, to at least two years. Limits the length of a probationary period for a preference-eligible employee to the length of time that the President may establish, consistent with the purposes of this Act.

Directs the head of each agency to ensure that: (1) any announcement of a vacant position within such agency and any offer of appointment made to any individual clearly states the terms and conditions of the probationary period applicable to such position; (2) any individual who is required to complete a probationary period receives timely notice of the performance and other requirements which must be met in order to successfully complete the probationary period; and (3) certification to that effect is made, supported by a brief statement of the basis for that certification, in such form and manner as the President may by regulation prescribe.

Extends the probationary period for positions within the Senior Executive Service to two years.

Allows an employee to appeal from an adverse action

Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the concurrent resolution on the budget for FY2006 or for any ensuing fiscal year to be consistent with the spending limitation specified in the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985, as amended by the Social Security Personal Savings Guarantee and Prosperity Act of 2004.

Makes it out of order in the House of Representatives or in the Senate to consider any concurrent budget resolution for FY2006 or for any fiscal year thereafter, or any amendment thereto or conference report thereon, that is not consistent with such spending limitation. Permits a waiver or suspension of such point of order in the House of Representatives or the Senate only by an affirmative vote of two-thirds of the Members, duly chosen and sworn. Requires an appeal of the ruling of the chair in the Senate to be limited to one hour, to be equally divided between, and controlled by, the mover and the manager of the concurrent resolution.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the rate of the old-age, survivors, and disability income tax (OASDI) to be reduced by a specified percentage in any year following a year in which the OASDI rate ratio exceeds 125%.

Great Lakes Navigation System Sustainability Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to manage and allocate funding for all of the individually authorized commercial and recreational navigation projects in the Great Lakes Navigation System (Great Lakes) as components of a single, comprehensive system, recognizing the interdependence of the projects. Directs the Secretary to establish a program to fund eligible operations and maintenance projects of the Great Lakes Navigation System with the objective of maintaining such projects to their authorized depths and widths. Requires the Secretary to consult with congressional delegations from states that border the Great Lakes in developing annual priorities for the apportionment of funding. Authorizes appropriations from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund for FY2014-FY2023 for such operations and maintenance. Requires the Secretary to give a higher priority to projects that: (1) are not subject to the harbor maintenance fee, (2) have not had commercial cargo loaded or unloaded from their harbor during the previous two fiscal years, and (3) have a non-federal sponsor that provides a 50% cost share.

Sweetgrass Hills Protection Act of 1995 - Establishes the Sweetgrass Hills Natural Area within the Bureau of Land Management's Sweetgrass Hills Area of Critical Environmental Concern in north central Montana to protect the exceptional scenic, wildlife, water quality, and cultural characteristics of lands along the Sweetgrass Hills. 
Directs the Secretary of the Interior to acquire lands or interests within the boundaries of the natural area that are necessary to carry out this Act by donation, purchase with donation or appropriated funds, or exchange.  Prohibits the State of Montana or any political subdivision from acquiring lands within the natural area by donation or exchange. 
Prohibits:  (1) lands within the natural area from being open to location of mining claims under Federal law; (2) the Secretary from issuing any lease under Federal or State law for lands within the natural area; and (3) lands within the natural area from being available for disposal of mineral materials under the Materials Act of 1947. 
Prohibits the issuance of patents for any location or claim made in the natural area under Federal law.  Grants jurisdiction to the U.S. Claims Court to render judgement on any claim against the United States for property rights in the natural area.

Hiring Heroes Tax Incentive Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a business-related tax credit of 15% of wages paid to a qualified employee who is either a member of the Ready Reserve or the National Guard and who is separated from the Armed Forces. Allows such credit for up to $10,000 of a person's wages per year. Terminates such credit after 2013.

Prohibits the President from providing economic assistance, military assistance, or arms transfers to:  (1) the Government of Sudan unless the President certifies to the Congress that such Government has taken appropriate action to eliminate chattel slavery in Sudan; or (2) the government of any foreign country that participates, or is otherwise involved, in the establishment or conduct of slavery originating from Sudan, directly or indirectly. 
Directs the Secretary of State to designate an individual who is assigned to the diplomatic mission in Khartoum, Sudan, to be responsible for monitoring slavery in Sudan. 
Requires the President to:  (1) instruct the U.S. representative to each international financial institution to which the United States is a member to use the U.S. vote to oppose any assistance from that financial institution to Sudan until the Government of Sudan has taken the actions described in this Act to eliminate chattel slavery in Sudan; and (2) instruct the U.S. permanent representative to the United Nations to actively pursue the passage of any resolution by the United Nations Security Council that enhances the cooperation of other countries in the application of the spirit and intent of this Act.

Medicare Established Provider Act of 2015 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to develop and implement a system to designate providers of services and suppliers who represent a low risk for submitting fraudulent claims for payment under Medicare as established providers for purposes of applying specified protections. Under such system: (1) providers and suppliers shall demonstrate that at least 90% of their claims for payment for items and services furnished for which any review was conducted under Medicare were determined to be eligible for payment or partial payment, and at least 90% of such claims were appealed; and (2) the system shall provide for identification of established providers within appropriate systems of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and for a global track record of compliance by providers and suppliers.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to strike and sell bronze duplicates.
Authorizes appropriations.

E-Mail User Protection Act - Prohibits persons from transmitting unsolicited bulk electronic mail messages to: (1) an interactive computer service with knowledge that the message falsifies an Internet domain, header information, date or time stamp, originating e-mail address or other identifier; or (2) an individual who has specifically communicated to the violator that individual's desire not to receive such mail. Provides civil and criminal penalties for violations of this Act. Grants the Federal Trade Commission enforcement powers under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Furthering Accountability and Individual Rights within the Military Act of 2014 or the Fair Military Act - Directs the Secretary of the military department concerned to ensure that: (1) the written performance appraisals of each member of the Armed Forces include an assessment of the member's support for the sexual assault prevention and response program of the Armed Force concerned; and (2) the performance appraisals of each commanding officer indicate the extent to which the commanding officer has or has not established a command climate in which allegations of sexual assault are properly managed and evaluated, and a victim can report criminal activity, including sexual assault, without fear of retaliation. Modifies the Military Rules of Evidence to state that the general military character of an accused is not admissible for the purpose of showing the probability of innocence. Directs the Secretary concerned to ensure that provisions of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2014 relating to the military justice system and this Act relating to sexual assault prevention and response apply to the U.S. Military Academy, the Naval Academy, the Air Force Academy, and the Coast Guard Academy in the same manner and to the same extent as such provisions apply to an Armed Force. Amends Federal law to require States to extend the same parking privileges to qualified motor vehicles from other States as it grants to qualified motor vehicles designated under State or local law for transporting an individual with a disability that limits or impairs the ability of the individual to walk. 
Directs the Secretary of Transportation to withhold five percent of the amount required to be apportioned to any State in the first fiscal year succeeding FY 1995 in which the State is not in compliance with this Act.  Requires ten percent of such amount to be withheld in the second fiscal year succeeding such year if the State remains noncompliant. 
Sets forth provisions regarding the availability of withheld funds after September 30, 1997, and the availability of subsequently apportioned funds after a State becomes compliant.

Clean Up Earmarks Act of 2010 or the CUE Act of 2010 - Directs the Comptroller General to audit randomly each fiscal year 5% of the Senate earmarks chosen at random. Requires the audit to include: (1) an adequate amount of small and large program earmarks; (2) 50% of earmarks requested by members of the Senate Committee on Appropriations and 50% requested by Senators not on that Committee; and (3) 50% of earmarks requested by Members of the House of Representatives and 50% requested by Senators not on the House Committee on Appropriations.

Amends rule XLIV (Earmark) of the Standing rules of the Senate to increase the threshold for a point of order against a request for a congressional earmark to two-thirds (67) of the Members of the Senate.

Directs the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives to improve the Web site earmarks.gov.

Expresses the sense of the Senate that: (1) the subcommittees of the Committee on Appropriations should hold hearings on earmark requests in excess of $1 million during which Members who request such earmarks should be invited

Securing the Cities Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) Director for Domestic Nuclear Detection to establish the Securing the Cities program to enhance the U.S. ability to detect and prevent terrorist attacks and other high consequence events utilizing nuclear or other radiological materials that pose a high risk to homeland security in high-risk urban areas.  The DHS Director shall: (1) assist state, local, tribal, and territorial governments in designing and implementing, or enhancing existing, architectures for coordinated and integrated detection and interdiction of nuclear or other radiological materials that are out of regulatory control; (2) support the development of a region-wide operating capability to detect and report on nuclear and other radioactive materials out of regulatory control; (3) provide resources to enhance detection, analysis, communication, and coordination to better integrate state, local, tribal, and territorial assets into federal operations; (4) facilitate alarm adjudication and provide subject matter expertise and technical assistance on concepts of operations, training, exercises, and alarm response protocols; (5) communicate with, and promote sharing of information about the presence or detection of nuclear or other radiological

Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forests Land Exchange Act of 2007 - Directs that the land exchange between Grand Creek, LLC and the United States in Colorado proceed if Grand Creek, LLC offers to convey title to the non-federal land. Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to convey to Grand Creek, LLC, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the federal land.

Requires the values of the non-federal and federal lands to be determined by the Secretary through appraisals performed in accordance with the Uniform Appraisal Standards for Federal Land Acquisitions and the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice.

Authorizes the Secretary to equalize the values of the lands by reducing the acreage of the non-federal land to be conveyed, making a cash equalization payment to Grand Creek, LLC, or a combination of an acreage reduction and a cash equalization payment.

Directs the Secretary to require Grand Creek, LLC, to: (1) pay for any necessary land surveys of the non-federal and federal land to be exchanged; and (2) enter into an agreement with the Secretary to allow public use of land owned by Grand Creek, LLC, to provide unimpeded access to St. Mary's Glacier along the

Guaranteed Health Coverage for Pre-Existing Conditions Act of 2014 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group health insurance coverage from imposing any preexisting condition exclusion. Defines "preexisting condition exclusion" as a limitation or exclusion of benefits relating to a condition based on the fact that the condition was present before the date of enrollment in the plan or coverage. Prohibits treating genetic information as a preexisting condition in the absence of a diagnosis of the condition related to such information. Prohibits applying the preexisting condition exclusion provisions of this Act to coverage offered by a health insurance issuer in the individual market in the same manner as it applies to coverage offered by a health insurance issuer in the group market. Requires a health insurance issuer that offers health insurance coverage in the group market to accept every employer and every individual in a group in a state that applies for such coverage. Allows such issuer to restrict coverage enrollment to open or special enrollment periods. Requires an issuer to establish special enrollment periods for qualifying events. Requires a health insurance issuer that offers health insurance coverage in the individual market to accept every individual in a group that applies for coverage. Allows such issuer to restrict coverage enrollment to open or special enrollment periods. Requires

Workplace Integrity Act - Amends Federal civil service law to prohibit an employee from being granted official time in connection with any matter covered by such Act. Authorizes official time to be granted: (1) to an employee representing an exclusive representative, for a purpose allowable under this Act; or (2) to an employee in a unit represented by an exclusive representative, for a purpose allowable under this Act. Prohibits granting official time under this Act to any employee, except: (1) to allow such employee to present or process a grievance on behalf of an employee in a unit represented by the exclusive representative, or to be present during a grievance proceeding involving such an employee; or (2) in connection with any consultation or meeting with management officials officially requested or approved by the agency. Requires the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to report to the President and each House of the Congress on the use of official time under this Act.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax exemption for the financing of alternative motor vehicle facilities. Defines "alternative motor vehicle facility" as an automobile development and production facility which was built before 1981 and which through financing by the net proceeds of the issue is retrofitted or reconstructed to make such facility compatible for the development and production of qualified alternative motor vehicles or of qualified alternative motor vehicles and component parts for such vehicles.

Military Families Act - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) or the Attorney General to adjust the status of an eligible alien to that of an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence if the alien: (1) applies for such adjustment; (2) is admissible to the United States as an immigrant; (3) pays a processing fee; and (4) is physically present in the United States.

Makes such benefits only available to an alien who is: (1) a parent, spouse, child, son, or daughter of a living Armed Forces member or a deceased Armed Forces member who died as a result of service-incurred injury or disease; or (2) a son or daughter of such parents who has a Filipino parent who was naturalized pursuant to the Immigration Act of 1990.

Defines "Armed Forces member" as a person who: (1) is, or was at the time of the person's death, a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted for permanent residence; (2) is serving, or has served honorably on or after October 7, 2001, as a member of the National Guard or the Selected Reserve or in an active-duty status in the military, air, or naval
Preventing a Government Shutdown Act - Provides for continuing appropriations in the absence of regular appropriations.

Senior Nutrition Act of 2002 - Amends the Agriculture and Consumer Protection Act of 1973 to revise eligibility requirements for participation in the commodity supplemental food program (CSFP) for elderly persons. Makes an elderly person eligible for CSFP if the person is at least 60 years of age and: (1) is eligible for food stamp benefits under the Food Stamp Act of 1977; or (2) has a household income that is less than or equal to 185 percent of the most recent Federal Poverty Income Guidelines published by the Department of Health and Human Services. Authorizes appropriations for CSFP through FY 2008. Prohibits use of CSFP funds to reimburse the Commodity Credit Corporation for commodities donated to the CSFP.

Mortgage Disclosure Simplification Act of 2007 - Amends the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to develop and prescribe standard written forms for statement of the essential terms of a federally related mortgage loan.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) require that such forms be used in all transactions involving federally related mortgage loans; and (2) provide the lender or mortgage broker with a completed form that sets forth certain loan terms and specified information to the borrower within three days after the application for the mortgage loan is made.

Health Insurance Rate Review Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to declare that nothing in the Act shall be construed to prohibit a state from imposing requirements on health insurance issuers with respect to rates that are in addition to the requirements of this Act and that are more protective of consumers. Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to determine whether a state insurance commissioner or relevant state regulator is adequately prepared to undertake the corrective actions required under this Act. Directs the Secretary or the relevant state insurance commissioner or regulator to ensure that any excessive, unjustified, or unfairly discriminatory rates are corrected prior to implementation, or as soon as possible thereafter, including through mechanisms such as denying rates, modifying rates, or requiring rebates to consumers.

Protecting Neighborhoods from Oil Pollution Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (commonly known as the Clean Water Act) to direct the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to issue regulations requiring an owner or operator of an oil storage or processing facility to permanently close the facility if: (1) it is located within one mile of 100 or more residential units, and two or more covered discharges occur at the facility within any 10-year period; or (2) the facility is the source of groundwater contamination affecting 100 or more residential units.

Defines "covered discharge" as a discharge of oil greater than 40 gallons from any source.

Requires the Administrator to include in such regulations: (1) a definition of "permanently close," including requirements for removal of all liquid and sludge, closing of all connecting lines and piping, and posting of closure signs; (2) any additional closure and post-closure requirements determined to be appropriate; (3) a deadline for closure; (4) any waivers or extensions of closure; and (5) a definition of "substantial threat to the public health or welfare" and an "imminent and substantial endangerment to

Veteran Employment Through Technology Education Courses Act or the VET TEC Act - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out a five-year pilot program under which the Secretary shall provide eligible veterans with the opportunity to enroll in high technology programs of education offered by an entity other than an institution of higher learning. Requires the Secretary to give preference to a provider that offers tuition reimbursement for any student who: (1) completes a program of education offered by the provider; and (2) does not find full-time meaningful employment within 180 days after the date the student completes the program.

Veterans' Burial Benefits Enhancement Act of 2003 - Amends Federal law to allow a State to claim a burial plot allowance if the State: (1) claims a burial in a national cemetery; and (2) was discharged from active military service for a disability incurred or aggravated in line of duty, or is a veteran of any war.

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to lease to lessees, and upon terms and conditions the Secretary considers appropriate, any unutilized or underutilized land or facilities of the National Cemetery Administration.

Directs the Secretary to establish a national cemetery in each geographic area identified by the Secretary in order to ensure that veterans who reside in such area reside not more than 50 miles from an open national cemetery.

Designates Route 66 as "America's Main Street" and requires the Secretary of the Interior to establish an "Office for the Preservation of America's Main Street" to: (1) support efforts of State and local public and private persons and entities in the States to preserve Route 66 by providing technical assistance, participating in cost-sharing programs, and making grants and loans; (2) act as a clearinghouse for communication among Federal, State, and local agencies and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of Route 66; and (3) assist the States in determining the appropriate form of and establishing and supporting a non-Federal entity or entities to perform the functions of the Office after the Office is terminated.

Requires the Office to: (1) sponsor a road sign program on Route 66 to be implemented on a cost-sharing basis with State and local organizations; (2) provide assistance in the preservation of Route 66 in a manner that is compatible with the idiosyncratic nature of the highway; and (3) not prepare or require preparation of an overall management plan for Route 66, but cooperate with the States and local public and private persons and entities in developing local preservation plans to guide efforts to protect the most important

Camera Accountability Maintenance and Transparency in Policing Act of 2017 or the CAM TIP Act of 2017 This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to authorize the Bureau of Justice Assistance to make grants to states, local governments, and Indian tribes for the acquisition, operation, and maintenance of body-worn cameras for law enforcement officers.  Grants may be used to implement programs requiring the use of body-worn cameras by law enforcement officers in a jurisdiction that: (1) establishes policies and procedures for when law enforcement officers should wear, activate, and deactivate body-worn cameras; (2) ensures the protection of civil liberties of members of the general public using body-worn cameras; (3) limits the use of recordings of body-worn cameras to monitor the conduct of law enforcement officers outside of their official interactions with the public; (4) develops standards for the effective placement of a body-worn camera on a law enforcement officer's body; (5) describes best practices for receiving an accurate narrative from recordings of body-worn cameras; (6) establishes policies for the collection and storage of recordings of body-worn cameras; (7) limits the availability of recordings of body-worn cameras

Improving Corporate Governance Through Diversity Act of 2017 This bill requires the head of an executive agency to require a contractor to submit to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) specified data relating to diversity, including the racial, ethnic, and gender composition of the board of directors and the C-level executives of the contractor. The agency shall report on the data submitted quarterly and annually to Congress and the Office of Minority and Women Inclusion. The SEC shall revise corporate governance regulations to require that when presented in a proxy or information statement relating to the election of directors, the qualities and skills of a director, along with the director's gender, race, ethnicity, and affiliation with a historically underrepresented group, should be presented in a chart or matrix form.

Medicaid Mammography Coverage Act of 1993 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act (SSA), as amended by the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1990, to provide for coverage of screening mammography under Medicaid. 
Provides for:  (1) medical assistance for screening mammography performed on a woman under age 35; (2) availability of medical assistance for only one screening mammography performed on a woman between ages 34 and 40; (3) in the case of a woman over age 39, but under age 50, who is at a high risk of developing breast cancer, medical assistance is not required to be made available for a screening mammography performed within 11 months of a previous screening mammography; and (4) in the case of a woman over age 49, medical assistance is not required to be made available for a screening mammography performed within 11 months of a previous screening mammography. 
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to review periodically appropriate frequency for performing screening mammography, based on age and such other factors as the Secretary believes to be pertinent. 
Provides for conformance with

Smart Water Management Conservation and Efficiency Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish and carry out a smart water management pilot program to award grants to utilities, municipalities, water districts, and other authorities that provide drinking water, wastewater treatment, or water reuse services to demonstrate and deploy novel and innovative technology-based solutions that will: (1) increase the energy and water efficiency of drinking water, wastewater treatment, and water reuse systems; (2) improve drinking water, water reuse, and wastewater treatment systems to help communities make significant progress in conserving water, saving energy, and reducing costs; and (3) support the implementation of innovative processes and the installation of advanced automated systems that provide real-time data on energy and water. Directs the Secretary to annually evaluate each grant project and make best practices identified in the evaluations available to the public.

College Research Education and Teacher Excellence (CREATE) Opportunity Act of 2012 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to make permanent the tax credit for increasing research activities. Increases the percentage of contract research expenses that may be allocated to colleges and universities. Includes research in the social sciences and the arts and humanities in the definition of "qualified research" for purposes of the tax credit. Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to allow students to receive up to two Federal Pell Grants in a single award year. Defines "student" to mean a person who is enrolled: (1) on at least a half-time basis for a period of more than one academic year, or more than two semesters or an equivalent period of time, during a single award year; and (2) in a program of instruction at the junior or community college for which the college awards an associate degree or a certificate. Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to revise requirements for the repayment of Federal Direct Loans to students who receive more than one Federal Pell Grant in a single award year.

Check the Box for Homeless Veterans Act of 2013 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) establish in the Treasury the Homeless Veterans Assistance Fund to provide services to homeless veterans; and (2) allow individual taxpayers to designate on their tax returns a portion of any overpayment of tax or an additional contribution for the fund.

Stop Turning Out Prisoners Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit prospective relief in a civil action with respect to prison conditions from extending further than necessary to remove the conditions that are causing the deprivation of the Federal rights of individual plaintiffs in that action.  Prohibits the court from granting or approving any relief, in such an action, unless it finds that such relief is narrowly drawn and the least intrusive means to remedy the violation of the Federal right.  Prohibits the court from granting or approving relief to reduce or limit the prison population, unless the plaintiff proves that crowding is the primary cause of the deprivation of the Federal right and no other relief will remedy that deprivation.  Terminates prospective relief, in such an action, two years after the later of: (1) the date the court found the violation of a Federal right that was the basis for the relief; or (2) the date of the enactment of this Act.  Entitles a defendant or intervenor to immediate termination of prospective relief, if it was approved or granted in the absence of a finding by the court that prison conditions violated a Federal right.  Requires the court to promptly rule on any motion to modify or terminate prospective relief in such an action.  Requires any prospective relief subject

Marine Navigation Safety Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish in the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund a Marine Navigation Safety Account.  Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer to such Account specified tax revenues and interest revenues received in 1991 and 1992.  Makes Account amounts available for expenditures related to commercial marine navigation programs and activities of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). 
Amends the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 to provide for transfers from the Marine Navigation Safety Account to NOAA for commercial marine navigation programs and activities.
Librarian Education and Development Act of 2003 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to extend loan forgiveness for certain public elementary and secondary school teachers and librarians.

.  (Sec. 1) This bill extends through FY2014 the authority provided by the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 under the temporary agricultural assistance program.  The bill suspends, through FY2014, certain agricultural price support authorities and the authorization of supplemental agricultural disaster assistance.  The bill makes exceptions for mandatory program funding, specified conservation program funding, trade authorities, a survey of foods purchased by school food authorities, rural development authorities, market loss assistance for asparagus producers, supplemental agricultural disaster assistance, Pigford claims, and the Heartland, habitat, harvest, and horticulture Act of 2008.

Innovation Protection Act - Establishes in the Treasury the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Fund.

Requires: (1) the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to pay fees to the Director of the USPTO for the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Revolving fund; and (2) the Director to report to Congress on the operation of the USPTO, including spending, and plans for modernization.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the property subject to a liability test for purposes of the assumption of liability provisions.

Hazardous Materials Cooperative Research Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to establish a hazardous materials cooperative research program.

Requires the Secretary to establish an independent governing board to select projects and studies to be carried out under the program. Requires the board to select cooperative research studies of hazardous materials transportation that are cross-cutting in nature and that consider issues not adequately addressed by existing federal or private sector research programs. Gives priority to research studies that will yield results immediately applicable to risk analysis and mitigation or that will strengthen the ability of first responders to respond to incidents and accidents involving transportation of hazardous materials.

Directs the Secretary to make grants to, and enter a cooperative agreement with, the National Academy of Sciences to carry out projects and studies under the cooperative research program.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to deposit into three separate accounts for the Quinault Indian Nation (the Tribe) funds appropriated in satisfaction of an award granted to the Tribe before the U.S. Claims Court, less attorney fees and litigation expenses, and including all interest accrued to the date of disbursement.  Requires the Tribe to:  (1) establish a separate account for the principal amount of the judgment funds; and (2) use those funds to establish a Permanent Fisheries Fund.  Prohibits the principal amount from being expended by the Tribe.  Requires the principal amount to be invested in accordance with the Tribe's investment policy.  Requires the Tribe to establish separate accounts for all investment income earned on amounts in the Permanent Fisheries Fund and all investment income earned on the judgment funds during the period beginning on September 19, 1989, and ending on the date of distribution of the funds to the Tribe.  Requires funds deposited in the first account to be available to the Tribe to carry out fisheries enhancement projects and to pay expenses incurred in administering the Permanent Fisheries Fund.  Requires each such project to be specified in the approved annual budget of the Tribe.

Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area Study Act of 2005 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, in cooperation with the Four Corners Heritage Council, to conduct a study to assess the feasibility and suitability of designating the Four Corner region of the states of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Utah as the Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area.

Protecting Dissenting Viewpoints and Voices Act of 2017 This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from revoking any license or other authorization of, or otherwise taking action against, any person on the basis of viewpoints taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content that is broadcast or otherwise disseminated by such person or any person affiliated with such person.  The bill also prohibits the FCC from placing a condition on any approval, review, or decision with respect to viewpoints to be taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content broadcast or otherwise disseminated by the person seeking such approval, any successor of such person, or any person affiliated with such person or successor.  The bill declares that nothing in this Act shall be construed to affect the FCC's authority to take action on the basis of, or to place a condition on an approval described in such subsections with respect to:  a violation of specified provisions of the federal criminal code concerning broadcast of obscene,淫秽, or profane material, or conduct that would constitute a violation if content were disseminated by other means;  a violation of, or conduct that the FCC has the authority to require

Skilled Workforce Enhancement Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers of up to 500 employees a business tax credit for 80 percent of the training expenses of their highly skilled metalworking trades apprentices.  Limits the amount of such credit to $100,000 for each qualified trained employee.

Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act - Amends the Antitrust Criminal Penalty Enhancement and Reform Act of 2004 to prohibit any person, or any officer, employee, contractor, subcontractor, or agent of such person, from discharging, demoting, suspending, threatening, harassing, or discriminating against a whistleblower in the terms and conditions of employment because: (1) the whistleblower provided or caused to be provided to the person or the Federal Government information relating to any violation of, or any act or omission the whistleblower reasonably believes to be a violation of, the antitrust laws or any violation of another criminal law committed in conjunction with a potential violation of the antitrust laws; or (2) the whistleblower filed, testified, participated in, or otherwise assisted an investigation or proceeding filed about to be filed (with any knowledge of the employer) relating to any violation of, or any act or omission the whistleblower believed to be a violation of, the antitrust laws or another criminal law committed in conjunction with a potential violation of the antitrust laws.

Exempts a whistleblower who planned and initiated: (1) a violation or attempted violation of the antitrust laws; (2) a violation or attempted violation of another criminal law in conjunction with a

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to sell the land in tracts of not less than 40 acres.  Requires the Secretary to reserve easements for existing facilities such as roads, telephone lines, pipelines, electric power transmission lines, or other facilities or improvements in place.  Requires the Secretary to reserve such easements for roads as the Secretary of Agriculture finds necessary to assure access to lands of the United States or to meet public needs.  Requires the Secretary to be responsible for the costs and recovery of any historic or prehistoric sites located upon the lands to be conveyed.  Requires the Secretary to use a deed reservation to retain historic or prehistoric properties in the ownership of the United States instead of site recovery, if agreeable to the acquiring party. 
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the acquiring party or its successor in title all the undivided mineral interest of the United States in any parcel or tract sold pursuant to this Act.  Requires the Secretary to sell the mineral interests at the fair market value determined by the Secretary of the Interior after taking into consideration such appraisals as the Secretary deems necessary or appropriate.

Great Lakes Pipeline Safety Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to study the economic and environmental risks to the Great Lakes of oil or other hazardous liquid spills or leaks from a rupture, breakage, or other failure of onshore, underwater pipeline facilities within the Straits of Mackinac.  The study shall:   meet the content requirements of an environmental impact statement;  describe the potential impacts of such spills or leaks to human health and welfare, wildlife populations, ecosystems, shorelines, property, economic activity, and water quality in the Great Lakes and connecting waterways;  include an assessment of spill responses in a variety of likely and worst-case spill scenarios in those waters; and  include a supplemental study.  DOT shall terminate the operations of an onshore, underwater pipeline facility located in the Straits of Mackinac if the Administrator of the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration determines that such facility poses a sufficient risk of hazard to life, property, or the environment to necessitate such termination.

Grand Jury Reform Act of 1998 - Amends the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure to require the court, upon impaneling a grand jury, to instruct and charge the grand jury on its rights, responsibilities, and duties, including specified rights and duties with respect to:  (1) inquiring into criminal offenses alleged to have been committed within the jurisdiction; (2) calling and interrogating witnesses; (3) requesting production of a book, paper, document, or other object, including exculpatory evidence; (4) finding credible evidence of each material element of the crime charged before returning a true bill; (5) requesting that the attorney for the government draft indictments for charges other than those originally requested by that attorney; and (6) the obligation of secrecy. 
Requires the court, upon service of a subpoena requiring any witness to testify or produce information at any proceeding before a grand jury impaneled before a district court, to give the witness adequate and reasonable notice of specified rights and privileges, including the right to counsel, privilege against self-incrimination, subject matter of the grand jury investigation, whether the witness's own conduct is under investigation by the grand jury, the criminal statute, the violation of which is under consideration by the

Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop a plan for the purchase, storage, and rotation of a six-month supply of vaccines routinely recommended for children and adults by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. Requires the Secretary to: (1) fully implement such plan; and (2) require manufacturers of vaccines included in such supply to provide at least one year notice of a discontinuance of the manufacture of a vaccine.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to pay a specified amount of compensation to any individual who: (1) was a member of the Armed Forces, a civilian employee of the United States, or an employee of a contractor of the United States during World War II; (2) served in or with the Armed Forces during World War II; (3) was captured and held as a prisoner of war or prisoner by Japan in the course of such service; and (4) was required by the Imperial Government of Japan or one or more Japanese corporations to perform slave labor during World War II.

Classroom Safety Act of 2000 - Amends the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) to authorize school personnel to discipline (including expel or suspend), in the same manner in which such personnel may discipline a child without a disability, a child with a disability who: (1) carries or possesses a weapon to or at a school, on school premises, or to or at a school function, under the jurisdiction of a State or a local educational agency (LEA), or (2) possesses or uses illegal drugs, or sells or solicits the sale of a controlled substance while at a school, on school premises, or to or at a school function, under the jurisdiction of a State or LEA. Authorizes personnel to modify the disciplinary action on a case-by-case basis.Requires that nothing in this Act shall be construed to prevent a child with a disability who is disciplined pursuant to such authority from asserting a defense that the carrying or possession of the weapon, or the possession of an illegal drug or sale or solicitation of the sale of a controlled substance, was unintentional or innocent.Provides that a child expelled or suspended under this Act shall not be entitled to continue educational services, including a free appropriate public education, during the term of such expulsion

Duty Suspension Facilitation Act of 2010 - Requires the International Trade Commission (ITC) to submit to the Senate Committee on Finance and the House Committee on Ways and Means proposed legislation which includes recommendations regarding amendments to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTS) in connection with the temporary suspension or reduction of duty.

Directs the ITC, in formulating such recommendations and proposed legislation, to: (1) solicit and give consideration to the views of interested federal agencies and the public; and (2) provide for a public hearing.

Prohibits the ITC from recommending in the proposed legislation any suspension or reduction in duty if: (1) an interested federal agency determines such suspension or reduction is not in the interest of the United States and that determination is included in the record of the public hearing; (2) such suspension or reduction is objected to by a domestic producer who demonstrates that there is domestic production of the article for which suspension or reduction of duty is recommended in commercially available quantities; (3) the loss in revenue to the United States from such suspension or reduction of duty exceeds $500,000 annually; or (4) the suspension or reduction in duty is to be effective for a period that exceeds

National Park System New Area Studies Act - Amends the National Park System General Authorities Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior, along with the annual budget submission, to submit to specified congressional committees a list of areas recommended for study for potential inclusion in the National Park System.  Requires the Secretary to give consideration, in developing such list, to those areas that have the greatest potential to meet the established criteria of national significance, suitability, and feasibility.  Requires the Secretary to give special consideration, in developing such list, to themes, sites, and resources not already adequately represented in the National Park System. 
Prohibits the initiation of a study of the potential of an area for inclusion in the System after the date of enactment of this Act, except as provided by specific authorization of an Act of Congress. 
Provides that nothing in this Act shall:  (1) limit the authority of the National Park Service to conduct preliminary resource assessments, gather data on potential study areas, provide technical and planning assistance, prepare or process nominations for administrative designations, update previous studies, or complete reconnaissance surveys of individual areas requiring a total expenditure of less than $25,000; and (2) be construed to apply to or to affect or alter the study of any river

DHS Paid Administrative Leave Accountability Act of 2015 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the head of each Department of Homeland Security (DHS) component to report to the Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO) of DHS on the number of employees who had been on administrative leave, or any other type of paid non-duty status without charge to leave, for personnel matters for a period of six consecutive months or longer as of the last day of the period covered by the report. The CHCO shall: (1) maintain records of the number of DHS employees who are placed on administrative leave or paid non-duty status without charge to leave for personnel matters and the costs associated with such leave or non-duty status; and (2) determine any appropriate actions to be taken by DHS to resolve any personnel matter objectively, appropriately, and expeditiously or to reduce the use of administrative leave and paid non-duty status without charge to leave in addressing any personnel matter. (Sec. 3) The CHCO shall develop and implement a DHS-wide policy in accordance with existing federal guidance specifically related to the use of administrative leave, or any other type of paid non-duty status without charge to leave, for personnel

Work Made for Hire and Copyright Corrections Act of 2000 - Amends Federal copyright law to remove Federal copyright provisions concerning sound recordings and other audiovisual works.  Revises the definition of "work made for hire" to exclude any such provisions.  Prohibits the courts or the Copyright Office from giving any legal significance to or interpreting any judicial determination in determining whether a work is a work made for hire.  Makes such provisions inapplicable to judicial determinations made before enactment of this Act. 
Repeals provisions of Federal copyright law concerning:  (1) the Register of Copyrights; and (2) fees.

Tribal Colleges and Universities Faculty Loan Forgiveness Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to make forgiveness or cancellation of loans under the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) and Direct Loan (DL) programs available to individuals who teach full-time at a Tribal College or University.Requires the Secretary of Education to carry out a program of assuming or canceling obligations to repay specified percentages of FFEL and DL amounts for certain full-time faculty members at Tribal Colleges or Universities. Prohibits repayment or cancellation of more than $15,000 in aggregate of such loans for any student.Amends the Public Health Service Act to make FFEL and DL forgiveness available to nursing instructors at Tribally Controlled Colleges or Universities or institutions listed in the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994.

Taxpayers' Cancer Research Funding Act of 1996 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow every individual (other than a nonresident alien) whose adjusted income tax liability for the taxable year is $5 or more to designate that $5 be paid over to the Breast and Prostate Cancer Research Fund.  Establishes such Fund.  Requires amounts in the Fund to be used to supplement, not supplant, existing funding for breast and prostate cancer research.

Provide Access and Retain Continuity Act or the PARC Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to enter into agreements with States that submit approved agreements to provide for those States to conduct eligible activities. Allows a State to submit to the Secretary a petition to enter into an agreement for purposes of conducting eligible activities. Requires the Secretary to approve or deny such a petition within 90 days after receipt of the petition. Requires the Secretary to reimburse States for non-Federal funds expended for eligible activities. Deems a petition and the proposed agreement submitted with the petition approved if the Secretary does not approve or deny the petition within 90 days after receipt.

Safe and Secure Border Infrastructure Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to establish a grant program to construct transportation and supporting infrastructure improvements at existing and new international border crossings to facilitate the safe, secure, and efficient cross-border movement of motor vehicles, non-motor vehicles, cargo, and individuals, including pedestrians.

Makes eligible for such grants highway or bridge projects, public transportation projects, demonstration and pilot projects related to innovative cross border systems management, and passenger and freight rail transportation projects.

Directs the Secretary, in awarding such grants, to give priority to projects that: (1) improve the safety and security at facilities in the United States, including ports of entry; (2) facilitate safe, secure, and legal trade crossings to alleviate border congestion and reduce the economic effect of border wait times and delays; (3) implement innovative technologies that enhance safety, security, or efficiency at the border; (4) coordinate a system of projects that improve security and systems efficiencies at ports of entry; (5) facilitate economic development strategies with respect to safety and security; and (6) implement congestion relief and air quality management strategies to improve the environment.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a 5 percent excise tax on the gross receipts of a covered passenger cruise. Defines "covered passenger cruise" as a voyage of a commercial passenger cruise vessel that extends over one or more nights during which passengers embark or disembark in the United States. Exempts from such tax any voyage: (1) on any vessel owned or operated by the United States, a State, or any subdivision thereof; (2) which occurs exclusively on U.S. inland waterways; or (3) in which a vessel in the usual course of employment proceeds, without an intervening foreign port of call, from one port or place in the United States to the same port or place or to another port or place in the United States.

Establishes the Intermodal Infrastructure Trust Fund into which shall be appropriated such taxes. Makes amounts in such Fund available for specified transportation improvement projects.

Country-of-Origin Labeling for Fuels Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to: (1) study and report to Congress on appropriate methods and standards for requiring motor vehicle fuel suppliers and retailers to disclose country-of-origin information regarding motor vehicle fuel; and (2) prescribe related regulations.

King Holiday and Service Act of 1993 - Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a Martin Luther King, Jr. Federal Holiday Commission to assist in the first observance of the Federal legal holiday honoring Martin Luther King, Jr. 
Authorizes the Commission to make grants to eligible entities to pay for the Federal share of the cost of planning and carrying out service opportunities on the Federal legal holiday honoring Martin Luther King, Jr.  Makes eligible for such grants entities the State, community, institution of higher education, local educational agency, State educational agency, private industry council, or community-based agency. 
Sets the Federal share of the cost of such activities at 30 percent. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Hass Avocado Quality Assurance Act of 2007 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to issue regulations to ensure that all Hass avocados sold to consumers in the United States meet the minimum maturity standards (as measured by percentage of dry matter) for sale to a consumer of the state of California, as required by regulations issued pursuant to California law governing the minimum maturity standards of Hass avocados for sale to a consumer.

Makes such requirements inapplicable to Hass avocados: (1) intended for consumption by charitable institutions; (2) intended for distribution by relief agencies; (3) intended for commercial processing into products; or (4) that the Secretary determines should not be subject to such requirements.

Directs the Secretary to use inspectors that inspect avocados for compliance with the Agricultural Adjustment Act, reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, to conduct inspections under this Act.

Authorizes the Secretary to: (1) divert, export, or repack and reinspect any Hass avocados that do not meet the requirements of this Act; and (2) require any person who violates this Act to forfeit to the United States the

Help Organ Procurement Expand Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a nonrefundable tax credit for the donation of a kidney, liver, heart, pancreas, pancreas islet cells, lung, or intestine. Excludes the donation of an organ under specified circumstances, including when the donor has been killed with assistance from a physician, when the otherwise eligible individual has authorized the withdrawal or denial of life sustaining medical treatment of the donor, when the organs to be donated come from an unborn child or human fetus that was aborted, when the donor has committed suicide, or when legal consent failed to be obtained from the donor or their family prior to the organ recovery.

Unemployment Compensation, Reemployment, and Fairness Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the limitation on the amount of compensation payable to an individual in a self-employment program an individual who participates in such program with the approval of the State agency. 
Amends the Social Security Act to require the State agency charged with the administration of the State law to provide an early review of the individual's reemployment prospects not later than the last day of the fifth week for which compensation is payable in an unemployed individual's benefit year.  Requires such agency to provide reemployment review information to other State employment and training program staff, job search and placement services, counseling, testing, occupational and labor market information, assessment, and referral to employers, technical and training program staff to assist with reemployment services, and followup evaluation and assistance to individuals participating in reemployment activities.  Authorizes the agency to provide reemployment reviews and, to the extent effective, reemployment services for workers who have received notice of permanent layoff or impending layoff, or workers in occupations which are experiencing limited demand due to technological change, impact of imports, or plant closures. 
Requires the Secretary of Labor to prescribe such regulations as are necessary to carry out the

Responsible Debt Relief and Democracy Reform Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to authorize the President to cancel or reduce amounts owed to the United States by foreign countries as a result of concessional or nonconcessional loans, guarantees, or credits only if certain additional requirements are satisfied, including that the foreign country: (1) ensures freedom of the press, of association, and of justice; (2) has made progress in reducing corruption; (3) is elected through free and fair elections; (4) does not engage in a consistent pattern of gross violations of internationally recognized human rights; and (5) does not repeatedly provide support for acts of international terrorism. Authorizes the President to waive one or more of these requirements for emergency humanitarian relief, national security, or progress in meeting the requirements.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the President should urge the U.S. Executive Director at each international financial institution to which the United States is a member to use U.S. influence to urge cancellation or reduction of debt owed to such institution only if the country meets the same requirements applicable to debt cancellation or reduction to the United States.

21st Century Federal Pell Grant Plus Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to double the amount of the Federal Pell Grant for students who are eligible for such grant and who are pursuing a degree with a major in, or a certificate or program of study relating to, engineering, mathematics, science (such as physics, chemistry, or computer science), or a foreign language.

Directs the Secretary of Education to develop and update, and publish in the Federal Register, a list of: (1) engineering, mathematics, and science degrees, majors, certificates, or programs that if pursued by a student may enable the student to receive the increased Federal Pell Grant amount; and (2) foreign language degrees, majors, certificates, or programs that if pursued by a student may enable the student to receive such increased amount.

Veterans' Employment Transition Support Act of 2005 or the VETS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a business-related tax credit for hiring qualified veterans who performed services in a combat zone or a hazardous duty area. Defines "qualified veterans" as individuals who are veterans of at least 10 percent of their service in such a zone or duty area and who are honorably discharged from active duty.

United States Mariner and Vessel Protection Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Commandant of the Coast Guard to deploy a maritime safety and security team on a temporary basis, not to exceed six months, to deter, protect against, and rapidly respond to acts of piracy against vessels in international waters.

Directs the Commandant to notify the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the appropriate congressional committees no later than ten days after the deployment of such team.

Directs the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating to issue regulations establishing standards and circumstances under which an individual is authorized to use force (including lethal force) against an individual in the defense of a vessel against piracy. Provides that: (1) an owner, operator, time charterer, or master of vessel shall not be liable for damages in any action brought in federal or state court arising out of the use of force authorized by such regulations, including the use of or failure to use a firearm so authorized; (2) an individual shall not be liable for damages in any action brought in federal or state court arising out of use of force authorized by such regulations by that individual unless the individual is grossly negligent or engages in willful

Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2005, the duty on certain manufacturing equipment.

Directing Dollars to Disaster Relief Act of 2015 (Sec. 3) This bill requires the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to develop and implement an integrated plan to control and reduce administrative costs for major disasters. FEMA must: (1) implement the plan, (2) compare the costs and benefits of tracking administrative cost data for major disasters by the public assistance, individual assistance, hazard mitigation, and mission assignment programs, and (3) clarify FEMA guidance and minimum documentation requirements for a direct administrative cost claimed by a grantee or subgrantee of a public assistance grant program.  FEMA must also report on the development and implementation of the plan.

Children First Act of 2010 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of the Social Security Act to: (1) exclude child care assistance from the definition of assistance under the TANF program; (2) increase funding for child care; and (3) require the certification of procedures to ensure that child care providers comply with applicable state or local health and safety standards.

Increases the age at which a child must be required to work (from 6 to 13) in order to be eligible for TANF assistance.

Subjects to the individual and case data reporting requirements of the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 any TANF funds expended for child care, whether or not transferred to that Act, and exempts such funds from the quarterly report requirement.

Office of Biometric Identity Management Authorization Act of 2018 or the OBIM Authorization Act of 2018 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) the Office of Biometric Identity Management. The bill sets forth the duties of the Office Director, who shall:  lead DHS's biometric identity services to support anti-terrorism, counter-terrorism, border security, credentialing, national security, and public safety;  enable operational missions across DHS by receiving, matching, storing, sharing, and analyzing biometric and associated biographic and encounter data;  deliver biometric identity information and analysis capabilities to DHS, federal, state, local, and tribal agencies, foreign governments, and private sector entities;  support the law enforcement, public safety, national security, and homeland security missions of other federal, state, local, and tribal agencies;  manage the operation of DHS's primary biometric repository and identification system and manage Biometric Support Centers;  oversee the implementation of DHS-wide standards for biometric conformity;  enter into data sharing agreements with federal, state, local, and foreign agencies to support immigration, law enforcement, national security, and public safety missions;  maximize interoper

National Trails System Willing Seller Act - Amends the National Trails System Act to prohibit the Federal Government from acquiring land or interest in land outside the exterior boundaries of any federally administered area for the Oregon, Mormon Pioneer, Lewis and Clark, Iditarod, and Nez Perce National Historic Trails and the Continental Divide, North Country, Ice Age, and Potomac Heritage National Scenic Trails, except with the owner's consent. Limits the Government's authority to acquire fee title for such trails to an average of not more than one-quarter mile on either side of the Oregon and Lewis and Clark Trails.

Authorizes appropriations for the acquisition of land or interests in land for the Natchez Trace National Scenic Trail.

Prohibits prevailing rate employees of federal agencies from being paid more than the rate payable under the applicable wage schedule in accordance with federal law during the period beginning on January 1, 2014, and ending on the normal effective date of the applicable wage survey adjustment that is to take effect in FY2014. Prohibits such an adjustment also during the period beginning on the day after the end of such period and ending on September 30, 2014. Provides that such an adjustment shall be less than the rate payable under such law by more than the sum of: (1) the percentage adjustment taking effect in FY2014 under the General Schedule, and (2) the difference between the overall average percentage of the locality-based comparability payments taking effect in FY2014 and the overall average percentage of such payments which was effective in the previous fiscal year.

Prohibits other prevailing rate employees and employees covered by other specified provisions of law from being paid during the periods for which this Act applies at a rate that exceeds the rates that would be payable were this Act applicable to such employee.

Personal Exemption Fairness Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require, beginning after 2010, that the dollar amounts otherwise in effect for any taxable year be multiplied by the applicable multiplier for the taxable year which applies to the statistical area in which the taxpayer's primary place of abode during the taxable year is located.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to determine and publish a cost-of-living index for each statistical area.

Amends the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Act of 1990, as amended by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2002, to postpone, until FY2007, the closure and realignment of military installations in the United States.

Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection Advisory Board Enhancement Act This bill amends the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 to require the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to establish advisory boards to: (1) advise and consult with the CFPB in the exercise of its functions under the federal consumer financial laws with respect to eligible financial products or services, and (2) provide information on emerging practices of small businesses that offer or provide financial products or services to consumers primarily for personal, family, or household purposes. The CFPB must appoint at least 15 but no more than 20 board members who are representatives of small businesses that: (1) provide such financial products or services, and (2) serve in a rural or underserved area. The CFPB must also establish a credit union advisory council and a community bank advisory council to advise and consult with the CFPB on consumer financial products or services that impact credit unions and community banks, respectively.

Declaration of Official Language Act of 1997 - Makes English the official language of the U.S. Government. 
States that English is the preferred language of communication among U.S. citizens. 
Requires the Government to promote and support the use of English for communications among U.S. citizens.  Requires Government communications with U.S. citizens to be in English. 
States that all U.S. citizens should be encouraged to read, write, and speak English to the extent of their physical and mental abilities. 
Requires the Immigration and Naturalization Service to:  (1) enforce the established English language proficiency standard for all applicants for U.S. citizenship; and (2) conduct all naturalization ceremonies entirely in English. 
Makes exceptions to this Act for the use of a language other than English for religious purposes, training in foreign languages for international communication, or the use of non-English terms of art in government documents. 
Preempts any State or Federal law which is inconsistent with this Act. 
Makes this Act not intended to affect programs in schools designed to encourage students to learn foreign languages.
