Directs the Secretary of Defense to commence the redeployment of units and members of the Armed Forces deployed in Iraq as part of Operation Iraqi Freedom and contractors operating in Iraq and funded using amounts appropriated to the Department of Defense (DOD). Requires completion of such redeployment within 180 days after the commencement of such redeployment.

Prohibits the use of DOD funds to increase the number of members serving in Iraq beyond the number of members serving in Iraq as of January 1, 2007, unless the increase has been specifically authorized in advance by an Act of Congress.

Authorizes the Secretary to retain in Iraq members of the Armed Forces for the purpose of providing security for the U.S. Embassy and other U.S. diplomatic missions in Iraq, protecting American citizens, serving in roles consistent with customary diplomatic positions, engaging in targeted special actions limited in duration and scope to killing or capturing members of al-Qaeda and other terrorist organizations with global reach, and training and equipping members of the Iraqi Security Forces.

Directs the President to transfer to the government of Iraq all right, title, and interest held by the United States in any military facility in Iraq that was constructed, repaired, or improved using amounts appropriated to DOD and occupied by a unit of the

Child Immunization Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends title IV (Aid to Families with Dependent Children) (AFDC) of the Social Security Act to deny AFDC benefits to a State for a child under six years old unless the State has received from one or more physicians written verification that the child:  (1) has been examined every six months since the child was born in the case of a child under 19 months old, and every year thereafter; (2) has been immunized in accordance with recommendations issued by the Surgeon General of the Public Health Service; and (3) has no contraindication which exempts the child from receiving an immunization. 
Requires States to conduct appropriate education and outreach activities designed to:  (1) increase public awareness of the importance of preventive health care and immunizations for pre-school children; and (2) inform the public about the availability of preventive health care and immunization services for pre-school children, and related support services and clinic information. 
Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act to require child care providers to submit to them, at required intervals and in accordance with rules issued by the Secretary of Health and Human Services, certificates signed by a physician who
Home Energy Savings Incentives Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a nonbusiness tax credit for improvements to a principal residence using natural gas or electricity.

Federal Computer Security Act - Requires the Inspector General of each agency that operates a federal computer system that provides access to classified or personally identifiable information to report to the Comptroller General and specified congressional committees on: (1) the contents of such reports regarding the agency's use of logical access controls and multi-factor logical access controls; (2) data security management practices used by the agency; and (3) policies and procedures for ensuring that entities, including contractors, that provide services to the agency are implementing such practices.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on any impediments to agency use of effective security software and security devices.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from employment tax the wages paid by a qualified employer (other than the United States, any state, or any political subdivision thereof, or any instrumentality of such entities) to certain individuals hired in 2010 in a trade or business or in furtherance of activities related to the purpose or function constituting the basis of the employer's tax-exempt status. Defines "qualified employer" as any employer which is not a governmental entity and which is not an educational institution. Allows such employers to elect to have the exemption from employment tax for such individuals not applied. Exempts such individuals from the work opportunity tax credit. Appropriates to the Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance Trust Funds amounts equal to the reduction in revenues to the Treasury by reason of the amendments made by this Act.

Allows a business tax credit for the retention of certain newly-hired individuals in 2010.

Department of Homeland Security Data Framework Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to develop a data framework to integrate existing DHS datasets and systems for access by authorized personnel in a manner consistent with legal authorities and privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties policies and protections.  In developing the framework, DHS shall ensure that the following information is included:  all information acquired, held, or obtained by DHS that falls within the scope of the information sharing environment, including homeland security information, terrorism information, weapons of mass destruction information, and national intelligence; and  any information or intelligence relevant to priority mission needs and capability requirements of the homeland security enterprise.  DHS shall: (1) ensure that the data framework is accessible to DHS employees who have an appropriate security clearance, are assigned to perform a function that requires access to information in such framework, and are trained in applicable standards for safeguarding and using such information; (2) issue guidance for authorized DHS employees who have access to the data framework; (3) ensure that such guidance enforces a duty to share between offices and components of DHS when accessing or contributing to the framework for mission needs; (4) promulgate data standards and instruct

Veterans Health Care Budget Reform and Transparency Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, beginning with FY2011, to make new discretionary budget authority provided in an appropriations Act for the appropriations accounts of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) available for the fiscal year involved, and includes new discretionary budget authority for such appropriations accounts that first become available for the first fiscal year after such fiscal year.

Specifies the VA medical care accounts to be the subject of such new budget authority: (1) medical services; (2) medical support and compliance; and (3) medical facilities.

Directs the Comptroller General to study the adequacy and accuracy of the budget projections made by the Enrollee Health Care Projection Model, its equivalent, or other methodologies, as utilized for the purpose of estimating and projecting VA health care expenditures with respect to the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.

Native American Housing Enhancement Act of 2005 - Amends the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 to make Indian tribes that exercise self-government powers eligible for housing assistance under title V (Farm Housing) of the Housing Act of 1949.

Amends the Cranston-Gonzales National Affordable Housing Act to make Indian tribes, tribally designated housing entities, or other agencies primarily serving Indians eligible for YouthBuild grants.

Black Hills National Forest and Rocky Mountain Research Station Improvement Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to sell or exchange certain land in South Dakota, including: (1) specified parcels of land owned by the Secretary and the Secretary of the Interior; and (2) certain land owned by the Secretary of the Interior and donated to the Secretary by the President for the construction of the Black Hills National Forest. Authorizes the Secretary to accept cash equalization payments from such exchanges exceeding 25% of the total value of the land. Authorizes the Secretary to use solicitations of offers for sale or exchange of such land. Requires any funds received from such sales or as cash equalization payments to be deposited into the fund established by the Sisk Act and to be available for expenditure, on appropriation, for: (1) the acquisition from willing sellers of land and interests in land in South Dakota; and (2) the acquisition or construction of administrative improvements in connection with the Black Hills National Forest. Authorizes appropriations. Authorizes the Secretary to provide for the acquisition of property for the laboratory facility for the Rocky Mountain Research Station in Rapid City, South Dakota, from willing sellers located within the boundaries of South Dakota. Requires that such property be located within the boundaries of the State for the acquisition

Veterans Conservation Corps Authorization Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, in cooperation with the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) and the Secretary of Commerce, to establish a veterans conservation corps to: (1) provide training and employment to unemployed veterans who are not enrolled in any other federal training program; (2) assist eligible veterans in the transition from service in the Armed Forces to civilian life; and (3) assist the federal government in maintaining federal land and water.

Directs the Secretary to employ such veterans for a one-year period, with the option for an additional one-year extension, to carry out specified work projects. Authorizes the Secretary to establish a program for the short-term employment of such veterans attending institutions of higher education.

Requires each such veteran to be assigned to a work project that: (1) furthers the purposes of the corps; and (2) falls within one or more of specified categories, including transportation improvements, erosion control, landscape and recreation, habitat protection and restoration, data collection, and additional project categories identified in this Act.

Requires the Secretary, in cooperation with the VA and the Secretary of Commerce, to establish a program to provide to such veterans education or training necessary to enable them to carry out such work projects.

State Health Care Flexibility Act of 2011 - Authorizes a qualifying state to opt out of the application of any or all of specified provisions of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) with respect to health insurance coverage within such state. Defines a "qualifying state" as a state that: (1) enacts a law after enactment of this Act to opt out of any or all of such provisions, and contains a list of each such provision; (2) expresses the intent to continue to administer health coverage-related laws as in effect in the state on March 22, 2010, or that provides for implementation of related state laws enacted after such date; and (3) provides to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Secretary of the Treasury a notification that such law was enacted.

Senior$afe Act of 2015 This bill provides immunity from liability for civil or administrative actions for disclosures made by individuals who have received specified training regarding the identification and reporting of the possible exploitation of a senior citizen to a state financial regulatory agency, federal financial institutions regulatory agency, law enforcement agency, or the adult protective services agency of a state, if such individual: (1) served as a supervisor, compliance officer, or legal advisor for a covered financial institution, and (2) made such disclosure in good faith and with reasonable care. A "covered financial institution" is: (1) a state financial regulatory agency; (2) each of the federal financial institutions regulatory agencies; (3) a law enforcement agency; and (4) the adult protective services agency of a state. A covered financial institution may provide training regarding such identification and reporting to each of its officers or employees who: (1) may come into contact with a senior citizen as a regular part of their duties; or (2) may review or approve the financial documents, records, or transactions of a senior citizen in connection with providing financial services to a senior citizen.

Manufacturing Advisory Council Establishment Act of 2004 - Establishes the President's Council of Advisors on Manufacturing to advise the President on policy matters affecting the domestic manufacturing sector and to assist in the development of policies that will: (1) reduce production costs within the manufacturing sector; (2) promote the competitiveness of U.S. products in international markets; (3) encourage innovation, investment, and productivity in the manufacturing sector; and (4) ensure an adequate supply of skilled workers in the manufacturing sector.

Requires the Council to assist the Secretary of Commerce in securing private sector involvement for Department of Commerce activities.

Fair Trade in Grain Act of 1993 - Requires an end-use certificate that meets specified requirements to be included in the documentation covering the entry of any foreign grain.  Requires a consignee of imported foreign grain to submit to the Secretary of Agriculture a quarterly report that certifies:  (1) what percentage of the foreign grain covered by the end-use certificate was used by the consignee during the quarter; and (2) that the grain was used for the purpose stated in the end-use certificate. 
Requires the Secretary to prescribe such requirements as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of the Act.  Provides for:  (1) customs and civil penalties for failure to comply with the requirements of this Act; and (2) the Commissioner of Customs to prohibit the entry of foreign grain unless the importer presents an end-use certificate. 
Amends the Agricultural Trade Act of 1978 to direct the Secretary to provide agricultural commodities or cash payments, or both, to promote the export of wheat to Mexico. 
Directs the administering authority to initiate a countervailing duty and an antidumping duty investigation with respect to Canadian wheat subsidies in connection with U.S. wheat exports.

Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) and the Internal Revenue Code to permit the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) to accept from an employer a ratified collective bargaining agreement with respect to a multiemployer plan that provides for a reduction in the level of contributions made by a contributing employer and appropriate reduction in level of future benefit accruals for any participants for a period of not more than five years (or such shorter period as determined by the PBGC) provided that the PBGC determines that: (1) the employer will be unable to pay its debts when due and will be unable to continue business without a reduction in its contribution rates; (2) the aggregate withdrawal liability of the contributing employer with respect to all multiemployer pension plans exceeds $750 million, or such lower amount as determined by the PBGC; (3) there is substantial doubt as to the collectability of the withdrawal liability if the employer were to withdraw from the plan; (4) the reduced contributions are not reasonably expected to have an adverse effect on the PBGC's deficit; (5) other creditors, stakeholders, and other parties to which the contributing employer is obligated have accepted reductions that are comparable to those of the pension plan;

Amends Federal law to provide that funds made available under the Northern Mariana Islands Act of 1992 shall not be obligated until 60 days after the Secretary of the Interior certifies to specified congressional committees that the following conditions have been fulfilled:  (1) the number of aliens present in the Islands for work or residency does not exceed the 1992 average daily number of such aliens present in the Islands; (2) the Islands implement a petitioning mechanism to measure and compare the number of alien admissions with the 1992 average and provide the Immigration and Naturalization Service with necessary information to make such determination; (3) the Islands have enacted and is enforcing measures to raise revenues and expend for public purposes in addition to those revenues which would have been raised under the Act of 1992 of at least the same amount of net revenue that would otherwise have been raised in 1992; (4) the Islands is implementing a rate schedule that will phase in charges for all (except low-income) users of utilities which will recover the full operating, maintenance, and debt service cost of the power utility services and, as a minimum, the operating and maintenance costs of the water and sewer utility services; (5)

Master Teacher Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Education to conduct a demonstration project under which competitive grants shall be awarded to local educational agencies to increase teacher salaries and employee benefits for teachers who enter into contracts with the local educational agencies to serve as master teachers.

Tax Reduction and Economic Growth Act of 1995 - Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to notify the President and the Congress if, for any of specified periods, economic growth as measured by the change in real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at an annual rate is estimated to be less than 1.5 percent and the rate of national unemployment (seasonally adjusted) is estimated to be greater than 6.5 percent. 
Authorizes the President to declare temporary tax reductions to provide a quick and necessary fiscal stimulus to the economy.  Requires any such declaration to be transmitted to the Congress. 
Provides for temporary tax modifications and a surtax where economic growth requirements subsequently are satisfied. 
Declares that any reduction or increase in receipts resulting from this Act shall not be considered for any purpose under the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985.

Children's Products Safety Act of 2007 - Amends the Consumer Product Safety Act to require, as a prerequisite to the sale of a children's product (a toy or other article intended for use by a child under 60 months of age that is introduced into the interstate stream of commerce), certification by a manufacturer that the product complies with applicable consumer product safety standards or rules. Requires certification to include certification for compliance with all consumer product safety rules promulgated under the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and any other Act administered by the CPSC declaring a consumer product a banned hazardous product.

Requires: (1) any test or testing program on the basis of which a certificate is issued to be conducted by a nongovernmental independent third party qualified to perform such tests or testing programs; and (2) the CPSC to prescribe a rule for children's products as added by this Act.

Prohibits the importation of a children's product that is not accompanied by a certificate from a third-party verification entity.

Choice in Welfare Tax Credit Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a credit equal to the amount of cash contributions made to a qualifying charity which are not identified on the taxpayer's return.  Limits such credit to $100 ($200 for a joint return).  Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to certify a charity as qualified if the charity:  (1) is organized and operating under U.S. law and is required to file a return; (2) is certified by the Secretary as meeting certain requirements relating to the charitable purpose of the organization; and (3) primarily assists the poor.  Requires the Secretary to reasonably expect that the annual exempt purpose expenditures of the charity will not be less than 70 percent of the annual aggregate expenditures.  Requires the Secretary to provide copies of the qualifying charity's annual return to individuals requesting such returns.

Crop Risk Options Plan Act of 2013 - Amends the Federal Crop Insurance Act to provide producers with the option of purchasing additional crop insurance coverage based on: (1) an individual yield and loss basis, or (2) an area yield and loss basis, with an optional combination of both.  Limits additional coverage to a part of the deductible under the individual policy.  Requires the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation (FCIC) to offer producers the opportunity to purchase insurance in combination with a policy or plan of insurance offered under the Act that would allow indemnities to be paid to a producer equal to a part of the deductible under such policy or plan. Requires such coverage to be triggered if losses in the area exceed 10% of normal levels.  Requires the FCIC to use data collected by the Risk Management Agency or the National Agricultural Statistics Service, or both, to determine actual production history.

Flat Alternative Individual Return Tax Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual to elect a new tax rate of 20 percent on the excess of the individual's gross income over certain standard deductions.  Requires a three-fifths (60) vote in the House of Representatives or the Senate to waive or suspend this limitation.

National Whale Conservation Fund Act of 1998 - Amends the National Fish and Wildlife Establishment Act to authorize the Foundation to establish a national whale conservation endowment fund. 
Authorizes the Foundation to:  (1) accept, receive, solicit, hold, administer, and use any gift, devise, or bequest made to the Foundation for the express purpose of supporting whale conservation; and (2) deposit in the endowment fund any funds made available to the Foundation. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to transfer to the Foundation any amount (or portion thereof) received as a civil penalty or settlement or award for damages in a legal proceeding relating to damage of natural resources. 
Directs the Directors of the Board to ensure that any amounts transferred to the Foundation for the endowment fund are deposited in that fund in accordance with this Act. 
States that it is the intent of Congress that in making expenditures from the endowment fund to carry out activities specified in that paragraph, the Foundation should give priority to funding projects that address the conservation of populations of whales that the Foundation determines:  (1) are the most endangered; or (2) most warrant, and are most likely to benefit from, research managment, or educational activities that may be funded with amounts

Justice for Public Safety Officers Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to: (1) make it a crime to kill or attempt to kill a federally protected safety officer while that officer is engaged in official duties, or on account of the performance of official duties, or kills a former federally protected safety officer on account of the past performance of official duties as such (murder or manslaughter); and (2) make it a crime to move or travel in interstate or foreign commerce with intent to avoid prosecution, or custody or confinement after conviction, under the laws of the place from which he flees or for a crime punishable by a fine and/or imprisonment for any term of years not less than 10 years (attempted murder or conspiracy to murder).

Secure Fence Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to take actions to achieve and maintain operational control over the entire international land and maritime borders of the United States.

Directs the Secretary to provide for least two layers of reinforced fencing, the installation of additional physical barriers, roads, lighting, cameras, and sensors extending from 10 miles west of the Tecate, California, port of entry to 10 miles east of the Tecate, California, port of entry, extending from 10 miles west of the Calexico, California, port of entry to 5 miles east of the Douglas, Arizona, port of entry, extending from 5 miles west of the Columbus, New Mexico, port of entry to 10 miles east of El Paso, Texas, extending from 5 miles northwest of the Del Rio, Texas, port of entry to 5 miles southeast of the Eagle Pass, Texas, port of entry, and extending 15 miles northwest of the Laredo, Texas, port of entry to the Brownsville, Texas, port of entry.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) conduct a study on the feasibility of a state of-the-art infrastructure security system along the northern international land and maritime border

Directs the Under Secretary for Science and Technology in the Department of Homeland Security to provide for the conduct of an independent study of the effects on human health caused by the use of backscatter x-ray machines at airline checkpoints operated by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). Requires the study to be: (1) initiated no later than 90 days after the enactment of this Act; (2) conducted by an independent laboratory selected by the Under Secretary, in consultation with the National Science Foundation, from laboratories with expertise in the conduct of similar studies; and (3) to the maximum extent practicable, consistent with standard evaluations of radiological medical equipment. Requires the laboratory, in conducting the study, to: (1) use calibration testing equipment developed by the laboratory for purposes of study; and (2) use commercially available calibration testing equipment as a control. Directs the Under Secretary to provide for an independent panel, in consultation with the National Science Foundation, with expertise in conducting similar evaluations, to evaluate the data collected under the study to assess the health risks posed by backscatter x-ray machines to individuals and groups of people screened or affected by such machines. Requires the panel to: (1) conduct a literature review of relevant clinical and academic literature; and (2) consider

Federal Railroad Safety Authorization Act of 1994 - Amends Federal transportation law to authorize appropriations for Federal Railroad Safety Administration (FRSA) hours of service pilot projects. 
Authorizes a railroad or railroads and all labor organizations representing any class or craft of directly affected covered service employees to jointly petition the Secretary of Transportation for approval of a waiver of compliance with the hours of service requirements of this Act to enable the establishment of one or more pilot projects to demonstrate the possible benefits of implementing alternatives to the strict application of such requirements to such class or craft of employees, including requirements concerning maximum on-duty and minimum off-duty periods.  Authorizes the Secretary to waive in whole or in part compliance with this Act for a period of no more than two years, if the Secretary determines that such waiver is in the public interest and is consistent with railroad safety.  Authorizes extension of such waiver for additional periods of up to two years, after notice and opportunity for comment.  Requires publication of an explanation of any waiver granted in the Federal Register. 
Directs the Secretary to report to the Congress on the effectiveness of all pilot projects established pursuant to such a waiver, the status of all other waivers granted, and recommendations for appropriate legislative changes. 
Directs the Secretary to report bi

Emergency Unemployment Compensation Amendments of 1993 - Amends the Emergency Unemployment Compensation Act of 1991 to extend the program of emergency unemployment compensation (EUC) and to modify the final phase-out date. 
Amends the Federal Unemployment Tax Act to extend the program of temporary disability compensation for railroad workers. 
Directs the Secretary of Labor to establish a program for encouraging the adoption and implementation by all States of a system of profiling all new claimants for regular unemployment compensation to determine which claimants may be likely to exhaust regular unemployment compensation and may need reemployment assistance services to make a successful transition to new employment. 
Directs the Secretary to provide technical assistance and advice to the States in the development of model profiling systems and the procedures for such systems.  Requires the Secretary to provide funding for such activities. 
Directs the Secretary to report to the Congress on the operation and effectiveness of the profiling systems adopted by the States, and the Secretary's recommendation for continuation of the systems and any appropriate legislation. 
Authorizes appropriations. 
Designates all direct spending amounts provided by this Act (for all fiscal years) and all appropriations authorized by this Act (for all fiscal years) as emergency requirements within the meaning of part C of the Balanced Budget

Amends the Small Business Act to prohibit the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) from collecting a guarantee fee for a loan made to a veteran or spouse of a veteran of not more than $150,000 on or after October 1 of the first fiscal year beginning after the date of enactment of this Act. Makes such requirement inapplicable to loans made during an upcoming fiscal year if the President's budget includes a cost for the veteran loan program that is above zero.

Ban Poisonous Additives Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to ban the use of bisphenol A (BPA) in: (1) food and beverage containers for children, including in unfilled baby bottles and cups; and (2) infant formula containers. Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to: (1) issue a revised safety assessment for food containers composed of BPA, and (2) determine whether there is a reasonable certainty that no harm will result from aggregate exposure to BPA through food containers or other items composed of BPA, taking into consideration potential adverse effects from low dose exposure and the effects of exposure on vulnerable populations.

Trade Promotion Authority Extension and Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Bipartisan Trade Promotion Authority Act of 2002 to extend the President's authority to submit to Congress a trade promotion bill for five years after July 1, 2011. Requires such a bill to include a report from the: (1) Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations; and (2) International Trade Commission on the economic impact of trade agreements implemented on or after July 1 of the fifth preceding calendar year.

Requires the President to submit to Congress a report on the extension of trade authorities procedures during the five-year period beginning on July 1, 2011, and each five-year period thereafter, unless the Congress adopts an extension disapproval resolution after April 1, and before July 1, of the year in which any such five-year period begins. Requires such a report to contain: (1) the report of the Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations; and (2) a review and analysis of the economic impact on the United States of all trade agreements implemented on or after July 1 of the fifth preceding calendar year.

Terminates congressional reporting requirements after a disapproval resolution is adopted. Defines "extension disapproval

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2017 This bill amends the federal bankruptcy code to provide that any unsecured claim of a governmental unit against the debtor or the estate that arises before the filing of the bankruptcy petition, or that arises after the filing of the petition but before the debtor's discharge from debt, as a result of the sale, transfer, exchange, or other disposition of any property used in the debtor's farming operation: (1) shall be treated as an unsecured claim arising before the date on which the petition is filed; (2) shall not be entitled to priority under the bankruptcy laws; (3) shall be provided for under a plan; and (4) shall be discharged in accordance with the bankruptcy laws.  A governmental unit may file a proof of claim for such a claim that arises after the date on which the petition is filed. If a debtor files a tax return after the filing of the petition and the claim relates to the tax return, the debtor shall serve notice of the claim on the governmental unit charged with the responsibility for collecting the tax. If notice of a claim has been served, the governmental unit may file a proof of claim not later than 180 days after the date on which the notice was served

Commit to Opioid Medical Prescriber Accountability and Safety for Seniors Act or the COMPASS Act This bill requires the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to identify outlier prescribers of opioids and notify them annually. The CMS must establish a threshold, based on prescriber specialty and geographic area, to identify whether a prescriber is an outlier compared to other prescribers. The CMS may exclude certain hospice service recipients, cancer patients, and prescribers subject to an investigation by the CMS or the Office of Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services from the analysis.

Desert Community Lands Act This bill requires the Department of the Interior to convey to the town of Apple Valley, California, and to the cities of Twentynine Palms and Barstow and Victorville, California, certain federal land in the San Bernardino County, California, including the reservation of a permanent easement and right of way for flood control, utility, pipeline, or telecommunications facilities located within the strips of land described in the right of way grant from the Department of the Interior to Pacific Gas and Electric Company, dated March 2, 1965, and the easement from J. Harley Long to Pacific Gas and Electric Company, dated February 4, 1957.

Alcohol Advertising Accountability Act of 1996 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report annually to the Congress on alcohol advertising, its profile, and its effects. 
Requires the Secretary to convene at least two public hearings before a panel to be established by the Secretary to review alcohol advertising in all media and promotional activities undertaken to promote the sale of alcoholic beverages. 
Requires the panel to review:  (1) alcohol advertising in all media, including broadcast and cable television, other electronic means, and print and outdoor advertising; and (2) promotional activities undertaken to promote the sale of alcoholic beverages. 
Requires the Secretary's report to include:  (1) an identification of the media used by alcohol advertising to reach children, the total expenditures for alcoholic beverage advertising in each media and in promotions, the extent to which media program audiences are under the age of 21, the types and themes of alcohol advertising in all media, the extent to which other promotional efforts used to market alcoholic beverages which appear in clothing, sporting events, contests, and concerts appeal to individuals under the age of 21, and an evaluation of the relationship between alcohol advertising practices and underage drinking, drunk driving, and related public health problems; and (2) recommendations

Mortgage Cancellation Relief Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an exclusion from gross income for up to $50,000 of the cost of repaying a qualified residential mortgage. Defines "qualified residential indebtedness" as debt incurred or assumed in connection with real property used as a principal residence and secured by such property.

Local Zoning Decisions Protection Act of 2017 This bill declares that the final rule of the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) entitled "Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing," published in the Federal Register on July 16, 2015, and any successor rule is nullified, as is the notice of HUD relating to the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Assessment Tool, published in the Federal Register on December 31, 2015, and any successor notice or rule.  No federal funds may be used to design, build, maintain, utilize, or provide access to a federal database of geospatial information on community racial disparities or disparities in access to affordable housing.  HUD shall jointly consult with state and local officials and officials of public housing agencies to develop recommendations to further the purposes and policies of the Fair Housing Act.

Honorable Stephanie Tubbs Jones College Fire Prevention Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to establish a demonstration program to award competitive grants to eligible entities for the purpose of installing fire sprinkler systems, or other fire suppression or prevention technologies, in student housing and dormitories owned or controlled by such entities.

Defines an "eligible entity" as: (1) an institution of higher education, including an institution eligible to receive assistance under part A (Institutional Aid) or B (Student Assistance) of title III of the Higher Education Act of 1965; or (2) a social fraternity or sorority exempt from taxation whose active membership consists primarily of students in attendance at an institution of higher education.

Gives priority to entities that demonstrate the greatest financial need.

Requires the Secretary to develop a plan to inform entities of the need for such grants of the fact that they may be eligible to apply for such grants.

Requires the Secretary to make available the remainder of the reserved amounts for use by other eligible entities if there are insufficient number of qualified applicants to award the reserved amounts required.

Requires grant applicants to provide (directly or through donations from public or private entities) non-federal matching funds in an amount equal to at least 50% of the cost of

Food Sharing Act of 2017 This bill amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to increase and extend through FY2018: (1) the grant program for community food projects, and (2) the grant program for gleaning projects.  In carrying out this bill, the Department of Agriculture (USDA) may: (1) provide technical assistance to an eligible entity regarding gleaning projects, processes, and development; and (2) share information concerning gleaning projects with the public, researchers, and practitioners.

Social Security COLA Limitation Act of 1994 - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to revise the formula for cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) to higher OASDI primary insurance amounts. 
Amends other Federal programs to apply the COLA formula to such program benefits. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to apply the COLA formula to limitations on benefits and contributions under qualified plans. 
Provides for the continued application of this Act through December 1998.

HOPE VI Green Building and Technical Assistance Act of 2007 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to prohibit the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development from making a housing revitalization grant to an applicant unless the applicant's revitalization plan complies with the green communities criteria checklist of the national Green Communities program.

Requires the Secretary to use at least two% of the housing revitalization grant program funds appropriated for any fiscal year to assist potential applicants and applicants in obtaining technical assistance in developing and planning revitalization programs.

State Temporary Economic Priority (STEP) Act - Authorizes a State to transfer or consolidate certain federal-aid highway, education, and job training program funds after the United States experiences economic growth at an annual rate of less than 1% for two calendar quarters and continuing until 18 months after the U.S. experiences economic growth at an annual rate of 1% or more for two calendar quarters.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2009 - Amends federal law to direct the Secretary of Transportation to withhold specified graduated percentages of a state's apportionment of certain federal-aid highway funds for FY2013-FY2015 if the state has not enacted and is not enforcing a law requiring the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual who is convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence.

Opioid Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to one or more states to carry out a one-year pilot project to develop a standardized peer review process and methodology to review and evaluate prescribing and pharmacy dispensing patterns, through a review of prescription drug monitoring programs (PDMPs) in the states receiving such grants. Requires the recipients to develop a systematic, standardized methodology to identify and investigate questionable or inappropriate prescribing and dispensing patterns of substances on schedule II or III under the Controlled Substances Act. Requires a state receiving a grant to: (1) make the information with respect to controlled substances from the PDMP available to state regulators and licensing boards, and (2) with respect to any other controlled substances, make the information available to state regulators and licensing boards. Allows a quality improvement organization with which the Secretary has entered into a contract under part B of title XI of the Social Security Act to serve as the subgrantee to develop peer review processes.  Directs the Secretary to award: (1) five-year grants to eligible entities to facilitate training in order to increase the capacity of health care providers to conduct patient screening, brief interventions, and referral to treatment as needed

Kids 2000 Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to the Boys and Girls Clubs of America for the purpose of funding effective after-school technology programs, such as PowerUp, in order to provide: (1) constructive technology-focussed activities that are part of a comprehensive program to provide access to technology and technology training to youth during after-school hours, weekends, and school vacations; (2) supervised activities in safe environments for youth; and (3) full-time staffing with teachers, tutors, and other qualified personnel.Requires the Boys and Girls Clubs of America to make subawards to local clubs authorizing expenditures associated with providing technology programs, including the hiring of teachers and other personnel, procurement of goods and services, or such other purposes as are approved by the Attorney General.

Joe Testaverde Adult Stem Cell Research Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand, intensify, and coordinate NIH activities regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires the Director to make grants and contracts to public or nonprofit private entities to pay costs of planning, establishing, improving, and providing basic operating support for centers of excellence in conducting such research. Requires each center to conduct basic and clinical research on qualifying adult stem cells, which should include investigations into the cause, diagnosis, early detection, prevention, control, and treatment of disease.

Allows a center to expend amounts provided to carry out a program to make individuals aware of research opportunities at the center and to provide referrals for health and other services and patient care costs for research. Requires the center to demonstrate its availability and access to clinical services.

Requires the Director to provide for: (1) coordination of information among centers; (2) a program to make available for research samples of tissues and genetic materials that are of use in qualifying adult stem cell research; and (3) means through which the public can obtain information on and comment on NIH programs regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Solar Fuels Innovation Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to require the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out the Solar Fuels Basic Research Initiative to expand theoretical and fundamental knowledge of photochemistry, electrochemistry, biochemistry, and materials science useful for the practical development of experimental systems to convert solar energy to chemical energy.  DOE must: (1) leverage expertise and resources from the Basic Energy Sciences Program and Biological and Environmental Research Program within DOE's Office of Science and the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, (2) organize activities under the Initiative to include multidisciplinary teams leveraging expertise from the National Laboratories, universities, and the private sector to pursue aggressive, milestone-driven basic research goals, and (3) carry out a program to support research needed to bridge scientific barriers and discover knowledge relevant to artificial photosynthetic systems.  DOE must also carry out a program to support research needed to replicate natural photosynthetic processes by use of artificial photosynthetic components and materials.
Directs the Director of National Intelligence to make publicly available on an Internet website all captured documents, including those collected before and after enactment of this Act.

Iran Sanctions Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to expand the sanctions against Iran with respect to the development of its petroleum resources and export of refined petroleum to Iran.

Authorizes the President to waive such sanctions for a limited time if the President determines that a person has, with actual knowledge: (1) made an investment of $20 million or more (or any combination of investments of at least $5 million each, which in the aggregate equals or exceeds $20 million in any 12-month period), that directly and significantly contributed to the enhancement of Iran's ability to develop its petroleum resources; or (2) provided Iran with refined petroleum resources or engaged in an activity that could contribute to the enhancement of Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources.

Requires the President to report to Congress on refined petroleum exports to Iran.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Cultural Resource Programs at the National Park Service, to facilitate the development of guidelines and a program of technical assistance and grants that will set priorities for the preservation of the Route 66 corridor.  Requires the Secretary to designate officials of the National Park Service stationed at locations convenient to the States to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs. 
Directs the Secretary to:  (1) support efforts of State and local public and private persons, nonprofit Route 66 preservation entities, Indian tribes, State Historic Preservation Offices, and entities in the States for the preservation of the Route 66 corridor by providing technical assistance, participating in cost-sharing programs, and making grants; (2) act as a clearinghouse for communication among Federal, State, and local agencies, nonprofit Route 66 preservation entities, Indian tribes, State historic preservation offices, and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of the Route 66 corridor; and (3) assist the States in determining the appropriate form of and establishing and supporting a non-Federal entity or entities to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs after those programs are terminated. 
Authorizes the Secretary to:  (1) enter into cooperative agreements for study, planning

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited investment tax credit for the purchase of certain tangible stage 3 aircraft modification property.  Defines "stage 3 aircraft modification property" as tangible depreciable property which is:  (1) an integral part of and modification of a nonstage 3 aircraft (including the installation of different engines or the retrofit of the existing engines with sound attenuation devices); (2) certified by the Federal Aviation Administration and is made to qualify the aircraft for the stage 3 noise level requirements; and (3) the original use of which begins with the taxpayer.  Allows such credit against regular and alternative minimum tax.

Taking Account of Institutions with Low Operation Risk Act of 2015 or the TAILOR Act of 2015 This bill requires the federal financial regulatory agencies to tailor any regulatory action to limit the regulatory compliance impact, cost, liability risk, and other burdens as is appropriate for the risk profile and business model involved. The financial regulatory agencies must also consider: (1) the impact that such regulatory action has on the ability of the institution or class of institutions to flexibly serve evolving and diverse customer needs; (2) the potential unintended impact of examination manuals or other regulatory directives that work in conflict with the tailoring of such regulatory action; and (3) the underlying policy objectives of the regulatory action and statutory scheme involved.

This bill directs the payroll administrator of a house of Congress, if by April 15, 2017, has not agreed to a concurrent budget resolution for FY2018, to deposit in an escrow account all mandatory payments for compensation of Members of Congress serving in that house, and release such payments to those Members only upon the earlier of: (1) the day on which the house agrees to such a resolution, or (2) the last day of the 115th Congress.  The bill requires the payroll administrator to provide for the same withholding and remittance with respect to a payment deposited in an escrow account that would apply to such payment if it were not subject to this bill.  The payroll administrator shall release for payments to Members of that house any amounts remaining in any escrow account at the end of the 115th Congress.  The bill also requires the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Inspector General to annually determine whether OMB and the President are in compliance with a statutory requirement that the President submit a budget to Congress.  No funds may be appropriated from the Treasury for the pay of OMB or its deputy directors or the Deputy Director for Management of OMB during any period of noncompliance

Technological Resource to Assist Criminal Enforcement (TRACE) Act - Amends the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act to require a licensed manufacturer or importer of firearms to: (1) test fire manufactured or imported firearms as specified by the Attorney General; (2) prepare ballistics images of the fired bullet and cartridge casings; (3) make the records available to the Attorney General for entry into a computerized database; and (4) store the fired bullet and cartridge casings.Directs the Attorney General to assist firearm manufacturers and importers in complying with such requirements by: (1) acquiring, installing, and upgrading ballistics equipment and bullet and cartridge casing recovery equipment; (2) hiring or designating sufficient personnel to develop and maintain a ballistics database; (3) providing education about the role of ballistics; (4) providing for the coordination among law enforcement, regulatory agencies, and the firearm industry to curb firearm-related crime and illegal firearm trafficking; and (5) taking other necessary steps to make ballistics testing effective.Directs the Attorney General to: (1) establish a computer system through which State and local law enforcement agencies can promptly access ballistics records; and (2) require training for ballistics examiners.Requires the Attorney General to conduct mandatory ballistics testing

Buy America Update Act - Amends Federal transportation law to revise Buy American requirements for Federal-aid highway program (FAHP) projects to require that: (1) the cost of components and subcomponents produced in the United States is more than 60% of the cost of all components of the rolling stock; and (2) final assembly of the rolling stock have occurred in the United States.

Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to review certain regulations governing the FAHP and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to determine whether manufactured products other than those containing steel and iron should be considered for purposes of domestic content preferences.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) initiate a rulemaking to develop audit procedures for the Federal Highway Administration (FHA) to review offeror and recipient compliance with Buy American provisions, and issue guidance on best practices for pre-award and post-delivery audits by recipients; (2) conduct a supplier scouting process for domestic suppliers that can provide compliant products for which a waiver will be sought; and (3) publish a summary of the scouting report and the reasons for any decision made by the Secretary to grant a waiver.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) consult with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) before issuing

Directs the Secretary of Education to discharge or cancel the federal student loan indebtedness of: (1) an eligible spouse of a public servant who died (or dies) or who became (or becomes) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in the terrorist attack on September 11, 2001; (2) a surviving debtor who owes a federal student loan that is a consolidation loan used jointly by that debtor and an eligible victim (a person who died (or dies) or who became (or becomes) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in such attack); and (3) a parent of an eligible victim if the parent owes a consolidation loan used to repay a PLUS loan incurred on behalf of the victim or a PLUS loan incurred on behalf of a victim who died (or dies) or who became (or becomes) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in such attack.

Eating Healthy at School Act of 2010 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to study and report to Congress on: (1) the effectiveness and efficiency of administrative review systems to ensure that each local educational agency (LEA) participating in the school lunch and school breakfast programs complies with specified provisions of the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act and the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, including provisions regarding nutrition, eligibility, meal counts, and claims for reimbursement; (2) alternative processes and procedures that may improve the effectiveness and efficiency of such review systems; (3) the optimal frequency for carrying out such reviews; and (4) any alternative processes and procedures for establishing a more effective and efficient administrative review system that consider the practicality of implementing such alternative processes and procedures, including the cost and burden of implementation that would be imposed on LEAs, schools, and states.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer funds to the Secretary to carry out this Act.
Heavy Truck, Tractor, and Trailer Retail Federal Excise Tax Repeal Act of 2017 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to eliminate the excise tax on new heavy trucks, tractors, and trailers.

Rape Survivor Child Custody Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to states that have in place a law that allows the mother of any child that was conceived through rape to seek court-ordered termination of the parental rights of her rapist with regard to that child, which the court shall grant upon clear and convincing evidence of rape.

Women and Alcohol Research Equity Act of 1996 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to provide for an increase in the amount of funds expended for research on alcohol abuse and alcoholism among women.

Airline Passenger Fairness Act - Amends Federal transportation law to require the Secretary of Transportation to take certain actions on the initiative to prevent unfair or deceptive practices and unfair methods of competition in the airline industry, including an air carrier's failure to inform a ticketed passenger, upon request, whether the flight on which the passenger is ticketed is oversold, to permit a passenger holding a confirmed reserved space on a flight to use portions of that passenger's ticket for travel, rather than the entire ticket, regardless of the reason any other portion of the ticket is not used, to deliver a passenger's checked baggage within 24 hours after arrival of the flight on which the passenger travelled and on which the passenger checked the baggage, except for reasonable delays in delivery of such baggage, to provide a consumer full access to all fares for that air carrier, regardless of the technology the consumer uses to access the fares if such information is requested by that consumer, to provide notice to each passenger holding a confirmed reserved space on a flight with reasonable prior notice when a scheduled flight will be delayed for any reason (other than reasons of national security), to inform passengers accurately and truthfully of the reason for the delay, cancellation, or diversion of a flight, to refund the full purchase price of an unused

HSA Accessibility and Portability Act of 2006 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to allow a health insurance issuer to elect to meet certain requirements for small group market access instead of complying with the guaranteed issue requirement.

Requires the issuer to accept or reject all eligible individuals within entire groups at the time of such election.

Requires the issuer to provide group health insurance coverage for individuals covered by the election, but not exceeding 150% of the standard individual rate applicable to such coverage in the state in which the policy was initially issued.

Directs the issuer to furnish to the Secretary of Health and Human Services information to monitor the impact of such election on access to, and affordability of, health insurance coverage in the small group and individual markets.

Greater Sage Grouse Protection and Recovery Act of 2016 This bill prohibits the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture from making a finding under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 with respect to the greater sage grouse in a state that has a state management plan before September 30, 2026.  In order to foster coordination between a state management plan and federal resource management plans that affect the greater sage grouse, upon notification by the governor of a state with a state management plan, Interior and the Department of the Interior must agree to modify any federal resource management plan that affects the greater sage grouse in the state for a period of at least five years.  Any withdrawal, or amendment or modification of a federal resource management plan, that is inconsistent with a state management plan must be stayed retroactively for the three years before the withdrawal, amendment, or modification was issued.  With regard to any major federal action consistent with a state management plan, any findings, analyses, or conclusions regarding the greater sage grouse or its habitat under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 must not have a preclusive effect on the approval or implementation of the major federal action in that state. Safe, Convenient, Reliable, Efficient, Effective, Next-Generation, Functional, and Secure TSA Act of 2016 or the SCREEN FAST Act This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to establish a pilot program at three category X airports to: (1) reconfigure and install security systems that increase efficiency and reduce vulnerabilities in airport terminals, particularly at airports that have large open areas where screening is conducted; and (2) develop and test prototypes of screening security systems and security checkpoint configurations to expedite the movement of passengers.  The TSA shall carry out the pilot programs using amounts: (1) appropriated to the TSA before this bill's enactment and available for obligation as of such date, and (2) amounts obtained as reimbursements from airports under such programs.  The bill authorizes the TSA Under Secretary for Security to: (1) provide or accept services, supplies, equipment, personnel, and facilities, with or without reimbursement, to or from any other public or private entity on such terms as the Under Secretary may consider appropriate, and (2) accept a monetary gift or bequest, to be available until expended, upon the request of any person.

Fort Stanton and Rio Bonito Corridor Vegetation Management Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the Bureau of Land Management, to solicit competitive bids for and enter into vegetation sales contracts for the purpose of using livestock grazing as a vegetation management tool on specified lands under the jurisdiction of the Secretary in Fort Stanton, New Mexico, and near Fort Stanton within the Rio Bonito Corridor.  Ratifies any such contracts entered into before the enactment of this Act. 
Requires that management of such lands be consistent with any applicable land and resource management plan under the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976. 
Provides for the distribution and use of the proceeds from such contracts.

Pay Accountability Act - Requires the payroll administrator of a House of Congress (either the House of Representatives or the Senate) to withhold from the payments otherwise required to be made with respect to the pay period for the compensation of each Member of Congress who serves in that House an amount equal to the product of: (1) an amount equal to one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of pay applicable to the Member for the pay period; and (2) the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit is reached. Requires the payroll administrator to deposit all withheld amounts in an escrow account and transfer them to the Secretary of the Treasury on the last day of the Congress involved, which shall be used for deficit reduction.

Requires the White House Office to withhold from the payments otherwise required to be made with respect to the pay period for the compensation of the President or Vice President an amount equal to the product of: (1) an amount equal to one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of compensation of the President or Vice President (as the case may be) for the pay period; and (2) the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit

Agricultural Credit Expansion Act - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to expand the farm loan eligibility of limited liability companies (LLCs) to include certain operating-only entities and certain embedded entities.

Breast Cancer Patient Education Act of 2012 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to provide for the planning and implementation of an education campaign to inform breast cancer patients about the availability and coverage of breast reconstruction, prostheses, and other options.

Judicial Transparency and Ethics Enhancement Act of 2006 - Amends the federal judicial code to establish the Office of Inspector General for the Judicial Branch of the U.S. government, with the head of the Office as the Inspector General appointed by the Chief Justice.

Requires the Inspector General, with respect to the Judicial Branch, to: (1) conduct investigations of matters pertaining to the Judicial Branch that may require oversight or other action within the Judicial Branch or by Congress; (2) conduct and supervise audits and investigations; (3) prevent and detect waste, fraud, and abuse; and (4) recommend changes in laws or regulations governing the Judicial Branch.

Prohibits the discharge, demotion, threat, suspension, harassment, or discrimination against an employee in the terms and conditions of employment because of any lawful act done by the employee to provide information, cause information to be provided, or otherwise assist in an investigation regarding any possible violation of federal law or regulation, or misconduct, by a judge or any other employee in the Judicial Branch.

Cormorant Management and Natural Resources Protection Act - Amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to delegate to a state the authority to develop and submit a management plan for cormorants in the state.Requires the Secretary of the Interior to conduct educational and informational activities for the owners and operators of aquaculture facilities to improve their efforts to prevent cormorants from consuming aquatic species being reared in aquaculture facilities, which contributes to the proliferation of cormorants.

Tax Relief for Victims of Disasters Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make the earned income made available for certain dislocated workers and the earned income of individuals who worked in hazardous occupations in a federally declared disaster applicable to a qualified federally declared disaster individual (i.e., a disabled veteran, a dependent of a disabled veteran, or a disabled veteran who performed substantially all of his or her employment services in the disaster area); (2) allow a tax deduction for losses attributable to a federally declared disaster occurring after December 31, 2010, and before January 1, 2013, that arise in the disaster area and are attributable to a federally declared disaster; and (3) allow an additional tax exemption for 60-day periods of housing for a qualified federally declared disaster displaced individual.

Defines a "qualified federally declared disaster displaced individual" as a disabled veteran, a dependent of a disabled veteran, or a disabled veteran who performed substantially all of his or her employment services in the disaster area.

Hospice Evaluation and Legitimate Payment Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a hospice physician, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, or physician assistant (as those terms are defined in Medicare part C (Hospice and Palliative Care Program)), or other health professional designated by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), to have a face-to-face encounter with the individual to determine continued eligibility of the individual for hospice care prior to the first 60-day period and each subsequent recertification, and to attest that such visit took place.  Requires the Secretary to take into account the results of such evaluation before the period.  Directs the Secretary to implement the revisions in payment for hospice care furnished on or after such date, unless the Secretary determines that the demonstration program would adversely affect access to quality hospice care by beneficiaries.  Directs the Secretary to establish a Medicare Hospice Payment Reform demonstration program for a two-year period, beginning on or after October 1, 2013.  Requires the Secretary to conduct an evaluation of the demonstration program, including an analysis of whether the use of the revised payment methodology has improved the quality of patient care

National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to: (1) enhance and expand infrastructure and activities to track the epidemiology of neurological diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease; and (2) incorporate information obtained through such activities into a National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) ensure that the System facilitates further research on neurological diseases; (2) provide for the collection and storage of information on the incidence and prevalence of neurological diseases in the United States, as well as other information on neurological diseases; (3) provide for the collection and storage of information relevant to analysis on neurological diseases; and (4) make information and analysis in the System available to federal agencies and to the public.

Requires the Secretary to consult with individuals with appropriate expertise in carrying out this Act.

Authorizes the Secretary to award grants to, or enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with, public or private nonprofit entities to carry out activities under this Act.

Requires the Secretary to make information and analysis in the System available to federal agencies and to the public.

Millennium Challenge Compact Improvement Act (MCIA) - Amends the Millennium Challenge Act of 2003 to: (1) limit the duration of a Compact to five years; and (2) authorize a Board determination that a Compact includes a project that cannot be completed in five years or less to approve a duration of not more than 10 years.

Authorizes an eligible country and the United States to: (1) have in effect more than one Compact at any given time; and (2) have entered into subsequent Compacts after the expiration of existing Compacts. Allows a concurrent Compact (including a regional Compact) only if the Board determines that the country is making considerable and demonstrable progress in implementing the terms of its existing Compact and supplementary agreements. Allows a subsequent Compact only if the Board determines that the country has substantially met the objectives of prior Compacts between the country and the United States and supplementary agreements, or the Board determines that the eligible country has demonstrated sufficient capacity to perform successfully on a subsequent Compact.

Authorizes the assistance contemplated by the Act to be provided through a Compact with a country individually, and/or through a Compact with two or more countries in the same geographic region collectively.

Amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to require the Secretary of Agriculture to deny permanent eligibility subsidies to a person or legal entity that is determined to be ineligible for such subsidies based on income.  Requires such person or legal entity to reimburse the Secretary for the full amount of any benefit or payment that the person or legal entity has received while ineligible. 
Requires the Secretary to request the Administrator of the Internal Revenue Service to verify the average adjusted gross income, average adjusted gross farm income, and average adjusted gross nonfarm income of a person or legal entity applying for eligibility subsidies.  Requires the Administrator to notify the Secretary of the results of such verification.  Requires the Secretary to deny the issuance of applicable payments and benefits to an ineligible person or legal entity under similar terms and conditions to those for denial of eligibility for direct payments under the Supplemental Security Income program. 
Authorizes an ineligible person or legal entity to request a reconsideration of such denial by the Farm Service Agency office serving the applicant's location.  Requires the person or legal entity to submit evidence, accompanied with a certification by a certified public accountant, to support a claim that the person or legal entity satisfies the income eligibility requirements.  Requires the Secretary to submit such evidence to the Administrator for a second determination
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer an income-based credit for providing long-term care services to others.

Chickasaw National Recreation Area Land Exchange Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the Chickasaw Nation, within six months after the Nation conveys to the United States all right, title, and interest in and to certain non-federal land, the Chickasaw National Recreation Area lands and interests therein, identified as Tract 102-25 on a map.

Requires the fair market values of the Federal and non-federal land to be determined by an appraisal acceptable to the Secretary and the Nation. Provides for equalization of values if the fair market values are not equal.

Provides that the conveyance of the non-federal land shall not take place until the completion of all items included in the Preliminary Exchange Agreement among the City of Sulphur, the Chickasaw Nation, and the National Park Service (NPS), except for the one providing for the Federal land to be taken into trust for the benefit of the Chickasaw Nation. States that the item provided for the Federal land to be taken into trust for the benefit of the Chickasaw Nation shall not apply.

Requires the Secretary, upon completion of the land exchange, to: (1) revise the boundary of Chickasaw National

Immigration Anti-Discrimination Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require all civil penalties collected to be credited to the appropriation to be used in carrying out such Act. 
Authorizes appropriations for FY 1994 for activities of regional offices of the Special Counsel for Immigration-Related Unfair Employment Practices within the Department of Justice. 
Amends the Act to require the Comptroller General and the Attorney General to report annually to the Congress on the enforcement of such Act. 
Requires the Special Counsel to provide for agreements with Federal and State agencies involved with enforcement of laws prohibiting discrimination on the basis of national origin under which such agencies would receive charges respecting unfair immigration-related employment practices and promptly forward such charges to the Special Counsel. 
Directs the Special Counsel to establish a national, toll-free telephone service to receive charges of unfair immigration-related employment practices and otherwise provide for such outreach efforts as will educate the public concerning the provisions of this Act. 
Directs the Attorney General to provide technical assistance to States and local governments concerning the provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act and the roles provided for receipt of charges of violations of such provisions.

Satellite Home Viewer Protection Act of 1996 - Amends Federal broadcasting law to require a satellite carrier that makes secondary transmissions of a primary transmission made by a network station to provide a written statement to a subscriber describing and quoting the network's territorial restrictions. 
Revises procedures for signal intensity measurements.  Requires a satellite carrier, upon a challenge by a network station regarding whether a subscriber is an unserved household within the predicted grade B contour of the station, to inform the subscriber in writing from the network station that it has challenged the subscriber's receipt of the signal from the satellite carrier, and offer the subscriber the option of the carrier conducting a measurement of the signal intensity of the subscriber's household to determine whether the household is unserved.  Requires the subscriber, if the carrier does not request in writing the measurement, to reimburse the carrier the costs of the measurement.  Requires the subscriber, if the carrier requests the measurement, to give reasonable notice to the network station issuing the challenge that the carrier will be conducting the measurement. 
Authorizes satellite carriers and network broadcasters to negotiate the terms and conditions, including technical standards and costs, of such measurement.  Requires a complete description of the agreed upon terms to be filed with the Register of Copyrights.  Requires

Ronald Reagan Memorial Act of 2000 - Authorizes the Ronald Reagan Memorial Commission to establish the Ronald Reagan Memorial in accordance with this Act, on federal lands administered by the National Park Service in the District of Columbia.Requires the Commission to: (1) recommend a permanent location for the Memorial; and (2) select a design for the Memorial.

This bill directs the Department of the Interior to offer for sale to qualified entities, for fair market value, any remaining interest of the United States in and to 4,276 acres of covered land in Mohave County, Arizona.  Conveys such land to a qualified entity upon acceptance of an offer and completion of a sale.  Requires that any prior interests in the locatable minerals and the right to use the surface for mineral purposes held by the qualified entity under a mining claim, millsite, tunnel site, or any other federal land use authorization applicable to the covered land conveyed to the qualified entity shall merge all interest of the United States in and to the covered land to ensure that the qualified entity receives fee simple title to the purchased covered land.  Directs Interior to determine the fair market value of the covered land to be conveyed under this bill in accordance with the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 and the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice.  Requires the qualified entity to pay all costs related to the conveyance of the covered land, including the costs of surveys and other administrative costs associated with the conveyance.

Bodegas as Catalysts for Healthy Living Act - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make grants to: (1) a locally-based organization that represents small businesses; and (2) a local redevelopment agency that is chartered, established, or otherwise sanctioned by a state or local government. Requires the use of grant amounts for one or more of the following activities: (1) to provide assistance to independently owned and operated small businesses, such as bodegas and corner stores, in expanding their inventory to include fresh fruits and vegetables and healthy alternatives; and (2) to provide assistance to community-based organizations, such as community health centers, in carrying out related consumer education and outreach activities.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) and title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to cover additional primary and preventive services relating to obesity treatment and prevention, supervised exercise sessions, stress testing, lifestyle modification education, and culinary arts education for promoting proper nutrition.

Border Enforcement Security Task Force Reauthorization Act of 2017 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to revise the composition and reporting requirements of the Border and Transportation Security Unit (BEST) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).  The bill requires the unit to be composed of at least one member of each of the Coast Guard Investigative Service and the geographically responsible Coast Guard Sector Intelligence Office, if the unit has a port security nexus.  The DHS Secretary shall report to Congress on the unit's effectiveness in: (1) enhancing border security, (2) disrupting and dismantling transnational criminal organizations, and (3) reducing drug trafficking, arms smuggling, child exploitation, illegal alien trafficking and smuggling, violence, and kidnapping along and across U.S. borders.  The bill authorizes the Department of State to deny a request by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), or U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to authorize a danger pay allowance for any employee of any such agency.
