Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Program, to be carried out by the Under Secretary for International Trade of the Department of Commerce, for the promotion of policies to reduce production costs and encourage innovation, investment, and productivity among U.S. businesses that produce or export clean energy technologies or related services.

Directs the Under Secretary to provide information and other assistance to U.S. businesses, particularly small- and medium-sized businesses, to promote the production and exportation of clean energy technologies and related services.

Medicare Certified Registered Nurse First Assistant Direct Reimbursement Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for Medicare coverage of surgical first assisting services of certified registered nurse first assistants.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to: (1) extend the Medicare prescription drug (PDP) initial enrollment period for 2006 and 2007; (2) suspend, through December 31, 2007, the late enrollment penalty for nonparticipating PDPs; (3) allow open enrollment and disenrollment in prescription drug plans during the first 12 months of enrollment; and (4) limit, through 2006, the number of times a covered part D drug may be removed from the PDP formulary without a change in coverage.

Waco Mammoth National Monument Establishment Act of 2011 - Establishes the Waco Mammoth National Monument in Texas as a unit of the National Park System.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into cooperative management agreements with Baylor University and the city of Waco, Texas.

Authorizes the Secretary to acquire by donation from the city any land or interest in land owned by the city within the proposed boundary of the Monument.

Directs the Secretary to complete a general management plan for the Monument.

Prohibits the use of federal funds to pay the costs of: (1) carrying out a cooperative agreement under this Act, (2) acquiring land for inclusion in the Monument, (3) developing a visitor center for the Monument, (4) operating or maintaining the Monument, (5) constructing exhibits for the Monument, or (6) developing the general management plan. Allows the use of non-federal funds to pay any costs that may be incurred by the Secretary or the National Park Service (NPS) in carrying out this Act.

Terminates the designation of the Monument as a unit of the National Park System if federal funds are required for the operation and maintenance of the Monument. Requires any land acquired by the Secretary from the city to revert to

Methane Hydrate Research and Development Amendments Act of 2015 This bill amends the Methane Hydrate Research and Development Act of 2000 to authorize the Department of the Interior to award grants to, or enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with, institutions that:   conduct basic and applied research to identify, explore, assess, and develop methane hydrate as a commercially viable source of energy;  identify and characterize methane hydrate resources using remote sensing and seismic data;  develop technologies required for efficient and environmentally sound development of methane hydrate resources;  conduct basic and applied research to assess and mitigate the environmental impact of hydrate degassing;  develop technologies to reduce the risks of drilling through methane hydrates;  conduct exploratory drilling, well testing, and production testing operations on permafrost and nonpermafrost gas hydrates; and  expand education and training programs in methane hydrate resource research and resource development through fellowships or other means for graduate education and training.  Interior must conduct a long-term environmental monitoring program to study the effects of production from methane hydrate reservoirs.

Local Emergency Health Services Reimbursement Act of 2002 - Amends the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 to provide for Federal reimbursement of uncompensated emergency health services furnished to undocumented aliens by States and local governments, hospitals, or other providers.

Student Credit Card Transparency Act of 2009 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to require each creditor of a college student who has a college student credit card to submit to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) an annual report containing the terms and conditions of all business, marketing, and promotional agreements with a college student's credit card issuer, and all agreements with colleges, alumni organizations, or foundations that provide college student credit cards.

Requires the Board to submit to Congress and make public an annual report that lists the information concerning such credit card agreements submitted by each institution of higher education, alumni organization, or foundation.

Directs the Comptroller General to review the reports submitted by creditors and the marketing practices of creditors to determine the impact that college affinity card agreements and college student card agreements have on credit card debt.

Small Business Jobs Act of 2015  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for the hiring of certain employees by a small employer. A small employer is an employer who employs between 2 and 100 employees in a calendar year and whose place of business is in a county with an annual unemployment rate that is at least 1% higher than the national rate. The credit applies to employees who are employed, on average, at least 30 hours per week and who first begin work for the employer in a trade or business of the small employer. The credit is not available to tax-exempt small employers. The credit is not allowed for wages paid after December 31, 2017.

Gas Price and Refinery Capacity Relief Act of 2013 - Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to require refineries to submit to the Administrator of the Energy Information Administration (EIA) information describing: (1) the schedule of the refinery for any planned refinery outage, including the dates for the planned outage at least one year in advance of the date of the expected outage or the date the outage is scheduled and the estimated inventories and production of refined petroleum products during the period; and (2) any unplanned refinery outages as soon as practicable.  Requires the Administrator to: (1) review information on planned refinery outages and unplanned refinery outages reported by refineries and that is available from commercial reporting services, (2) analyze that information to determine whether the scheduling of a planned refinery outage or an unplanned refinery outage may nationally or regionally substantially affect the price or supply of any refined petroleum product by decreasing its production and causing or contributing to a retail or wholesale supply shortage or disruption, and (3) alert the Secretary of Energy (DOE) of any refinery outage that the Administrator determines may nationally or regionally substantially affect the price or supply of a refined petroleum product.  Directs the Secretary

School-Based Respiratory Health Management Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to give States that: (1) require that each public elementary school and secondary school have in place a plan for having on the school premises a trained personnel of the school during all operating hours of the school a school nurse or one or more other individuals who are trained personnel of the school; and (2) provide for the certification of a comprehensive school-based allergies and reversible lower airway disorders management program that includes a method to identify all students of such school with a diagnosis of allergies and reversible lower airway disorders, an individual student allergies and reversible lower airway disorders action plan for each student with a diagnosis of such conditions, allergies and reversible lower airway disorders education for school staff, rescue medications for allergies or reversible lower airway disorders, efforts to reduce the presence of environmental triggers of allergies and reversible lower airway disorders, and a system to support students through coordination with family members, primary care providers, and others as necessary. Give additional preference to such States in determining the priority of their schools for the administration of rescue medications for allergies and reversible lower airway disorders.

USDA Civil Rights Resolution Act of 2000 - Amends the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1999 to provide for a waiver of the statute of limitations for administrative determinations made by the Department of Agriculture (USDA) that affect the civil rights of U.S. agricultural producers. Authorizes a complainant to petition the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice to review such a determination and make recommendations to resolve the complaint.

Amends the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 to repeal the zero mortality rate goal for commercial fishing incidental take of marine mammals.  Modifies the goal of take reduction plans to require the long-term goal of the plan to be to reduce, within five years after its implementation, the incidental mortality or serious injury of marine mammals in the course of fishing operations taking into account the economics of the fishery, the availability of existing technology, and existing State or regional fishery management plans.

Rapid DNA Act of 2014 - Amends the DNA Identification Act of 1994 to require the National DNA Identification Laboratory to: (1) provide the laboratory with a qualified agency name and address, and (2) provide the laboratory with a qualified agency's membership from federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies. Requires the laboratory to provide qualified agency members with training in the operation of a sample-to-answer DNA system. Requires the laboratory to provide qualified agency operators with training in the operation of a sample-to-answer DNA system. Requires the laboratory to provide qualified agency personnel with training in the operation of a sample-to-answer DNA system. Requires the laboratory to provide qualified agencies with: (1) proficiency testing guidelines for the analysis of DNA samples using sample-to-answer DNA analysis systems, and (2) a qualified agency's membership from federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies. Requires laboratories that perform forensic DNA analyses to use a qualified agency for the collection of biological material for DNA analysis. Requires laboratories that perform routine evidence DNA analysis to use a qualified agency for the collection of biological material for DNA analysis. Requires laboratories that perform blind external proficiency tests to use a qualified agency for the collection of biological material for DNA analysis. Requires laboratories that perform forensic DNA

New Economy Workforce Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make an immigrant visa available to an alien who: (1) does not have a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) if there is no qualified individual to whom such a visa may be made available who has such a degree; or (2) is not a high school graduate (if there is no qualified individual to whom such a visa may be made available who has a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) or who is a high school graduate). Requires the determination of educational status to be made using the most recent evidence with respect to educational credentials proffered by the alien.Requires that, for purposes of such educational status determination, an alien is not eligible for a visa unless the alien has a bachelor's degree (or higher degree).Requires the Secretary of State to: (1) promulgate regulations regarding the allocation of immigrant visas, made available under this Act, pursuant to the amendments made by this Act; and (2) promulgate regulations to carry out the requirements of this Act with respect to determining foreign degree equivalence and verifying educational credentials.

Preserving Access to Manufactured Housing Act of 2013 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to revise the definition of "mortgage or originator" to exclude from the definition of "mortgage or originator" a retailer of manufactured or modular homes or its employees unless such retailer or its employees receive compensation or gain for engaging in activities in excess of any compensation or gain received in a comparable cash transaction.  Revises the definition of "high cost mortgage" to include a first mortgage on a consumer's principal dwelling that is considered personal property (or is a consumer credit transaction that does not include the purchase of real property on which a dwelling is to be placed) by an annual percentage rate at consummation of the transaction that exceeds the average prime offer rate by more than: (1) 8.5% points, in the case of a transaction in an amount of $50,000 or more, but less than $75,000; (2) 10.5% points, in the case of a transaction in an amount of more than $30,000, but less than $50,000; or (3) 12.5% points

Marine Mammal Rescue Assistance Act of 1999 - Amends the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish the John H. Prescott Marine Mammal Rescue Assistance Grant Program to provide grants to eligible stranding network participants for the recovery or treatment of marine mammals, the collection of data from living or dead marine mammals for scientific research regarding marine mammal health, and facility operation costs that are directly related to those purposes.  Directs the Secretary to ensure that funds provided as grants are distributed equitably among the designated stranding regions.  Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to tax dividends as net capital gain, with qualified dividend income (dividends received from domestic corporations) excluded from such income as nonresident alien individual dividends.

Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area Act of 2014 - Establishes the Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area in Utah to provide for: (1) enhancement of recreational uses, and (2) the use of off-highway vehicles.  Requires the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), to administer the Recreation Area and the proposed exchange parcel (the acreage of BLM land identified on the map as "Proposed Exchange Parcel") in accordance with applicable federal laws and rules and consistent with the administration of the Sand Mountain Open OHV Area, as in existence on the day before enactment of this Act.  Excludes the proposed exchange parcel from the Recreation Area.  Requires the land described above to remain open, in perpetuity, to the use of off-highway vehicles.  Directs the Secretary, if Utah offers to convey title to the non-federal land, to accept the offer and convey title to the federal land to Utah.  Requires the value of the federal and non-federal land to be exchanged to be equal.

Drug Price Competition Act of 2009 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) to require a first applicant for a generic drug to submit and maintain a patent certification for the drug for the entire 180-day period before generic drugs may be marketed. Requires such an applicant also to: (1) submit and maintain a certification for each unexpired patent for which a first applicant for a generic drug had submitted a certification for the drug on the first day on which a substantially complete application containing such a certification was submitted; and (2) refrain from patent infringement actions within 45 days after submission of such a certification, or if an action was brought within such time period, obtain a court decision that the patent is invalid or not infringed. Makes an applicant eligible to receive approval immediately effective before any other applicant begins commercial marketing.

Requires the FDA to grant approval of a generic drug to an applicant who has not violated the requirements of this Act.

Veterans' Compensation Rate Amendments of 2001 - Amends Federal provisions concerning veterans' disability compensation to increase the rates of such compensation and to provide for additional compensation for veterans' dependents, including children, and for certain disabled adult children.

Hibben Center for Archaeological Research Act of 2002 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, in cooperation with the University of New Mexico, to construct and occupy a portion of the Hibben Center for Archaeological Research.Requires the University to offer to enter into a long-term lease with the United States that: (1) provides to the National Park Service (NPS) space in the Center for storage, research, and offices; and (2) is acceptable to the Secretary.Requires the Secretary to enter into cooperative agreements with the University, other units of the NPS, other Federal agencies, and Indian tribes for: (1) the curation of and conduct of research on artifacts in the museum collection; and (2) the development, use, management, and operation of the portion of the Center leased to the NPS.

Workplace Religious Freedom Act of 1999 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to revise the definition of "religion" for purposes of the Act to include all aspects of religious observance, practice, and belief, including religious holidays, observance of religious rules and regulations, dress codes, and observance of religious practices. 
Revises the definition of "religion" for purposes of the Act to require that an employer's action be an affirmative and bona fide effort to resolve the religious conflict before the conflict becomes so extreme that it is no longer the fault of the employer. 
Revises the definition of "religion" for purposes of the Act to require that an accommodation be a reasonable accommodation if it will not result in the inability of an employee to perform the essential functions of the employment position. 
Revises the definition of "religion" for purposes of the Act to require that an employer's refusal to accommodate a religious observance or practice without a reasonable accommodation be an unlawful employment practice. 
Declares that an employer shall not be required to pay premium wages or confer premium benefits for work performed during hours to which such wages or benefits would ordinarily be applicable, if work is performed during such hours only

National Fish and Wildlife Policy Fellowship Program Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to award one-year fellowships to qualified graduate and post-graduate level students engaged in advanced degree programs concerning freshwater and anadromous fish, wildlife, conservation management, or biology.

Voluntary Protection Program Act - Directs the Secretary of Labor to enter into cooperative agreements with employers to encourage establishment of comprehensive safety and health management systems to protect employees from occupational hazards. Directs the Secretary to establish a voluntary protection program to encourage excellence and recognize its achievement in both the technical and managerial protection of employees from occupational hazards.

Scotchman Peaks Wilderness Act of 2016 This bill designates specified National Forest System land in Idaho as the Scotchman Peaks Wilderness.  The Wilderness Act is amended to: (1) permit the Secretary of Agriculture to take measures within the wilderness area to control fire, insects, and disease; and (2) allow activities or uses on land outside the wilderness area to be seen or heard within the wilderness area.  The Department of the Interior must ensure that Indian tribes have access to the wilderness area for traditional cultural and religious purposes.

Federal Land Exchange Improvement Act of 1995 - Amends the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 to increase the maximum amount of land eligible for approximately equal value treatment. 
Requires amounts received from such transactions to be deposited into a special fund in the Treasury.  Makes such fund available for processing land exchanges.  Prohibits amounts in the fund from exceeding $12 million at any time.  Requires amounts received from such transactions which, but for this provision, to be covered over into the Treasury as miscellaneous receipts. 
Requires an environmental assessment to be prepared for any exchange under such Act pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969.  Requires completion of required conferencing or consultation within 45 days after the date on which the conference or consultation is initiated.  Prohibits any action from being taken on the non-Federal land acquired in an exchange until the Secretary concerned has complied with the National Environmental Policy Act and Endangered Species Act concerning such action and necessary amendment to the land management plan applicable to such land and such action. 
Authorizes the Secretary concerned to dispose of lands by exchange to make minor adjustments to the boundary of a unit of the public lands or the National Forest System as may be necessary

Reciprocity and Fairness in Foreign Investment Act - Prohibits a foreign person that is owned or controlled by the government of a foreign country from acquiring or holding: (1) an equity interest, or other evidence of ownership, in a U.S. corporation, partnership, or other business entity organized under U.S. law, or (2) real property in the United States unless such foreign country allows U.S. persons to acquire or hold the same interests or property in comparable entities.

Permits a foreign person to acquire or hold a property interest in, or control operations, management, or security operations of, critical infrastructure in the United States to the same extent as the foreign country of which that person is a national allows U.S. persons to acquire or hold equivalent property interests or other evidences of ownership in, or to control operations, management, or security operations of, comparable critical infrastructure in that country.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to issue regulations to carry out this Act. Imposes civil penalties of up to $500,000 on any foreign person who violates this Act.

Directs the Surface Transportation Board to promulgate regulations adopting a simplified dispute resolution mechanism. 
Authorizes the Board to impose conditions to encourage and expand competition between and among rail carriers in the affected region or the national rail system, if such conditions do not cause substantial harm to the benefits of the transaction to the affected carriers or the public. 
Authorizes the Board to grant temporary relief when it finds it necessary and appropriate to do so to remedy inadequate service. 
Revises the definition of "agreement" affecting only the transportation of household goods to eliminate the exclusion of certain agreements affecting only the transportation of household goods. 
Authorizes appropriations. 
Authorizes the Chairperson of the Board to designate a new Chairperson with the advice and consent of the Senate.

Makes funds appropriated to the Architect of the Capitol for the Capitol Power Plant available to construct, operate, and maintain on a reimbursable basis battery recharging stations in parking areas under the jurisdiction of the House of Representatives on Capitol grounds for use by privately owned vehicles used by Members of the House or authorized employees.

Authorizes the Architect to use one or more vendors on a commission basis.

Requires the Architect to: (1) charge fees or charges for electricity provided to Members and authorized employees sufficient to cover the costs of construction and operation of the battery recharging stations, including associated costs; and (2) report to the appropriate congressional committees on the financial administration and cost recovery of such activities.

Amends the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to revise requirements for the loan guarantee program.

Allows the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to waive the requirement to provide a third-party credit report if: (1) the applicant's or project's third-party credit rating is not relevant to the determination of the credit risk of the project; and (2) the project costs are not projected to exceed $100 million, and the applicant agrees to accept the credit rating assigned to the applicant by the Secretary.

Authorizes the head of the loan guarantee program to recruit and directly appoint into the competitive service, and retain agents and legal and other professional advisors in connection with guarantees and related activities authorized under the loan guarantee program.

Authorizes an eligible project to be located on two or more non-contiguous sites in the United States.

Authorizes a project sponsor or applicant to submit an application for more than one eligible project.

Authorizes the Secretary to waive the requirement that the Secretary retain a certain percentage of the loan amount for administrative costs if the Secretary selects the most cost-effective method of payment for the loan.

Authorizes the Secretary to retain agents and legal and other professional advisors in connection with guarantees and related activities authorized under the loan guarantee program.

No Qualified Teacher Left Behind Act of 2004 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA) to revise the definition of "highly qualified teacher" for purposes of ESEA teacher certification requirements.

Requires a plan submitted to the Secretary of Education under ESEA for a teacher certification grant to ensure that all teachers who are highly qualified but are teaching in a rural school district are so certified by the end of the 2008-2009 school year.

Authorizes additional funds for FY 2005 and 2006 and 2007 for teacher recruitment, retention, and professional development in rural school districts.

Prohibits any entity from receiving ESEA teacher certification funds unless it ensures that all elementary school and secondary school teachers employed by the entity and teaching in core academic subjects are highly qualified by the end of: (1) the 2005-2006 school year; or (2) the 2008-2009 school year for teachers in rural school districts.

Housing Opportunity and Mortgage Equity Act of 2013 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to each carry out a program to provide for the refinancing of qualified mortgages owned or guaranteed by such enterprise through a refinancing mortgage, and for the purchase of and securitization of such refinancing mortgages, in accordance with policies and procedures that the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) shall establish. Defines "qualified mortgage" as a mortgage: (1) that is an existing first mortgage that was made for the purchase of, or refinancing of another first mortgage on, a one-to-four family dwelling, including a condominium or a share in a cooperative ownership housing association, that is occupied by the mortgagor as his or her principal residence; (2) that is owned or guaranteed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac; and (3) that was originated on or before the enactment of this Act. Requires the mortgagor to request the enterprise and the mortgagor's payment of a fee to the servicer of the mortgage to initiate the refinancing process.

National Nurse Act of 2011 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to establish within the Office of the Surgeon General of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) a full-time position, to be known as the National Nurse for Public Health, to be filled by a registered nurse.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to appoint the National Nurse for Public Health in accordance with Commissioned Corps Instruction CC23.4.6 (relating to Chief Professional Officer Nominations), as in effect on February 13, 2008.

Requires the appointment of the individual serving as the Chief Nurse Officer of the Public Health Service as of the date of enactment of this Act as the first National Nurse for Public Health.

Requires the National Nurse for Public Health to: (1) provide leadership and coordination of Public Health Service nursing professional affairs for the Office of the Surgeon General and other agencies of the Public Health Service, including providing representation for the U.S. government at the Global Forum for Government Chief Nursing and Midwifery Officers; (2) serve as a member of the Federal Nursing Service Council; (3) represent the Surgeon General and the Public Health Service in communications with groups and societies

White House Inspector General Act of 1996 - Amends the Inspector General Act of 1978 to provide that the President shall nominate an individual as the Inspector General of the Executive Office of the President. 
Provides that the Inspector General of the Executive Office of the President shall be under the authority, direction, and control of the President with respect to audits or investigations, or the issuance of subpoenas, which require access to information concerning:  (1) ongoing criminal investigations or proceedings; (2) undercover operations; (3) the identity of confidential sources, including protected witnesses; (4) deliberations and decisions on policy matters; (5) intelligence or counterintelligence matters; or (6) other matters the disclosure of which would constitute a serious threat to U.S. national security or cause significant impairment to the national interests. 
Authorizes the President to prohibit the Inspector General from carrying out or completing any audit or investigation or issuing any subpoena after the Inspector General has decided to initiate, carry out, or complete such audit or investigation or to issue such subpoena if the President determines that:  (1) the disclosure of that information would interfere with the core functions of the constitutional responsibilities of the President; and (2) the prohibition is necessary to prevent

Ensuring Quality in the Unemployment Insurance Program (EQUIP) Act This bill amends title III (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to require a state to provide to an eligible individual who is unemployed and receiving OASDI benefits a drug screen before the individual is paid regular compensation. The state may deny regular compensation to an individual who tests positive for a controlled substance.

Olympic Commemorative Coins Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, beginning in 1997, to issue one-dollar commemorative coins, each of which shall:  (1) weigh 26.73 grams; (2) have a diameter of 1.5 inches; (3) contain 90 percent silver and 10 percent alloy; and (4) bear the design selected by the Secretary. 
Directs the Secretary, in each year before a year in which the Summer or Winter Olympic Games are held in the United States, to develop an expanded multi-coin commemorative coins program. 
Requires the Secretary to pay surcharges received from coin sales to the United States Olympic Committee (USOC).  Requires that at least 25 percent of such surcharges be used for the objects and purposes of the Amateur Sports Act of 1978. 
Expresses the sense of Congress that each coin edition issued under this Act should be self-sustaining and should be administered so as not to result in any net cost to the Numismatic Public Enterprise Fund.

Bridge Ice and Snow Prevention Pilot Program Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and implement a pilot program to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the use of technologies to prevent ice, snow, and other adverse weather effects associated with freezing temperatures on bridges on the National Highway System (NHS).

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to up to five states to conduct projects under the pilot program. Requires the Secretary to select: (1) up to 20 highway bridges for participation in the program; and (2) technologies to be tested that are likely to improve bridge safety, extend the life of a bridge, and promote energy efficiency. Limits the federal share payable on account of a project carried out under the pilot program to 80% of the project cost. Requires the Secretary to carry out the pilot program for no more than five fiscal years.

Strategic Deterrent Sustainment Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to report to the congressional defense and appropriations committees on the capability of the U.S. industrial base to: (1) maintain, modernize, and sustain the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) system until at least 2030; and (2) replace the Minuteman III with a follow-on land-based strategic deterrent system after 2030.

Requires the Secretary's report to include: (1) a description of any current plans for extending the Minuteman III system after 2020 to 2030, including plans for testing sufficient to account for any aging and obsolescence found in the system and an assessment of the risks associated with such plans after the shutdown of associated production lines; (2) a description of any current plans to maintain the system after 2030, including an assessment of any risks associated with such plans after the shutdown of associated production lines; (3) an explanation why the Minuteman III system is no longer considered to be of the highest national defense urgency; (4) an analysis of existing commonalities between the service life extension program for

Television Violence Reduction Through Parental Empowerment Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require that apparatus designed to receive television signals be equipped with circuitry designed to enable viewers to block the display of channels, programs, and time slots.  Requires such apparatus to enable viewers to block display of all programs with a common rating. 
Prohibits persons from shipping, manufacturing, assembling, or importing such apparatus into the United States except in accordance with rules prescribed by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) pursuant to the authority granted by such Act.  Requires such rules to provide performance standards for such blocking technology.  Requires that all such apparatus be able to receive the rating signals which have been transmitted by way of line 21 of the vertical blanking interval and which conform to the signal and blocking specifications established by the FCC. 
Directs the FCC to take such action as it determines appropriate to ensure that blocking service continues to be available to consumers.

Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund Amendments Act of 1997 - Amends the Solid Waste Disposal Act to direct the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to distribute to States at least 85 percent of the funds appropriated to the Agency from the Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund each fiscal year for the reasonable costs under cooperative agreements entered into with the Administrator for:  (1) State actions under the remedial action program; (2) necessary administrative expenses directly related to corrective action and compensation programs; (3) enforcement of an approved State or local underground storage tank program or similar State or local provisions; (4) State and local corrective actions pursuant to regulations; and (5) corrective action and compensation programs for releases from underground storage tanks in any instance, as determined by the State, in which the financial resources of an owner or operator, excluding resources provided by such programs, are inadequate to pay the cost of a corrective action without significantly impairing the ability of the owner or operator to continue in business.  Prohibits the use of such funds by States for purposes of providing financial assistance to an owner or operator in meeting requirements respecting underground storage tanks contained in regulations and in effect on the date of enactment of this Act or in similar State programs.

Jobs Now Act of 2017 This bill amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to direct the Department of Labor to carry out a two-year pilot program to award competitive grants to general local government units or community-based organizations to retain, employ, or train employees providing a public service for such units.

Helping Individuals Return to Employment Act or the HIRE Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants for the hiring of unemployed individuals to benefit communities, particularly those in historically underutilized business zones and renewal communities with a high unemployment rate.

Requires such grants to be used to hire unemployed individuals residing in such communities, including individuals age 16 and older, with priority for those who have been unemployed for more than a year.

Prohibits: (1) an individual whose employment is funded under this Act from working for an employer at which a collective bargaining agreement is in effect covering the same or similar work, unless the consent of the labor organization at such employer is obtained and negotiations have taken place between such labor organization and the employer as to the terms and conditions of such employment; and (2) an individual whose employment is funded under this Act from displacing other employees whose employment is not funded under this Act. Prohibits a grant recipient from hiring an employee or employees with funds under this Act for any employment which the grant recipient would otherwise hire an employee who has been furloughed.

Provides that the amount of any unemployment compensation payable to an individual employed under a grant under this Act is a pro rata portion of the unemployment compensation which would otherwise

Congressional Medal of Honor Memorial Coin Act of 2003 - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue not more than 50,000 $5 gold coins and 250,000 $1 silver coins in commemoration of the recipients of the Congressional Medal of Honor. Requires the coin design to be emblematic of the values and abilities necessary to earn such medal, such as gallantry and intrepidity.

Authorizes the Secretary to issue the coins only between January 1, 2005, and December 31, 2005.

Requires any coin sale to include a surcharge of $35 per coin for the $5 coins and $10 per coin for the $1 coins. Requires the proceeds from such surcharges to be paid promptly to the Riverside National Cemetery Support Committee, a nonprofit organization established under the laws of California, for the purposes of: (1) maintaining the National Medal of Honor Memorial at Riverside National Cemetery; and (2) constructing and maintaining such memorials as the Riverside National Cemetery Support Committee and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs may jointly designate.
Amends Federal bankruptcy law to provide for the priority of claims for retiree health benefits in cases under chapter 7 and 11.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require tax-exempt organizations to provide to the public, on a specified annual return, the names and addresses of any officer, director, trustee, or highly compensated employee of the organization who, at any time before the date of the application: (1) was a member or employee of an organization described in this Act; (2) was an unindicted coconspirator with respect to a terror finance scheme of such organization; or (3) was an employee of any charity found liable for certain tax-exempt activities.

Eating Disorders Awareness, Prevention, and Education Act of 2003 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to include as a component of the school improvement program under title I of that Act programs to improve the identification of students with eating disorders, increase awareness of such disorders among parents and students, and train educators on effective eating disorder prevention and assistance methods.Directs the Secretary of Education to carry out a program to develop, distribute, and promote the broadcasting of public service announcements to improve public awareness and to promote the identification and prevention of eating disorders.Directs the National Center for Education Statistics and the National Center for Health Statistics to conduct a study on the impact eating disorders have on educational advancement and achievement.
Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 - Extends the farm security and rural investment program through FY2008 and the peanut storage program through FY2009.

Voluntary Opportunities for Increasing Contributions to Education Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer a credit for 75 percent of certain cash contributions to schools, with a maximum credit of $500 for individuals and $100,000 for corporations. Defines "qualified charitable contribution" as cash contributions to a school tuition organization, for the improvement, renovation, or construction of a school facility used primarily to provide education at the elementary or secondary level, and for the acquisition of computer technology or equipment, or for related training, for use in such a school facility.

Veterinary Workforce Expansion Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to award competitive grants to eligible entities to increase the number of veterinarians in the workforce.

Requires the Secretary to give preference to applicants that demonstrate a comprehensive approach by involving more than one school of veterinary medicine, department of comparative medicine, department of veterinary science, school of public health, or school of medicine that offers postgraduate training for veterinarians in a public health practice area.

Second Chance Voting Rights Act of 2006 - Prohibits the denial or abridgment of the right of a U.S. citizen to vote because that individual has been convicted of a criminal offense.

Authorizes the Attorney General to obtain declaratory or injunctive relief to remedy a violation of this Act. Provides for a private right of action for aggrieved persons.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a deduction for student loan payments by medical professionals practicing in rural areas.  Limits the amount of such deduction to $5,000.

Cocopah Lands Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to take specified lands in Yuma County, Arizona, into trust for the Cocopah Tribe of Arizona, if the Tribe transfers title to such lands to the Secretary and there are no recognized environmental problems or adverse legal claims to such lands, including outstanding liens, mortgages, or taxes owed.

Considers such lands to be part of the Tribe's initial reservation.

Provides that for the delivery of federal services to enrolled Tribe members, the Tribe's service area shall be Yuma County, Arizona.

Prohibits using such trust lands for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

National Icebreaker Fund Act of 2015 This bill establishes the National Icebreaker Fund in the Treasury to be available for obligation and expenditure only for: (1) construction, alteration, and renovation of icebreakers for the Coast Guard; and (2) lease or charter of such vessels.  Amounts in the fund may be obligated or expended only in amounts authorized by law.  The Department of the Interior shall deposit in the fund: (1) all funds appropriated to the department in which the Coast Guard is operating for construction, alteration, and renovation of icebreakers or for the lease or charter of such vessels; (2) all receipts from the disposition of such vessels by the federal government; (3) unobligated funds that are transferred to the fund; (4) contributions of money and proceeds of other contributions accepted by the bill; and (5) all funds appropriated to the Department of Defense or any other federal agency for construction, alteration, and renovation of icebreakers or for the lease or charter of such vessels.  The Department of the Interior may transfer to the fund any unobligated funds remaining from funds under the department's administrative control.  The Department of the Interior may accept from any person, foreign government, or

Authorizes the President to conclude an agreement with Mexico to establish the United States-Mexico Border Health Commission to:  (1) conduct a comprehensive needs assessment in the border area for the purposes of identifying, evaluating, preventing, and resolving health problems that affect the general population of the area; (2) implement the actions recommended by the needs assessment by assisting in the coordination of public and private efforts to prevent, resolve, and educate such population concerning such health problems; and (3) formulate recommendations to the U.S. and Mexican Governments concerning a fair and reasonable method by which the government of one country would reimburse a public or private person in the other country for the cost of a health care service that the person furnishes to a citizen or resident alien of the first country who is unable, through insurance or otherwise, to pay for the service. 
Authorizes the Commission to perform additional functions, including to conduct or sponsor investigations, research, or studies designed to identify, study, and monitor health problems that affect the general population in the border area. 
Requires the Commission to establish no fewer than two regional border offices. 
Directs the Commission to submit an annual report to both the U.S. and Mexican Governments regarding all Commission activities.

Authorizes the Secretary of Education to award a grant to Teach For America, Inc., the national teacher corps of outstanding recent college graduates who commit to teach for two years in underserved communities in the United States, to implement and expand its program of recruiting, selecting, training, and supporting new teachers.

Requires the Secretary, in carrying out such grant program, to enter into an agreement under which the grantee agrees to use grant funds to: (1) provide teachers to local educational agencies (LEAs) in urban and rural communities that are experiencing a shortage of highly qualified teachers; (2) pay the cost of recruiting, selecting, training, and supporting new teachers; and (3) serve a substantial number and percentage of underserved students.

Requires grant funds to be used by the grantee to carry out each of the following activities: (1) recruiting and selecting teachers through a highly selective national process; (2) providing preservice training to teachers through a rigorous summer institute that includes hands-on teaching experience and significant exposure to education coursework and theory; (3) placing teachers in schools and positions designated by LEAs as high need placements serving underserved students; and (4) providing ongoing professional development activities for teachers' first two years in the classroom, including regular classroom observations

EQIP Improvement Act of 2018 This bill amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to revise the environmental quality incentives program (EQIP) by: (1) limiting payments to 75% of costs associated with planning, design, materials, equipment, installation, labor, management, maintenance, or training (except for certain high-priority practices); (2) limiting payments to 100% of the income foregone by the producer; and (3) requiring the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to coordinate the EQIP program with the conservation effects assessments carried out by USDA to ensure that the assessments consider the practical limitations and costs and benefits encountered in implementing the program and to use the information collected through the assessments to direct funds of the program to contracts that will optimize environmental benefits.  The bill limits payments to: (1) 40% of the costs associated with planning, design, materials, equipment, installation, labor, management, maintenance, or training for certain high-priority land management practices or vegetative practices that are cost-effective means of addressing the most pressing specific impairments that threaten to degrade or impair water quality, water quantity, soil or related natural resources within a local watershed, or a specific natural resource

Requires the Secretary of Transportation, upon receiving a petition submitted by the sponsor of a commercial service airport (or by the attorney general of a State on behalf of one or more persons, including governmental entities, with respect to an airport) claiming that fares for scheduled air transportation at the airport are unreasonably high, or that competition between air carriers at the airport is inadequate, to investigate and hold a public hearing on the petition before the expiration of the 90-day period beginning on the date of receipt of the petition.  Requires:  (1) a public hearing to be held in the community served by the airport if requested in the petition and if practicable; (2) an air carrier providing air transportation at the airport to provide to the Secretary certain information concerning fares for air transportation and air service at the airport necessary to make findings in response to the petition; (3) a sponsor of an airport or a State attorney general submitting a petition to be provided an opportunity to testify at the public hearing; and (4) the Secretary to issue written findings in response to the issues raised in the petition. 
Authorizes the Secretary, if a new petition is received with respect to an airport for which the Secretary has previously conducted an investigation and public hearing, to decide not to

Jason's Law - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to implement a pilot program to address the shortage of long-term parking for commercial motor vehicles on the National Highway System (NHS).

Requires the Secretary to allocate funds made available for the program among states, metropolitan planning organizations, and local governments. Requires funds allocated to be used for projects that: (1) serve the NHS; and (2) include specified activities, such as construction of safety rest areas, of commercial motor vehicle parking facilities adjacent to commercial truck stops and travel plazas, opening existing facilities to commercial motor vehicle parking, and making capital improvements to public commercial motor vehicle parking facilities that are closed seasonally.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish a military occupational specialty transition (MOST) program to provide eligible veterans with skills relevant to the job market. Defines an "eligible veteran" as any veteran whose military occupational specialty at the time of discharge has limited transferability to the civilian job market, who is not otherwise eligible for education or training services, who has not acquired a marketable skill since leaving military service, who was discharged under conditions not less than general under honorable conditions, and who has been unemployed for at least 90 days during the 180-day period preceding the date of application for the program. Requires the program to provide for payments to employers who provide for eligible veterans a program of apprenticeship or on-the-job training if: (1) such program is approved; (2) the rate of pay for veterans participating in the program is not less than the rate of pay for nonveterans in similar jobs; and (3) the Secretary reasonably expects that the veteran will be qualified for employment in that field upon completion of training and the employer providing the program will hire the veteran at the completion of training. Sets forth requirements for payment to employers, including a monthly maximum of $20,000 and $1,666.6

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the expensing allowance for certain qualified Gulf Opportunity Zone property. Defines "qualified Gulf Opportunity Zone property" as property: (1) which is eligible for the expensing allowance for depreciable business property; (2) substantially all of the use of which is in the Gulf Opportunity Zone and is in the active conduct of a trade or business by the taxpayer in such Zone; (3) the original use of which in the Gulf Opportunity Zone commences with the taxpayer on or after August 28, 2005; (4) which is acquired by the taxpayer on or after August 28, 2005, but only if no written binding contract for the acquisition was in effect before August 28, 2005; and (5) which is placed in service by the taxpayer on or before December 31, 2007.

Enhanced Veteran Healthcare Experience Act of 2011 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) the current health care system of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is neither fiscally efficient nor effective in providing easily accessible treatment for all veterans; (2) health care can be provided more efficiently to provide veterans with care that is available closer to where they live and to allow veterans more flexibility in choosing their own doctors; and (3) better health care can be provided to veterans at little-to-no increased cost to the taxpayer by replacing the fee-based care system of the VA with the veterans enhanced care program and reprogramming funds to that program.

Revises the VA's enhanced contract care authority for health care needs to require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to contract with a non-VA provider for health services if VA facilities are not capable of furnishing such services. Sets forth criteria for a provider to be eligible for such contract, including that the provider: (1) demonstrates the ability to provide non-VA health care services to veterans; (2) meets or exceeds VA internal credentialing standards and Utilization Review Accreditation Commission standards; (3) has care coordinators who help veterans make, confirm, and keep medical appointments;

National Fab Lab Network Act of 2013 - Establishes the National Fab Lab Network as a federally-chartered nonprofit corporation to facilitate the creation of a national network of local fab labs (facilities equipped with an integrated suite of fabrication tools to convert digital designs into functional physical things and scanning tools to convert physical things into digital designs, and available for a range of individual and collaborative educational, commercial, creative, and social purposes, based on guidelines established by the National Fab Lab Network [NFLN]). Directs the NFLN to: (1) serve as the coordinating body for the creation of a national network of local fab labs in the United States, (2) provide a first point of contact for organizations and communities seeking to create fab labs, (3) link funders and sites with operational entities that can source and install fab labs, provide training, assist with operations, account for spending, and assess impact, (4) perform outreach for individuals and communities on the benefits available through the NFLN, (5) facilitate use of the NFLN in synergistic programs, such as workforce training, job creation, research broader impacts, and the production of civic infrastructure, and (6) offer transparency in the management, governance, and operation of the NFLN.

Post-Deployment Health Assessment Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to issue guidance for the provision of an in-person mental health screening for each member of the Armed Forces who is deployed in connection with a contingency operation. Excludes members who were not subjected or exposed to combat stress during deployment in the contingency operation concerned.

Requires the Secretary to share with the Secretary of Veterans Affairs such information on members of the Armed Forces that is derived from confidential mental health screenings, including screenings and health assessments and other in-person screenings provided before this Act's enactment, as the Secretaries consider appropriate to ensure continuity of mental health care and treatment of members of the Armed Forces during their transition from Department of Defense (DOD) to Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health care and treatment.

Drinking Water Affordability Act of 2016 This bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to revise the process for promulgating national primary drinking water regulations. Currently, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) must promulgate a new national primary drinking water regulation whenever a state establishes a drinking water quality standard that is not among the states' national primary drinking water standards. This bill eliminates the EPA's authority to revise national primary drinking water regulations unless a state transfers the regulatory authority to the EPA. The bill also revises the requirements for the revolving loan funds for disadvantaged communities. The current maximum loan term is 30 years. This bill increases the maximum loan term to 35 years. The EPA must approve the loan application within 18 months after the completion of the project for which the loan was made. The EPA must also approve the loan application within 18 months after the state has met the project's requirements. The EPA may extend the loan term for up to 40 years after the project's completion. The EPA must approve the loan application within 18 months after the state has met the project's requirements. The EPA must approve the loan application within 18 months after the state has met the project's requirements.

Consumer Credit Card Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to prohibit creditors from using any adverse information concerning any consumer, including any information in any consumer report or any change in the consumer's credit score, as the basis for increasing any annual percentage rate of interest (APR) applicable to a consumer's credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan, or to remove or increase any introductory APR applicable to such account, for reasons other than actions or omissions of the consumer directly related to such account.

Requires the limitation on the use of adverse information by a credit card issuer to be clearly and conspicuously described to the consumer in any required disclosure or statement.

Requires a creditor, in a clear and conspicuous manner, to disclose to a consumer the following repayment information regarding any outstanding balance on the account, including the required minimum monthly payment, the number of months it would take to pay the entire amount of the current outstanding balance if the consumer pays only the required minimum monthly payments and no further advances or extensions of credit are made with respect to such account: (1) the APR in effect on the date on which the disclosure is made; and (2) an APR based on an index, formula, or contractual provision that is, or

American Textile Technology Innovation and Research for Exportation (ATTIRE) Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a competitive grant program to fund textile research and innovation and to promote increased textile exports. Limits grant recipients to institutions of higher education and not-for-profit research institutions, including not-for-profit industry associations whose core mission is to support textile research and innovation. Requires preference in awarding such grants to collaborative research organizations that emphasize peer-reviewed research by leading academic and industry experts.  Requires funds authorized to be appropriated for the grant program to be used for research and development activities that achieve: (1) building and sustaining innovation, competitiveness, and best practices in the U.S. textile industry; (2) contributing to transforming the U.S. textile and apparel industry into a highly flexible supply chain capable of responding to rapidly changing market demands; (3) discovering, designing, and developing new materials, and innovative and improved manufacturing and integrated systems, essential to the success of a modern U.S. textile industry; (4) training personnel, establishing industrial partnerships, and creating transfer mechanisms to ensure the utilization of technologies developed; (5) strengthening the nation's textile research and educational efforts by uniting diverse experts and resources in unique collaborative projects; and (6) facilitating the creation of

Veterans Benefits Network Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make grants to an eligible entity (a state or local government, a regional council of governments, or a private entity) to establish or expand a regional technology system to provide an active database and enrollment system that can be used by a coordinated network of private, public, and nonprofit entities to assist veterans and their family members in applying for benefits and services offered by such entities that participate in the network.

Directs the Secretary to give priority to an eligible entity that provides services to individuals residing in a geographic area where a large number of veterans and members of the Armed Forces reside.

Counseling in Shelters Act of 2002 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Assistant Secretary for the Administration on Children, Youth, and Families, to make grants to eligible entities for the purpose of providing on site mental health and substance abuse counseling and referral services to women and children who have been subjected to domestic or sexual violence. Requires recipients to: (1) hire licensed professionals and dedicated staff to provide such counseling and services; and (2) provide training to those professionals.

Social Security Protection and Tax Relief Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a 12 percent tax on an individual's "social security taxable income." Defines such income. Decreases the old age, survivors, and disability income (social security taxes) tax rates.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow penalty-free withdrawals from individual retirement plans for: (1) first homebuyer residences; or (2) higher education expenses.

Lamprey Wild and Scenic River Act - Amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate the 11.5-mile segment of the Lamprey River in New Hampshire as a recreational river.  Requires the segment to be administered by the Secretary of the Interior through cooperative agreements between the Secretary and the State of New Hampshire and the towns of Durham, Lee, and Newmarket, New Hampshire, under provisions authorizing the Secretary to make agreements with the Secretary of the Interior for the purpose of assisting in the implementation of the Lamprey River Management Plan. 
Directs the Secretary to offer assistance concerning continued involvement of the town of Epping, New Hampshire, in the implementation of the Plan and in consideration of potential future addition of the portion of the river within Epping as a component of the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Police Gun Buyback Assistance Act - Authorizes the Attorney General to make grants to assist States and local governments in eliminating the practice of transferring decommissioned firearms to any person and in destroying decommissioned firearms.  Requires a State or local government to certify that it has in effect a law or policy that: (1) eliminates the practice of transferring decommissioned firearms to any person; and (2) provides for the destruction of a decommissioned firearm.  Allows a State or local government to transfer a decommissioned firearm to a law enforcement agency.  Requires a State or local government that receives a grant to only use that grant to purchase new firearms.

Amends the Bretton Woods Agreements Act to require the U.S. Governor of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to accept the amendments to the IMF Articles of Agreement approved by the Board of Governors of the IMF. 
Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to instruct the U.S. Executive Director of the IMF to seek an agreement to include the Bank for International Development (BID) as a prescribed holder of Special Drawing Rights (SDR).  Requires the Secretary to provide for the contribution to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, in each of FY 2004 through 2006, of one-third of the SDRs received by the United States pursuant to such amendments. 
Directs the Secretary to seek to enter into negotiations for the purpose of inducing the IMF member countries to contribute to the Global Fund the SDRs allocated pursuant to such amendments.

United States-Israel Homeland Security Foundation Act - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish a United States-Israel Homeland Security Foundation to award conditional grants to joint business ventures between U.S. and Israeli private corporate entities to develop, manufacture, sell, or otherwise provide products and services with applications related to homeland security.

Requires the Secretary to use not less than $25 million of the funds available in the Acceleration Fund for Research and Development of Homeland Security Technologies to administer the Foundation if it is established. Requires the Secretary to use not less than $25 million of such funds to support the efforts of the Binational Industrial Research and Development Foundation to make grants to joint U.S.-Israeli business ventures for projects related to homeland security if the Secretary decides not to establish the Foundation.

STEM Network Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make grants to eligible networks to expand science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education.

Defines "eligible" as a state-based STEM network or similar organization that: (1) aims to increase student achievement in the STEM disciplines at the elementary and secondary schools in its state, particularly at schools with a high concentration of low-income students and at rural schools; and (2) may include the participation of state officials, educators, administrators, parents, industry leaders, philanthropists, and representatives from the STEM communities.

Supporting Education for Returning Veterans Act of 2008 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award three-year grants to institutions of higher education to establish programs that support veterans who are students at such institutions by providing and coordinating services that address their academic, financial, physical, and social needs.

Requires each such program to include: (1) establishing a Center of Excellence for Veteran Student Success on the campus of the institution that provides a single point of contact to coordinate comprehensive support services for veterans who are students; (2) establishing a support team for veterans who are students; and (3) providing a full-time or part-time coordinator whose primary responsibility is to coordinate the program. Allows a program to include the following optional activities: (1) outreach to, and recruitment of, veterans; (2) supportive instructional services for veterans; (3) assistance in obtaining student financial aid; (4) housing support; (5) providing classes that are limited to veterans to help them fulfill general education requirements; and (6) providing activities designed to ease the transition of veterans to life on campus.

Requires the Secretary to develop an evaluation and accountability plan for such programs.

Export Enhancement Act of 1999 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to extend the OPIC (Organization for the Promotion of International Commerce) program.  Revises environmental standards. 
Revises the composition of the OPIC Board of Directors. 
Requires the Trade and Development Agency (TDA) to require corporations and other entities to:  (1) share the costs of feasibility studies and other project planning services funded by OPIC; and (2) reimburse the TDA those funds provided, if the corporation or entity succeeds in project implementation. 
Revises OPIC funding. 
Requires the Trade Promotion Coordinating Committee (TPCC) to:  (1) report on actions taken to eliminate the areas of overlap and duplication identified among Federal export promotion activities; (2) coordinate efforts to sponsor or promote any trade show or trade fair; (3) work with relevant State and national organizations, including the National Governors' Association, that have established trade promotion offices; and (4) report on actions taken to promote better coordination between State, Federal, and private sector export promotion activities. 
Amends the Export Enhancement Act of 1988 to change the reporting schedule for TPCC reports from September

Great Falls Preservation and Redevelopment Act of 1993 - Establishes the Great Falls Historic District in Paterson, New Jersey. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make grants to, and enter into cooperative agreements with, nonprofit entities for:  (1) the purchase of property or easements; (2) emergency stabilization; and (3) the establishment of a coordinated fund. 
Requires such grants and agreements to be used to carry out this Act, including an evaluation of the condition of historic and architectural resources and the environmental and flood hazard conditions within the District, as well as recommendations for rehabilitating, reconstructing, and adaptively reusing such resources, establishing gateways to the District, and restoring, improving, and developing raceways and adjacent areas. 
Authorizes the Secretary to enter into cooperative agreements with property owners within the District for the preservation and interpretation of such properties. 
Authorizes the Secretary to enter into cooperative agreements with New Jersey or any political subdivision for rendering, on a reimbursable basis, rescue, firefighting, and law enforcement services, cooperative assistance by nearby law enforcement and fire preventive agencies, and for other appropriate purposes. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Authorizes the Commandant of the Coast Guard to transfer to Presque Isle Township, Michigan, possession of the Historic Fresnel Lens from the Presque Isle Light Station Lighthouse.  Requires the Township to install the Lens in the Lighthouse to operate it as a Class I private aid to navigation.  Provides for reversion of the Lens and for the cessation of U.S. operation of aids to navigation at the Lighthouse upon such installation. 
Authorizes the Commandant to transfer to the Township any additional U.S. personal property related to the Lens that the Commandant considers appropriate for conveyance.  Requires the Commandant, if the Lens is conveyed to the Township, to convey any personal property previously transferred to the Township. 
Requires the Township to:  (1) operate the Lens as a Class I private aid to navigation; and (2) hold the United States harmless for any claim arising with respect to personal property conveyed. 
Prohibits further conveyance of an interest in such property without the Commandant's advance approval.  Provides for the reversion of the Lens and for the cessation of U.S. operation of aids to navigation at the Lighthouse upon such further conveyance.

Katie Sepich Enhanced DNA Collection Act of 2010 - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to provide for incentive payments to states for the implementation of minimum and enhanced DNA collection processes.

Provides for a 5% bonus to states that implement a minimum DNA collection process and use it for a year, and a 10% bonus to states that implement an enhanced DNA collection process and use it for a year, over the next fiscal year.

Defines "minimum DNA collection process" as a process under which the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is searched at least one time against samples from certain individuals who are at least 18 years of age: (1) who are arrested for, charged with, or indicted for a criminal offense under state law that consists of murder or voluntary manslaughter or any attempt to commit murder or manslaughter; (2) who are arrested for, charged with, or indicted for a criminal offense under state law that has an element involving a sexual act or sexual contact with another and that is punishable by imprisonment for more than 5 years, or an attempt to commit such an offense; or (3) who are arrested for, charged

Hardship Outlays to protect Mortgagee Equity (HOME) Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the tax on early distributions from tax-exempt retirement plans, for purposes of determining the aggregate lifetime dollar limitation, distributions used to pay qualified principal residence mortgage payments.

American Opportunity Tax Credit Extension Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make permanent the Hope Scholarship tax credit; (2) increase the amount of such credit to 100% of qualified tuition and related expenses (currently, 75%) that do not exceed $2,000, plus 25% of such expenses that exceed $2,000 but do not exceed $4,000; (3) allow such credit for four years (currently, two years); (4) include course materials in the definition of "qualified tuition and related expenses" for purposes of such credit; and (5) increase the tax credit amount and income limits for such credit.

.  Kissimmee River Wild and Scenic River Study Act of 2018 (Sec. 3) This bill amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate the segment of the Kissimmee River in Florida as a potential addition to the National Wild and Scenic River System.  The Department of the Interior must study and report on the effects of this designation.

Small Company Capital Formation Act of 2011 - Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to direct the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to add a class of securities to the securities exempted under the Act in accordance with the following terms and conditions: (1) the aggregate offering amount of all securities offered and sold within the prior 12-month period in reliance on such exemption shall not exceed $50 million; (2) such securities may be offered and sold publicly; (3) such securities shall not be restricted securities; (4) the civil liability provision in the Act shall apply to any person offering or selling such securities; (5) the SEC may solicit interest in the offering before filing any offering statement, on such terms and conditions as it may prescribe in the public interest or for the protection of investors; (6) the SEC shall require the issuer to file audited financial statements with it annually; and (7) such other terms, conditions, or requirements as the SEC may determine necessary in the public interest and for the protection of investors, which may include a requirement that the issuer prepare and electronically file with the SEC and distribute to prospective investors an offering statement, and any related documents, in such form and with such content as

Custodial Interrogation Recording Act - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to direct the Attorney General to make grants to states and local governments to achieve the complete and accurate recording, by both audio and video means, of every custodial interrogation occurring within such state or local government. Prohibits the portion of the costs of a program funded by a grant under this Act from exceeding 75%. Defines "custodial interrogation" as questioning or other conduct by a law enforcement officer which is reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response from an individual and occurs when reasonable individuals in the same circumstances would consider themselves in custody.

Worker-Executive Parity Act of 2009 - Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to prohibit deferred compensation arrangements for disqualified directors or executive officers of a single-employer defined benefit plan from accruing to a plan year in which the annual limit on benefits and benefit accruals imposed on a defined benefit plan for a plan year in which the plan sponsor is a governmental entity exceeds a specified amount.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a community-based overweight and obesity prevention program. Requires the Secretary to award grants and contracts to eligible entities to: (1) plan evidence-based programs for the prevention of overweight and obesity among children and their families through improved nutrition and increased physical activity; or (2) implement such programs. Defines "eligible" as a community partnership that demonstrates community support and includes specified stakeholders. Grants the period of five years, subject to renewal.

Authorizes the Secretary to award a grant or contract to an entity only if the entity: (1) demonstrates that it will establish a steering committee to provide input on the assessment of, and recommendations on improvements to, the entity's program funded through the grant or contract; and (2) has conducted or will conduct an assessment of the overweight and obesity problem in its community.

Requires the Secretary to give preference to eligible entities that: (1) will serve communities with high levels of overweight and obesity and related chronic diseases; or (2) will plan or implement activities for the prevention of overweight and obesity in school or workplace settings.
Tax Equity Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide regional cost-of-living adjustments in individual income tax rates.

Mud Dump Permanent Closure and Remediation Act of 2000 - Amends the Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act of 1972 to prohibit dumping at the Historic Area Remediation Site (a site known by that name that is located east of Sandy Hook, New Jersey) after the date of enactment of this Act.  Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, after the date of issuance of standards for remediation materials, to issue permits authorizing the transportation of dredged materials to the Site solely for the purpose of providing for remediation of the site.  Prohibits the Secretary from issuing any further permits authorizing the transportation of dredged materials to the site for any purpose upon satisfying the goal specified in this Act. 
Requires the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop and publish in the Federal Register standards for evaluating dredged materials to be used solely for remediation purposes at the Site.  Requires the Administrator to ensure that the materials used for remediation:  (1) contain significantly lower levels of contaminants than exist at the Site; (2) will significantly reduce contamination levels in biota and sediments at the Site; and (3) will reduce both the number, extent, and magnitude of undesirable
