Emergency Mortgage Loan Modification Act of 2008 - Sets forth a standard for a servicer of pooled residential mortgage loans to implement a modification or plan of action (or, if such action is unsuccessful or infeasible, engage in other loss mitigation, including accepting a short payment or partial discharge of principal or agreeing to a short sale of the property) to the extent that the servicer believes the particular action will maximize the net present value realized on the loan, including over that which would be realized through foreclosure.

Deems a servicer of residential mortgage loans to be acting on behalf of the securitization vehicle in the best interest of all investors and holders of beneficial interests in the pooled loans, in the aggregate, if for a loan in default, the loan servicer makes reasonable and documented efforts to implement a modification or plan of action, or engages in other loss mitigation, including acceptance of a short payment or partial discharge of principal or agreeing to a short sale of the property, if the servicer believes the particular action will maximize the net present value realized on the loan.

Deems a servicer of residential mortgage loans that acts in a manner consistent with the duty set forth in this Act to be immune from liability for entering into a qualified loan modification or plan of

International Commerce Enhancement Act - Amends the Arms Export Control Act to: (1) authorize the President to approve the export of defense articles and services to any country for which the value of such export is at least $25 billion (currently, $14 billion); and (2) waive certain military export controls for defense articles and services for which the value of such export is at least $85 billion (currently, $50 billion) and for which the President has reason to believe that such articles or services will be used for cooperative research and development (CRD) in support of a foreign military operation.

Provides that the waiver of such military export controls shall not apply in the case of a proposed transfer to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), or any member country of such Organization, Japan, Australia, or New Zealand.

Waives certain requirements for the certification of a proposed sale to a country other than a country which is a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, Japan, Australia, or New Zealand, or to any other organization, if the Congress, within 30 days after receiving such certification, or with respect to a proposed sale to any other country or organization, certifies that such sale is for defense articles and services for which the value of

Rush Hour Congestion Relief Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish and implement a traffic incident management program to assist States and localities in: (1) regional traffic incident management planning; and (2) carrying out projects to mitigate the effects of traffic delays resulting from accidents, breakdowns, and other non-recurring incidents on highways.

Authorizes the use of funds apportioned to a State under this Act for: (1) regional collaboration and coordination activities that lead to regional traffic incident management policies, programs, plans, procedures, and agreements; (2) purchase or lease of telecommunications equipment for first responders as part of the development of a regional traffic incident management program; (3) purchase or lease of equipment to support the clearance of traffic incidents; (4) payments to contractors for towing and recovery services as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (5) rental of vehicle storage or staging areas immediately adjacent to roadways as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (6) traffic service patrols as part of a regional traffic incident management program; (7) enhanced hazardous materials incident response; (8) traffic management systems in support of traffic incident management; (9) traffic incident management training; (10)

Safer Trucks and Buses Act of 2015 This bill requires the Department of Transportation (DOT) to ensure that covered motor carrier Compliance, Safety, Accountability Safety Measurement System scores and performance data is not made available to the public.  Covered motor carrier data may not be admitted into evidence or used in a civil action for damages resulting from an incident involving a motor carrier.  DOT must enter into an agreement with the National Academy of Public Administration to have the Academy study and report on how to improve the Compliance, Safety, Accountability initiative of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

Colorectal Cancer Detection Act of 2018  This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of colorectal cancer screening blood-based tests.  The bill establishes a frequency limit for colorectal cancer screening tests and sets forth a payment amount for qualifying colorectal cancer screening blood-based tests.

Infertility Research Centers Act of 2002 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health to make grants to, or enter into contracts with, public or nonprofit private entities for the development and operation of centers to conduct activities for the purpose of improving methods of preventing infertility.Directs the Director to provide for the establishment of two such centers.Requires each center to: (1) conduct clinical and other applied research, including clinical trials of new or improved drugs and devices for the diagnosis and treatment of infertility in males and females; (2) develop protocols for training physicians, scientists, nurses, and other health and allied health professionals; (3) conduct training programs for such individuals; (4) develop model continuing education programs for such professionals; and (5) disseminate information to such professionals and the public.Authorizes a center to provide stipends for health and allied health professionals enrolled in programs under this Act, and to provide fees to individuals serving as subjects in clinical trials.Authorizes appropriations.Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to enter into agreements with qualified health professionals under which such health professionals agree to conduct research with respect to infertility prevention, in consideration of the Government agreeing to repay, for each year of such service, not more

Forest Service Administrative Review Act - Amends the Forest Service Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to establish by regulation a pre-decisional administrative review process that will serve as the sole means by which a person can seek administrative review regarding proposed actions that would have an adverse effect on the healthy forest ecosystem of the state of Washington. Requires the Secretary to provide notice of, and distribute, the proposed decision along with the final environmental assessment or environmental impact statement (EIS) following the conclusion of the pre-decisional administrative review process for such an action. Exempts an action from such pre-decisional review process if the Chief of the Forest Service determines that an emergency situation exists for which immediate implementation of the action is necessary. Directs the Forest Service, in the case of an action exempted from such pre-decisional review, to: (1) provide notice of the final decision for the proposed action, and (2) provide for an expedited post-decisional review process. Allows the Forest Service to implement an action exempted from such pre-decisional review immediately after notice is provided of such action's final decision and implementation. Applies specified provisions of the Healthy Forests Restoration Act of 2003 regarding judicial review and requests

Federal Reserve Accountability Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Comptroller General to conduct reviews of the accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls of credit facilities established by the Federal Reserve Board or any federal reserve bank, including when such activities are carried out by or on behalf of the Board or any official of a federal reserve bank.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from disclosing to any person or entity, including to Congress, the names or identifying details of specific participants in any of the audited facilities or identifying details regarding assets or collateral held by, under, or in connection with any of the audited facilities. Requires a nondisclosure obligation to expire and the Comptroller General to release a nonredacted version of any reports on specific credit facilities one year after termination of the relevant credit facility.

Authorizes the Comptroller General to make and retain copies of books, accounts, and other records provided by an agency as the Comptroller General deems appropriate. Grants the Comptroller General access to the officers, employees, contractors, and other agents and representatives of any single and specific partnership or corporation or any credit facility established by an agency.

Directs the Board to place on its home website a link entitled "Audit" which shall link to

Cures Can Be Found Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for: (1) the donation of qualified stem cell research and storage contributions; and (2) the payment of certain expenses related to qualified stem cell research and storage.

Regulatory Integrity Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires the head of each executive agency to make publicly available on the agency website or in the regulations.gov rulemaking docket a searchable list of: (1) pending agency regulatory actions, and (2) public communications about those actions.  The list must include:   the date the agency began developing or considering the action, its status, an estimate of the date it will be final and in effect, a brief description, and a list of actions issued by the agency that duplicate or overlap with it; and  the findings of a regulatory impact analysis, if one has been conducted.  Each public communication must specify whether the agency is considering alternatives, accepting or will be accepting comments, and is the source of the information to the intended recipients.  The bill sets forth reporting requirements.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to: (1) develop and issue public service announcements that advertise and promote the pharmacist profession, highlight its advantages and rewards, and encourage individuals to enter the profession; (2) award grants to support State and local advertising campaigns to promote the pharmacist profession, highlight its advantages and rewards, and encourage individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds to enter the profession; and (3) establish a demonstration project to enhance the participation of pharmacists in the National Health Service Corps Loan Repayment Program.

Authorizes the Secretary to make awards of grants or contracts to qualifying schools of pharmacy for the purpose of assisting such schools in acquiring and installing computer-based systems to provide pharmaceutical education.

Knife Owners' Protection Act of 2017 This bill allows a person who is not otherwise prohibited by federal law from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a knife or knives to transport them from any place where such person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport such a knife or knives to any other place where such person may lawfully do so if: (1) in the case of transportation by motor vehicle, the knife or knives are not directly accessible from the passenger compartment or are in a locked container, glove compartment, or console; or (2) in the case of transportation by other means, the knife or knives are contained in a locked container.  Any knife or tool designed for enabling escape in an emergency incorporating a blunt tipped safety blade, a guarded blade, or both, for cutting safety belts may be carried in the passenger compartment and need not be secured in a locked container, glove compartment, or console. This bill shall not apply to the transport of any such knife or tool in the passenger cabin of aircraft whose passengers are subject to airport screening procedures of the Transportation Security Administration.  A person who is transporting a knife or knives in compliance with this bill may not be arrested or otherwise detained for violation of any state or local law related to the possession

Child Modeling Exploitation Prevention Act - Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to prohibit an employer from employing a child model in exploitive child modeling (modeling involving the use of a child under age 17 for financial gain without the purpose of marketing a product or service other than the image of the child). Defines "exploitive child modeling" as modeling involving the use of a child under age 17 for financial gain without the purpose of marketing a product or service other than the image of the child.

Includes employment of a minor in violation of such prohibition as oppressive child labor.

Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit, with the intent to make a financial gain, the display or offering of the image of an individual engaged in exploitive child modeling. Exempts an image which, taken as a whole, has serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value.

Presidential Transition Act of 2000 - Amends the Presidential Transition Act of 1963 to require the President, during the transition period, to pay expenses for briefings, workshops, or other activities to acquaint key prospective Presidential appointees with the types of problems and challenges that most typically confront new political appointees when they make the transition from campaign and other prior activities to assuming the responsibility for governance after inauguration.Directs the Administrator of the Office of Management and Budget to develop a transition directory based upon such activities.Requires the Office of Government Ethics to study and report to specified congressional committees on improvements to the financial disclosure process for Presidential nominees required to file reports under the Ethics in Government Act of 1978.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to transfer certain reservation land in North Dakota to the Secretary of the Interior to be held in trust for the benefit of the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe.  Directs the Secretary of the Army to convey such land to the state of North Dakota.

International Remittance Services Enhancement and Protection Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Credit Union Act to require a financial institution or money transmitting business initiating an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer to provide specified disclosures to the consumer before consummation of the transaction.Requires the appropriate federal agencies to jointly prescribe regulations that require any such institution or business to provide specified disclosures to a consumer initiating an international money transfer before consummation of the transaction.

Animal Agriculture Environmental Incentives Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer animal feeding operation a credit for 25 percent of the eligible nutrient management costs of the operation.  Defines "eligible nutrient management costs" as amounts paid or incurred to purchase a calibrated manure spreader or eligible processing equipment for use at an animal feeding operation.
Provides for a one-year extension of the date for compliance by certain covered entities with administrative simplification standards for electronic transactions and code sets.

Protection from Sexual Predators Act of 1997 - Expresses the sense of the Congress that States should:  (1) more seriously consider the relatively high recidivism rate of sexual offenders when deciding whether to plea bargain with first-time sexual offenders and whether to grant parole to sexual offenders; and (2) review their treatment and parole supervision programs for sexual offenders to assure that such programs are fulfilling their goals, and if not, replace or abandon such programs. 
Amends the Federal criminal code to subject to life imprisonment any person who, in a specified circumstance, violates provisions of such code or engages in conduct that would violate such provisions, if the conduct had occurred in U.S. special maritime and territorial jurisdiction and:  (1) that conduct is in interstate or foreign commerce; (2) the person engaging in that conduct crossed a State line with intent to engage in such conduct; or (3) the person thereafter engages in conduct that is a violation of provisions regarding sex offenses. 
Amends the Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act of 1994 to make a State ineligible for a grant under such Act unless it has provided assurances to the Attorney General that it has in effect laws which allow the court to impose a sentence of life in

Meat and Poultry Products Traceability and Safety Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Meat Inspection Act and the Poultry Products Inspection Act to require that cattle, sheep, swine, goats, and horses, mules, and other equines presented for slaughter for human food purposes, and the carcasses or parts of carcasses and the meat and meat food products of those animals, shipped in interstate commerce, be identified in a manner that enables the Secretary of Agriculture to trace: (1) each animal to any premises or other location at which the animal was held at any time before slaughter; and (2) each carcass or part of a carcass and meat and meat food product of such animals forward from slaughter through processing and distribution to the ultimate consumer.

Requires the Secretary to establish a traceability system for all stages of production, processing, and distribution of meat and meat food products and poultry and poultry food products that are produced through such slaughtering.

Veterans Timely Access to Health Care Act - Requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to prescribe an appropriate standard for access to care, applicable to waiting times at VA health-care facilities, for a veteran seeking primary care from the VA, which shall be 30 days. Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to: (1) periodically review the performance of VA health-care facilities compared to such standard; and (2) submit to the congressional veterans' committees an annual report providing an assessment of VA performance in meeting such standard. Provides that such requirement shall not apply to a veteran enrolled or seeking care at a VA facility within a VA geographic service area that has a compliance rate of 90% or more. Directs the Secretary to make such compliance rate determination not later than July 1 of the first calendar year after enactment of this Act. Requires the Secretary to submit to such committees a comprehensive report on the experience of the VA during each calendar quarter with respect to waiting times for veterans seeking appointments with a VA health-care provider.

Historically Women's Public Colleges or Universities Historic Building Restoration and Preservation Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to award grants to historically women's public colleges or universities for the preservation and restoration of historic buildings and structures on their campuses.  Requires such grants to be awarded from amounts appropriated to carry out the National Historic Preservation Act (16 U.S.C. 470 et seq.) for FY 2001 through 2005.  Sets forth matching requirements for buildings and structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places.  Limits the amount of funds available for such grants to $16 million for FY 2001 through 2005.

Global Investments in America's Cities Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require at least 3,000 of the visas made available under such Act to be reserved for qualified immigrants seeking to invest in a new commercial enterprise which will create employment in an economically distressed urban area. Requires such visas to be reserved for aliens who: (1) have invested or are actively investing in the new enterprise; (2) have completed an investment agreement with a qualified venture capital operating company for an investment in that new enterprise of at least $250,000; or (3) have completed an investment agreement with one or more angel investors for an investment in that new enterprise of at least $250,000.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on the EB-5 Visa Program.

Small Business Expansion and Hiring Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for the retention of certain individuals newly hired before 2013. Defines "retained worker" as a qualified individual who: (1) was employed by the taxpayer on any date during the taxable year, (2) was so employed for a period of not less than 52 consecutive weeks, and (3) whose wages for such employment during the last 26 weeks of such period equaled at least 80% of such wages for the first 26 weeks of such period. Allows a limited credit for a business location.

Making Education Affordable Act This bill amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Department of Education (ED) to award grants to institutions of higher education that carry out dual or concurrent enrollment programs or early college high school programs that enable high school students to earn college credits while in high school. ED shall give priority to institutions that serve students from low-income families, students from rural communities, or students who are the first in their family to receive postsecondary education. Institutions shall use grant funds to:  carry out such programs; provide teachers, principals, and other school leaders with professional development activities that enhance the provision of such programs; and  support activities such as curriculum design, establishment of a course articulation process, outreach programs to provide elementary school and secondary school students information about and academic preparation for the transition programs, helping students meet eligibility criteria for postsecondary courses, and coordinating secondary and postsecondary support services and academic calendars.  Institutions may use grant funds for costs associated with carrying out such programs, including the costs of: (1) tuition and fees, books, and required instructional materials; and (2) transportation to and from such programs.

Helping Responsible Homeowners Act - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to each carry out a program to provide for the refinancing of qualified mortgages on single-family housing owned by such enterprise through a refinancing mortgage, and for the purchase of and securitization of such refinancing mortgages, in accordance with this Act and policies and procedures that the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) shall establish. Prohibits the FHFA Director from charging the mortgagee any up-front fee beyond the standard guarantee fee for the refinancing of the qualified mortgage through the refinancing mortgage. Makes new mortgages originated by a servicer or creditor who refuses to resubordinate a second lien on a qualified mortgage who is ineligible for purchase or guarantee by such associations. Terminates the requirement for an enterprise to refinance qualified mortgages under this Act after the one-year period after the enactment of this Act. Directs the Director, at his or her discretion, to extend the program in one-year increments.

Women's Human Rights Protection Act of 1993 - Declares that the Congress believes that abuses against women would have greater visibility and protection of women's human rights if the advocate were responsible for integrating women's human rights issues into U.S. human rights policy. 
Directs the Secretary of State to report to the Congress on the steps taken to create the position of special assistant to the Assistant Secretary to promote international women's human rights within the overall human rights policy of the Government of the United States. 
Directs the Secretary to report to the Congress if the United Nations Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) has not been submitted for ratification to the Senate.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to include the use, sale, or exchange of infrastructure property (as defined by this Act) as qualifying income for purposes of determining publicly traded partnership status. Defines "infrastructure property" to include property related to roads and improvements, train tracks and improvements, airports, docks and wharves, sewage facilities, solid waste disposal facilities, electricity transmission and distribution, natural gas transmission and distribution, and communications facilities. Exempts from the tax deduction for income from domestic production activities the income derived from publicly traded partnerships. Makes the activities of publicly traded partnerships eligible for the tax deduction for income from distribution and transmission of funds. Makes infrastructure property eligible for accelerated cost recovery systems. Provides for the tax deduction for exchange of property held for productive use or investment to apply to all infrastructure property.

Independent Pharmacy Protection Act of 2006 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require each contract with a prescription drug plan (PDP) sponsor under Medicare part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) to provide for: (1) direct deposit payments to pharmacies for covered part D drugs; (2) increased dispensing fees for generic drugs; and (3) payments within ten days to a participating pharmacy that is not part of a chain of pharmacies consisting of more than three pharmacies at different locations for a covered part D drug dispensed through the pharmacy.

Requires the payment of dispensing fees to encourage use of generic drugs.

Prohibits a prescription drug plan from decreasing the amount of the dispensing fee paid by the plan to a participating pharmacy for a brand name drug to an amount less than the amount paid by such plan for such drug on enactment of this Act. Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to waive such prohibition for a dispensing fee paid by a plan for a brand name drug.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish the Return of Talent Program to permit eligible aliens to temporarily return to their country of citizenship in order to make a material contribution to it if the country is engaged in post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction activities, for a period not exceeding 24 months, unless an exception is granted.

Makes eligible for such Program an immigrant who: (1) has been lawfully admitted to the United States for permanent residence; (2) demonstrates an ability and willingness to make a material contribution to the post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction in the alien's country of citizenship; and (3) is a U.S. citizen of a country in which U.S. Armed Forces are engaged in combat or peacekeeping operations, or a country which has received funding from the U.S. Agency for International Development in response to a declared U.N.-initiated disaster, that is beyond the ability of such country's response capacity and warrants a U.S. Government response.

Lifelong Improvements in Food and Exercise (LIFE) Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to carry out a national program to conduct and support activities regarding individuals who are overweight or obese in order to make progress toward the goal of significantly reducing the number of cases of obesity among individuals in the United States.

Requires the Secretary to carry out, with respect to individuals who are overweight, the following: (1) activities to train health professionals to recognize that patients are overweight and to recommend prevention activities regarding such condition, including educating patients on the relationship between such condition and cardiovascular disease, diabetes and other health conditions, and on proper nutrition and regular physical activities; (2) activities to educate the public with respect to the condition of being overweight, including the development of a strategy for a public awareness campaign; and (3) the development and demonstration of intervention strategies for use at worksites and in community settings, such as hospitals and community health centers.

SOAR to Health and Wellness Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a pilot program, to be known as Stop, Observe, Ask, and Respond to Health and Wellness Training (or SOAR to Health and Wellness Training), to provide training to health care providers and other related providers, at all levels, on human trafficking. The pilot program shall train providers to: (1) identify potential human trafficking victims; (2) work with law enforcement to report and facilitate communication with such victims; (3) refer victims to social or victims service agencies or organizations; and (4) provide such victims with coordinated, victim centered, culturally relevant, comprehensive, evidence based, gender responsive, age appropriate, and trauma informed care. HHS shall collect data on the number of facilities operating under the pilot program and the number of providers trained through the pilot program during FY2018-FY2022.

Seniors Financial Fraud Prevention Act of 2010 - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to establish a separate office within the FTC to prevent fraud targeting seniors and to assist the FTC with: (1) monitoring the market for mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud targeting seniors; (2) disseminating to seniors and families and caregivers of seniors general information on mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud targeting seniors, as well as information on means of referring complaints of fraud targeting seniors to appropriate law enforcement agencies; and (3) establishing procedures to log and acknowledge receipt of complaints by individuals who believe they have been the victim of fraud in connection with the conduct of mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet.

Community Health Center Volunteer Provider Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to provide liability protection for volunteer practitioners providing services to patients at health centers under the Act.

Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Database Act of 2004 or Dru's Law - Directs the Attorney General to: (1) make publicly available in a registry (the public registry) all information contained in the National Sex Offender Registry, via the Internet, regarding a person convicted of a criminal offense against a victim who is a minor or a sexually violent offense or a sexually violent predator; and (2) allow users of the public registry to determine which registered sex offenders are currently residing within a specified radius of a location indicated by the user of the public registry.

Requires the public registry to provide, to the extent available, specified information regarding such person, including: (1) the name and any known aliases; (2) the date of birth; (3) the current address and any subsequent changes of address; (4) a physical description and current photograph; (5) the nature of and date of commission of the offense; (6) the date on which the person is released from prison, or placed on parole, supervised release, or probation; and (7) any other information the Attorney General considers appropriate.

Gerardo Hernandez Airport Security Act of 2014 - Directs the Assistant Secretary of Homeland Security (Transportation Security) (TSA) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to: (1) conduct outreach to all U.S. airports at which the TSA performs, or oversees the implementation and performance of, security measures, and provide technical assistance as necessary, to verify such airports have in place individualized working plans for responding to security incidents inside the airport's perimeter, including active shooters, acts of terrorism, and incidents that target passenger-screening checkpoints; and (2) identify best practices that exist across airports for security incident planning, management, and training and establish a mechanism through which to share such best practices with other airport operators nationwide.  Directs the Assistant Secretary to: (1) certify to specified congressional committees that all screening personnel have participated in practical training exercises for active shooter scenarios, and (2) provide an analysis of how the TSA can use cost savings achieved through efficiencies to increase over the next five fiscal years the funding available for checkpoint screening law enforcement support reimbursable agreements. Stock Option Accounting Reform Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require an issuer of securities to disclose in its annual report on securities registration the fair value of all stock options granted to its executives and key employees after December 31, 2004.

Exempts small business issuers and requires the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to study the economic impact of mandatory expensing of all employee stock options.

Livestock Concentration Report Act - Establishes a Commission on Concentration in the Livestock Industry to:  (1) determine whether the study of concentration in the red meat packing industry adequately examined and identified procurement markets for slaughter cattle in the continental United States, analyzed the effects that slaughter cattle procurement practices, and concentration in the procurement of slaughter cattle, have on the purchasing and pricing of slaughter cattle by beef packers, examined the use of captive cattle supply arrangements by beef packers and the effects of the arrangements on slaughter cattle markets, examined the economics of vertical integration and of coordination arrangements in the hogslaughtering and processing industry, examined the pricing and procurement by hogslaughtering plants operating in the Eastern corn belt, reviewed pertinent research literature on issues relating to the structure and operation of the meat packing industry, and reviewed the farm-to-retail price spread for livestock during the period beginning on January 1, 1993, and ending on the date the report is submitted; (2) request the Attorney General to report on the application of the antitrust laws and operation of other Federal laws applicable, with respect to concentration and vertical integration in the procurement and pricing of slaughter cattle and of slaughter hogs by meat packers; (3) review laws and regulations

Law Enforcement Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Federal criminal code to authorize an individual to carry a concealed firearm if that individual is:  (1) a qualified law enforcement officer or a qualified former law enforcement officer; and (2) carrying appropriate written identification. 
Declares that this Act shall not be construed to:  (1) exempt from Federal or State firearms laws prohibiting or restricting the possession of a firearm on Federal or State property; or (2) supersede or limit the laws of any State that grant rights to carry a concealed firearm that are broader than the rights granted under this Act or permit private persons or entities to prohibit or restrict the possession of concealed firearms on their property. 
Authorizes the consent of the Congress to any two or more States to enter into compacts or agreements for cooperative effort in enabling individuals to carry concealed weapons as dictated by State laws and to establish agencies or guidelines for making effective such agreements.  Reserves the right to alter, amend, or repeal this Act.

Art-in-Architecture Act of 1993 - Requires that not less than one-half percent of the funds made available for new construction, building purchase, acquisition, or prospectus-level repair and alteration projects be made available for art projects for the building.  Authorizes the Administrator to increase or decrease such percentage amount for a project warranting more or less artwork. 
Requires the preliminary planning and design of each new Federal building to include planning for art commissions. 
Requires the Administrator to commission works of art by living American artists to be placed in Federal buildings. 
Requires the Administrator to:  (1) establish procedures for commissioning works of art, with an emphasis on the participation of community representatives; and (2) publicize each prospective art project and give artists a reasonable period of time to respond for consideration. 
Requires the Administrator to provide for necessary services to maintain and preserve the works of art in a state of high quality. 
Requires the agency fine arts officer to maintain a registry of portfolios and statements of qualifications for artists interested in being considered for art projects.

Promoting Self-Reliance for the World's Poorest Act of 2002 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to reauthorize and increase the amounts of specified microenterprise development credits.Authorizes the Administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development (AID) to provide for the development of methods to measure the level of poverty of clients of sustainable poverty-focused microenterprise programs. Requires the Administrator to implement interim and final poverty measurement methods for such programs.

Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge Act - Establishes the Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge as an international wildlife refuge area.

Bright Idea Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to initiate a project to establish technical standards for general service lamps. Requires the Secretary to take necessary action to require that at least 95% of lamps sold, offered for sale, or otherwise made available in the United States meet such standards if the Secretary determines that such lamps are generally available for purchase throughout the United States at costs that are substantially equivalent to the cost of the lamps they would replace.

Requires the Secretary to report periodically to specified congressional committees on the development and promulgation of standards for lamps and lamp-related technology.

Authorizes the Secretary to carry out a lighting technology research and development program to: (1) support the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of lamps and related technologies sold, offered for sale, or otherwise made available in the United States; and (2) assist manufacturers of general service lamps in the manufacturing of lamps that achieve specified lumens per watt ratings.

Directs the Secretary to carry out a comprehensive national program to educate consumers about the benefits of using light bulbs that have improved efficiency ratings.

Directs the Secretary, in cooperation with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), to report to Congress on recommendations relating to the means by which the federal

.  Traveler Redress Improvement Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) to ensure the availability of the DHS Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (DHS TRIP) redress process to adjudicate inquiries for individuals who: (1) are U.S. citizens or lawfully resident aliens who have received enhanced screening at an airport passenger security checkpoint three or more times in any 60-day period; and (2) believe they have been wrongly identified as a threat to aviation security.  The TSA must: (1) report on the implementation of the redress process, (2) review and update the Privacy Impact Assessment for Secure Flight programs to ensure such assessment accurately reflects the operation of such programs, and (3) conduct a comprehensive review of its intelligence-based screening rules every 120 days.  The Office of Intelligence Analysis of the TSA must notify the following entities of any change, update, implementation, or suspension of such a rule: (1) the Office of Civil Rights and Liberties of the TSA; (2) the Office of the Ombudsman; (3) the Office of Traveler Engagement; (4) the Office of Civil Rights and Liberties of the
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2007, the duty on certain organic chemicals.

Teacher Tax Credit Act of 2007 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a full-time kindergarten, elementary, and secondary school teacher, instructor, counselor, aide, or principal a refundable tax credit for up to 50% of qualified expenses (e.g., books, supplies, computer equipment, and transportation) incurred by such teacher for the school year, as long as such expenses do not exceed $300. Defines "qualified expenses" as expenses for books, supplies (other than nonathletic supplies for courses of instruction in health or physical education), computer equipment (including related software and services) and other equipment, and supplementary materials used by an eligible teacher in the classroom.

Allows a teacher an additional refundable tax credit for expenses incurred in a professional development program related to the curriculum and academic subjects in which the teacher provides instruction.

States that it shall be U.S. policy to: (1) take all necessary steps to support the U.S. commitment to ensure the physical security and protection of Camp Liberty/Hurriya residents, members of the opposition Mujahedeen e-Khalq (MEK), and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in ensuring the rapid and orderly resettlement of all residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya to safe locations outside of Iraq; and (2) permit the admission as refugees of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya to the United States, who express a desire for such resettlement.

Directs the United States to: (1) ensure the safety of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya; (2) provide the UNHCR with the necessary assistance to process the applications by the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya for refugee status and to secure their orderly resettlement in safe locations outside of Iraq, including in the United States for any such residents who express such a desire; (3) timely admit as refugees the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya in the United States; and (4) report to Congress on steps taken to guard the safety of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya

Basic Pilot Program Extension and Expansion Act of 2003 - Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to extend the pilot program for basic immigration and citizenship eligibility (known as the citizen attestation program) for 11 years.

Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to expand the operation of the citizen attestation program to all 50 States by December 1, 2004.

Requires the Secretary to report to the congressional defense and appropriations committees: (1) whether certain problems associated with the program have been resolved; and (2) actions to resolve any outstanding problems.

Amends the Departments of Commerce, Justice, and State, the Judiciary, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1993 to authorize the Secretary to give priority, in processing petitions for certain immigrant visas, to petitions filed by aliens seeking admission under a pilot program for economic development in regional centers.

Extends the pilot program for five years.

Directs the General Accounting Office to report to Congress on the immigrant investor program.

Enhancing Nutrition in Medical Education Act of 2004 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to award grants to accredited schools of medicine to integrate innovative curricula on nutrition into medical education.

Requires the Secretary to ensure that such curricula focus on preventive health measures, including: (1) education on the causes, treatment, and prevention of obesity; (2) education and counseling to ensure appropriate diet for healthy people; (3) prevention and treatment of common nutritional deficiencies; (4) appropriate and inappropriate use of herbs and supplements; (5) recognition and treatment of common eating disorders; and (6) identification of special dietary needs, eating disorders, and appropriate routes of referral for medical nutrition therapy.

Requires schools to establish multidisciplinary planning committees to develop such curricula.

Dismemberment Abortion Ban Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal criminal code to make it a crime to knowingly perform a dismemberment abortion and thereby kill an unborn child. A dismemberment abortion is a procedure in which a woman removes a portion of the unborn child's body, usually one limb, and then extracts the remaining body parts. This bill makes a dismemberment abortion that is necessary to save the life of a pregnant woman or her mother ineligible for the criminal sanction of dismemberment abortion. A woman or a parent who is injured by dismemberment abortion may seek monetary damages and other relief from the person who committed the violation. A woman or a parent who is injured by dismemberment abortion may not be prosecuted for conspiracy to violate this bill or for a related offense based on a violation of this bill.

No Entry for Supporters of the Iranian Regime Act of 2010 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make any alien who: (1) engages in an activity for which sanctions may be imposed pursuant to the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996, an activity relating to the proliferation by Iran of weapons of mass destruction or the means of delivery of such weapons, an activity relating to support for international terrorism by the government of Iran, or any other activity with respect to Iran for which sanctions may be imposed, a subject of inadmissibility; (2) is the chief executive officer, president, or other individual in charge of overall management of, or a shareholder with a controlling interest in, an entity that engages in such an activity; or (3) is a spouse or minor child of an alien who engages in such an activity.

Authorizes the Secretary of State to notify an alien of such inadmissibility and the reason for it.

Authorizes the President to waive the inadmissibility requirements and admit an alien to the United States if: (1) the alien is a spouse or minor child of an alien who engages in such an activity, or the chief executive officer, president, or other individual in charge of overall

Amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to require each State regulatory authority to: (1) establish proceedings to examine the degree to which distributed resources (electric power sources connected directly to the distribution network or on the customer side of the meter) contribute ancillary services; (2) prescribe appropriate measures to ensure adequate ancillary services so that grid interconnection for distributed resources is safe, reliable, and efficient; (3) establish proceedings to examine the effects of net metering and customer-owned distributed generation on resource planning of each electric utility; and (4) determine whether electricity rates established for net metering service are just and reasonable and not unduly preferential or discriminatory, in accordance with State law.

Requires each State regulatory authority and each nonregulated electric utility: (1) within one year, to commence the consideration of the standards established by this Act; or (2) set a hearing date for such consideration. Requires each State regulatory authority and each nonregulated electric utility, within two years, to complete the consideration and make the determination.

Synthetics Trafficking and Overdose Prevention Act of 2016 or the STOP Act of 2016 This bill amends the Tariff Act of 1930 to revise the requirements for entry of merchandise into the United States by the owner or purchaser.  The bill also amends the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 to revise the requirement for a customs fee for non-letter class mail.  The bill amends the Trade Act of 2002 to direct the Department of the Treasury to require the Department of the Postmaster General to provide to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) the information required to verify the identity of the owner or purchaser of non-letter class mail.  The bill prohibits the Department of State from concluding any international postal arrangement that is inconsistent with this bill.

Ports-to-Forts Act of 2012 - Authorizes the Maritime Administrator of the Department of the Navy to make a grant to a state or port authority to assist that state or port authority to conduct repair or construction activities relating to a commercial strategic seaport. Defines "commercial strategic seaport" as a port (including bridges, roads, rail systems, and other infrastructure that is part of the port) that the Secretary of Defense has determined to be vital to the readiness and cargo throughput capacity of the Department of Defense (DOD).

Requires a state or port authority, to be eligible for such a grant, to submit to the Administrator an application that includes a certification that any grant funds received by the state or port authority shall be used only for such activities.

Accessing Medicare Therapies Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require that the amount paid by a Medicare beneficiary for a prescription drug be the same as the amount incurred out-of-pocket for such drug, including the cost of any negotiated price for such drug furnished under a compassionate treatment program. Defines "compassionate treatment program" as a Medicare prescription drug benefit program administered by a tax-exempt organization that distributes prescription drugs to eligible part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) individuals free or at nominal charge on the basis of the organization's assessment of financial need of such individuals.

Criminal Terrorism Improvements Act of 2006 - Amends the federal criminal code to: (1) make it a crime to commit a terrorist offense (defined as a felony offense that is a federal crime of terrorism or an offense under specified provisions of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, the Nuclear Regulatory Act of 1970, the Missile Defense Act of 1991, the War on Terrorism Act of 1997, or the Civil Rights Act of 1964) in the course of which conduct results in the death of a person; (2) make it a crime to participate in such nuclear and weapons of mass destruction threats to the United States; (3) make it a crime to engage in certain terror related crimes (defined as a federal offense that is an attempt or conspiracy to commit a specified offense or offense under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, the Nuclear Regulatory Act of 1970, the Missile Defense Act of 1991, the War on Terrorism Act of 1997, or the Civil Rights Act of 1964); (4) make it a crime to knowingly deny a convicted terrorist access to federal benefits;

Agricultural Water Conservation Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 30 percent of the water conservation system expenses of a taxpayer who: (1) purchases and installs a water conservation system for at least 50 percent of the gross income of the taxpayer normally derived from a trade or business; (2) uses a water conservation plan approved by the Natural Resources Conservation Service of the Department of Agriculture or the Bureau of Reclamation of the Department of the Interior; (3) has a land service area identified as an area of extreme drought severity on the Palmer Drought Severity Index published by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration or a water shortage by the Natural Resources Conservation Service; and (4) has an irrigation water savings of at least 5 percent attributable to the system.

Dollar Bill Act of 2013 - Directs the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to: (1) designate a specific week (the Target Week) starting no earlier than 90 days from the enactment of this Act and ending no later than 120 days from the enactment of this Act, and then employ a random process to select a specific day, hour, minute, and second during the Target Week, which shall not be publicly disclosed, at the Target Moment; and (2) at the Target Moment, make the value of the U.S. dollar equal to the price of gold on the exchange operated by the Commodities Exchange, Inc. (COMEX) of the New York Mercantile Exchange, Inc., as of the Target Moment and maintain the value of the U.S. dollar within plus or minus 2% of such price (the Target Range) thereafter. Directs the Board to use its banking and bank regulatory powers to maintain and promote stable and effective financial markets during and after the transition to a defined value for the U.S. dollar.  Entitles all entities that depreciate capital assets for tax purposes to 100% expensing of all capital investment for tax purposes in the year that the investment

Dairy Promotion Fairness Act - Amends the Dairy Production Stabilization Act of 1983 to require the Secretary of Agriculture to appoint up to two members of the National Dairy Promotion and Research Board who represent dairy product importers and are subject to assessments under the order to reflect the proportion of domestic production and imports supplying the U.S. market. 
Requires the Secretary to determine the rate of assessment on imported dairy products in the same manner as the rate of assessment per hundredweight or the equivalent of milk. 
Prohibits the use of Assessments collected on imported dairy products for foreign market promotion. 
Amends the Dairy Promotion Stabilization Act of 1983 to authorize importer(s) of imported dairy products to vote in the dairy product referendum.

Pesticide Maintenance Fees Reauthorization Act - Amends the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act to increase the maintenance fees for pesticide registrations. Extends the authority of the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to promulgate regulations regarding pesticide tolerance processing fees.

Hippocratic Oath and Patient Protection Act of 1996 - Prohibits a health carrier, under a contract or agreement with a health care provider or enrollee, from:  (1) preventing or limiting the provider's protected communication to a patient or the public; (2) operating an improper incentive plan; or (3) including indemnification clauses. 
Requires a health carrier to disclose to a health care provider and to an enrollee:  (1) a list of all services and benefits offered under the health plan; (2) the procedures used in authorizing, approving, limiting, or denying services or benefits under the plan; and (3) any health care provider incentive plan that exists under the contract or agreement. 
Defines a "protected communication" as a communication of information relevant to the care or course of treatment of a patient.  Limits such a protected communication to the exception of a trade secret or a knowing misrepresentation by a health care provider. 
Makes a health care provider incentive plan improper, unless it meets the requirements of the Social Security Act for physician incentive plans. 
Prohibits a health carrier from providing indemnification for any liability from a civil action brought by, or on behalf of, an enrollee or a

SuperPAC Elimination Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to remove limitations on direct contributions by U.S. citizens and residents to candidates in federal elections.  The bill also requires a principal campaign committee of a candidate who receives an aggregate amount of contributions in excess of $200 from any contributor during a calendar year to notify the Federal Election Commission and the Department of State.

Buy America 2.0 Act  This bill prohibits funds made available to carry out a federal transportation or infrastructure project using federal funds from being obligated for a project unless the steel, iron, and manufactured goods used for the project are produced in the United States.  The bill exempts such prohibition from application in any case or category of cases in which the head of the federal department or agency overseeing a project finds that: (1) applying such prohibition would be inconsistent with the public interest, (2) iron, steel, and the relevant manufactured goods are not produced in the United States in sufficient and reasonably available quantities and of a satisfactory quality, or (3) inclusion of iron, steel, and manufactured goods produced in the United States will increase the cost of the overall project by more than 25%.  The bill shall be applied in a manner consistent with U.S. obligations under international agreements.  The bill amends the Public Transportation Buy America Act to require that for each fiscal year from FY2021 through FY2026, the cost of all components of the rolling stock shall be: (1) more than 75% of the cost for FY2021, 80% of the cost for FY2022

Terrorism Elimination Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the Counter-Terrorism Trust Fund.  Authorizes appropriations to such Fund for counter-terrorism efforts.  Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to issue Freedom Bonds in response to the acts of terrorism perpetrated against the United States on September 11, 2001. 
Authorizes each taxpayer to designate on his or her tax return that a specified portion (but not less than $1) of any tax overpayment and any cash contribution which the taxpayer includes with such return shall be deposited into the Counter-Terrorism Trust Fund. 
Directs the Attorney General to impose an additional 15 percent surcharge for applications for immigrant or nonimmigrant visas under the Immigration and Nationality Act and to deposit such surcharge into the Counter-Terrorism Trust Fund.

Federal Facility Accountability Act of 2013 - Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) to require federal agencies to comply with the National Contingency Plan for the response to a hazardous substance or pollutant release at a federal facility.  Waives federal immunity from any state substantive or procedural requirements applicable to the response at a federal facility.  Makes the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) responsible for promulgating and enforcing the National Contingency Plan.  Authorizes the Administrator, if the President delegates or assigns any duties or powers under CERCLA to a federal agency other than the Administrator, to review actions and regulations taken pursuant to such delegation or assignment to ensure consistency with the guidelines, rules, regulations, or criteria established by the Administrator under CERCLA.

Ensuring Full Use of Federal Health Care Funding Act of 2014 - Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make grants to qualified entities in a state from funds recouped from such entity from that state that are not obligated by the state for expenditure before April 1, 2014. Requires the Secretary to use all such funds to make grants, before the beginning of the open enrollment period for 2015, to qualified entities to carry out activities in the state consistent with specified requirements.

Department of Homeland Security Component Privacy Officer Act of 2008 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate full-time privacy officials within each component of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to implement the privacy policy established by the senior official appointed by the Secretary. (The senior official is responsible for implementing DHS policies regarding the protection of the privacy of individuals.) Sets forth the responsibilities of each privacy official, including to: (1) report directly to both the head of the official's component and the senior official; (2) ensure that personal information contained in Privacy Act systems of records is handled in compliance with federal privacy law; and (3) assist in drafting and reviewing privacy impact assessments, privacy threshold assessments, and system of records notices for proposed rulemakings and regulations within the component and for new or substantially changed program or technology that collects, maintains, or disseminates personally identifiable information. Requires component heads to ensure that the privacy official designated: (1) has the information, material, and resources necessary to fulfill such responsibilities; (2) is advised of proposed policy changes and the development of new programs, rules, regulations, procedures, or guidelines during the planning stage and is included in the

Medicare Prescription Drug Lifeline Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a process under which an applicable individual may terminate enrollment in the prescription drug plan or the Medicare Advantage-Prescription Drug (MA-PD) plan in which such individual is enrolled and enroll in any prescription drug plan or MA-PD plan that: (1) provides some coverage of covered Medicare part D drugs after the individual has reached the initial coverage limit but has not reached the annual out-of-pocket threshold; and (2) serves the area in which the individual resides.

Directs the Secretary to ensure that an applicable individual that resides in a PDP region in which there is no prescription drug plan that provides some coverage of brand name covered Medicare part D drugs (as defined in title XVIII of the Social Security Act) after the individual has reached the initial coverage limit but before the individual has reached such annual out-of-pocket threshold, may enroll in a prescription drug plan that provides such coverage but is in another PDP region. Directs the Secretary to determine the PDP region in which the individual may enroll.

Requires the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on: (1) the costs to the Medicare program of eliminating the initial coverage limit

Political Broadcasting Access Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require broadcast station licensees to make available annually free broadcast time for political advertising.  Subjects licensees that fail to make such available to a fine and imprisonment. 
Sets forth standards for allotting free broadcast time to political parties. 
Requires cable operators to make available annually free cable time for political advertising.  Subjects operators that fail to make such available to a fine and imprisonment.

Enhancing Employment and Training Through Education Act of 2013 - Amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to carry out pilot projects to identify best practices for employment and training programs under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP, formerly known as the food stamp program) to raise the number of work registrants who obtain unsubsidized employment, increase their earned income, and reduce their reliance on public assistance.

Veterans Access to Care Accountability Act - Directs the Comptroller General to conduct random, periodic audits of Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) medical facilities and the Veterans Integrated Service Networks to assess compliance with standards regarding timely access of veterans to VA health care.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to: (1) notify eligible veterans of the status of appointments for hospital care, medical services, or other health care that have been extended for more than 30 days; and (2) make efforts to schedule such appointments at VA facilities or through non-VA health care providers within seven days after receipt of a report that finds such an appointment was extended for more than 30 days.

Defines "eligible veteran" as a veteran who is eligible for hospital care, medical services, or other health care under VA laws.

Directs the Inspector General of the VA to notify congressional veterans' committees and the Secretary if the VA Inspector General determines that a VA medical facility director or other VA official has purposefully misrepresented patient records or other data to conceal a failure of the facility to comply with patient access or care standards of the VA or for the purpose of qualifying for a performance award. Prohibits the Secretary from paying a bonus or award, including a performance award, to any director

Bounty Hunter Accountability and Quality Assistance Act of 1998 - Directs the Attorney General to develop model guidelines for the State control and regulation of persons employed or applying for employment as bounty hunters. 
Requires the guidelines to include recommendations regarding:  (1) whether a person seeking employment as a bounty hunter should be required to submit to a fingerprint-based criminal background check prior to entering into the performance of duties as a bounty hunter, or whether such employment should be prohibited if the person has been convicted of a felony offense under Federal or State law; (2) bounty hunters and bounty hunter employers should be required to obtain adequate liability insurance for actions taken in the course of performing duties as a bounty hunter; and (3) State laws should provide for the prohibition on bounty hunters entering any private dwelling, unless the bounty hunter first knocks on the front door and announces the presence of one or more bounty hunters, and for the official recognition of bounty hunters from other States. 
Requires the guidelines to include an analysis of the estimated effect, if any, of the adoption of such guidelines by the States on:  (1) the cost and availability of bail; and (2) the bail bond agent industry. 
Prohibits construing this Act to authorize the promulgation

Reinstatement of Enrollment for Medicaid Eligibility of Disadvantaged Youth (REMEDY) Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to require a state Medicaid program to provide that in the case of any individual who is a youth at the time of release from a public institution, and who was enrolled for medical assistance under the state Medicaid plan immediately before becoming an inmate, the state must suspend (rather than terminate) such enrollment during the period in which the individual is an inmate. Requires reinstatement of such enrollment upon release from such institution, unless and until there is a determination that the individual is no longer eligible to be so enrolled.

Amends SSA title XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program) (SCHIP) to require a state SCHIP plan to provide that in the case of any child who becomes an inmate of a public institution and who is still a child at the time of release, the state must suspend (rather than terminate) such enrollment for such child during the period in which the child is an inmate. Requires reinstatement of such enrollment upon release from such institution, unless and until there is a determination that the child is no longer eligible to be so enrolled.

Amateur Radio Parity Act of 2016 (Sec. 3) This bill directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to amend regulations governing amateur radio stations to prohibit the application of any private land use restriction, including a restrictive covenant, to such stations that: (1) on its face or as applied precludes communications in an amateur radio service; (2) fails to permit a licensee in such a service to install and maintain an effective outdoor antenna on property under the exclusive use or control of the licensee; or (3) does not constitute the minimum practicable restriction on such communications to accomplish the lawful purposes of a community association seeking to enforce such restriction.  The FCC, in amending such regulations, shall: (1) require any licensee in an amateur radio service to obtain prior approval from a community association concerning installation of an outdoor antenna, (2) permit a community association to prohibit installation of any antenna or antenna support structure by a licensee in an amateur radio service on common property not under the exclusive use or control of the licensee, and (3) subject to such requirements, permit a community association to establish reasonable written rules concerning height, location, size, and aesthetic impact of, and installation requirements for, outdoor antennas and support structures for the

Dorothy Buell Memorial Visitor Center Lease Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Porter County Convention, Recreation and Visitor Commission to establish a joint partnership with respect to the management of the Dorothy Buell Memorial Visitor Center located south of the Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore.

Authorizes the Secretary to enter into an agreement with the Commission to lease space in the Center for use as a visitor center for the Lakeshore. Authorizes the use of employees of the Lakeshore to provide visitor information and education at the Center.

Public Land Technical Amendments Act of 2006 - Amends the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2005 to redesignate the Gaylord A. Nelson Wilderness as the Gaylord Nelson Wilderness.

Amends the Robert E. Lee Memorial Act to transfer the Arlington House from the George Washington Memorial Parkway to the Robert E. Lee Memorial.

Amends the Petrified Forest National Park Expansion Act of 2004 to extend the boundary of the Petrified Forest National Park in Colorado to include the lands numbered 640/20,038K, and dated September 2005.

Extends the authorization of appropriations for the Department of the Interior for

Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the Federal Financing Bank to prepay its obligations to the Small Business Administration (SBA) in the form of a debenture purchased by the SBA and guaranteed by the SBA, at the election of the borrower securing such debenture and with the approval of the SBA, by paying to the Bank the amount of the unpaid principal balance due on the debenture on the date of the prepayment (plus accrued interest at the coupon rate on the debenture) and the amount of the repurchase premium.  Requires the SBA to pay to the Bank the difference between the repurchase premium paid by the issuer of the debenture and the repurchase premium that the Bank would otherwise have received. 
Sets forth a schedule of the repurchase premium for a given prepayment. 
Requires the debenture to be outstanding and neither the loan that secures the debenture nor the debenture itself to be in default on the date the prepayment is made. 
Requires State or personal funds, which may include refinancing under SBA programs, to be used to prepay the debenture.
