Authorizes appropriations for: (1) the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) for FY 1969, 1978, 1983, 1986, and 1991; (2) the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the Science, Space, and Technology Education Trust Fund; (3) the Departments of Veterans Affairs and Housing and Urban Development for small business administrative provisions; (4) NASA for FY 1992 and 1993; (5) the Land Remote Sensing Policy Act of 1992; (6) the Commercial Space Act of 1998; (7) the Commercial Reusable In-Space Transportation Act of 90; (8) the Departments of Veterans Affairs and Housing and Urban Development for FY 2002 and 2003 administrative provisions; (9) NASA for FY 2005; and (10) the National Space Grant College and Fellowship Act of 2002.

Working Families' Access to Health Innovations Act of 2013 - Amends the Small Business Act to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to guarantee up to 90% of the amount of a loan made to a qualified eligible professional for the acquisition of health information technology (HIT) for use in such professional's medical practice and for the costs associated with the installation of such technology. Limits the maximum loan principal amount to: (1) $350,000 for any single professional, and (2) $2 million for a single group of affiliated professionals. Authorizes the Administrator to impose: (1) a guarantee fee not to exceed 2% of the total guaranteed portion of any loan, and (2) annual servicing fees not to exceed 0.5% of the outstanding balance of the guarantees on lenders' books. Prohibits the charging of any service fees, processing fees, origination fees, application fees, points, brokerage fees, bonus points, or other fees to a loan applicant or recipient. Limits the interest rate charged on a loan guaranteed under this Act to 25 basis points below the rate provided for a loan under the SBA's small business program. Requires loans guaranteed under

EMTALA Regulatory Improvement Act of 2003 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a procedure to notify hospitals and physicians when an investigation under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) is closed.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) request a review by a peer review organization before making a compliance determination as part of the process of terminating a hospital's participation in Medicare; and (2) establish a Technical Advisory Group to review issues related to the EMTALA and its implementation.

Vision Zero Act of 2017 This bill authorizes the Department of Transportation to award grants to local governments to develop Vision Zero plans to eliminate transportation-related fatalities and serious injuries. A Vision Zero plan must include: (1) projects or policies to eliminate transportation-related fatalities and serious injuries using existing transportation and health data and consideration of risk factors; (2) plans for implementation of, education of the public about, and enforcement of such projects or policies; (3) a description of how such projects, policies, and enforcement will equitably address the safety needs of low-income and minority communities and protect the rights of members of such communities with respect to title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964; (4) a description of the required involvement of various subdivisions of a local government in the implementation of the plan; and (5) a mechanism to evaluate progress of the implementation of the plan.  The bill also authorizes the Department to award grants to up to five local governments to support the implementation of a Vision Zero plan. In selecting grant recipients, the Department shall consider the extent to which an entity: (1) provided an opportunity for public input in the development of the plan, (2) considered existing plans and planning processes in the drafting of

Small Business Hardship Relief Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the employer health insurance mandate a small business that is experiencing a hardship during the calendar year in which such month begins. Defines "hardship" as a business demonstrating to the satisfaction of the Secretary of the Treasury that it has missed two or more consecutive loan payments, is a debtor in a title 11 case, received a notice from a utility that it is preparing to stop providing services to it by reason of nonpayment of amounts owed for utility service, received a notice of eviction of foreclosure, experienced a fire, flood, other natural or human-caused disaster that resulted in substantial damage to its property, or experienced such other hardship as the Secretary may determine. Exempts such a business also from the hardship exemption if it has experienced such hardship for five consecutive years.

Directs the Director of the National Weather Service to notify the Secretary of Health and Human Services whenever any State, county, municipality, or other jurisdiction is subject to a heat emergency which threatens the health of its residents.  Authorizes an emergency fund for low income heat emergency assistance (LIHEAP) and forsenior residents. 
Directs the Secretary to direct the Governor of each State in which the emergency was declared that a portion of LIHEAP shall be designated by the State for the express use of providing energy to cool the residencies of current LIHEAP recipients, augmented by funds provided by this Act, during heat emergencies. 
Directs the Administrator of the General Services Administration to receive notification of any declaration of a heat emergency and initiate procedures to locate any equipment, fixtures, and appliances (including, but not limited to, air conditioners and fans) that are currently available through the Federal Supply Service or any other entity overseeing surplus Federal property. 
Directs the Administrator to initiate expedited procedures to distribute such property to representatives of States and municipalities affected by the heat emergency, and to social service agencies and individuals located in those areas.

Rail-Highway Grade Crossing Safety Act of 1994 - Amends Federal transportation law to require States to use Federal funds to provide incentive payments to local jurisdictions for the permanent closing of public at-grade rail-highway crossings.  Requires the Secretary of Transportation to set aside specified amounts of Federal funds for the surface transportation program for a public information and education program to help prevent and reduce motor vehicle accidents, injuries, and fatalities, to improve driver performance at railway-highway crossings, and to help prevent trespassing on rail rights-of-way and the resulting injuries and fatalities. 
Directs the Secretary to set aside specified amounts of Federal funds for the surface transportation program for a grade crossing corridor safety incentive program.

Fairness and Accountability in Reorganizations Act of 2006 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to require the court, when reviewing a debtor's plan of reorganization, to consider the appropriateness of compensation for employees and key employees, including bonuses, in determining whether the plan is reasonable.

Prohibits the court from approving, or subjecting to approval by the court, the payment of a performance, incentive, or other bonus, or any other compensation enhancement, to officers, managers, or consultants retained by the debtor before or after the filing of the petition, in the absence of court approval of certain transfers or obligations outside the ordinary course of business, and without deference to the debtor's request for such payments, that are essential to the debtor's survival or orderly liquidation and maximization of value of its assets.

Directs the court, in determining whether a plan provides for necessary modifications in employee benefits and protections to permit the reorganization of the debtor and assures that all creditors, the debtor, and affected parties are treated fairly and equitably, to take into account the ongoing impact on the debtor of its relationship with all subsidiaries and affiliates, regardless of whether any such subsidiary or affiliate is domestic or nondomestic, or whether any such subsidiary or affiliate is a

Frank Buckles World War I Memorial Act - Authorizes the World War I Memorial Foundation to establish a memorial rededicating the District of Columbia War Memorial as a National and District of Columbia World War I Memorial, including: (1) full restoration of the existing Memorial; and (2) the addition of an appropriate sculptural or other memorial element.

Requires the Foundation to: (1) solicit and accept private contributions for the Memorial; and (2) deposit excess funds received for its establishment in the Treasury.

Satisfying Energy Needs and Saving the Environment Act or the SENSE Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Clean Air Act to allow operators of coal refuse electric utility steam generating units to elect comply with either an emissions standard for hydrogen chloride or an emissions standard for sulfur dioxide that meets specified requirements. The bill prohibits requiring an operator to comply with both an emission standard for hydrogen chloride and an emission standard for sulfur dioxide.

Nutria Eradication and Control Act of 2009 - Establishes a nutria eradication program under which the Secretary of the Interior may provide financial assistance to the states of Maryland, Louisiana, Delaware, Oregon, Virginia, and Washington to implement measures to: (1) eradicate or control nutria; and (2) restore wetland damaged by nutria.

Requires the Secretary and the National Invasive Species Council to: (1) give consideration to specified reports for purposes of the program; (2) continue, in cooperation with the appropriate state departments, a long-term nutria control or eradication program with the objective to significantly reduce and restore the damage nutria cause to coastal wetland in the states of Louisiana and Maryland; and (3) develop, in cooperation with the appropriate state departments, long-term nutria control or eradication programs with the objective to significantly reduce and restore the damage nutria cause to coastal wetland in the coastal states of Delaware, Oregon, Virginia, and Washington.

Consumer and Community Choice in Access Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to authorize the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to require cable operators that provide interconnection, using cable system facilities, with the Internet to offer such interconnection on terms and conditions that are fair, reasonable, and nondiscriminatory.  Requires such conditions to include the obligation to provide interconnection with the facilities and equipment of any Internet service provider on terms and conditions that are functionally and economically equivalent to the interconnection provided to any other Internet service provider, whether or not affiliated with the cable operator.  Authorizes the FCC to establish the terms and conditions of such interconnection if it determines that a cable operator is not complying. 
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to provide that a service that provides high-speed data service and that seeks to obtain channel capacity under such Act may not be treated as seeking channel capacity for a commercial use until the FCC establishes open access or interconnection standards and obligations under such Act. 
Subjects a telecommunications service that is provided by a cable system to regulation as a common carrier service.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the Department of Defense (DOD) should undertake actions to ensure that family members of members of the National Guard and Reserve who are deployed have full access to mental health care during the periods of mobilization, deployment, and demobilization of such members.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to prescribe regulations that provide for reimbursement under the TRICARE program for any mental health care specified in this Act for a family member of a covered member of the National Guard or Reserve during the period of deployment. Defines "covered member" as any member of the National Guard or Reserve on active duty for more than 30 days for a deployment in connection with Operations Iraqi Freedom and Enduring Freedom who, while so on active duty, is covered by the TRICARE program on a for self and family basis.

Strengthening Local Transportation Security Capabilities Act of 2018 (Sec. 3) This bill directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to prioritize the assignment of officers and intelligence analysts from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and, as appropriate, from the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the DHS to locations with participating state, local, and regional fusion centers in jurisdictions with a high-risk surface transportation asset in order to enhance the security of such assets. Officers and analysts assigned to such locations shall participate in the generation and dissemination of transportation security intelligence products, with an emphasis on terrorist and other threats to surface transportation assets that: (1) assist state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies in deploying their resources to help detect, prevent, investigate, and respond to terrorist and other threats; (2) promote more consistent and timely sharing of threat information among jurisdictions; and (3) enhance DHS's situational awareness of such threats. (Sec. 4) The Transportation Security Administration shall make available to public and private sector stakeholders a framework for establishing an integrated and unified operations center responsible for overseeing daily operations of a transportation

NEPA Reciprocity Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a program to eliminate duplicative environmental reviews and approvals under State and Federal law of projects.  Directs the Secretary to approve each application submitted by a State for participation in the program if the Secretary finds that the proposed alternative environmental review and approval procedures of the State are substantially equivalent to the applicable Federal environmental laws and Federal regulations.  Excludes the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 and the Endangered Species Act of 1973 from any decision by the Secretary to approve or disapprove any application submitted pursuant to this Act.

Witness Security and Protection Grant Program Act of 2011 - Directs the Attorney General to award competitive grants to eligible state, tribal, and local governments to establish or maintain witness protection programs in cases involving: (1) homicide, or serious violent felony or serious drug offense; and (2) gangs or organized crime.

Requires the Attorney General to evaluate grant applicants based upon: (1) lack of infrastructure to support a witness assistance program; (2) witness intimidation; (3) cases not prosecuted due to witness intimidation; (4) per capita number of homicides, violent felonies, or serious drug offenses; (5) organized crime; and (6) other appropriate criteria.

Directs the Attorney General, upon a grant recipient's request, to provide the appropriate Department of Justice (DOJ) offices with technical assistance to establish or maintain such a program.

Requires the Attorney General to develop and disseminate to states and other relevant entities best practice models for witness protection and assistance.

Expresses the sense of Congress that states and other relevant entities should use such models to evaluate, improve, and develop witness protection or witness assistance.

Limits: (1) the federal share of project costs to 75%; and (2) the non-federal share for in-kind

Oil Industry Merger Antitrust Enforcement Act - Amends the Clayton Act to place the burden of proof in a civil action alleging that a merger, acquisition, or other transaction affects commerce and may substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly in the business of processing, storing, marketing, selling, or otherwise making available petroleum, oil, or natural gas, or products derived from petroleum, oil, or natural gas, in the hands of the defendant or defendants to establish by a preponderance of the evidence that the merger, acquisition, or transaction will not substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the Department of Justice Antitrust Division (DOJ) to review and revise all enforcement guidelines and policies, including the Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued April 2, 1992, and revised April 8, 1997, and the Non-Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued June 14, 1984, and modify those guidelines to: (1) specifically address mergers and acquisitions in oil companies and among companies involved in the production, refining, distribution, or marketing of oil, gasoline, natural gas, heating oil, or other petroleum-related products; and (2) ensure

Amends the Clean Air Act to redefine "renewable biomass" to include materials, pre-commercial thinnings, or invasive species from National Forest System land and public lands that are byproducts of preventive treatments that are removed to reduce hazardous fuels, reduce or contain disease or insect infestation, or restore ecosystem health, and any organic matter that is available on a renewable or recurring basis from non-Federal land or land belonging to an Indian or Indian tribe that is held in trust by the United States or subject to a restriction against alienation imposed by the United States.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA) and title 10 of the United States Code to require local educational agencies (LEAs) receiving ESEA assistance to provide, upon a request made by a military recruiter or an institution of higher education (IHE), access to the name, address, and telephone listing of each secondary school student served by the LEA, unless the parent of such student has submitted the prior consent request.

Allows a parent of a secondary school student to submit a written request to the LEA that the student's name, address, and telephone listing not be released for purposes of such access without prior written consent of the parent. Prohibits the LEA from releasing the student's name, address, and telephone listing for such purposes without the prior written consent of the parent.

Requires each LEA to notify the parents of the students served by the LEA of the option to make such request.

Prohibits anything in such Act from being construed to allow an LEA to withhold access to a student's name, address, and telephone listing from a military recruiter or IHE by implementing an opt-in process or any other process other than the written consent request process.

American Freedom Agenda Act of 2007 - Repeals the Military Commissions Act of 2006.

Authorizes the President to establish military commissions for the trial of war crimes only in places of active hostilities against the United States where an immediate trial is necessary to preserve fresh evidence or to prevent local anarchy.

Prohibits the President from detaining any individual indefinitely as an unlawful enemy combatant absent proof by substantial evidence that the individual has directly engaged in active hostilities against the United States, provided that no U.S. citizen shall be detained as an unlawful enemy combatant.

Entitles any individual detained as an enemy combatant by the United States to petition for a writ of habeas corpus.

Prohibits U.S. civilian or military tribunals from admitting as evidence statements extracted from the defendant by torture or coercion.

Prohibits any federal agency from gathering foreign intelligence in contravention of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA). Subordinates the President's constitutional power to gather foreign intelligence to this provision.

Requires the House of Representatives and the Senate to file a declaratory judgment action in an appropriate federal district court to challenge the constitutionality of a presidential signing statement declaring the President's intent to disregard provisions of a bill he

Creating Opportunities for Military Members to Use Transportation Efficiently Act of 2014 or the COMMUTE Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD) to establish a Military Community Infrastructure Program to provide grants to eligible entities for transportation infrastructure improvement projects in military communities. Authorizes grant funds to be used for: (1) road construction; (2) mass transit and parking facilities construction; (3) pedestrian and bicycle access upgrades; and (4) public transportation system upgrades. Requires a project to be related to improving access to a military installation and to be located in an urbanized area and a growth community. Directs the Secretary to conduct a traffic impact study for any urbanized area that expects a significant increase in traffic related to a military installation.

Amends the San Luis Rey Indian Water Rights Settlement Act to revise the supplemental water supply program for the benefit of the San Luis Rey Indian Water Authority and the local entities. 
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to arrange for the development of not more than 16,000 acre-feet per year of supplemental water from public lands within the boundaries of the State of California outside the service area of the Central Valley Project, obtain such water either from water conserved by authorized works or through a contract with the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, or construct the works necessary to conserve 16,000 acre-feet per year and arrange to deliver such water to the Bands and the local entities by exchange or through such District and other parties with conveyance facilities. 
Holds the 16,000 acre-feet of water in perpetuity by the United States in trust for the Authority and makes the use of such water non-competitive under existing law. 
Authorizes appropriations for the works. 
Makes the water made available for consumptive use by California Contractors for purposes of satisfying the funding requirements of the seven-party agreement between the Secretary and the Contractors.  Requires any contractor using such water to reimburse the Contractors who contributed the least funds.

Broadband Internet Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit an incumbent local exchange carrier from being subject to certain requirements with respect to facilities and equipment used exclusively to provide advanced service, or to provide such service, in any State in which 70 percent of the carrier's loops in its service territory are DSL-capable. 
Bars the prices, terms, and conditions of any advanced service by an incumbent local exchange carrier from being subject to regulation if the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) determines that advanced service is being offered by an unaffiliated advanced service provider in competition with the incumbent local exchange carrier within a geographic area served by a central office. 
Directs the FCC, if it so determines, to approve an incumbent local exchange carrier's petition for unconditional relief from such pricing restrictions. 
Bars the rates, terms, and conditions of advanced service offered by an incumbent local exchange carrier or its successor or assigns from being subject to regulation in any geographic area in which the carrier was not the local incumbent exchange carrier on February 8, 1996. 
Requires an incumbent local exchange carrier furnishing such advanced service to file with the FCC a schedule of charges and practices for such advanced service in

Protecting Domestic Violence and Stalking Victims Act - Amends the federal criminal code to: (1) expand the definition of "intimate partner" for purposes of the sale or other disposition of a firearm by an individual (or a former dating partner) to a person subject to a court order for stalking or domestic violence-related offenses; (2) expand the definition of "person subject to a restraining or similar order" from which a person prohibited from possessing or receiving a firearm; and (3) expand the definition of "person subject to a court order for stalking or domestic violence-related offenses" to include a person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of stalking under federal, state, territorial, or tribal law, or of a crime that involves conduct which would be prohibited if committed within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States.

Insider Trading Prohibition Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to prohibit: (1) any person from purchasing, selling, or entering into any security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement while in possession of material, nonpublic information relating to such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement, or relating to the market for such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement, if such person knows, or recklessly disregards, that such information has been obtained wrongfully, or that such purchase, sale, or entry would constitute a wrongful use of such information; and (2) any person whose own purchase or sale of a security, security-based swap, or entry into a security-based swap agreement would violate such prohibitions (communicating person) from wrongfully communicating material, nonpublic information relating to such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement, or relating to the market for such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement, to any other person if the other person purchases, sells, or enters into any security-based swap agreement to which such communication relates, or communicates the information to another person who makes or causes such a purchase, sale, or entry while in possession

Desalination Energy Consumption Reduction Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to make incentive payments to the owners of qualified desalination facilities to encourage the utilization of the best available technology to reduce the consumption of electrical energy in the desalination process. Defines "qualified desalination facility" as a facility that: (1) produces for sale to domestic customers desalinated seawater, brackish groundwater, or surface water whose source water is greater than 1000 milligrams per liter total dissolved solids; (2) is owned or operated by a state or local government, an Indian tribe, or a corporation responsible for providing municipal water service pursuant to state or tribal law; (3) is first used to produce commercial desalinated water during the ten-year period beginning on October 1 of the first fiscal year occurring after the enactment of this Act; and (4) uses the best available technology.

Requires the Secretary to establish a formula for making incentive payments to owners of qualified desalination facilities producing potable water from source waters ranging from 1,000 to 35,000 milligrams per liter total dissolved solids or more. Provides that the payment shall range from 30 cents per

Customs Training Enhancement Act - Directs the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to establish and carry out educational seminars at U.S. ports of entry to improve the ability of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) personnel to classify and appraise imported articles in accordance with U.S. customs laws, including to improve the ability of CBP personnel to identify and prevent the mislabeling and transshipment of articles.

Requires the Commissioner to establish a process to solicit, evaluate, and select interested parties to assist in providing instruction in the seminars.

Seeds for the Future Act - Amends the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to ensure that at least $50 million of specified competitive research grants is used each fiscal year for the development of public cultivars.

Directs the Secretary, in making such grants, to give priority to high-potential research projects that lead to the release of public cultivars.

Requires the Secretary to ensure that the terms and renewal process for such grants facilitate the development and commercialization of public cultivars through long-term grants of at least five years.

Requires the Secretary to submit annual reports to Congress on all public cultivar and breeding research funded by USDA, including: (1) a list of public cultivars and varieties of public cultivars developed and released in a commercially available form; (2) areas of high priority research; (3) identified research gaps relating to public cultivar development; and (4) an assessment of the state of commercialization for cultivars that have been developed.

Amends the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 to direct the Under Secretary for Research and Technology to appoint a coordinator within the Research, Education, and Extension Office to coordinate research activities at the Department relating to the

Patient Access to Durable Medical Equipment Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to extend the transition period from June 30, 2016, to June 30, 2017, for payment rates for durable medical equipment (DME) under the Medicare program. (Sec. 3) The bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to: (1) prohibit a bid submitted for DME items and services furnished on or after July 1, 2017, from being less than the fee schedule amount that would otherwise be determined for such items and services furnished on or after January 1, 2017; and (2) require the CMS Secretary, in making any adjustments to payment rates for DME items and services furnished on or after January 1, 2019, to solicit and take into account stakeholder input and the highest amount bid by a winning supplier in a competitive acquisition area, as well as a comparison of each of the following with respect to non-competitive acquisition areas and competitive acquisition areas. Organic Farmer and Consumer Protection Act of 2017 This bill amends the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 to authorize appropriations for the national organic program for FY2018-FY2023. The Department of Agriculture (USDA) shall modernize international trade tracking and data collection systems of the national organic program.  USDA may share confidential business information with federal and state government officers and employees and certifying agents involved in an investigation of potential violations of organic certification requirements.  USDA shall have access to available data from cross-border documentation systems administered by other federal agencies, including the Automated Commercial Environment system of the U.S. Customs and Border Patrol and the Phytosanitary Certificate Issuance and Tracking system of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.  USDA shall grant an accredited certifying agent the authority to require increased additional documentation or verification before granting certification in the case of a known area of risk or when there is a specific area of concern.  USDA shall issue regulations to limit the type of operations that are excluded from certification.  USDA shall: (1) require an annual authorization for each certifying agent that intends to operate in any foreign country, and (2) have oversight and approval authority over any certifying

Survivor Benefits Improvement Act of 2013 - Extends from two to five years the initial period for increased dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses of veterans who have served on active duty in the Armed Forces for a period of less than two years. Makes eligible for such compensation the remarriage of a surviving spouse of a veteran after the age of 55. Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide to any child of a veteran of covered service in Thailand who is suffering from spina bifida the health care, vocational training and rehabilitation, and monetary allowance required to be paid to a child of a Vietnam veteran who is suffering from spina bifida if such veteran served in the active military, naval, or air service in Thailand during the period beginning on January 9, 1962, and ending on May 7, 1975, and has been exposed to a herbicide agent during such service. Directs the Secretary to carry out a two-year pilot program on the feasibility and advisability of providing group retreat settings for the assessment of the suitability of providing grief counseling services to surviving spouses of veterans who die while serving on active duty in the Armed Forces.

Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund Act of 1998 - Establishes in the Treasury the Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund.  Credits such Fund with a specified amount from amounts received from tobacco product manufacturers for programs to reduce use of tobacco products by minors and for health-care research.  Makes such Fund available to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs for:  (1) medical care and services; and (2) medical research, rehabilitation research, and health systems research.

Medicaid Directory of Caregivers Act or the Medicaid DOC Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid program to publish annually on its website a directory of fee-for-service providers (including primary and specialty care physicians) participating in a state Medicaid program.

Fluke Fairness Act of 2013 - Requires the Mid-Atlantic Fishery Management Council to submit to the Secretary of Commerce and the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (Commission) a modified fishery management plan for, or an amendment to, the commercial and recreational management of summer flounder (a species of fish found in both state and federal waters and managed through a joint fishery management plan between the Council and the Commission) under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act. Requires the Council, in preparing such plan or amendment, to consult with the Commission to ensure consistent management throughout the range of the species. Prohibits the Council from allocating commercial or recreational catch quotas for summer flounder on a state-by-state basis using historical landings data that does not reflect the status of the stock, based on the most recent scientific information. Directs the Secretary, if the Council fails to submit a plan or amendment that may be approved, to prepare and approve such plan or amendment.  Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on the implementation of such plan or amendment, including an assessment of whether such implementation complies with the national standards for fishery conservation and management set out in the Magnuson-Stevens Act.

Ending Maternal Mortality Act of 2018 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop and submit to Congress a national plan to reduce the rate of preventable maternal mortality. HHS must include in each biennial plan: (1) a list of objectives for meeting the goals of the plan, and (2) a strategy for implementing the plan across HHS agencies and offices. HHS must also address:   increasing public understanding of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity;  improving understanding of the root causes of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity;  improving data collection;  identifying at-risk populations and eliminating disparities;  supporting and expanding maternal mortality review committees;  assessing hospital culture of safety in maternity care and how best to provide resources to improve outcomes;  improving health and treatment services for expectant mothers struggling with substance use and mental health disorders;  studying and supporting local and targeted responses to maternal death; and  identifying federal programs and activities to reduce maternal mortality and making recommendations for improving the effectiveness and coordination of such programs and activities.  HHS must make each plan submitted to Congress publicly accessible on its website.

Backcountry Landing Strip Access Act - Prohibits the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture from taking any action that would permanently close, restrict, or render or declare as unserviceable any aircraft landing strip located on federal land under their respective jurisdictions unless: (1) the action has been approved by the head of the aviation department of the state in which the landing strip is located; (2) notice of the proposed action is published in the Federal Register; (3) a 90-day public comment period on the action is provided; and (4) the relevant Secretary and the state aviation department head have taken into consideration any comments received.

Requires the Secretaries to: (1) establish a national policy for governing backcountry aviation issues relating to the management of federal land under their jurisdiction; and (2) require relevant officials to adhere to such policy.

Medicare and Medicaid Hospital Self-Referral Amendments of 1996 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to require a discharge plan for an individual entitled to Medicare coverage to:  (1) not specify or otherwise limit the qualified provider which may provide post-hospital care; and (2) identify, in a form and manner specified by the Secretary of Health and Human Services, any provider (to whom the individual is referred) in which the hospital has a disclosable financial interest or which has such an interest in the hospital. 
Requires a hospital with a financial interest in a provider of post-hospital services to maintain and disclose to the Secretary certain information on such individual's financial interest, the number of individuals who were discharged who required the type of services provided by such provider, and the percentage of such individuals who received such services from such provider (or another such provider). 
Requires the Secretary to make such information available to the public.

Veterans Acquiring Community Care Expect Safe Services Act of 2017 or the Veterans ACCESS Act (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to deny or revoke the eligibility of a health care provider to provide non-VA health care services to veterans if the VA determines that the provider:   was removed from VA employment due to conduct that violated a VA policy relating to the delivery of safe and appropriate health care, violated the requirements of the provider's medical license, had a VA credential revoked and the grounds for such revocation impacts the provider's ability to deliver safe and appropriate health care, or  violated a law for which a term of imprisonment of more than one year may be imposed.   The VA may deny, revoke, or suspend the eligibility of a health care provider to provide non-VA health care services if: (1) the health care provider is under investigation by the medical licensing board of a state in which the provider is licensed or practices, (2) the health care provider has entered into a settlement agreement for a disciplinary charge relating to the practice of medicine by the provider, or (3) the VA determines that such action is appropriate under the circumstances.  The VA shall suspend the eligibility of a health care provider

Scenic Columbia Gorge Restoration Act of 2017 This bill requires the Department of Agriculture (USDA), acting through the Chief of the Forest Service, to begin proposing response activities for lands within a national scenic area adversely impacted by a catastrophic event within 30 days after the event concludes.  The USDA shall allow 30 days for public scoping and comment regarding the activity, 15 days for filing an objection, and 15 days for the agency response to the objection.  An environmental assessment for the activity shall be completed within 60 days after the event concludes.  A categorical exclusion is available for any response activity that: (1) does not exceed 10,000 acres, and (2) includes lands that are visible from key viewing areas, provide screening for human development, are part of a municipal watershed, or contain utility or power transmission right-of-ways.  Consultation under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 shall not be required if the USDA determines that the response activity is not likely to adversely affect a listed species or designated critical habitat.  No court order, preliminary injunction, or injunction pending appeal shall be issued with respect to any decision to prepare or conduct the activity.

Treatment of Indian Tribal Natural Resource Income Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from Federal income tax income derived from a natural resources-related activity by Indians or a qualified Indian entity.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) authorize the President to appoint a new Commissioner of Internal Revenue from individuals recommended by a Selection Commission; (2) establish such Commission; and (3) provide for the term of the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to be six years.

Government Audit Reform Act of 2010 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) should follow the recommendations of the Government Accountability Office (GAO) report entitled "Single Audit: Opportunities Exist to Improve the Single Audit Process and Oversight" (GAO-09-307R).

Requires the Director, or the head of the office or entity designated by the Director, to: (1) monitor the implementation of specified audit provisions by federal agencies; (2) evaluate the process for the single audit and the program-specific audit to identify simplified alternatives for achieving the purposes of the Single Audit Act of 1984 and the Single Audit Act Amendments of 1996 for the audits of small and large recipients; and (3) evaluate the implementation of the recommendations made to OMB by the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency in the report entitled "Report on National Single Audit Sampling Project," dated June 2007."

Andrew Prior Act or Andrew's Law - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to provide that, in the event of the death of a borrower of a private educational loan, or if such borrower is totally and permanently disabled, neither the borrower's estate nor any cosigner of such loan shall be obligated to repay the outstanding principal or interest on the loan.

Critical Infrastructure Protection Act or CIPA - (Sec. 2) Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to include in national planning scenarios the threat of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) events and to conduct outreach to educate owners and operators of critical infrastructure, emergency planners, and emergency responders at all levels of government of the threat of EMP events. Directs the Secretary, acting through the Under Secretary for Science and Technology, and in consultation with other relevant agencies and departments of the federal government and relevant owners and operators of critical infrastructure, to conduct research and development to mitigate the consequences of EMP events. Requires the Secretary to submit a recommended strategy to protect and prepare the critical infrastructure of the American homeland against EMP events and biennial updates on the status of the strategy. (Sec. 3) Declares that nothing in this Act shall be construed to grant any regulatory authority. (Sec. 4) Prohibits this Act from being carried out only by using funds appropriated under the authority of other laws.

Professional's Access to Health Workforce Integration Act of 2015 This bill authorizes the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities, or the Office of Minority Health to award grants to eligible entities to:   provide services to assist unemployed and underemployed skilled immigrants, residing in the United States, who are internationally educated health professionals, enter into the American health workforce with employment matching their health professional skills and education, and advance in employment to positions that better match their health professional education and expertise;  provide training opportunities to reduce barriers to entry and advancement in the health workforce for skilled, internationally educated immigrants;  educate employers regarding the abilities and capacities of internationally educated health professionals;  assist in the evaluation of foreign credentials; and  facilitate access to contextualized and accelerated courses on English as a second language.

Veterans Benefits Administration Improvement Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit to specified congressional committees a comprehensive plan for the improvement of the processing of veterans compensation and pension claims.

Healthy Schools Partnerships Act of 2010 - Amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a demonstration project under which the Secretary shall make grants to a school food authority that demonstrates it has collaborated, or will collaborate, with one or more local partner organizations to achieve the purposes of the Act, which are to: (1) assist schools in improving the nutritional standards of school meals and the overall school environment; and (2) use local resources and expertise to promote collaborations and develop sustainable and replicable models for making systemic changes that promote good nutrition and healthy living among students.

Requires the Secretary, in making grants, to give priority to entities that demonstrate: (1) a severe need to improve the school environment; (2) a commitment by community partners to make in-kind or cash contributions; and (3) the ability to measure results.

Small Business Investment Improvement Act of 1999 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to revise the definition of "interest" for purposes of the loan authority for small business concerns.  Includes only the maximum mandatory sum, expressed in dollars or as a percentage rate, that is payable with respect to the business loan amount received by the small business concern, including the value, if any, of contingent obligations, including warrants, royalty, or conversion rights, granting the small business investment company an ownership interest in the equity or increased future revenue of the small business concern receiving the business loan. 
Amends the Small Business Act to increase the amounts of the loan authority for small business concerns.

Pro-Growth Budgeting Act of 2012 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to prepare for each major bill or resolution reported by any congressional committee a macroeconomic impact analysis of the budgetary effects of such legislation for the ten fiscal-year period beginning with the first fiscal year for which an estimate was prepared under the Act and each of the next three such fiscal years. Requires such analysis to describe the potential economic and fiscal impact of the legislation on major economic variables, including real gross domestic product (GDP), business investment, the capital stock, employment, interest rates, and labor supply. Requires the analysis to also describe the potential fiscal effects of the legislation, including any estimates of revenue increases or decreases resulting from changes in GDP. Directs the CBO Director to submit to such committee the analysis, together with the basis for the analysis.

Requires the CBO Director, in addition to the baseline projections, to submit to the House and Senate Budget Committees a supplemental projection assuming extension of current tax policy for the fiscal year commencing on October 1 of that year and a supplemental projection for the 10 fiscal years beginning with that fiscal year, assuming the extension of current tax policy.
