Federal Land Freedom Act of 2015 This bill authorizes a state that has established an oil and gas leasing, permitting, and regulatory program to: (1) submit to the Department of the Interior, the Department of Agriculture, and the Department of Energy a declaration that such program has been established or amended; and (2) seek to transfer responsibility for leasing, permitting, and regulating oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy development from the federal government to the state.  Upon submission of such declaration, the state may lease, permit, and regulate exploration and development of oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy on federal land located in the state in lieu of the federal government.  Any state action to lease, permit, or regulate such activities shall not be subject to federal action under specified laws.  A state lease or permit shall include provisions for the collection of royalties or other revenues in an amount equal to the amount of royalties or revenues that would have been collected if the lease or permit had been issued by the federal government.

Pink Tax Repeal Act - Prohibits any person from selling or offering for sale in interstate commerce two substantially similar consumer products from the same manufacturer that are priced differently based on the gender of the individuals for whose use the products are intended or marketed, or any services that are substantially similar if they are priced differently based on the gender of the individuals for which they are performed, offered, or marketed.

Treats a violation as an unfair or deceptive act or practice under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Authorizes state attorneys general to bring a civil action in an appropriate U.S. district court to: (1) enjoin further violation of this Act by the defendant, (2) compel compliance with this Act, or (3) obtain damages, restitution, or other compensation on behalf of residents of the state.

Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act - Amends Federal law to permit an employee of a land management agency serving under a time-limited appointment in the competitive service to compete for a permanent appointment in the competitive service if: (1) the employee was appointed initially under open, competitive examination to the time-limited appointment; (2) the employee has served under such appointments for a period or periods totaling at least 24 months without an intervening break of at least two years; and (3) the employee's performance has been at an acceptable level of performance throughout such period or periods.

Requires an employee serving under a time-limited appointment in the competitive service to be offered any successor permanent position that the agency decides to fill and, upon his or her concurrence, be appointed to such position if: (1) the job announcement for the time-limited position stated that there was potential for the position to become permanent; or (2) the employee's first time-limited appointment by such agency occurred before this Act's enactment. Requires the employee, in either instance, to have: (1) served under a time-limited appointment or appointments in a position or positions in such agency with the same or substantially similar major duties and qualification requirements as the successor permanent position for a

Amends the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act of 1986 to revise the requirement that the owner or operator of a facility be notified of a release of a hazardous substance within 15 minutes of having knowledge of it.  Revises the requirements of such Act with respect to the comprehensive environmental response, compensation, and liability Act of 1980.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that no gain or loss shall be recognized by a common trust fund or any participant by reason of a transfer to a regulated investment company, if: (1) such common trust fund transfers substantially all of its assets to one or more regulated investment companies in exchange solely for stock in such company or companies to which such assets are so transferred; and (2) such stock is distributed by such common trust fund to participants in such common trust fund in exchange solely for their interests in such common trust fund.

Nuclear Power Plant Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to direct the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to initiate a rulemaking to revise its regulations to ensure that each licensed nuclear power plant utilization facility can withstand and adequately respond to: (1) an earthquake, tsunami (for a facility located in a coastal area), strong storm, or other event that threatens the facility; (2) a loss of the primary operating power source for at least 14 days; and (3) a loss of the primary backup operating power source for at least 72 hours.

Requires the revision of such regulations to provide for: (1) a requirement that each licensed facility be equipped with resilient containment, safety, and diagnostic systems sufficient to withstand such circumstances; (2) a requirement that licensees have at least 14 days worth of emergency power system fuel onsite with which to power the facility in the event of a loss of the primary operating power source; (3) a requirement that licensees have sufficient secondary emergency power to power the facility in the event of a loss of both the primary operating power source and the emergency power system for at least 72 hours; (4) a requirement that license

Peer Support Communities of Recovery Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to revise the peer support program. Under the current program, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) must award grants to recovery community organizations to conduct community-based peer support services. This bill allows HHS to award grants to eligible entities (national nonprofit entities focused on substance use disorder with a network of local affiliates and partners that are geographically and organizationally diverse, or nonprofit organizations that are focused on substance use disorder, established by individuals in personal or family recovery, and serving prevention, treatment, recovery, payor, faith-based, and criminal justice stakeholders in the implementation of local addiction and recovery initiatives) to establish regional technical assistance centers to provide regional technical assistance for: (1) implementation of regionally driven, peer-delivered addiction recovery support services before, during, after, or in conjunction with addiction treatment; (2) establishment of recovery community organizations; and (3) establishment of recovery community centers. HHS must provide for the establishment of such centers with specified amounts for FY2019-FY2023.

Child Care Criminal Background Check Act of 2009 - Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to require a State to certify that it will require child care providers that are licensed by the State or that receive funds under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Program to obtain a comprehensive criminal background check of: (1) each employee who provides child care services; (2) each applicant for employment to provide such services; and (3) each family child care provider who provides or applies to provide such services.

Requires a provider that is not so licensed or funded to refuse to employ, for specified periods of time, an individual to provide such services: (1) if such individual was convicted of a crime of violence or a crime against children; (2) to an eligible child without the supervision of an employee whose criminal background check satisfies requirements, pending receipt of such individual's background check; and (3) to an eligible child with the supervision of an employee whose criminal background check satisfies requirements and for a period exceeding 90 days, pending receipt of such individual's background check.

Requires a provider's request for a comprehensive criminal background check of each employee of, and each applicant for employment by, a State-licensed or funded child

Volunteer Emergency Services Recruitment and Retention Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to permit the election, at the option of its sponsor, of treating a length of service award plan as an eligible deferred compensation plan for purposes of the employee retirement income security act of 1974 (ERISA). Defines "length of service award plan" as any plan paying solely length of service awards to bona fide volunteers on account of qualified services performed by such volunteers.

Exempts such programs from ERISA requirements for employee pension benefits.

Medicaid Reform and Personal Responsibility Act of 2017 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require states to apply a work requirement for able-bodied adults without dependents under Medicaid. A state must condition medical assistance on an able-bodied adult without dependents' satisfaction of a work requirement and specified job training and community service requirements. An able-bodied adult without dependents shall not receive medical assistance if the able-bodied adult without dependents: (1) refuses to register as employed or unemployed and actively looking for employment for less than 12 consecutive months, (2) refuses without good cause to satisfy a work requirement, (3) refuses without good cause to accept an offer of employment at a site or plant not subject to a strike or lockout at a wage not less than the higher of the applicable federal or state minimum wage or 80% of the wage that would have governed had the minimum hourly rate under the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 been applicable to the offer of employment, (4) refuses without good cause to provide the state with sufficient information to determine the employment status or job availability of the able-bodied adult without dependents, or (5) voluntarily and without good cause quits a job

Directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Commerce, in cooperation with the Secretary, to develop and implement a comprehensive program for fish screens, fish passage devices, and other measures agreed to by local interests and relevant federal agencies for water diversions by local governmental entities in Oregon, Washington, Montana, and Idaho that provide water supplies.  Sets forth program goals.  Requires non-federal participation in the program to be voluntary.  Requires the Secretary to take no action that would result in any non-federal entity being held financially responsible for any action unless the entity applies to participate in the program. 
Requires the program to be developed and executed on the basis of specified criteria, including the consultation with other federal, state, and local agencies. 
Requires a recommended fish screen, fish passage device, or other measure to:  (1) meet the requirements of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service or the National Marine Fisheries Service, as applicable, and any state requirements; and (2) be agreed to by all interested federal and non-federal entities. 
Requires:  (1) the cost of studies conducted in connection with the program to be shared in accordance with provisions of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986; (2) the non-f

Randy Barrett Act - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to provide for waiver of the five-month waiting period for entitlement to benefits based on disability in cases in which an individual is terminally ill and not entitled to disability benefits under OASDI for any month solely by reason of the waiting period.

DMZ War Veterans Recognition Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, to place a plaque on or near the grounds of the Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., to commemorate the sacrifices of those who served, were wounded, or were killed from 1953 until the present in the defense of the Republic of Korea.

Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2008 - (Sec. 3) Amends the Coast and Geodetic Survey Act to authorize the Administrator of the Coast and Geodetic Survey to create, support, and maintain a Joint Hydrographic Institute.

Authorizes the Administrator to acquire hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services to: (1) support the conservation and management of coastal and ocean resources; (2) save and protect life and property; (3) support the resumption of commerce in response to emergencies, natural disasters, and man-made disasters; and (4) meet homeland security and maritime domain awareness needs, including carrying out mission assignments.

(Sec. 4) Revises the composition of the National Hydrographic Services Review Panel to include two Co-directors (currently, one Director) instead of one Secretary.

Revises the compensation of Panel members to reimburse them for actual and reasonable expenses incurred in the performance of their duties.

(Sec. 5) Authorizes appropriations for FY2009-FY2012 for: (1) nautical mapping and charting functions, except for conducting hydrographic surveys; (2) hydrographic surveys, including the leasing or time chartering of vessels; (3

Community Gardening and Nutrition Act of 2014 - Amends the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 to require the Director of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) to establish a Community Garden Pilot Program to carry out the work of the Community Development Block Grant Program. Requires the Director, in conducting the Program, to carry out at least 40 projects.  Requires the Director to give priority to: (1) volunteers with experience in health, nutrition, and gardening; (2) projects located in varied geographic regions; and (3) selecting a balance of urban and rural projects.  Authorizes FY2014 appropriations.

Federal Internship Improvement Act - Requires the head of each executive agency to appoint an internship coordinator within the agency operating an internship program.

Directs the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to make publicly available on the Internet: (1) the name and contact information of the internship coordinator for each agency; and (2) information regarding application procedures and deadlines for each internship program.

Requires the Office to establish and maintain a centralized electronic database that contains the names, contact information, and relevant skills of individuals who have completed or are nearing completion of an internship program and are currently seeking full-time federal employment.

Requires the agency operating an internship program to conduct an exit interview, and administer a survey, with each intern who completes such program.

Requires the head of each agency to annually submit to OPM a report assessing the internship program, including information regarding demographic characteristics of interns, the steps taken to increase the percentage of interns offered permanent federal jobs, and exit interviews conducted with interns.

Concussion Treatment and Care Tools Act of 2010 or the ConTACT Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to: (1) establish concussion management guidelines that address the prevention, identification, treatment, and management of concussions in school-aged children, including standards for such children to return to play after experiencing such a concussion; and (2) convene a conference of medical, athletic, and educational stakeholders to assist in the establishment of such guidelines.

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to states for purposes of: (1) collecting information on the incidence and prevalence of concussions among school-aged children attending or participating in such entities; (2) implementing the guidelines; (3) funding implementation by such entities of preseason baseline and post-injury testing; and (4) any other activity or purpose specified by the Secretary.

Requires the Secretary to coordinate in an appropriate manner with the heads of other federal agencies that carry out activities related to concussions and other traumatic brain injuries.

Hunter and Farmer Protection Act of 2015 This bill amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to prohibit any person from taking any migratory game bird by baiting or on or over any baited area if the person knows or reasonably should know that the area is baited. Baited areas are defined as: (1) any area on which salt, grain, or other feed has been placed, exposed, deposited, distributed, or scattered, if the salt, grain, or feed could lure or attract migratory game birds; and (2) in the case of waterfowl, a standing, unharvested crop that has been manipulated through activities such as mowing, discing, or rolling, unless the activities are normal agricultural practices.  A person is also prohibited from placing or directing the placement of bait on or adjacent to an area for the purpose of causing, inducing, or allowing any person to take or attempt to take any migratory game bird by baiting or on or over the baited area.

International Money Transfer Disclosure Act - Directs the appropriate Federal agencies to jointly prescribe regulations that require any financial institution or money transmitting business which initiates an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer to provide specified disclosures to the consumer before the consummation of the transaction.

Mental Health First Act of 2013 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Administrator of the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) to award grants to states, political subdivisions, Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and nonprofit private entities to initiate and sustain mental health first aid training programs. Requires such programs to train individuals in the following categories to accomplish specified objectives: (1) emergency services personnel and other first responders, (2) police officers and other law enforcement personnel, (3) teachers and school administrators, (4) human resources professionals, (5) faith community leaders, (6) nurses and other primary care personnel, (7) students enrolled in an elementary school, a secondary school, or an institution of higher education, (8) their parents, (9) veterans, and (10) other individuals, audiences, or training populations.

Mandate Prevention Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require a point of order in the rules of the House of Representatives for any legislation that would increase the direct costs of federal private sector mandates by an amount that causes the thresholds specified in the Act to be exceeded, unless: (1) the legislation provides new budget or entitlement authority in the House or direct spending authority in the Senate for each fiscal year for such mandates included in the legislation in an amount equal to or exceeding the direct costs of such mandate; or (2) the legislation includes an authorization for appropriations in an amount equal to or exceeding the direct costs of such mandate, and such legislation identifies a specific dollar amount of the direct costs of such mandate for each year up to 10 years during which such mandate shall be in effect, identifies any appropriation bill that is expected to provide for federal funding of such direct costs, and requires the responsible federal agency to determine whether there are insufficient appropriations for such direct costs each fiscal year and to notify the appropriate authorizing committees of Congress of the determination.

Amends Rule XVIII (Miscellaneous Provisions) of the Rules of the House of Representatives to require a point of order in the rules of the Senate for

Free File Act of 2016 This bill continues the IRS Free File program, which provides free commercial-type online individual income tax preparation and electronic filing services to the lowest 70% of taxpayers by income. The IRS must work with the private sector through the program to identify and implement innovative new program features to improve and simplify the taxpayer's experience with completing and filing individual income tax returns in voluntary compliance.

.  Presidential Library Donation Reform Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires each presidential library fundraising organization to submit quarterly reports to the National Archives and Records Administration on every contributor who gave the organization a contribution or contributions (whether monetary or in-kind) totaling $200 or more for the quarterly period. The reports must be published on the website of the National Archives within 30 days after each quarterly filing.  The requirement to submit such information shall continue until: (1) the later of the following occurs, or (2) the President whose archives are contained in the presidential archival depository no longer holds the Office of President.  It shall be unlawful for contributors or fundraising organizations to knowingly and willfully submit false material information or omit material information. Violators shall be subject to criminal penalties.  It shall be unlawful for a person to knowingly and willfully: (1) make such a contribution in the name of another person, (2) permit his or her name to be used to effect such a contribution, or (3) accept a contribution made by one person in the name of another person. Violators shall be subject to criminal penalties under the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.

Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Promotion Act of 1998 - Amends the Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to use up to $1 million for each of FY 1999 through 2003 for the promotion of additional stamp sales.  Requires the Secretary to report to the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission and specified congressional committees on all expenditures.

Renewable Energy Investment Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2018: (1) the investment in renewable electricity production tax credit; (2) new clean renewable energy bonds; (3) the investment tax credit for solar energy, wind energy, and geothermal energy; and (4) the investment in advanced energy facilities tax credit.

Extends through 2018: (1) the tax credits for investment in alternative fuel property (alcohol fuels, biodiesel, and renewable diesel); and (2) the research and development tax credit for fungible biofuels.

National Reconstruction Study Area Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, to complete a study of the area comprised of historical sites in the historic district of Beaufort, South Carolina, relating to the Reconstruction Era (the study area) to assess the suitability and feasibility of designating the study area as a unit of the National Park System.

Directs the Attorney General to provide for the granting of posthumous citizenship, as of September 10, 2001, to a person who died as a result of an injury incurred in one or more of the following events: (1) the hijacking of American Airlines Flight 11 on September 11, 2001, the crash of that aircraft into the World Trade Center in New York, New York, and the subsequent destruction that resulted; (2) the hijacking of United Airlines Flight 175 on such date, the crash of that aircraft into the World Trade Center in New York, New York, and the subsequent destruction that resulted; (3) the hijacking of American Airlines Flight 77 on such date, the crash of that aircraft into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, and the subsequent destruction that resulted; and (4) the hijacking of United Airlines Flight 93 on such date, and the crash of that aircraft in Stony Creek Township, Pennsylvania.

Strengthening Background Checks Act of 2013 - Amends the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 to direct the Attorney General to withhold 10% of the amount that would otherwise be allocated to a state that does not comply with the requirements of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (OCSA) regarding the National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) by the expiration of a two-year period after the Attorney General has determined that the state is making a reasonable effort to comply with such requirements. Authorizes the Attorney General to waive such withholding and provide for additional penalties for states that comply with such requirements. Requires states to implement laws and policies that require them to provide to the Attorney General at least 90% of the records required under OCSA and NICS.

Freedom to Fish Act - Amends the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to prohibit any fishery management plan prepared by a Regional Fishery Management Council or the Secretary of Commerce from establishing areas closed to recreational fishing unless: (1) there is a clear indication that recreational fishermen are the cause of a specific conservation problem and that less severe conservation measures will not adequately provide for conservation and management of the affected stocks of fish; (2) the closed area regulation includes specific measurable criteria to determine the conservation benefit of the closed area on such fish and provides a timetable for periodic review of the continued need for the closed area; (3) the closed area is no larger than that which is supported by the best available scientific information; or (4) provision is made to reopen the closed area to recreational fishing whenever any such condition that was the basis of the closure no longer exists.

Amends the National Marine Sanctuaries Act to direct the Secretary to provide such a Council with the opportunity to propose and revise all regulations applicable to fishing within designated marine sanctuaries according to the standards and procedures of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act. Requires such regulations, upon approval by the Secretary, to apply within the exclusive economic zone and permits application within a

State Court Interpreter Grant Program Act - Directs the Administrator of the Office of Justice Program of the Department of Justice to make grants to States to develop and implement programs to assist individuals with limited English proficiency to access and understand State court proceedings in which they are a party.

Directs the Administrator to allocate, for each fiscal year, $500,000 of the amount appropriated for the Attorney General's Office of Multilingual Access to Justice to establish a court interpreter technical assistance program to assist States receiving such grants.

Social Security Caregiver Credit Act of 2018 This bill amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to provide for a monthly benefit amount for a caregiver of a dependent relative for each month during which the caregiver was engaged for at least 80 hours in providing care without monetary compensation for up to five years of such service. The bill provides a formula for determining the amount of such monthly benefit based on the national average wage index for the second calendar year preceding the year in which the month occurs.

Sexual Assault Prosecution Act of 2002 - Amends the Federal criminal code to provide that an indictment for any offense committed in violation of the prohibition against sexual abuse of children may be found at any time without limitation. (Currently, such an indictment may be found only after a specified period of delay.)Directs the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, in coordination with the Assistant Attorney General of the Office of Justice Programs of the Department of Justice, to develop a plan to grant voluntary awards to States to facilitate DNA analysis of all casework evidence of unsolved crimes.

Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to subject over-the-counter hearing aids to regulations governing food, drugs, and devices.  The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) must promulgate regulations to establish a category of over-the-counter hearing aids. The regulations must: (1) provide reasonable assurances of the safety and efficacy of over-the-counter hearing aids, (2) establish or adopt output limits appropriate for over-the-counter hearing aids, (3) require appropriate labeling, and (4) permit the sale of over-the-counter hearing aids without a prescription. The FDA must also determine whether over-the-counter hearing aids require a premarket notification. The bill prohibits states from establishing requirements that would restrict or interfere with the servicing, marketing, sale, dispensing, use, customer support, or distribution of over-the-counter hearing aids. The FDA must update and finalize the draft guidance of the Department of Health and Human Services entitled "Regulatory Requirements for Hearing Aid Devices and Personal Sound Amplification Products," issued on November 7, 2013.

Red Cliffs Desert Reserve Completion Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to pay James Doyle, out of money not otherwise appropriated, a sum representing the amount to which he may be entitled in order to make himself whole for any damages and losses sustained by reason of the U.S. Government's taking of approximately 2,000 acres of his land located in the St. George area of Utah, now designated as the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve and set aside as habitat for the Mojave desert tortoise, a species listed under the Endangered Species Act of 1973.

Teaching Children to Save Lives Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Education to award grants to eligible local educational agencies (LEAs) or targeted schools for implementing nationally recognized CPR and AED training courses.

Defines "targeted school" as a public elementary school or secondary school that provides education to students in any of grades 6 through 12.

Authorizes LEAs or targeted schools to use the grant for: (1) training individuals in CPR and AED skills and instruction; (2) obtaining printed instructional materials; (3) obtaining manikins; (4) obtaining AED training devices; and (5) obtaining other equipment as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

Directs the Secretary to award such grants based on one or more of following priorities: (1) demonstrated need for initiating a CPR or AED training program in a targeted school or community served by targeted schools; (2) demonstrated need for continued support of an existing CPR or AED training programs in targeted schools or communities served by targeted schools; (3) demonstrated need for expanding an existing CPR or AED training program by adding training in the use of an AED; (4) opportunities to encourage and foster partnerships with and among community organizations to aid in providing CPR

Comprehensive Problem Gambling Act of 2011 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Administrator of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to establish and implement programs for the prevention, treatment, and research of pathological and other problem gambling.

Requires the Administrator, acting through the SAMHSA Administrator, to carry out a national campaign to increase knowledge and raise awareness within the general public with respect to problem gambling issues, including by: (1) augmenting and supporting existing national campaigns and producing and placing public service announcements; (2) encouraging media outlets to provide information, aimed at preventing problem gambling; (3) targeting radio and television audiences of sporting and gambling events; and (4) evaluating and reporting to Congress on the effectiveness of such activities.

Requires the Administrator to: (1) establish and implement a national program of research on problem gambling; and (2) develop a treatment improvement protocol specific to problem gambling.

Requires the Administrator to integrate problem gambling into existing alcohol, tobacco, and other drug prevention programs, where practical.

Welfare Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act (SSA) to prohibit States from providing cash benefits for a minor child born to:  (1) a recipient of TANF assistance; or (2) a person who received such assistance at any time during the ten-month period ending with the birth of the child.  Makes such prohibition inapplicable to children born into families that do not include any other children, children born as a result of rape or incest, and States that have opted out of such application. 
Prohibits the use of State waivers of TANF requirements to deny TANF to a family that has a child to a family member eligible for TANF. 
Requires States to reduce the amount of TANF assistance otherwise payable to a family if an individual in such family refuses to engage in work required by this Act, or to terminate such assistance if the individual refuses to engage in work after the first or second refusal.  Requires a State to terminate TANF assistance for any individual who refuses to engage in work after the third refusal. 
Increases from 50 percent to 75

Requires the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation to establish and maintain a national clearinghouse for information on incidents of crime and terrorism committed against or directed at: (1) any animal enterprise; (2) any commercial activity because of the perceived environmental impact of such activity; or (3) any person because of such person's perceived connection with or support of any such enterprise or activity.
Requires the Director to: (1) accept, collect, and maintain information submitted by law enforcement agencies and victims of such incidents; (2) collate and index such information for purposes of cross-referencing; and (3) provide such information upon request to assist in the investigation of such incidents.

Gun Victim Compensation Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to make any person who sells, delivers, or otherwise transfers a firearm or a handgun to a person who is under age 18 (or who has been adjudicated as a mental defective or committed to a mental institution) liable for damages caused by a discharge of the transferred firearm by the transferee.  Makes such liability inapplicable to:  (1) a handgun transferred to a juvenile in the course of employment, in the course of ranching or farming related to activities at the residence of the juvenile (or on property used for ranching or farming at which the juvenile is performing activities related to the operation of the farm or ranch), target practice, hunting, or a course of instruction in the safe and lawful use of a handgun; (2) a handgun transferred by inheritance of title (but not possession) to a juvenile; (3) a handgun delivered by a juvenile for consideration; or (4) a transfer of a handgun for consideration if the transfer is made in accordance with State and local law and with the prior consent of the juvenile's parent or legal guardian who is not prohibited by Federal, State, or local law from possessing a firearm.

Small Business Relief and Job Creation Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a small business to claim a tax credit for hiring an unemployed individual during 2018 and 2019 who is certified as eligible to receive unemployment compensation under state or federal law during the one-year period ending on the hiring date or whose employment was terminated before January 1, 2018.  The credit applies to wages paid or incurred during 2018 and 2019 that are at least 7.5% (currently, 40%) of the employee's gross receipts. The bill also modifies the eligibility requirements for the credit.

Stop the Sale of Murderabilia Act of 2013 - Amends the federal criminal code to: (1) impose a fine and/or prison term of up to 10 years for an inmate of a federal or state prison convicted of a crime of violence who knowingly deposits for mailing or delivery, or causes to be delivered by mail, any property, article, or object with intent that it be placed in interstate or foreign commerce; and (2) allow an inmate to mail or deliver or cause to be delivered by mail title to real property, title to motor vehicles, or security if the mailing or delivery is to satisfy a debt that is imposed by law or a court order, or is incurred for legal services, a mortgage on the primary residence of the inmate, or the education or medical care of the inmate or a member of the inmate's immediate family.  Authorizes civil forfeiture of any real or personal property used to commit a crime, obtained as a result of such crime, or both.  Authorizes civil remedies, including injunctive relief, damages, and attorney fees, for persons aggrieved by conduct prohibited by this Act.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior or the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to develop and implement a process to expedite access to federal lands for eligible organizations and individuals to conduct good Samaritan search-and-recovery missions, which are searches for one or more missing individuals believed to be deceased at the time that the search is initiated.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) develop search-and-recovery focused partnerships with search-and-recovery organizations to coordinate good Samaritan search-and-recovery missions on federal lands and expedite and accelerate mission efforts for missing individuals; and (2) notify an eligible organization and eligible individual of the approval or denial of a request to carry out a good Samaritan search-and-recovery mission within 48 hours after the request is made.

MMA Territorial Equity for Low-Income Individuals Act of 2004 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for equitable treatment of residents of U.S. territories under the Medicare prescription drug, transitional assistance, and cost-sharing subsidies programs.

Volunteer First Responder Housing Act - Makes a qualified volunteer first responder eligible for a verified adjustment in annual income, in the amount of $18,000, under the Department of Agriculture single family housing guaranteed loan program.

Directs the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to amend: (1) HUD regulations to provide that a qualified volunteer first responder qualifies as a firefighter or emergency medical technician for purposes of the Good Neighbor Next Door Sales Program; and (2) such regulations to provide that, to qualify to purchase a home through the Program, a qualified volunteer first responder shall submit to the Secretary a verification letter from the head of the eligible employer for which the qualified volunteer first responder volunteers, which shall: (1) include the date on which the qualified volunteer first responder joined the eligible employer as a volunteer; (2) attest to the Secretary that the qualified volunteer first responder continuously served as a volunteer for the eligible employer during the two-year period preceding the date of the verification letter, and met or exceeded the minimum requirements for active membership established by the employer during each of such two years; and (3) include a copy of the certification of the qualified volunteer first responder as a firefighter or other responder in the state, unit of general local government, or

Declares that the portion of the project for navigation, Rockland Harbor, Maine, authorized by the Act of June 3, 1896, consisting of a 14-foot channel located in Lermond Cove and beginning at a point with coordinates N. 99977.37, E. 340290.02, thence running easterly about 200.00 feet to a point with coordinates N. 100116.49, E. 340289.25, thence running westerly about 200.00 feet to a point with coordinates N. 100115.37, E. 340289.25, thence running southerly about 138.00 feet to the point of origin, is not authorized.

Redesignates the portion of the project for navigation, Saco River, Maine, authorized under the River and Harbor Act of 1960 as an anchorage area.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to publish a supplement to the major rehabilitation report for the Herbert Hoover Dike system, approved by

Forest Roads-Community Right-To-Know Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to meet with appropriate state and local government officials at least once each fiscal year to describe all agency plans or proposals that, within the next two fiscal years, will or may result in the permanent closure of forest roads on federal lands. Requires the Secretary concerned to provide information that at a minimum: (1) shows forest roads selected or proposed for permanent closure; (2) shows traffic patterns and volumes on the roads over the previous five years; and (3) explains how users of the roads will be adversely affected with longer travel times or adverse travel conditions by the permanent closure of the roads.

Requires the Secretary concerned to: (1) publish an announcement describing the proposed closure in the local newspaper of record for the area likely to be affected by the permanent closure of the road; and (2) permit the public to submit comments regarding the decision to select or propose the forest road for permanent closure.

Prohibits the permanent closure of a forest road unless: (1) advance notice of the permanent closure of the road is provided to the appropriate state and local government officials in the manner provided in this Act; and (2) the Secretary concerned complies with the public notice and

Estate and Gift Tax Phase-Out Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to phase out the estate and gift taxes through an increase in the unified estate and gift tax credit. 
Repeals Federal transfer taxes.

Common Sense Campaign Reform Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a credit, subject to limitations, for a portion of all qualified congressional campaign contributions. 
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to reduce the ceiling on multicandidate political committee (PAC) contributions to candidates. 
Increases the ceiling on contributions to candidates by persons other than multicandidate political committees. 
Prohibits a candidate for federal office from establishing, maintaining, financing, or controlling a political committee other than the principal campaign committee of the candidate. 
Prohibits any multicandidate political committee from making any contribution to another multicandidate political committee. 
Requires each authorized committee of a candidate to include in any report of contributions to such committee, with respect to any contribution of more than $25, the name and mailing address of the person making the contribution, and, in the case of an individual, the occupation and the name of the employer of the individual. 
Requires any separate segregated fund that is a multicandidate political committee to include in its name the name of the entity that establishes the fund. 
Requires any report required by this Act with respect to an authorized committee of a candidate to be signed by the candidate.

Developing Resources Immediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2009 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2009 - Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to revoke the President's authority to withdraw any lands of the outer Continental Shelf from disposition for exploration, development, or production of oil and gas, except as the President determines necessary for national security purposes.

Authorizes a state governor to petition the Secretary of the Interior for authorization to lease for oil and natural gas exploration and extraction in any area that is within 50 miles of the coastline of the state and within the lateral seaward boundaries of the state extended.

Prohibits the Secretary from approving a lease for drilling in any area that is withdrawn for national security purposes.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to deposit into the Clean and Alternative Energy Fund 30% of all rentals, royalties, bonus bids, and other sums due and payable to the United States from leases entered into under this Act for natural gas exploration and extraction activities. Requires the deposit of the remainder into the general fund of the Treasury.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to deposit into the Clean and Alternative Energy Fund 30% of the funds that would be received by the United

Federal Reserve Board Civil Rights Compliance Act of 1999 - Requires the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to post in conspicuous places upon its premises and at other places as determined by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), a notice to employees and applicants for employment setting forth: (1) excerpts from or summaries of the pertinent provisions of title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964; and (2) information pertinent to the rights and procedures applicable under such Acts to employees of, and applicants for employment by, the Board. 
Requires the Board to report to specified congressional committees describing in detail the actions taken by the Board to achieve compliance with title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

Neighborhood Security Act of 2003 - Authorizes the Attorney General, through the Office of Justice Programs, to award one or more grants to nonprofit organizations and professional associations to develop and improve Neighborhood Watches throughout the Nation. Requires funds from such grants to be used to: (1) complete a survey of Neighborhood Watches that identifies such programs by ZIP code; (2) establish a national registry of Neighborhood Watch leaders, with appropriate contact information; (3) identify best practices and model programs among Neighborhood Watches for educating community members about the prevention of terrorism and crime, preventing or assisting with the prevention of terrorism and crime, appropriately responding to terrorism and crime, and achieving broad community involvement in such activities; (4) create a manual for communities seeking to establish or improve a Neighborhood Watch; and (5) engage in outreach and respond to inquiries in order to disseminate information about the benefits of effective Neighborhood Watches, the means to establish new Neighborhood Watches, and the means to improve existing Neighborhood Watches. Requires the grantee to provide a Neighborhood Watch start-up kit which includes material useful for a Neighborhood Watch that is identified by the grantee in response to an appropriate request to create a Neighborhood Watch.

Education Savings Account and School Excellence Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow tax-free expenditures from an education individual retirement account for the elementary and secondary school expenses of a designated beneficiary.  Includes in such amount amounts paid to purchase tuition credits or certificates, or to make contributions to an account under a qualified State tuition program for the benefit of the beneficiary. 
Revises the definition of "qualified education expenses" to include expenses for:  (1) room and board, uniforms, transportation, and supplementary items and services required or provided by a public, private, or religious school in connection with such enrollment or attendance; and (2) academic tutoring and special needs services, books and supplies, computer equipment, and other equipment which are incurred in connection with the enrollment or attendance of the designated beneficiary as an elementary or secondary school student at a public, private, or religious school. 
Revises the special rules for applying the exclusion to elementary and secondary expenses to:  (1) require the aggregate amount of such expenses to not exceed the sum of the aggregate contributions to such account for taxable years beginning after December 31, 1998, and before January 1, 2003, and earnings on such

Restoring the Partnership for County Health Care Costs Act of 2015 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to allow a Medicaid benefit to be provided to a patient who is in custody in a public institution pending disposition of charges.  Title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act is amended to allow a Medicare service to be provided to a patient who is in custody in a public institution pending disposition of charges.  Title XVI (Supplemental Security Income) (SSI) of the Social Security Act is amended to withhold SSI benefits until the individual is no longer either in custody pending disposition of charges or an inmate of a public institution. Title XXI (Children's Health Insurance Program) (CHIP) of the Social Security Act is amended to allow CHIP benefits to be provided to a patient who is in custody in a public institution pending disposition of charges.

Telephone Call Privacy Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to revise the rules governing the use and disclosure of customer proprietary network information. 
Authorizes a person that receives or obtains consumer proprietary network information to disclose such information:  (1) pursuant to the standards and procedures established in the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure or comparable rules of other courts or administrative agencies, in connection with litigation or proceedings to which an individual who is the subject of the information is a party and in which the individual has placed the use, disclosure, or access to such information at issue; (2) to a court, and to others ordered by the court, if in response to a court order; or (3) to an investigative or law enforcement officer pursuant to a warrant or court order.  Sets forth requirements for court orders.

Internet of Things Consumer Tips to Improve Personal Security Act of 2017 or the IOT Consumer TIPS Act of 2017 This bill requires the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to develop voluntary, technology-neutral cybersecurity resources for consumers regarding the practices of consumers with respect to the protection and use of devices that are part of the Internet of Things (IoT). The FTC must ensure that the resources are publicly available on its website.

Indian Tribal Development Corporation Feasibility Study Act of 2004 - Amends the Native American Business Development, Trade Promotion, and Tourism Act of 2000 to direct the Secretary of Commerce to establish the Tribal Development Corporation Feasibility Study Group. Requires the Group to: (1) conduct a study to determine the feasibility of establishing an Indian Tribal Development Corporation; and (2) report to the congressional Indian and Appropriations Committees on the results of the study and any recommendations for further legislative action.

Terminates the Group 120 days after it submits its report. Authorizes appropriations for FY2005 and FY2006.

Railroad Hours of Service Act of 2010 - Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to waive hours-of-service requirements for railroad employees if the Secretary: (1) determines that such waiver is necessary to protect the health and safety of railroad employees; (2) prescribes regulations to require all deadhead transportation in excess of a specific number of hours to be counted as time on duty; and (3) notifies employees of their interim release from duty.

Defines "yardmaster employee" as an employee who supervises and coordinates the activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, including making up or breaking up trains and switching inbound or outbound traffic.

Prohibits the Secretary from waiving hours-of-service requirements for railroad employees for more than two hours in deadhead transportation per each tour of duty.

Requires signal employees operating motor vehicles requiring a commercial driver's license while on duty to be considered covered service.

Prohibits the Secretary from waiving hours-of-service requirements for railroad employees for more than two hours in yardmaster service per each tour of duty.

Requires dispatching service employees and yardmaster employees to be covered under the provisions of this Act if the Secretary determines that such waiver is necessary to protect the health and safety of such employees.

Federal Entrepreneur-in-Residence Act of 2012 - Directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to establish a Federal entrepreneur-in-residence program to appoint individuals to a position in the government service to carry out specified duties, including: (1) assisting federal agencies in improving outreach to small businesses and entrepreneurs; (2) providing recommendations on inefficient or duplicative agency programs and on methods to improve agency efficiency; (3) facilitating meetings and forums to educate small businesses and entrepreneurs on agency programs and initiatives; and (4) providing technical assistance or mentorship to small businesses and entrepreneurs in accessing agency programs.

Directs the Director to: (1) give priority to placing entrepreneurs-in-residence across the federal government at separate agencies, and (2) not appoint more than two entrepreneurs-in-residence to positions in the same agency during the same year. Limits an entrepreneur-in-residence to serving two years in any one agency.

Terminates the program after FY2016.

School-Based Asthma Management Program Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to give States additional preference in determining the need for, and providing, medical assistance in the provision of, asthma-related rescue medications to certain States that: (1) permit trained school personnel to administer epinephrine to any student of the school reasonably believed to be having an anaphylactic reaction; (2) maintain a secure, easily accessible supply of epinephrine and asthma-related rescue medication in a secure location; (3) permit trained school personnel to administer asthma-related rescue medication to any student of the school reasonably believed to have an asthma diagnosis; (4) maintain a plan for having on school premises during all operating hours a trained school nurse or other individuals who are trained school personnel; and (5) have in place a comprehensive school-based asthma management program.

Directs the Assistant Secretary for Educational Research and Improvement to submit to the Senate Committee on Appropriations a spending plan for activities funded through the Office of Educational Research and Improvement for each fiscal year, prior to the obligation of any funds for such fiscal year. 
Declares that the National Assessment Governing Board shall have exclusive authority over all policies, direction, and guidelines for establishing and implementing voluntary national tests for fourth grade English reading and eighteenth grade mathematics. 
Requires the Board to review and modify the current national test development contract, as necessary, and if the contract cannot be modified, to negotiate a new contract under Board control. 
Amends the National Education Statistics Act of 1994 to revise the composition of the National Assessment Governing Board.

Tobacco Program Administrative Reform Act of 1998 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to estimate the costs to be incurred by the Department of Agriculture during the next fiscal year to administer the tobacco quota program under the Agricultural Adjustment Act of 1938, the tobacco price support program under the Agricultural Act of 1949, carry out crop insurance programs for tobacco, and provide extension services related to tobacco production and marketing. 
Requires the Secretary to determine the market share of each tobacco product manufacturer and importer during the most recent calendar year and the amount of the assessment payable by such manufacturers or importers for that fiscal year. 
Establishes the Tobacco Assessment Fund.  Requires the Secretary to refund any excess amounts collected from tobacco product manufacturers and importers. 
Prohibits the use of amounts made available to the Secretary under this Act to change the crop insurance premiums assessed to tobacco producers relative to other crops.

This bill updates the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor Act of 1988 to: (1) state that the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor contained the only historic system of the Industrial Revolution that integrated anthracite mining and resource extraction, canals and railroads, commerce and heavy industry, and a remarkable number of the historic elements of the system are intact; (2) revise the purposes of the Act to include the preservation of the Corridor's conservation and natural resources; (3) require the National Park Service (NPS) to review and approve the strategic plan for the Corridor; (4) require the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor, Incorporated (the Corporation), to develop a strategic plan that takes into account the findings and recommendations of a study titled "Connecting Stories, Landscapes and People: Exploring the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor Partnership" conducted by the NPS Conservation Study Institute; (5) require the Corporation, upon enactment of this Act, to be the local management entity for the Corridor; (6) require the Corporation to assume the duties of the Commission for the implementation of the management action plan; (7) authorize the Corporation to use federal funds to: (1) make

Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area Act of 2015 This bill establishes the Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area in Utah to provide for: (1) enhancement of recreational uses, and (2) the use of off-highway vehicles.  The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) shall administer the recreation area and the proposed exchange parcel (the BLM shall only allow uses of the recreation area that are consistent with the purposes of this bill) and leave the parcel open, in perpetuity, to the use of off-highway vehicles.  If Utah offers to convey to the United States title to the non-federal land, the Department of the Interior shall accept the offer and convey the federal land to Utah.

Arsenic-Treated Wood Mandatory Labeling Act - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to require each piece of arsenic-treated wood offered for sale in the United States to have affixed to it a consumer warning label that displays the following statements: (1) "This piece of wood has been treated with arsenic." (2) "Arsenic exposure through the mishandling of this wood can cause cancer, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea." (3) "Never burn this wood; doing so will release arsenic into the air." (4) "To avoid the health risks associated with mishandling arsenic-treated wood, you must wear gloves, goggles, coveralls, and face masks when working with it." (5) "Wash exposed body areas thoroughly with soap and water after working with arsenic-treated wood." Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, to report to Congress on: (1) the status of any ongoing EPA review of the health risks associated with exposure to arsenic; and (2) recommendations for interim guidelines, pending the completion of such review, for the use of arsenic-treated wood in public and recreational facilities (including parks

Broadband Conduit Deployment Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to require states to evaluate the need for broadband conduit as part of any highway construction project that receives federal funding.  If the evaluation reveals an anticipated need for broadband conduit in the next 15 years, the conduit shall be installed under the hard surfaces (asphalt and concrete pavement, curb and gutter, and sidewalk) as part of the highway construction project.  In carrying out this requirement, DOT shall ensure that:  an appropriate number of broadband conduits are installed along the highway to accommodate multiple broadband providers;  the size of each conduit is consistent with industry best practices and is sufficient to accommodate potential demand;  hand holes and manholes for fiber access and pulling with respect to each conduit are placed at intervals consistent with industry best practices;  standards are established to carry out this requirement that consider the ability to accommodate broadband installation without impacting the safety, operations, and maintenance of the highway facility, its users, or others, population density in the area of the highway construction project, the type of highway involved, and existing broadband access in the area;  each conduit installed includes a pull tape and is capable of supporting fiber optic cable placement techniques consistent with industry best practices

Housing Assistance Authorization Act of 2007 - Prohibits the use of amounts authorized by this Act to lobby or retain a lobbyist for the purpose of influencing a federal, state, or local governmental entity or officer.

Authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to provide financial assistance to the Housing Assistance Council to: (1) develop the ability and capacity of community-based housing development organizations to undertake community development and affordable housing projects and programs in rural areas; and (2) make grants to the Raza Development Fund to provide technical and financial assistance to local non-profit organizations to undertake community development and affordable housing projects and programs serving low- and moderate-income households, particularly through organizations located in neighborhoods with substantial populations of income-disadvantaged Hispanic households. Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to the Housing Partnership Network to create, sustain, and improve access to affordable housing and community facilities that benefit very low-, low-, and moderate-income households and communities.

Emergency Unemployment Compensation Act of 2003 - Amends the Temporary Extended Unemployment Compensation Act of 2002 to provide for a permanent increase in the amount of temporary extended unemployment compensation (TEUC) for individuals who are in an extended benefit period.

Personal Health Investment Today Act of 2009 or the PHIT Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a medical care tax deduction for up to $1,000 ($2,000 for a joint return or a head of household) of qualified sports and fitness expenses in any taxable year. Defines "qualified sports and fitness expenses" as amounts paid for fitness center memberships, physical exercise programs, and equipment for use in a physical exercise or activity program.

Southern New Mexico and El Paso, Texas, Veterans Traumatic Brain Injury Care Improvement Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to report to Congress on the feasibility and advisability of establishing a polytrauma rehabilitation center or polytrauma network site of the VA in the southern New Mexico and El Paso, Texas, region that is within a reasonable driving distance of Fort Bliss, White Sands Missile Range, and Holloman Air Force Base.

Requires such report to include: (1) an assessment of the adequacy of existing VA facilities in such region to address matters that are otherwise addressed by polytrauma rehabilitation centers and polytrauma network sites of the VA; (2) a comparative assessment of the effectiveness of rehabilitation programs for individuals with traumatic brain injuries in urban areas with the effectiveness of such programs for individuals with traumatic brain injuries in rural and frontier communities; (3) an assessment of whether therapies that can prevent or remediate the development of secondary neurologic conditions related to traumatic brain injury can be interrupted by stress caused by living in an urban area; and (4) the relation of high cost of living to the recovery of veterans and the impact on their families in comparison to recovery in an area where there is a lower cost of living

Service Dogs for Veterans Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to commence a three-year pilot program to assess the benefits, feasibility, and advisability of using service dogs for the treatment or rehabilitation of veterans with physical or mental injuries or disabilities, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

Requires the Secretary to: (1) reimburse partners for costs relating to the pilot program; (2) provide a service dog to a number of veterans with physical or mental injuries or disabilities that is greater than or equal to the greater of 200 and the minimum number of such veterans required to produce scientifically valid results; and (3) ensure that half of the participants in the pilot program are veterans who suffer primarily from a mental health injury or disability, and the other half are veterans who suffer primarily from a physical injury or disability.

Requires the Secretary to conduct a scientifically valid research study of the costs and benefits associated with the use of service dogs for the treatment or rehabilitation of veterans with physical or mental injuries or disabilities.

Upper Mississippi Conservation and River Protection Act of 2012 or the Upper Mississippi CARP Act - Directs the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to conduct a study on the feasibility of: (1) temporarily closing the lock at the Upper St. Anthony Falls Lock and Dam to manage the threat of Asian carp (grass carp, silver carp, bighead carp, and black carp) traveling up the Mississippi River in Minnesota, and (2) implementing control measures at such Lock and Dam to manage such threat.  Defines "Asian carp" to mean grass carp, silver carp, bighead carp, and black carp.  Authorizes the Secretary to close such Lock and Dam if closure is determined to be necessary to manage the threat of Asian carp traveling up the Mississippi River in Minnesota.

Coordinating Assistance for TANF Recipients Act This bill amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make grants to states to conduct demonstration projects designed to implement and evaluate strategies to provide coordinated case management to help individuals receiving assistance under a state TANF program or any other state program funded with qualified state expenditures increase their employment and self-sufficiency. HHS must require each state that applies for a grant to: (1) describe how the state will develop an individual responsibility plan for each recipient, (2) describe how the state will coordinate the development of the plan with other programs and agencies providing benefits and services to the individual to help the recipient increase the employment and self-sufficiency of the recipient, (3) describe how the state will coordinate the delivery of the benefits and services to the recipient, (4) describe how the state will meet with the recipient at least monthly to review the employment status of the recipient and the recipient's participation in other activities, the benefits and services the recipient is receiving, and the progress of the recipient toward meeting the goals specified in the individual responsibility plan, and (5)

Veterans Comprehensive Hepatitis C Health Care Act - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide a blood test for the Hepatitis C virus to: (1) each veteran who served on active military duty during the Vietnam era, is enrolled to receive veterans' medical care, and requests such care or is otherwise receiving a physical examination or any other care or treatment from the Secretary; and (2) any other veteran who requests such test. Requires the Secretary to provide such a test to any veteran who presents one or more risk factors for that virus and requests such test.Directs the Secretary to provide increased training options to Department health care personnel to improve treatment of veterans with the Hepatitis C virus.Directs the Secretary to allocate funds for Hepatitis C detection and treatment in allocating funds appropriated for the Department for the "Medical Care" account to the Veterans Integrated Service Networks. Requires the Secretary to develop and implement a standardized policy to be applied throughout the Department health care system with respect to the Hepatitis C virus. Directs the Secretary to establish at least one, and not more than three, Hepatitis C centers of excellence.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program to encourage and assist producers, processors, and other handlers of agricultural commodities that are still fit for human consumption but are unmarketable because of grade, size, or quality restrictions imposed by a marketing order to donate them to selected food banks, soup kitchens, and homeless shelters in the United States to assist the homeless and needy.
Hire Now Tax Cut Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from employment taxes certain individuals hired in 2010 in a trade or business or in a tax-exempt organization.

Quit Smoking Incentive and Opportunity Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable tax credit for certain expenses paid for the benefit of the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse, or any dependent in order to quit smoking or reduce tobacco use. Limits the amount of such credit to $300 for amounts paid for tobacco products and $100 for amounts paid for counseling for tobacco use cessation.

Community Pharmacy Fairness Act of 2007 - Provides that antitrust laws shall apply to negotiations between certain independent pharmacies and health plans in the same manner as such laws apply to labor negotiations under the National Labor Relations Act.

Exempts from such application, however, negotiations relating to: (1) the Medicaid and SCHIP programs; (2) medical and dental care for members of the uniformed services; (3) the federal employees health benefits program; and (4) the Indian Health Care Improvement Act.

Copper Valley Native Allotment Resolution Act of 2007 - Grants rights-of-way across specified Native allotments to the Copper Valley Electric Association for an electric transmission line.

Declares that this Act does not apply to land owned by Ahtna, Inc. and any prior or current right-of-way agreements that may exist between Ahtna, Inc. and the Copper Valley Electric Association or the state of Alaska.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) appraise the value of the rights-of-way granted; (2) pay, if the owner of a Native allotment is alive, or assign of the owner of record, compensation for the grant of a right-of-way over the Native allotment; (3) issue recordable instruments that indicate the location of the rights-of-way over the Native allotments; (4) provide written notice of the compensation procedure for the rights-of-way to the owner of record for each Native allotment and, if the owner of record is deceased, the heir or assign of the owner of record; and (5) publish in the Federal Register and any newspaper of general circulation within the service area of the Association and the location of the relevant allotment notice of the compensation procedure and the location of the right

Influenza Vaccine Emergency Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require a manufacturer or distributor of influenza vaccine to include in a contract for such vaccine a provision that the sale to a purchaser is subject to: (1) a public health emergency declaration by the Secretary of Health and Human Services; and (2) a determination by the Secretary that the purchaser does not receive or lose possession of a quantity of vaccine for which payment has been made.

Requires the Secretary to compensate manufacturers or distributors of influenza vaccine who are affected by such an emergency.

Authorizes the Secretary, in lieu of the emergency declaration, to order a manufacturer or distributor to honor its contracts with States or political subdivisions of States for the sale of such vaccine if the manufacturer or distributor has conflicting obligations under its contracts for sale of the vaccine.

Requires any influenza vaccine to which the Secretary takes title under this Act to be provided: (1) to States and political subdivisions in accordance with the immunization program; and (2) to other public or private entities as appropriate.

Defines an "emergency declaration" as one made by the Secretary if the Secretary publishes in the Federal Register a declaration that there is a public health emergency by reason of a shortage of influenza vaccine.

Water System Adaptation Partnerships Act of 2009 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to make grants to water systems to assist in planning, designing, constructing, implementing, or maintaining any program, strategy, or infrastructure improvement: (1) to conserve water or increase water use efficiency; (2) to carry out water metering to measure water efficiency effectiveness of a water efficiency program; (3) to preserve or improve water quality; (4) to enhance water management by increasing source water preservation and protection, or natural or engineered green infrastructure in the management, conveyance, or treatment of water, wastewater, or stormwater; (5) to increase energy efficiency or the use and generation of renewable energy in the management, conveyance, or treatment of water, wastewater, or stormwater; (6) to support the adoption and use of advanced water treatment, water supply management, or water demand management technologies or processes that maintain or increase water supply or improve water quality; (7) to complete studies or assessments to project how climate change may impact the future operations and sustainability of the water system; or (8) to carry out any other activity or project to address any ongoing or forecasted climate-related impacts on the water quality

Health Care for Veterans of Project 112/Project SHAD Act of 2003 - Makes eligible for hospital care, medical services, and nursing home care any veteran who participated in Department of Defense (DOD) chemical and biological warfare testing from 1962 through 1973, including the program designated as "Project Shipboard Hazard and Defense (SHAD)" and related land-based tests. Extends such eligibility through December 31, 2005.

Amends Federal law to: (1) eliminate the pay and promotion bar for certain health care personnel; (2) provide additional pay for certain veterans' health administration (VHA) employees to perform health care duties on a regular basis during the day and on a Saturday; and (3) allow VHA employees appointed by the VETERANS' CANTEEN Service to be considered for appointment to a Department position in the competitive service for purposes of eligibility for a career appointment.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish a VHA warehouse and storage depot, a VHA space, buildings, and structures, and a VHA personnel department.

Safe, Efficient, Coordinated, Unified, Revitalized, Enhanced Visa Waiver Act - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish, as part of the integrated entry and exit data system required under the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996, an electronic system through which an alien seeking to enter the United States without a visa under the visa waiver program is required to submit biographical information prior to embarkation. Requires such system to: (1) include a method for an electronic determination to be made and an electronic response to be provided in 30 minutes or less, as to whether or not an alien submitting the information is eligible to be admitted to the United States as a nonimmigrant visitor; (2) include a method for requiring carriers and other corporations to inquire electronically, prior to an alien passenger's embarkation, whether the alien has been determined to be eligible for such an admission; and (3) be deployed as soon as possible after the enactment of this Act. Directs the Secretary to establish a fee to be charged to such aliens. Amends the Enhanced Border Security and Visa Entry Reform Act to require the Secretary, by October 26, 2005, to install at all ports of entry equipment

Pro-Growth Budgeting Act of 2014 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to prepare for each major bill or resolution reported by any congressional committee a macroeconomic impact analysis of the budgetary effects of such legislation for the ten fiscal year period beginning with the first fiscal year for which an estimate was prepared under the Act and each of the next three ten fiscal-year periods.  Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to submit to such committee the macroeconomic impact analysis, together with the basis for the analysis, which shall: (1) describe the potential economic impact of the legislation on major economic variables, including real gross domestic product, business investment, the capital stock, employment, interest rates, and labor supply; and (2) describe the potential fiscal effects of the legislation, including any estimates of revenue increases or decreases resulting from changes in gross domestic product.  Requires the CBO, upon completion of the fifth fiscal year after the enactment of any major bill or joint resolution for which it prepared an analysis, to report on the accuracy of the original macroeconomic impact analysis of such enacted bill or joint resolution and submit such reports to the congressional budget committees.

Amends the concurrent resolution on the budget for FY 2002 to revise the total budget authority, total budget outlays, the surplus or deficit, public debt, debt held by the public, net interest (900), and allowances (920) for FY 2002.

Increases the new budget authority and outlays allocated to the House Committee on Appropriations for FY 2002.

Amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act) to revise the general and special sequestration rules.

Preserving Data in Government Act of 2017 This bill requires that any open government data that is made available to the public for at least 90 consecutive days shall: (1) remain machine-readable, available in an open format, and part of the worldwide public domain or, if necessary, published with an open license; and (2) not be altered in such a way as to decrease the machine-readable nature of the open government data.  It shall not be a violation of this requirement to alter: (1) the digital location or format of open government data for the purpose of routine asset maintenance or long-term archiving if the alteration does not decrease the open public accessibility or the machine-readable nature of the data; or (2) the contents of open government data for purposes of updating the data or correcting an error in the data.  Any alteration of the digital location, format, or contents of open government data shall not constitute a renewal of the period for which the data has been made available to the public.  Any substantial alteration of the contents of open government data shall be recorded in a log that is made available to the public in an open format along with the data.
