Small Business Review Panel Technical Amendments Act of 1999 - Amends Federal law to require the head of the Environmental Protection Agency, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration of the Department of Labor, and the Internal Revenue Service to convene a panel to review any material the head has prepared in connection with the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996, including a draft proposed rule, before publishing an initial regulatory flexibility analysis of such rule.  Requires the head to convene the panel solely of full-time Federal employees of the office within the covered agency that will be responsible for carrying out the proposed rule, the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs of the Office of Management and Budget, and the Chief Counsel.  Requires the panel to:  (1) review any material the covered agency has prepared in connection with this Act; (2) collect advice and recommendations from the small entity representatives on issues related to the applicability of the Act to small entities and the type of small entities that might be affected; and (3) allow any small entity representative to make an oral presentation to the panel, if requested.  Requires the head to:  (1) print in the Federal Register the panel's report within 120 days after the head receives

Trade and Environment Enforcement Act or Green 301 Act - Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to include among the categories of prohibited trade practices those that constitute a persistent pattern of conduct that: (1) fails to effectively enforce environmental laws of a foreign country; (2) waives or otherwise derogates from such environmental laws or weakens the protections afforded by them; (3) fails to provide for judicial or administrative proceedings giving access to remedies for violations of such environmental laws; (4) fails to provide appropriate and effective sanctions or remedies for violations of such environmental laws; or (5) fails to effectively enforce environmental commitments in agreements to which a foreign country and the United States are a party.

Directs the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) to identify those foreign country trade practices that cause negative environmental impacts on the protection of human, animal, or plant life or health or the conservation of exhaustible natural resources in the United States, the foreign country, a third country, or internationally.

Improving Security for Investors and Providing Closure Act of 2013 or the Improving SIPC Act of 2013 - Amends the Securities Investor Protection Act of 1970 (SIPA) to authorize SIPC, at the time an action is initiated under SIPA, to allow all customers of the debtor in a bankruptcy proceeding to elect to receive a one-time payment from the SIPC Fund.  Limits such one-time payment to the lesser of: (1) the customer's net equity claim against the debtor, and (2) $500,000.  Prohibits subrogation of rights to any customer who receives such a one-time payment.  Requires SIPC to: (1) promptly notify each customer of the debtor of their rights under this Act, and (2) provide technical assistance to determine if they should make such an election.  Allows judicial review of certain SIPA determinations by a person who is not permitted to make an election under this Act because SIPC does not identify them as a customer of the debtor.

Civil Rights Amendments Act of 1993 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to include sexual orientation (as defined by this Act) among the categories of discrimination prohibited by such Act. 
Amends the Fair Housing Act to include sexual orientation (as defined by this Act) among the categories of discrimination prohibited by such Act.

Promoting Affordable Childcare for Everyone Act or the PACE Act This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make the child and dependent care tax credit refundable, (2) increase the rate of such credit, and (3) allow an inflation adjustment to the rate of such credit.

Absentee Ballot Track, Receive, and Confirm Act - Amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to direct the National Clearinghouse for Absentee Ballots to make a payment to a state to reimburse the state for the costs incurred in establishing, if the state so chooses to establish, an absentee ballot tracking program with respect to elections for federal office held in the state (including costs incurred prior to the date of the enactment of this Act).

Requires such a program to: (1) track and confirm the receipt of absentee ballots in an election for federal office under which the state or local election official responsible for the receipt of voted absentee ballots carries out procedures to track and confirm the receipt of such ballots, and makes information on the receipt of such ballots available to the individual who cast the ballot, by means of online access using the Internet site of the official's office; and (2) include information on whether the vote cast on the ballot was counted, and, in the case of a vote which was not counted, the reasons therefor.

Allows a state with an office without an Internet site to meet such description of a program if the official has established a toll-free telephone number that may be used by an individual who cast an absentee ballot to obtain

Homeowner Empowerment Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income a qualified mortgage distribution made before January 1, 2010, from an individual retirement plan, or from amounts attributable to employer contributions, directly by the plan trustee to a mortgagee with respect to a qualified mortgage of any individual. Defines "qualified mortgage" as any mortgage which is: (1) secured by the principal residence of the mortgagor; and (2) originated before January 1, 2008. Excludes any such distribution to the extent that such distribution exceeds $5,000.

Civil Rights Amendments Act of 2003 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to prohibit discrimination on the basis of religious or sexual orientation (including gender identity and expression).

Amends the Fair Housing Act to prohibit discrimination in housing sales, rentals, and brokerage services on the basis of religious or sexual orientation.

Prohibits the use of religious or sexual orientation as a basis for discrimination in employment.

Prohibits the use of religious or sexual orientation in any finding of discrimination or in the application of any quota.

Prohibits the use of religious or sexual orientation in any finding of discrimination or in the application of any quota.

Prohibits the use of religious or sexual orientation in any finding of employment discrimination or in the application of any quota.

Birthparent Assistance Act of 2008 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide certain services for birthparents who have placed a child for adoption, either directly or by grant to or contract with state or local governmental entities or public or private agencies or organizations, including licensed child welfare or adoption agencies or adoptive family groups and faith-based organizations.

Specifies such services for birthparents as: (1) post-legal adoption services; (2) individual, group, and family counseling; (3) establishment and operation of a nationally-available hotline to provide such counseling and other information relating to the availability of post-adoption services and benefits for birthparents; and (4) training of staff at hospitals and other appropriate birth care facilities relating to interaction of such staff with birthparents and adoptive families.

Animal Drug Amendments of 1994 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to exempt a new animal drug from certain requirements if its approved use is for a lawful veterinary order within the context of a veterinarian-client-patient relationship.

Role Models Academy Demonstration Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to establish a four-year, residential, military style academy that: (1) offers at-risk secondary school students coursework and vocational training leading to a diploma or certificate; (2) focuses on the education and vocational training of youth at risk of delinquency or dropping out of secondary school; (3) has teachers primarily composed of former members of the Armed Forces or Troops to Teachers Program participants; (4) operates a mentoring program; (5) may contain a Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps unit; (6) is housed on the site of any military installation closed pursuant to a base closure law; and (7) serves as a model for similar military style academies throughout the United States.

Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to allow a state-authorized public entity health benefits pool to apply to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) for a pass through of funding for health care benefits provided through that pool for coverage years beginning on or after January 1, 2014. Directs the Secretary to approve such an application if the Secretary determines that health care benefits provided through the pool: (1) will provide coverage that is at least as comprehensive as the state Medicaid program; (2) will provide coverage and cost-sharing protections against excessive out-of-pocket spending that are at least as affordable as the provisions of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) that require individuals and small employers participating in an Exchange to have minimum essential coverage; and (3) will result in cost savings to the federal government because the cost of providing health care benefits to individuals through the pool will be less than the cost of providing health care benefits to them had they become participants in a qualified health plan offered through an HHS Exchange.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) provide for an alternative means by which an aggregate amount determined based on the sum of premium tax credits, cost-sharing reductions, and small business credits that would have been provided with respect

Common Sense Nutrition Disclosure Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act to require food establishments to disclose the number of calories in the whole product, or the number of servings and information per serving, or the number of calories per the common unit division of the product (such as for a multi-serving item that is typically divided before presentation to the consumer).

Allows disclosure of the number of calories in a restaurant or similar retail food establishment's menu, including a menu board, by a remote-access menu (such as one available on the internet) instead of an on-premises menu.

Defines "reasonable basis" for a nutrient disclosure as that the disclosure is within acceptable allowances for variation in nutrient content.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Attorney General to ensure that all numerical limitations applicable to the issuance of H-1B (temporary nonagricultural work visa) nonimmigrants are applied in a manner that: (1) accurately reflects the actual number of aliens who commence employment in the United States as such a nonimmigrant in each fiscal year; and (2) does not count against any such limitation any visa issued to an alien based on a petition filed by an employer that is not used by the alien as the basis for admission into the United States and commencement of employment with such employer within a reasonable period of time subsequent to its issuance, any change of nonimmigrant classification or status authorized for an alien based on a petition filed by an employer that is not used by the alien to commence employment with such employer within a reasonable period of time subsequent to such authorization, or any visa (or authorization to change nonimmigrant classification or status) in excess of one, in cases in which multiple visas (or authorizations) are issued to a single alien in order to permit employment with more than one employer in the United States during identical or concurrent periods of time. Directs the Attorney General to take such steps as may be necessary to ensure that when an

Cell Phone Theft Prevention Act of 2012 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a provider of commercial mobile or commercial mobile data service from providing service on a mobile electronic device that has been reported to such provider as stolen: (1) by the person who holds the account with respect to such service, if such person submits to such provider a copy of a report made to a law enforcement agency regarding the theft; or (2) by another provider.

Requires a provider to which a mobile electronic device is reported stolen to inform all other providers.

Requires a provider to make available to the account holder the capability of deleting, from a remote location, all information that was placed on a mobile electronic device after its manufacture.

Prohibits a person from manufacturing in the United States or importing into the United States for sale or resale to the public a mobile electronic device unless such device is: (1) equipped with a unique identifier; and (2) configured to allow remote deletion of data.

American Elections Act of 2010 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit foreign nationals from making contributions, donations, or expenditures in connection with a federal, state, or local election.

Requires a corporation to certify its compliance with such prohibition.

Requires any communication made by a foreign national to a U.S. corporation or organization to include in a clearly spoken manner the name of the foreign national and the percentage of voting shares of the corporation or organization that is controlled by such foreign national or, if no such shares exist, the percentage of gross receipts that the corporation received from such foreign national in the immediately preceding fiscal year or the current pro-rated fiscal year.

Requires any communication made by a foreign national to a U.S. political committee to include in a clearly spoken manner the name of the foreign national and the percentage of votes that the national has in the national election and the percentage of gross receipts that the national received from foreign nationals in the national election.

Small Business Health Relief Act of 2011 - Title I: Making Coverage Affordable for Small Businesses - Repeals provisions of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care (PPACA) that: (1) require health plans to provide at least bronze, silver, gold, or platinum levels of coverage for certain small businesses, and (2) prohibit high deductible health plans from covering small businesses with a high deductible. Repeals also PPACA requirements that limit the number of small business enrollees to 5% of the total number of enrollees in a plan year. Repeals PPACA requirements that prohibit a high deductible health plan from covering small businesses with a high deductible. Repeals PPACA requirements that limit the number of small business enrollees to 5% of the total number of enrollees in a plan year. Repeals PPACA requirements that prohibit a high deductible health plan from covering small businesses with a high deductible. Amends the Public Health Service Act to repeal PPACA requirements that prohibit high deductible health plans from covering small businesses with a high deductible. Genetic Fairness Act of 1996 - Prohibits an insurer from:  (1) restricting coverage or the sale of a plan to an individual or family member; (2) denying or excluding an individual or family member from coverage; (3) imposing a rider that excludes coverage for certain benefits and services; (4) establishing differentials in premium rates or cost sharing; or (5) otherwise discriminating against an individual or family member in the provision of health care.  Prohibits an insurer from requiring an applicant for coverage or an individual or family member who is presently covered to be the subject of a genetic test or questions relating to genetic information. 
Requires an insurer to provide an enrollee with a written statement disclosing the rights of the enrollee under this Act in a form and manner that is noticeable to and understandable by an average enrollee. 
Provides for enforcement of this Act by the Secretary of Health and Human Services.  Authorizes a person to bring a civil action to enjoin any act or practice which violates this Act or to obtain other equitable relief to redress such violations.  Grants jurisdiction to the U.S. district courts with respect to such actions.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to local educational agencies that have made improvements in teacher quality and student achievement to enable such agencies to carry out school construction.

Education Modernization Fund Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make loans to States for the purpose of constructing and modernizing elementary schools and secondary schools.  Directs the Secretary to determine a formula for allocating funds to States for such loans.  Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer to the Education Modernization Fund a specified amount.

Derivatives and Hedge Fund Regulatory Improvement Act of 2008 - Directs the appropriate federal banking agencies, in coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to initiate a coordinated rulemaking regarding the entities under their jurisdictions that engage in transactions involving unregistered hedge funds or over-the-counter derivatives to: (1) extend the requirements of regulations relating to the safety and soundness of the financial system applicable to mutual funds under the Investment Company Act of 1940 to unregistered hedge funds, including requiring the fund to disclose its borrowing policies and requiring a shareholder vote to change such policy; (2) provide for the regulation of over-the-counter derivatives, including credit default swaps, interest rate swaps, currency swaps, mortgage-backed securities, asset-backed securities, collateralized debt obligations, and other derivatives that are not traded on a national securities exchange or by a registered securities association, in the public interest and for the protection of investors, the stability of the financial markets, and the well-being of the economy; and (3) prohibit insured depository institutions from trading derivatives for their own accounts.

Requires the agencies and authorities to issue the rules in final form that are designed to: (1) avoid systemic risks to the financial markets; (2) ensure safe and

Marriage Penalty Relief Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the standard deduction for marriage penalty relief to 200 percent of the maximum deduction available for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2002; (2) eliminate the marriage penalty in the 15 percent and 25 percent tax brackets; and (3) increase the amount of relief available for taxpayers claiming the earned income credit for children with noncustodial parents.

Repatriate Our Patriots Act - Prohibits a special veteran (an alien who was discharged or released from the Armed Forces under honorable conditions) from being removed from the United States. Defines "special veteran" to: (1) include individuals who were discharged or released under honorable conditions, but exclude those who have been convicted of certain offenses or who have been determined to be a child abuser or a pedophile; and (2) require a special veteran to be naturalized as a U.S. citizen upon filing the appropriate application, paying the appropriate fees, and taking and subscribing before an officer of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to the oath of allegiance required by section 337 of the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Authorizes a special veteran residing abroad to file for naturalization from abroad and to submit the oath of allegiance required by this Act abroad at U.S. embassies, consulates, and, as practicable, U.S. military installations overseas pursuant to the procedures available under the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 for naturalization proceedings overseas for members of the Armed Forces and their spouses and children.

Authorizes the Secretary of Homeland Security to waive the taking of such oath by a special veteran if, in

Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians Recognition Act - Extends Federal recognition to the Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians of Alabama.  Restores Federal rights and privileges that may have been abrogated before this Act's enactment by reason of Federal law that terminated recognition of the Tribe. 
Approves and ratifies the cession of all historical tribal lands to the United States.  Extinguishes all claims against the United States, a State or subdivision, or any other person or entity, by the Tribe arising subsequent to the cession, based upon any interest in or right involving such land. 
Declares that the Tribe has no historical land claim and cannot use Federal recognition to assert any historical land claim. 
Transfers all legal rights, title, and interests in lands held by the Tribe to the United States in trust for the use and benefit of the Tribe. 
Makes the Tribe eligible for all services and benefits that are provided by the Federal Government to Indians because of their status as federally recognized Indians.

Know Before You Fly Act - Amends federal transportation law to declare that it is an unfair or deceptive practice for any air carrier, foreign air carrier, or ticket agent to fail to include, in an internet fare quotation for a specific itinerary in air transportation selected by a consumer, a clear and prominent statement that additional fees for checked baggage and carry-on baggage may apply, along with a prominent link from that internet website page directly to a list of all such fees.

Requires a covered air carrier to publish, via a prominent link on its website, a clear statement indicating whether or not, with respect to a passenger whose travel is interrupted as a result of a widespread disruption, the air carrier will: (1) provide for hotel accommodations; (2) arrange for ground transportation; (3) provide meal vouchers; (4) arrange for air transportation on another air carrier or foreign air carrier to the passenger's destination; and (5) provide for sleeping facilities, food, and water inside the airport terminal.

Defines "widespread disruption" as the interruption of all or a substantial portion of the air carrier's system-wide flight operations, including flight delays and cancellations, as the result of the failure of one or more computer systems or computer networks of the air carrier.

Sport Fish Restoration and Recreational Boating Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Aid in Fish Restoration Act to extend the authorization of appropriations for the sport fish restoration program through FY2017.

Increases the maximum amount of appropriations for the sport fish restoration program for FY2012 and thereafter.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to transfer to the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating specified funds for national boating safety activities of national nonprofit public service organizations.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through FY2017 the exception to the limitation on transfers to a tax-exempt organization for purposes of determining whether such organization is a governmental unit.

Increases from 1.5 to 2 the maximum per capita per year transfer of funds to a tax-exempt organization that is a governmental unit for recreational boating safety programs.

Disaster-Affected Homeowners Notification Act of 2013 - Requires any agency head (the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development [HUD], the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency [FHFA], the Federal National Mortgage Association [Fannie Mae], or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation [Freddie Mac]) that makes available forbearance relief with respect to any covered mortgage, or any such agency head issues any notice or guidelines to mortgagees or servicers recommending or requiring such relief, to: (1) notify each mortgagor under a covered mortgage by telephone call or mail, and (2) provide for areas subject to such disaster declaration, community-wide notification in accordance with the guidelines issued. Direct notification shall inform the mortgagor that: (1) the mortgage is a covered mortgage, (2) the relief is available, (3) there is a moratorium on foreclosure with respect to covered mortgages, and (4) the mortgagor can obtain more information regarding such relief by contacting the relevant agency head.  Requires the applicable agency heads to issue guidelines regarding measures designed to provide notice and awareness of any relief in connection with a major disaster throughout the areas subject to such disaster declaration.

Help Extend Auditory Relief (HEAR) Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for: (1) Medicare coverage of hearing aids as durable medical equipment, and (2) Medicare coverage of hearing rehabilitation and hearing aid services.

Forest Service Financial Accountability Restoration Act of 1999 - Limits the total amount appropriated for the Forest Service to carry out discretionary programs and activities for a fiscal year to the sum of the amounts appropriated for the Forest Service in the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 1999.  Terminates such limitations on the level of Forest Service appropriations or obligations as the earlier of:  (1) the date on which the Forest Service is no longer an agency at high risk of waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement due to weaknesses in its accounting and financial reporting systems; or (2) the end of the fifth fiscal year subject to the limitations. 
Requires the Forest Service to maintain or increase, relative to the levels achieved during FY 1999, specified outputs from programs that directly reduce the natural resources restoration and maintenance backlog within the National Forest System.

Distributed Power Hybrid Energy Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy to develop and transmit to the Congress a distributed power hybrid systems strategy showing: (1) opportunities and priorities that might best be met with distributed power hybrid systems configurations; (2) barriers that exist to the use of such systems; (3) technology gaps that need to be closed; and (4) system integration tools needed to plan, design, build, and operate such systems for maximum benefits.Requires the Secretary to implement the strategy and report to the Congress on the use of, and experience with, distributed power hybrid systems in the United States and the research and development issues remaining to ensure the successful application of such systems.

National Urban Watershed Model Restoration Act - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to develop and carry out a pilot program to serve as a national model for the restoration of urban watersheds and community environments.  Requires such program to be carried out in the Anacostia River watershed, District of Columbia and Maryland. 
Authorizes the Administrator to set aside amounts for grants to local community groups and nonprofit organizations to foster community involvement in the decision making process, environmental educational goals, and restoration strategies. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Social Security Disability Amendments Act of 1994 - Amends title XVI (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to provide for disregard of the income and resources of an ineligible spouse when determining continued eligibility for OASDI benefits. 
Deems plans for achieving self-support that are not approved within 60 days to be approved until subsequently disapproved.  Expands plans for achieving self-support to include housing goals. 
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish by regulation time limits and other criteria:  (1) which are related to an individual's career or housing goal included in a plan for achieving self-support; and (2) that take into account the difficulty of achieving self-support based on the needs of the individual and the goals of the plan. 
Amends OASDI provisions to provide for the disregard of certain grant, scholarship, or fellowship income as earned income for purposes of determining an individual's eligibility for Supplemental Security Income (SSI). 
Amends OASDI provisions to provide for the SSI eligibility of students temporarily abroad.

Truth in Video Game Rating Act - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to prescribe rules to prohibit the following as an unfair and deceptive act or practice under the Federal Trade Commission Act: (1) a rating organization from assigning a content rating to any video or computer game that is to bear such a rating unless the organization has reviewed the game's playable content in its entirety; (2) a person from withholding or hiding game content from a rating organization; and (3) a rating organization from providing a content rating that grossly mischaracterizes the game content.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on: (1) the efficacy of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board's ratings system in assigning appropriate content ratings to video and computer games; (2) whether content ratings systems should be peer-reviewed; (3) whether an independent ratings system would result in more accurate and effective content ratings; and (4) the efficacy of a universal ratings system for visual content, including films, broadcast and cable television and video, and computer games.

Directs the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, to act as the lead federal agency for coordinating and disseminating information on existing federal programs and assistance that may be used to help initiate, develop, and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects for schools.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) review and report to Congress on existing programs and financing mechanisms available in or from the Departments of Agriculture, Energy, Education, and Treasury; (2) establish a federal cross-departmental collaborative coordination, education, and outreach effort to streamline communication and promote federal opportunities and assistance for such projects; (3) provide technical assistance for states, local educational agencies, and schools to help develop and finance such projects; (4) develop and maintain a single online resource website with contact information for relevant technical assistance and support staff in the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy for such entities to effectively access and use federal opportunities and assistance to develop such projects; and (5) establish a process for recognizing schools that have successfully implemented such projects and are willing to serve as resources for other local educational agencies and schools to assist initiation of similar efforts.

Nonprofit Energy Efficiency Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish a pilot program to award grants for the purpose of retrofitting nonprofit buildings with energy-efficiency improvements. Authorizes the Secretary to award a grant if an applicant submits a grant application at such time, in such form, and containing such information as the Secretary may prescribe. Directs the Secretary, in determining whether to award a grant, to apply performance-based criteria, which shall give priority to applications based on: (1) the cost-effectiveness of the energy-efficiency improvement, and (2) an effective plan for evaluation, measurement, and verification of energy savings. Limits each grant award to: (1) an amount equal to 50% of the energy-efficiency improvement, and (2) $200,000.  Authorizes appropriations for the grant program for FY2013-FY2016. Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to extend and increase funding for the Clean Energy Opportunities Program through FY2016.

Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to require plan administrators of individual account pension plans to include with the account statement a notice if the percentage of assets in the plan that consists of employer securities and employer real property exceeds 50 percent of the total account.  Excludes from such determination the employer securities and employer real property held through an investment option of the plan which is not designed to invest primarily in employer securities or employer real property. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to set forth limitations on the aggregate amount which may be excluded with respect to certain qualified retirement planning services provided to any individual during a taxable year.

Medicare HMO Protection Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to delay the effectiveness of a Medicare+Choice organization's termination of its plan until an adequate provider network has been established which will provide at least an equal level of insurance coverage as existed in the area affected by the termination on the date the organization informed the Secretary of its intention to terminate the contract. 
Authorizes the Secretary and the Medicare+Choice organization terminating coverage to negotiate during the period of delay for a new contract which will enable the organization to continue such coverage. 
Extends the initial Medicare+Choice contract period from one year to three years. 
Revises the requirements for enrollee notice at time of termination of Medicare+Choice contracts.

Focus on Children Act This bill amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to direct the Office of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 (the Office) to study and report to Congress on legislation that changes spending on children.  The Office must report on: (1) spending on children under appropriation Acts, (2) spending on children under entitlement authorities, (3) the share of federal spending that constitutes spending on children under appropriation Acts and spending on children under entitlement authorities, and (4) the level of spending on children and the share of federal spending that constitutes spending on children.  The Office must also report on the budget of the President and on the budget of the United States for the fiscal year prior to the one in which the bill was passed.  The Office may provide a warning report to Congress regarding a fiscal year in which outlays for interest on the public debt will exceed spending on children.  The Office must develop and maintain a dashboard and an open data portal that: (1) highlights key indicators of spending on children, and (2) uses visualization tools to assist the public in understanding trends in spending on children over periods of time.

Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund.  Appropriates to such Fund amounts equivalent to certain excise taxes received in the Treasury between September 30, 1997, and October 1, 2002, to the extent such taxes are not attributable to the Highway Trust Fund financing rate.  Makes such Fund available without fiscal year limitation to finance qualified expenses of:  (1) the National Railroad Passenger Corporation; and (2) each non-Amtrak State, to the extent that such States have qualified intercity passenger rail expenses incurred after September 30, 1997, and before October 1, 2002.  Directs the Secretary of Transportation to certify such expenses as qualified for a fiscal year on October 1 of such year, in an amount not to exceed the amount of receipts estimated by the Secretary of the Treasury to be transferred to the Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund for such fiscal year.  Requires the Secretary to determine and retain, not later than October 1, 2002, the amount in the Intercity Passenger Rail Fund necessary to pay any

Guam War Claims Review Commission Act - Establishes the Guam War Claims Review Commission to review the facts and circumstances surrounding the implementation and administration of the Guam Meritorious Claims Act and the effectiveness of such Act in addressing the war claims of American nationals residing on Guam between December 8, 1941, and July 21, 1944.  Directs the Commission to:  (1) review all relevant Federal and Guam territorial laws, records of oral testimony previously taken, and documents in Guam and the Archives of the Federal Government regarding Federal payments of war claims in Guam; (2) receive oral testimony of persons who personally experienced the taking and occupation of Guam by Japanese military forces, noting especially the effects of infliction of death, personal injury, forced labor, forced march, and internment; (3) determine whether there was parity of war claims paid to the residents of Guam under the Guam Meritorious Claims Act as compared with awards made to other similarly affected U.S. citizens or nationals in territory occupied by the Imperial Japanese military forces during World War II; (4) advise on any additional compensation that may be necessary to compensate the people of Guam for death, personal injury, forced labor, forced march, and internment;

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to carry out a program to be known as the Thurgood Marshall Legal Educational Opportunity Program.  Authorizes the Secretary to enter into a contract with, or make a grant to, the Council on Legal Education Opportunity, for a period of at least five years, to:  (1) identify low-income, minority, or disadvantaged college students who are eligible for assistance under this Act; (2) prepare such students for study at accredited law schools; (3) assist them to select the appropriate law school, apply for entry into law school, and receive financial assistance for such study; (4) provide support services to first-year law students to improve retention and success in law school studies; and (5) motivate and prepare such students with respect to law school studies and practice in low-income communities. 
Authorizes the provision of such services through prelaw information resource centers, summer institutes, midyear seminars, and other educational activities. 
Directs the Secretary to allocate not more than $5 million annually for the purposes of providing such services.

Federal Public Safety Officer Surviving Spouse Protection Act of 2005 - Amends Federal law to provide that a survivor annuity for a Federal public safety officer who was killed in the line of duty shall continue for the surviving spouse until age 55.

Drug Rebate Equalization Act of 2009 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require that payment for covered outpatient drugs dispensed to individuals eligible for medical assistance who are enrolled with the entity provided under the agreement entered into under Medicaid be subject to the same rebate required by the agreement as the state is subject to, and capitation rates paid to the entity be based on actual cost experience related to rebates and subject to federal regulations requiring actuarially sound rates.

Requires a Medicaid managed care organization with a contract to provide that: (1) payment for covered outpatient drugs dispensed to individuals eligible for medical assistance who are enrolled with the entity be subject to the same rebate required by the agreement as the state is subject to; and (2) capitation rates paid to the entity be based on actual cost experience related to rebates and subject to federal regulations requiring actuarially sound rates.

Allows a Medicaid managed care organization to exclude or otherwise restrict coverage of a covered outpatient drug on the basis of policies or practices of the organization, such as those affecting utilization management, formulary adherence, and cost sharing or dispute resolution, in lieu of any state policies or practices relating to the exclusion or restriction of coverage of such drugs, provided
Grants a Federal charter to the 29th Division Association, Incorporated (a nonprofit corporation organized under the laws of New Jersey).

Improving Department of State Oversight Act of 2015 This bill provides that any employee of the Special Inspector General for Iraq Reconstruction who completes at least 12 months of service before the termination of the Special Inspector General for Iraq Reconstruction and was not terminated for cause shall acquire competitive status for appointment to any position in the competitive service for which the employee possesses the required qualifications. The Department of State shall certify to Congress that it has made reasonable efforts to ensure the integrity and independence of the Office of the Inspector General Information Technology systems. The bill amends the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to require each Department of State bureau, post, or other office to report to the Inspector General any allegations of: (1) waste, fraud, or abuse in a Department program or operation; (2) criminal or serious misconduct on the part of a Department employee at the Foreign Service-1, General Security-15, or Guard-Major-15 level or higher; (3) criminal misconduct on the part of any Department employee; and (4) serious, noncriminal misconduct on the part of any authorized to carry a weapon, make arrests, or conduct searches.  No entity in the Department of State with concurrent jurisdiction over matters covered by such clauses may

Partnering to Detect and Defeat Tunnels Act This bill requires the Department of Defense (DOD) to seek to enter into agreements with Israel and with U.S. allies to develop technologies to detect and counter tunnels.  The DOD Secretary shall designate a military department or other DOD element to carry out such activities as the lead agency for developing such technology.  The Director of National Intelligence shall designate a senior intelligence officer to manage the collection and analysis of intelligence regarding the tactical use of tunnels by state and non-state actors.  DOD shall report to Congress on instances of tunnels being used to attack U.S. installations and on trends or developments in tunnel attacks worldwide.

Public Pension Parity Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income any amount received by an individual as a governmental pension under a public retirement system.  Limits the aggregate amount of such pension to the maximum benefits payable under title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act which could have been excluded from income for the taxable year.  Makes such exclusion inapplicable to any governmental pension received by the taxpayer during the taxable year unless the taxpayer (or the spouse or former spouse) performed the service giving rise to such pension.

Directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture to:  (1) assess and collect charges for the utilization of radio and television communications sites located on Federal lands administered by the Forest Service or the Bureau of Land Management at rates as the Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management shall establish or at such modified rates as are established under this Act; and (2) review annually the Schedule of Charges to reflect changes in the Consumer Price Index. 
Requires the Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management to transmit to the Congress notification of any such adjustment. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) additional users; and (2) administrative provisions. 
Requires the Secretaries to establish a broad-based advisory group to review the Schedule of Charges and other criteria for determining fair market value for radio and television communications site uses. 
Directs the Secretaries to jointly establish a broad-based advisory group composed of representatives from the nonbroadcast communications industry and the two agencies to review recommendations on acceptable criteria for determining fair market values and next best alternative use.

Directs the President to impose necessary steps, by imposing quotas, tariff surcharges, negotiated enforceable voluntary export restraint agreements, or otherwise, to ensure that the volume of steel products imported into the United States during any month does not exceed the average volume of steel products that was imported monthly into the United States during the 36-month period preceding July 1997.  Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, through the U.S. Customs Service, and the Secretary of Commerce to implement a program for administering and enforcing such restraints.  Authorizes the Customs Service to refuse U.S. entry of any steel products that exceed the allowable levels of imports of such products.  Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a steel import notification and monitoring program.  Requires any person importing certain steel products to obtain an import notification certificate before such products are entered into U.S. customs territory.  Directs the Secretary to compile and publish certain information concerning such imports.

Protecting Employees and Retirees in Municipal Bankruptcies Act of 2014 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to require a municipality to demonstrate that it is financially capable of paying its creditors, including employees or retirees, in good faith. Repeals the limitation on the authority to issue a stay pending an appeal of a determination that a municipality is eligible to be a debtor under bankruptcy. Grants the appropriate court of appeals jurisdiction for an appeal of a determination that a municipality is eligible to be a debtor under bankruptcy.  Revises the definition of "good faith" to mean the same in the National Labor Relations Act. Revises requirements for a municipality to satisfy the federal bankruptcy court's requirement that it is financially capable of paying creditors, including employees or retirees, to eliminate the requirement that the plan of reorganization satisfy the creditors' claims.  Requires the authorized representative of the employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement, or the authorized representative of individuals receiving retiree benefits, to agree to the plan of reorganization in a case in which it modifies a collective bargaining agreement, or modifies a retiree benefit, including an accrued pension, retiree health, or other retirement benefit otherwise protected by state or municipal law, or a retiree benefit as defined in federal law

Health Care Fraud and Abuse Advisory Opinion Act of 1994 - Amends titles XI (General Provisions) and XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue advisory opinions as to what constitutes prohibited remuneration, whether an arrangement or proposed arrangement satisfies the criteria for prohibited remuneration, what constitutes an inducement to reduce or limit services to individuals entitled to benefits under Medicare or Medicare part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance), and whether an arrangement or proposed activity violates other provisions of the Act.  Specifies matters not subject to advisory opinions. 
Provides that such opinions shall be binding as to the Secretary and the requesting party.  Prohibits the introduction of a party's failure to seek an opinion as evidence of the party's intent to violate specified provisions. 
Requires the Secretary to issue regulations establishing a system for the issuance of advisory opinions.  Sets forth the procedures to be followed by a party applying for an opinion and by the Secretary in responding to a request for an opinion.  Sets forth the manner in which advisory opinions will be made available to the public and the interval in which the Secretary shall respond to a request for an opinion.  Prohibits the Secretary from responding to a request

Alternative Minimum Tax Repeal Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to phase out the alternative minimum tax on individuals in 2011. Provides for a reduction of the alternative minimum tax on individuals prior to such phaseout.
Requires the Secretary of Transportation to maximize public participation in proposed rulemaking with respect to such regulations.

Ethanol Stimulus Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow small ethanol producers an increased ethanol production tax credit in two-two states. Defines "two-two state" as a state in which ethanol consumption is more than 2% of the aggregate amount of gasoline consumed and ethanol production is less than 2% of the aggregate amount of ethanol produced in all states.

Amends Federal law to require each Federal agency to make available by computer telecommunications or, if computer telecommunications means have not been established by the agency, by other electronic means (currently, by staff manual or instruction) all agency records that have become the subject of subsequent requests for substantially the same records. 
Requires each agency to make available by electronic means (currently, by staff manual or instruction) a general index of such records. 
Requires each agency to make available to the public by computer network or, if computer network means have not been established by the agency, by other electronic means (currently, by staff manual or instruction) a report on agency compliance with requests for records. 
Requires the Attorney General to:  (1) develop reporting and performance guidelines in connection with such reports by October 1, 1997; and (2) submit an annual report on or before April 1 of each calendar year which shall include a listing of the number of cases arising under the compliance provisions of this Act, the exemption involved in each case, the disposition of such case, and the cost, fees, and penalties assessed.

Amends the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 to prohibit the Export-Import Bank of the United States from guaranteeing, insuring, extending credit, or participating in the extension of credit to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for the People's Republic of China (PRC) unless the Board of Directors of the Bank determines that the entity has established and is adhering to the code of conduct set forth in this Act.  Provides that if the Bank determines that an entity is not adhering to such code, the Bank shall withdraw any guarantee, insurance, or credit that it has provided, and withdraw from any participation in an extension of credit to such entity.  Sets forth provisions regarding the code of conduct. 
Provides that this Act shall not apply to an entity that is a small business. 
Directs the Bank to include in its annual report on the status of the small business community a description of actions the Bank has taken to comply with this Act. 
Expresses the sense of Congress that the Bank and the Clearinghouse on Corporate Responsibility that is being developed by the Department of Commerce should work together to ensure that businesses are made aware of, and have access to, resources and organizations that can assist businesses in

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to convey to the State of Colorado all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to a parcel of real property, including improvements other than Kit Carson Chapel, consisting of approximately 512 acres and comprising the location of the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, to permit the State to utilize the property for purposes of a correctional facility. 
Prohibits the Secretary from making such conveyance unless the State agrees to provide appropriate public access to Kit Carson Chapel and the cemetery located on the real property.  Allows the State to satisfy such condition by relocating the chapel to Fort Lyon National Cemetery, Colorado, or another appropriate location jointly selected by the Secretary and the State. 
Prohibits the Secretary from making the conveyance until the date on which the Secretary opens not less than three health care facilities, and a nursing home care facility, in Veterans Integrated Service Network 19, which shall serve as replacement facilities for the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center. 
Prohibits the Secretary from making the conveyance until the Secretary completes the evaluation and performance of any environmental restoration activities required by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980, and by any

Genetic Privacy and Nondiscrimination Act of 2003 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit health discrimination on the basis of genetic information in both the group and the individual markets.

Victims of Abuse Access to Health Insurance Act - Prohibits health insurers from discriminating against or limiting health insurance coverage or benefits to, or establishing or varying premiums for: (1) an individual on account of being a victim of domestic violence; or (2) a group or employer on account of employing or providing or subsidizing such an individual. Prohibits a health benefit plan from considering a condition or injury that occurred as a result of domestic violence a pre-existing condition.

Imposes criminal and civil penalties for violations of this Act.

Army Arsenal Strategic Workload Enhancement Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD) to develop and promulgate measurable and enforceable guidelines for DOD, defense agencies, and the military services to have supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies made in factories or arsenals owned by the United States, to the extent those factories or arsenals can make them on an economical basis while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilizations, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to: (1) assign government-owned and government-operated DOD arsenals sufficient workload to ensure cost efficiency and technical competence in peacetime, while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilizations, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements; and (2) develop and promulgate guidelines to make arsenals available to DOD, defense agencies, and military services for procurement of supplies, components, parts, systems, and subsystems.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Army to waive the requirement that such arsenals be assigned sufficient workload if necessary for the national defense.

Janey Ensminger Act of 2016 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry to review the scientific literature relevant to the relationship between the employment or residence of individuals at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, for at least 30 days during the period beginning on August 1, 1953, and ending on December 21, 1987, and specific illnesses or conditions incurred by those individuals. The agency must: (1) determine each illness or condition for which there is evidence that exposure to a toxic substance at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, may be a cause of the illness or condition; and (2) categorize the evidence of the connection of such illness or condition to exposure as sufficient to conclude with reasonable confidence that the exposure is a cause of the illness or condition, or as modest supporting causation but not sufficient to conclude with reasonable confidence that exposure is a cause of the illness or condition. The agency must publish the list in the Federal Register and on the Internet website of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and update the list to add an illness or condition for which a determination has been made.  The bill am

Veterans Equal Treatment Act - Terminates the funding allocation formula for the Department of Veterans Affairs medical care system known as the Veterans Equitable Resource Allocation (VERA) system. Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to develop a new formula for the allocation of funds appropriated to the Department for medical care to the national service regions, known as Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs).

Safe and Affordable Drugs from Canada Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to publish a list of approved Canadian pharmacies from which individuals may purchase prescription drugs.

Off-Reservation Land Acquisition Guidance Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, before determining whether to take off-reservation land into trust for the benefit of an Indian tribe under the Indian Reorganization Act, to evaluate: (1) the anticipated benefits to the tribe associated with taking the off-reservation land into trust; and (2) any concerns raised by applicable State and local governments relating to the acquisition of the off-reservation land.

Requires the Secretary, in evaluating the anticipated benefits to the tribe and any such concerns, to prepare a report that includes an assessment of: (1) the impacts of taking the applicable off-reservation land into trust on the on-reservation unemployment rate, on reservation life and tribal membership if the members, dependents, and descendants of the Indian tribe relocate to the off-reservation land or adjacent communities, and on-reservation benefits of taking the off-reservation land into trust; and (2) whether the tribal government can efficiently exercise its governmental and regulatory responsibilities if a gaming facility is constructed on the off-reservation land.

Requires the Indian tribe requesting off-reservation land to be taken into trust to disclose and submit to the Secretary: (1) any plan, contract, agreement, or other information relating to the use, or intended use,

Save Our Seas Act of 2017 or the SOS Act of 2017 This bill amends the Marine Debris Act to require the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to work with other federal agencies and the Department of State and other federal agencies to: (1) develop outreach and education strategies to address both land- and sea-based sources of marine debris, and (2) promote international action to reduce the incidence of marine debris.  NOAA must determine whether there is a severe marine debris event and, if so, provide assistance to a state or NOAA in cooperation with such state to: (1) assist in the cleanup and response required by the severe marine debris event, or (2) determine what other activity is appropriate in response to the event.  NOAA's federal share of the cost of responding to a severe marine debris event shall be 100% if the event is funded by funds made available by an entity, including the government of a foreign country, to the federal government for the purpose of responding to the event.  NOAA's federal share of the cost of any other activity shall be 75% if the activity is funded by funds made available by an entity, including the government of a foreign country, to

Great Lakes Federal Effectiveness Act - Establishes the Great Lakes Research Council.  Directs the Council to:  (1) advise and promote the coordination of Federal research activities to avoid unnecessary duplication and ensure greater effectiveness in achieving ecosystem protection of the Great Lakes through the goals of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement; (2) prepare and provide to interested parties a document which includes an assessment of research activities needed to fulfill the Agreement's goals, an assessment of existing Federal expertise and capabilities in those activities needed to fulfill the Agreement's goals, and recommendations for Federal research priorities; (3) identify topics for and participate in meetings, workshops, symposia, and conferences on Great Lakes research issues; (4) make recommendations for the uniform collection of data for enhancing research and management protocols relating to the Great Lakes ecosystem; (5) advise and cooperate in the establishment of a comprehensive, multi-media data base for the Great Lakes ecosystem; and (6) ensure that the results, findings, and information regarding Great Lakes research programs conducted or sponsored by the Federal Government be disseminated in a timely manner, using as much as possible existing mechanisms.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a deduction, not to exceed $100 ($200 for a joint return), for any political contribution payment made by such individual within the taxable year.  Disallows such deduction to estates and trusts.

Cuba Sanctions Reform Act of 2004 - Expire, with respect to Cuba, restrictions on: (1) assistance under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961; (2) authorities conferred upon the President under the Trading with the Enemy Act; (3) exports to Cuba under the Export Administration Act of 1979; (4) sanctions under the Cuban Democracy Act of 1992, the Cuban Liberty and Democratic Solidarity (LIBERTAD) Act of 1996, and the Trade Sanctions Reform and Export Enhancement Act of 2000; (5) the denial of foreign tax credits with respect to certain foreign countries; (6) sugar imports; and (7) common carriers related to Cuba under the Communications Act of 1934. Authorize the President to impose specified export controls and exercise specified authority under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act with respect to Cuba.

Subject to expiration and renewal by joint resolution of the two Houses of Congress: (1) restrictions on travel to and from Cuba by U.S. citizens or residents and related transactions; and (2) annual remittances to Cuba.

Requires the district judge to hear the evidence and, if it is such as to warrant punishment, to punish such person in the same manner and to the same extent as for a contempt committed before a district judge.
(Sec. 3) Amends the Federal criminal code to grant the magistrate judge the power to enter a sentence for a petty offense. Grants the magistrate judge also the power to enter a sentence for a class A misdemeanor in a case in which the parties have consented.
(Sec. 4) Grants the magistrate judge the power to exercise all powers granted to the district court under the Federal judicial code in petty offense cases involving juveniles.

Community Investment and Empowerment Act - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to direct the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make competitive grants to economically disadvantaged communities that have potential for strong Class 1 commercial investment (retail grocery chains, food service retailers, restaurants and franchises, retail stores, cafes, shopping malls, and other shops) but continue to have a difficult time recruiting such investment.  Defines "Class 1 commercial investment" as retail grocery chains, food service retailers, restaurants and franchises, retail stores, cafes, shopping malls, and other shops.  Defines "economically underserved community" as an area suffering from low income and resultant low purchasing power, limiting its ability to generate sufficient goods and services to be used in exchange with other areas to meet current consumption needs.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to: (1) assess the U.S. economy to determine what goods the United States currently produces, where such goods are produced, in which manufacturing sector the United States is most competitive in the global economy, and what policies are necessary to maintain or increase such competitiveness; (2) develop a comprehensive national manufacturing strategy to increase the aggregate number of manufacturing jobs in the United States, identify emerging technologies to strengthen the competitiveness of the United States in the global marketplace, and strengthen manufacturing sectors in which the United States is most competitive in the global economy; (3) establish targets for the growth of U.S. manufacturing, including targets for job creation, for each of FY2012-FY2016; (4) conduct a survey of all federal agencies that provide support to U.S. manufacturers and report to Congress on the results of such survey; (5) report to Congress on progress and trends in U.S. manufacturing since the Secretary's 2004 "Manufacturing in America: A Comprehensive Strategy to Address the Challenges to United States Manufacturers" and 2009 "A Framework for Revitalizing American Manufacturing" reports; and (6) conduct biennial surveys of persons with headquarters in the United States that

Local Farm Vehicle Flexibility Act - Amends Federal transportation law to authorize the Secretary of Transportation to make grants to States for the operation of certain local farm vehicles (including articulated motor vehicles) on State-registered highways.  Defines "covered farm vehicle" to mean a motor vehicle that: (1) is registered or otherwise designated for use in, or for transportation activities related to, farm operations; (2) is equipped with a special registration plate or other State-issued designation to allow identification of the vehicle as a farm vehicle by law enforcement personnel; (3) is traveling in the State of registration or designation or in another State; (4) is operated by a farm owner or operator, a ranch owner or operator, or an employee or family member of one of such owners or operators; (5) is transporting agricultural commodities, livestock, agricultural supplies, or machinery to or from a farm or ranch; (6) is not used in the operations of a for-hire motor carrier; (7) has a gross vehicle weight rating or weight that is, whichever is greater, 26,001 pounds or less, or greater than 26,001 pounds and is traveling within the State of registration or designation or within 150 air

True Understanding of the Economy and Safety Act or the TRUE Safety Act - Directs the Comptroller General to assess the methodology followed by the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) in carrying out the efficacy of the 34-hour (restart) rule published on December 27, 2011, and to assess the Regulatory Impact Analysis that accompanied the final rule published by DOT on such rule. Requires the Comptroller General to submit a final report to Congress on such assessments, including any recommendations.  Declares that the restart rule shall have no force or effect until six months after the study report required by this Act has been submitted to Congress.

Women's Autoimmune Diseases Research and Prevention Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the Office on Women's Health in the Department of Health and Human Services to expand, intensify, and coordinate research and related activities of the Department with respect to autoimmune diseases in women. Requires the Director to coordinate such activities with other similar activities conducted by the other national research institutes and agencies of the National Institutes of Health to the extent that such Institutes and agencies have responsibilities that are related to autoimmune diseases in women. Requires the Director to conduct or support research to expand the understanding of the causes of, and develop methods for preventing, autoimmune diseases in women. Includes among the activities to be conducted or supported: (1) research to determine the prevalence of autoimmune diseases in women; (2) basic research concerning the etiology and causes of autoimmune diseases in women; (3) epidemiological studies to address the frequency and natural history of such diseases and the differences among men and women, and among racial and ethnic groups, with respect to such diseases; (4) development of diagnostic approaches to evaluating women with suspected autoimmune diseases; (5) clinical research for the development and evaluation of new treatments for women; (6) studies to gain a better understanding of methods of preventing autoimmune diseases

Redundant Remapping Reform Act of 2011 - Prohibits the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) from updating or publishing a national flood insurance program rate map during a specified covered period with respect to an area protected by a levee: (1) for which a community or other party has sought recognition under certain Federal regulations or any successor, and (2) with respect to which the Administrator has not issued a letter of final determination.

Prohibits the Administrator from updating or publishing a national flood insurance program rate map during a covered period with respect to an area protected by a levee that is being planned, constructed, or rehabilitated, if the scheduled completion date for such work occurs during the covered period. Allows the Administrator to update or publish a national flood insurance program rate map during a covered period with respect to an area protected by such a levee: (1) on or after the date on which the construction or rehabilitation is completed, or (2) on or after the date on which the Administrator determines that the planning, construction, or rehabilitation is experiencing an indefinite delay. Requires the Administrator to publish a notice to be used by levee owners to disclose to persons affected by the levees: (1) information relating to

Amends the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 to provide for special immigrant status (for translators, interpreters, or other capacities) for certain aliens serving with federal agencies in Iraq and Afghanistan. Authorizes the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to increase the number of such aliens under special immigrant status to the same extent as individuals admitted (or awaiting admission) to the United States under refugee status are admitted (or awaiting admission) to the United States.

Transparency in Energy Production Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of the Interior to make publicly available through the Internet: (1) information that describes for all covered operations the aggregate amount of each fossil fuel, by type and by state, produced under federal leases, as well as for gas reported the portion and source of such amount that was released by each of venting, flaring, and fugitive release; (2) information that accurately describes the estimated amounts of existing fossil fuel resources on federal lands under lease for the production of fossil fuels, and of federal lands that have potential for such leasing; and (3) information that describes the amount and sources of energy, in megawatts, produced from operating solar, wind, and geothermal projects on federal lands under lease for the production of renewable energy.  "Covered operations" means all fossil fuel operations that are subject to the mineral leasing laws or title V of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976, regardless of size, including production, storage, gathering, processing, transportation, and handling operations.  Interior shall initiate a process under the Federal Oil and Gas Royalty Management Act of 1982, the Mineral Leasing Act, or other applicable law

Directs the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate to make arrangements for the award, on behalf of Congress, of a single gold medal in honor of the U.S. soldiers who were prisoners of war at Bataan/Corregidor/Luzon, collectively, in recognition of their personal sacrifice and service to their country.

Government Shutdown Accountability and Economic Report Act of 2017 This bill requires the payroll administrator of each house of Congress to exclude from the payments otherwise required for a pay period the compensation of each Member of Congress who serves in that house an amount equal to the product of: (1) one day's worth of pay under the annual rate of pay applicable to such Member, and (2) the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect which occur during the pay period.  The bill also requires the payroll administrator of a house of Congress, if on any day during the 115th Congress a government shutdown is in effect, to withhold such compensation and deposit all amounts withheld in an escrow account.  The bill requires the Secretary of the Treasury to provide payroll administrators with necessary assistance to carry out this bill.  The bill requires the Director of the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to report to Congress on each of the following, based on the most recent information available to the CBO: (1) an estimate of the economic output lost on that day as the result of the government shutdown; (2) an estimate of any decrease in gross domestic product for the quarter that will occur as the result of the government shutdown;

Small Business Banking Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends Federal banking law to authorize: (1) any depository institution to permit the owner of any savings or demand deposit account to make up to 24 transfers per month, for any purpose, to another account of the owner in the same institution; (2) any depository institution to permit the owner of any deposit or account to make withdrawals from such deposit or account by negotiable or transferable instruments for the purpose of making payments to third parties; and (3) a lender or servicer of an escrow account to pay interest only if such payments are required by a contract between the lender or servicer and the borrower or by a specific statutory provision of the law in effect in the State in which the property secured by the loan is located. 
Amends the Federal Reserve Act to require that the Federal Reserve banks pay at least once a quarter the interest earned by the depository institutions on their reserves.

Border Security and Elimination of Sanctuary for Illegal Aliens Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to: (1) increase incentives to recruit individuals to become full-time active-duty border patrol agents; (2) develop a retention program for experienced border patrol agents; (3) deploy newly-developed and cutting-edge technologies to secure U.S. international land and maritime borders; and (4) make construction of the border fencing priority.

Requires state and local law enforcement agencies to notify ICE of an alien's unlawful presence in the United States and of his or her arrest.

Requires an alien arrested by ICE to be immediately detained, and presented before an immigration judge, and ordered removed without further hearing or review. Imposes criminal penalties for subsequent unlawful presence.

Drug-Induced Rape Prevention and Punishment Act of 1996 - Amends the Controlled Substances Act to impose a fine and/or imprisonment of up to 20 years for distribution of a controlled substance to an individual without that individual's knowledge, with intent to commit a crime of violence (including rape), against that individual.  Increases penalties for flunitrazepam (a benzodiazepine with effects similar to those of alcohol). 
Directs the Administrator of the Drug Enforcement Administration to study the appropriateness and desirability of rescheduling flunitrazepam as a Schedule I controlled substance. 
Authorizes the Attorney General to create educational materials regarding the use of controlled substances in the furtherance of rapes and sexual assaults.

Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Amendments of 1993 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to authorize the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission (EEOC) to request the head of any Federal agency, department, or unit to appear before the Commission to explain the reasons for any failure to submit a specified plan and to present any objections to any Commission requirement with respect to such plan.  Directs the Commission, if the agency, department, or unit has not submitted the plan by the time established by the Commission, to order the agency, department, or unit or any officer or employee of such agency, department, or unit to submit the plan before the end of such period as the Commission determines to be reasonable.  Authorizes the Commission, in enforcing compliance with any such order, to initiate a proceeding to determine:  (1) who is the officer or employee of the United States responsible for the failure of the agency, department, or unit to comply with such order and the circumstances surrounding the failure to comply; and (2) whether any disciplinary action is warranted against such officer or employee for such failure to comply.  Authorizes the Commission, in enforcing compliance with any order, to issue an order that:  (1) any officer or

Chacoan Outliers Protection Act of 1993 - Designates specified outlying areas of the San Juan Basin and surrounding areas as Chaco Culture Archaeological Protection Sites. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to assist the Navajo Nation in the protection and management of such Sites through a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement entered into pursuant to the Indian Self-Determination and Education Act.

(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on February 19, 2018.  (Sec. 1) This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to convey to the Tanana Tribal Council in Tanana, Alaska, all interest of the United States in and to certain property in the village of Tanana for use in connection with health and social services programs.  HHS shall convey such property to the Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation in Dillingham, Alaska, for use in connection with health and social services programs. Neither the Tanana Tribal Council nor the Corporation shall be liable for soil, surface water, groundwater, or other contamination resulting from the disposal, release, or presence of environmental contamination on any of the properties.

Dental and Optometric Care Access Act or the DOC Access Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require a group health plan or individual or health insurance coverage (including a plan or coverage offering limited scope dental or vision benefits) to provide, with respect to a doctor of optometry, doctor of dental surgery, or doctor of dental medicine that has an agreement to participate in the plan or coverage and that furnishes items or services that are not covered by the plan or coverage, that the doctor may charge the enrollee (a person enrolled under the plan or coverage) any amount determined by the doctor that is equal to, or less than, the usual and customary amount that the doctor charges individuals who are not so enrolled for such items or services.

Allows changes to plans only pursuant to a subsequent agreement signed by the doctor that documents the acknowledgment and acceptance of the doctor to such changes.

Prohibits: (1) an agreement between such a doctor and such a plan or coverage that offers limited scope dental or vision benefits from lasting more than two years; (2) such a plan or coverage from requiring a doctor participating in the provider network to be credentialed by any specific plan or coverage offering limited scope dental or vision benefits; and (3) such a plan
