Earmark Transparency Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the Clerk of the House of Representatives and the Secretary of the Senate to jointly establish a searchable website, available to the public at no cost, listing all requests by Members of Congress for congressionally directed spending items.

Requires such website to be comprised of a database including specified information for each such request, including the fiscal year in which the item would be funded, the number of the bill or joint resolution for which the request is made, if available, the amount of the initial request made by the Member of Congress, the amount approved by the committee of jurisdiction, the amount carried in the bill or joint resolution as passed by the House, as passed by the Senate, and as transmitted to the President, the name of the department or agency, and the account or program through which the item will be funded, the name and the state or district of the Member of Congress who made the request, the name and address of the intended recipient, the type of organization of the intended recipient, the project name, description, and estimated completion date, a justification of the benefit to taxpayers, whether the request is for a continuing project, and a description, if applicable

Less Imprecision in Species Treatment Act of 2018 or the LIST Act of 2018 This bill amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to revise the process for removing a species from the endangered and threatened species lists.  The Department of the Interior must initiate the procedures to remove a species from the lists if: (1) the goals of a recovery plan for the species developed under the Act have been met, or (2) the goals for recovery of the species have not been developed and Interior determines that the species has recovered sufficiently to no longer require the protection of the Act.  Interior must remove a species from any list if substantial scientific or commercial information demonstrates that the species is recovered or that recovery goals have been met.  Interior must also find, within 90 days after Interior receives or produces certain information regarding a species included in the lists, whether the listing was less likely to have occurred in the absence of that information. If Interior finds that a listing was determined on the basis of scientific or commercial information available to Interior that was inaccurate, fraudulent, or misrepresentative, Interior must remove the species from the lists.
Makes a national but not a U.S. citizen eligible for advanced training in, or financial assistance as a member of, the Senior Reserve Officers' Training Corps.

Veterans' Housing Benefits Enhancement Act of 2007 - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to furnish improvements and structural alterations for a member of the Armed Forces who has a total permanent disability incurred or aggravated in the line of duty in the active military, naval, or air service while such member is hospitalized or receiving outpatient medical care, services, or treatment for such disability if the Secretary determines that such member is likely to be discharged or released from the Armed Forces for such disability.

Makes eligible for specified housing assistance a disabled veteran or member of the Armed Forces with a severe burn injury.

Directs the Secretary to report to Congress on the adequacy of authorities available to the Secretary to assist disabled veterans in acquiring: (1) suitable housing units with special fixtures or movable facilities required for their disabilities; (2) residences already adapted with special features determined by the Secretary to be reasonably necessary as a result of their disabilities; or (3) such adaptations to their residences as are reasonably necessary because of their disabilities.

Makes eligible for specified housing assistance a disabled member of the Armed Forces who: (1) has a permanent disability in the range of 50% to 70% determined by the Secretary; (2) is hospitalized or receiving outpatient medical care, services,

Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals Reorganization Act of 2000 - Divides the current U.S. Court of Appeals for the ninth circuit into the following two circuits: (1) the ninth circuit composed of Arizona, California, and Nevada consisting of 20 judges, to be held regularly in San Francisco and Los Angeles; and (2) the twelfth circuit which includes Alaska, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Northern Mariana Islands, Oregon, and Washington, consisting of eight judges, to be held regularly in Portland and Seattle.

Main Street Survival Act - Expresses the sense of Congress that the President, acting through the Secretary of the Treasury, should encourage financial institutions that have received federal financial support to maintain historic levels of lending to small and medium-sized businesses.

Directs the Secretary to establish the Main Street Revolving Loan Fund Program to provide temporary loans to businesses that meet a specified size requirement.

Establishes in the Treasury a revolving loan fund for the Program.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) transfer and credit $1 billion to the revolving loan fund from dividends paid by financial institutions that have received financial assistance under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008; (2) use the fund to carry out the Program; and (3) deposit amounts received as payment on loans provided under the Program into the fund.

Sets forth loan eligibility and terms.

Prohibits the use of Program funds to significantly expand operations.

Limits the maximum loan amount to a particular business in any fiscal year.

Dairy Promotion Equity Act - Amends the Dairy Production Stabilization Act of 1983 to require that 2 members of the National Dairy Promotion and Research Board be representatives of dairy product importers. 
Requires dairy product importers to pay an assessment to the Board. 
Provides for a referendum on the Dairy Promotion Equity Act.

Balanced Trade Act of 2006 - Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to direct the President, whenever the United States current account deficit exceeds 2% of the gross domestic product (GDP), to: (1) determine that fundamental international payments problems do exist that require special import measures to restrict imports; and (2) declare a temporary import surcharge in the form of duties on imported articles.

Requires the period of the surcharge to end when there is no current account deficit, or a deficit that does not exceed 1% of the gross domestic product.

Iran Intelligence Oversight Act - Requires the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) to submit to Congress an updated National Intelligence Estimate on Iran within 90 days after the enactment of this Act. Requires the DNI to report to Congress if the estimate cannot be submitted by such date. Requires the National Intelligence Estimate to address: (1) the foreign policy and regime objectives of Iran; (2) the current status of the nuclear programs of Iran; (3) Iran's military and defense capabilities, including non-nuclear weapons of mass destruction programs and related delivery systems; (4) the relationship of Iran with terrorist organizations, the use by Iran of terrorist organizations in furtherance of its foreign policy objectives, and the factors that might cause Iran to reduce or end such relationships; (5) the prospects for support from the international community for various potential courses of action with respect to Iran; (6) the anticipated reaction of Iran to the courses of action set forth above; (7) the level of popular and elite support within Iran for the Iran regime, and for its civil nuclear program, nuclear weapons ambitions, and other policies, and the prospects for reform and political change within Iran; (8) the views among the populace and elites of Iran regarding the United States, including views on

Financial Accounting for Intangibles Reexamination (FAIR) Act - Expresses the sense of the Congress that, prior to changing existing rules of accounting for business combinations and intangible assets, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Accounting Standards Board should undertake a comprehensive reexamination of the appropriate methods of accounting for purchased and internally-generated intangibles including goodwill, and should await the results of related studies of these issues. 
Provides for the continued validity of the current method of accounting for business combinations (pooling of interests method) until the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Accounting Standards Board submit to the Congress a report on the appropriate methods of accounting for purchased and internally-generated intangibles. 
Establishes the Commission on Financial Accounting for Intangibles to:  (1) consider the general usefulness of financial statements prepared under generally accepted accounting principles in light of recent trends in the securities markets; (2) consider the impact that shortcomings in generally accepted accounting principles have on securities market volatility, capital allocation, and the investment of retirement fund assets, both individual and institutional; (3) consider methods to better identify, value, and account for purchased and internally-generated intangible assets; (4) examine the general questions surrounding the role of intangible assets in financial reporting

Immigration Backlog Reduction Act of 2011 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct an immigration officer who determines that an alien who is arriving in the United States, or who has not been admitted or paroled into the United States and has not been physically present in the United States continuously for the four-year period immediately prior to the date of the determination of inadmissibility to be removed from the United States without further hearing or review, unless: (1) the alien has been charged with a crime; (2) the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) determines that the alien presents a significant risk to national security; or (3) the alien indicates an intention to apply for asylum under section 208 or a credible fear of persecution and the officer determines that the alien has been physically present in the United States for less than one year.

Directs the officer, if an alien who is arriving in the United States, or who has not been admitted or paroled into the United States and has not been physically present in the United States continuously for the four-year period immediately prior to the date of the determination of inadmissibility is inadmissible and the alien indicates either an intention to apply for asylum or a credible fear of

Mortgage E-Verify Act of 2010 - Amends the Federal National Mortgage Association Charter Act to prohibit the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) from: (1) refinancing, restructuring, or modifying any single-family housing mortgage held by or backed by any security issued by Fannie Mae; or (2) purchasing, or issuing any security backed by, any single-family housing mortgage made for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of the mortgagor's previous single-family housing mortgage on the same property, unless the mortgagor's identity and work eligibility under such mortgage has been confirmed through an inquiry made under the basic pilot program of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 (E-Verify program).

Amends the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation Act to prohibit the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) from: (1) refinancing, restructuring, or modifying any single-family housing mortgage held by or backed by any security issued by Freddie Mac; or (2) purchasing, or issuing any security backed by, any single-family housing mortgage made for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of the mortgagor's previous single-family housing mortgage on the same property,

Cure for AIDS Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program, to establish and support an accelerated research program dedicated to the discovery of a cure for HIV/AIDS. Requires the Secretary to coordinate with at least one eligible nonprofit entity to establish research priorities for peer-reviewed funded research.

Acid Deposition and Ozone Control Act of 1997 - Amends the Clean Air Act to require the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to add any State to the single ozone transport region that contributed four parts per billion or more of ozone via aerial transport to the ozone level of any noncompliant area in the region for any of the second through tenth worst ozone days that occurred during the previous ten years. 
Requires any control measure adopted before this Act's enactment to apply to any State added after this Act's enactment. 
Directs the Administrator to require reductions in the emissions of nitrogen oxide and sulfur dioxide in any State added to the region to one-third of the 1990 levels by the year 2003.  Authorizes the Administrator to establish an allowance trading program to carry out such requirements.

.  (Sec. 1) This bill amends the Stock Exchange Act to make public, online, and available to Members of Congress and candidates for Congress, as well as certain executive branch officials, financial disclosure reports and related information. (Sec. 8) The bill repeals a related requirement that certain financial disclosure reports be filed through the congressional offices. (Sec. 11) The bill repeals a related requirement that certain financial disclosure reports be filed through the executive branch.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a 20-year recovery period for the depreciation of highly efficient heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and commercial refrigeration equipment installed in residential rental property and nonresidential real property before January 1, 2013. Allows a 25-year recovery period for the depreciation of other such equipment installed in residential rental property and nonresidential real property before January 1, 2013. Requires the use of the straight line method of depreciation for such property.

Financial Institution Customer Protection Act of 2014 - Prohibits an appropriate federal banking agency from suggesting, requesting, or ordering a depository institution to terminate a specific customer account or otherwise restrict or discourage it from entering into or maintaining a banking relationship with a specific customer unless: (1) the agency has a material reason for such action, and (2) such reason is not based solely on reputation risk.  Requires the agency, if it believes a customer poses a threat to national security, to state such belief satisfies the materiality requirement.  Requires the agency to provide such action in writing, along with a justification for it, including any specific laws or regulations the agency believes are being violated by the customer, if any.  Prohibits the agency from providing such justification solely on the basis of reputation risk to the institution.  Requires the agency to report annually to Congress on the number of specific customer accounts it suggested, requested, or ordered a depository institution to terminate during the previous year, as well as the legal authority under which it made such suggestions, requests, and orders.  Amends the Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery, and Enforcement Act of 1989 to revise requirements for summoning witnesses and requiring production of books and other records.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to render convicted of an aggravated felony or a firearm offense inadmissible. 
Prohibits the granting of a waiver of inadmissibility for aliens who are unlawfully present in the United States after the expiration of the authorized period of stay or who are unlawfully present in the United States without being admitted or paroled. 
Makes an alien who makes a misrepresentation to procure benefits for another alien inadmissible or ineligible for the finding of good moral character. 
Makes an alien inadmissible or deportable upon the commission of a crime rendering such alien inadmissible or deportable. 
Authorizes the Attorney General to detain an alien on a warrant issued by the Attorney General until a removal decision is made.  Authorizes the Attorney General to release an alien on bond of at least $2,000 with security approved by, and containing conditions prescribed by, the Attorney General.

Amends the Federal Reserve Act to subject to call by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) one-twelfth of the subscription to any qualifying member bank (member bank) with total consolidated assets of $10 billion or less.  Authorizes the Board, in making such call, to adjust the dollar amounts of total consolidated assets of qualifying member banks to reflect the change in the Gross Domestic Product Price Index, published by the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve Boundary Adjustment Act of 2004 - Amends the National Parks and Recreation Act of 1978 to adjust the boundary of the Barataria Preserve Unit, Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve, Louisiana.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire any land, water, and interests in land and water within the boundary of the Unit by donation, purchase with donated or appropriated funds, transfer from any other federal agency, or exchange.

Requires any federal land in the area identified on the map as "CIT Tract Addition" that is transferred without consideration to the administrative jurisdiction of the National Park Service (NPS) and any private land in the areas to be acquired only with the consent of the owner of the land.

Requires the Secretary to preserve and protect fresh water drainage patterns, vegetative cover, the integrity of ecological and biological systems, and water and air quality.

Authorizes the Secretary to: (1) acquire state land; and (2) acquire oil and gas rights.

Declares that any reference in a law, map, document, paper, or other U.S. record to the Barataria Marsh Unit shall be considered to be a reference to the Barataria Preserve Unit, and

Authorized Rural Water Projects Completion Act - Establishes the Reclamation Rural Water Construction Fund in the Treasury for the construction of rural water projects authorized by this Act. Requires the Secretary of the Interior to deposit into such Fund for FY2013-FY2029 amounts equal to the revenues that would otherwise be deposited for the fiscal year into the reclamation fund established by the Act of June 17, 1902. Allows the Secretary to expend from the Fund for FY2013-FY2034 up to specified amounts, plus any interest accrued in the Fund for the fiscal year in which the expenditures are made. Requires the Secretary to use amounts from the Fund to complete construction of rural water projects: (1) authorized to be carried out by the Secretary on or before the enactment of this Act, or (2) for which the Secretary has completed a feasibility report by September 30, 2012, that recommends the construction of a rural water project, and an Act of Congress has authorized the construction of the project. Prohibits the use of amounts from the Fund to pay for operation and maintenance costs of an authorized rural water project.  Requires the Secretary to invest such portion of the Fund as is not required

Iran Nuclear Nonproliferation Act - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) full diplomatic, political, and economic relations between the United States and Iran cannot be normalized unless and until enforceable safeguards are put in place to prevent weaponization of Iran's nuclear program and the government of Iran ends its support for international terrorist groups, but the attainment of these policy objectives should not constitute preconditions for any diplomatic dialogue; and (2) no congressional authorization for the use of military force in any Act of Congress enacted before the enactment of this Act constitutes, either implicitly or explicitly, an authorization for the use of military force against Iran or its nuclear program.

States the policy of the United States not to enter into a preemptive war against Iran in the absence of an imminent threat, and then only in accordance with international law and constitutional and statutory requirements for congressional authorization.

Prohibits the use of funds appropriated or otherwise made available to the Department of Defense or any other federal department or agency in carrying out any covert action for the purpose of causing regime change in Iran or any military action against Iran in the absence of an imminent threat, in accordance with international law and constitutional and statutory requirements for congressional authorization.

Amends the Small Business Administration Act to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to award competitive grants to eligible associations to establish and carry out programs under which qualified small businesses provide technical assistance to small businesses located in low participation areas within states that receive disproportionately low numbers of Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) or State Technology Transfer (STTR) grants.  Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to impose criminal penalties on aliens who remain in the United States for any period of time after their most recent visa or status has expired. Provides an exception for medical, public safety, or national security reasons.

Prohibits a first-time offender from being admitted to the United States for five years and from being granted a visa for ten years, respectively. Prohibits a subsequent offender from being admitted to the United States and from being granted a visa.

Requires the Secretary of State or the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to provide aliens with notice of such penalties when they apply to visas for entry into the United States.

Provides that a revocation of an alien's entry visa shall automatically cancel any other valid visa in the alien's possession.

Revises provisions regarding the sharing of information with foreign governments. Authorizes the Secretary of State to provide foreign governments with copies of Department of State and U.S. diplomatic and consular records pertaining to the issuance or refusal of visas or permits to enter the United States if it is in the U.S. national interest.

Directs the Attorney General and the Federal Bureau of Investigation to provide the Secretary with access to the criminal history record information contained in National Crime Information Center files for the purpose of determining

Outer Continental Shelf Enhanced Exploration and Deep Water Incentives Act - Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior, at the discretion of a lessee or on lessee petition, to reduce, suspend, or eliminate certain royalty or net profit shares in leases for oil and gas production in outer Continental Shelf waters.  Declares that no royalty payment shall be due on new production from any lease located in water depths of 200 meters or greater until the capital costs directly related to such new production have been recovered by the lessee out of the proceeds from such new production.  Subjects any production of oil or natural gas to royalties at the lease stipulated rate if the arithmetic average of the closing prices for the earliest delivery month on the New York Mercantile Exchange for light sweet crude oil or natural gas exceeds specified levels per barrel. 
Directs the Secretary to:  (1) designate as frontier areas portions of the outer Continental Shelf with respect to which the Secretary will exercise authority to reduce, suspend, or eliminate the requirement to pay royalties; and (2) define the term "frontier area" for purposes of carrying out such designation.

TPS Reform Act of 2016 This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to revise the process for granting temporary protected status (TPS) to an alien from a foreign country who is in the United States on a nonimmigrant visa.  The bill requires that an alien be designated as a foreign country upon enactment of an Act that contains a finding that:   there is an ongoing armed conflict within the foreign country and, due to such conflict, requiring the return of aliens who are nationals of that country would pose a serious threat to their personal safety;  there has been an earthquake, flood, drought, epidemic, or other immediately life-threatening environmental disaster in the foreign country resulting in a substantial, but temporary, disruption of living conditions in the area affected and the country is unable to handle adequately the return to the country of aliens who are nationals of the country; or  there exist extraordinary and temporary conditions in the foreign country that prevent aliens who are nationals of the country from returning to the country in safety and that allowing such aliens to remain temporarily in the United States is not contrary to U.S. national interest.  The bill terminates an alien's TPS upon enactment of an Act that contains a finding that the foreign country (or part of such country

Military Call-Up Relief Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the ten percent early withdrawal penalty distributions from qualified retirement plans made to individuals who are members of a reserve component called or ordered to active duty during the period of a presidentially declared national emergency.

Fair Credit Reporting Act Amendments of 2000 - Amends the Fair Credit Reporting Act to require a consumer reporting agency, upon the request of any consumer, to provide a free credit report annually at least once each calendar year.Provides that the information in a consumer's file furnished to a consumer reporting agency by a credit scoring agency or any other provider of information shall not be disclosed to the extent that it is sufficient to allow the consumer to contact the agency, or request a consumer report relating to the consumer from the agency, through the Internet or the World Wide Web.Directs the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Trade Commission to: (1) review and monitor the extent to which, and the manner in which, consumer reporting agencies and furnishers of consumer information to consumer reporting agencies are complying with the procedures, time lines, and requirements under the Fair Credit Reporting Act for the prompt investigation of the disputed accuracy of any consumer information and the prompt correction or deletion of any inaccurate or incomplete information or information that cannot be verified; and (2) report to the Congress on the results of such review.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make permanent the increased ($500,000) expensing allowance for depreciable business assets, including computer software; and (2) allow individual taxpayers a tax deduction for the purchase of a domestically manufactured automobile. Limits the amount of such deduction to $10,000 per vehicle. Terminates such deduction after 2010.

State Veterans Home Nurse Recruitment Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make payments to assist states in the hiring and retention of nurses and the reduction of nursing shortages at state homes.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a small manufacturers' computer hardware and software tax credit for the lesser of: (1) 50% of the cost of qualified computer hardware and software property; or (2) $35,000. Defines "qualified computer hardware and software property" as any computer hardware and software property for use in any small manufacturer (50 or fewer employees) located in the United States that is: (1) the original use of which commences with the taxpayer; and (2) which is property of a character subject to the allowance for depreciation. Terminates such credit after 2011.

Residential and Commuter Toll Fairness Act of 2009 - Authorizes states, counties, municipalities, and multi-jurisdictional transportation authorities that operate or manage roads, highways, bridges, railroads, busses, ferries, or other transportation systems to establish programs that offer discounted transportation tolls, user fees, or other fares for residents of specific geographic areas in order to reduce or alleviate toll burdens imposed upon such residents.

Taxpayer's Right to View Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a cable operator from collecting separate charges for video programming of a sporting, theatrical, or other entertainment event if such event is performed at a facility constructed, renovated, or maintained with tax revenues or by an organization that receives public financial support.  Authorizes the Federal Communications Commission and local franchising authorities to make determinations concerning the applicability of the prohibition.

Consumer Learning through Electronically-Accessible and Reasonable Cost Information Act of 2013 or the CLEAR Cost Information Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a subsection (d) hospital (a hospital serving fewer than 50 patients per day and having an average daily cost per procedure of $450 or less) to report payment data to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) on the actual amounts collected from uninsured and insured patients over the preceding two years for the five hundred most common diagnosis-related groups and ambulatory payment classification groups for which payment is made under Medicare in both the inpatient and outpatient settings. Requires the Secretary to post such data on a publicly accessible and searchable website in a form and manner that: (1) allows for meaningful comparisons of hospital collections and related policies by zip code, and (2) is readily understandable by a typical consumer. Requires a subsection (d) hospital to include a link to such posted data on its home website. Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require the Secretary of the Treasury to post the annual report of the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission on the public website of the Secretary in a form and manner that: (

Communities Committed to College Tax Credit Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of charitable contributions paid in cash to a qualified scholarship funding trust. Limits the annual amount of such tax credit to $200 million.

Clinical Trials Modernization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to establish a framework through which sponsors of drugs, biological products, or devices may submit proposals for the incorporation of adaptive trial designs, Bayesian methods, or other alternative statistical methods into proposed clinical protocols and marketing applications for drugs, biological products, or devices. The FDA must: (1) update and finalize the draft guidance addressing the use of adaptive trial design for drugs and biological products, and (2) issue draft guidance on the use of Bayesian methods in the development and regulatory review and approval, licensure, or clearance of drugs, biological products, and devices. The FDA must also establish a process for periodically evaluating postapproval studies or clinical trials to determine whether: (1) the trial or study is no longer scientifically warranted, or (2) the design, or the timelines applicable to the completion of, the study or trial should be renegotiated because of changes in medical practice or the standard of care.

Medicare Home Health Equity Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the formula for payment to home health agencies for services furnished for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 1997.  Restores the cost limits for such services and increases the cost limits for services furnished by home health agencies. 
Directs the Director of the Congressional Budget Office to estimate annually, and to certify to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the amount of savings to the Medicare program resulting from the interim payment system for home health services established by this Act.

Ensuring the Taxpayer a Fair Return for Federal Onshore Oil and Gas Resources Act of 2015 This bill amends the Mineral Leasing Act to increase the minimum bid price and annual rental rate for federal oil and gas and tar sands leases. The Department of the Interior must adjust these prices by the cost-of-living adjustment at least once every four years.  Interior's royalty rates are increased from 12.5% to 18.75%, with a 50% royalty share for on-shore oil and gas leases.  The bill also revises the distribution of royalties from federal oil and gas leases.

Kake Tribal Corporation Land Exchange Act - Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the Kake Tribal Corporation approximately 2,427 acres of land in the Copper River Meridian, Alaska, which shall be suitable for development, which shall be a municipal watershed area, and which shall be conveyed to Sealaska Corporation.

Caring Family Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual taxpayer an additional personal exemption from the tax for income attributable to the care of dependent individuals with long-term care needs in the taxpayer's home.

Serving Everyone with Reliable, Vital Internet, Communications, and Education Act of 2007 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to expand the assistance provided through the Lifeline Assistance Program and the Link Up Program by allowing low-income consumers participating in such programs to choose to use such assistance for any one of the following: (1) wire or wireless telephone service; (2) Internet access service; (3) wire or wireless broadband service; and (4) any evolving technology deemed to be consistent with the purposes of universal service.

Directs the FCC to study and report to Congress on: (1) the necessary benefit level for a household participating in the Lifeline Assistance Program or the Link Up Program which will encourage low-income consumers to seek broadband service; (2) projections on the potential of new broadband service consumers who would seek such service if economically accessible; (3) industry requirements to provide broadband service access in underserved areas; (4) data that illustrates the extent of current deployment of broadband service to residential users; and (5) policy proposals conducive to addressing gaps in broadband service availability.

Business Relief and Incentives for Small Entrepreneurs Act of 2007 or the Business RAISE Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow a 15-year recovery period for the depreciation of certain improvements to retail space, including new construction; and (2) classify certain qualified restaurant property as 15-year property for purposes of the tax deduction for depreciable business property.

Expands the eligibility of disabled veterans for the work opportunity tax credit.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to study the economic and trade impact of agricultural exports of food products from cloned animals, including: (1) the domestic and international trade economic implications of permitting commercialization of milk and meat from cloned animals and their progeny into the food supply; (2) consumer and exporter behavioral responses that must be factored into the economic and health impact analyses; and (3) the health effects and costs attributable to milk from cloned animals in the food supply.

Directs the Secretary to contract with the National Academy of Sciences to study and report to Congress on the safety of food products derived from cloned animals.

Remains in effect until the Secretary of Health and Human Services issues the final risk assessment.

On-the-Job Training Tax Credit Act of 2015  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers with not more than 500 full-time employees during the taxable year a tax credit for up to 50% of the cost of providing training to their employees. The credit applies to training that is: (1) an apprenticeship program registered and certified with the Department of Labor, (2) a program licensed, registered, or certified by a state workforce investment board or apprenticeship agency or council, (3) conducted by a vocational or technical education school, community college, industrial or trade training organization, or labor organization, (4) a program that conforms to apprentice training programs developed or administered by an employer trade group or committee, or (5) an industry-sponsored or administered program that is clearly identified and commonly recognized. The credit is not allowed to an employer if the employee who receives the credit is not employed for at least 40 hours per week for at least two years.

National Parks Capital Improvements Act of 1996 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into a memorandum of agreement with an entity to act as an authorized fund raising organization for the benefit of the Grand Canyon National Park and any other national park designated by the Secretary that has an approved general management plan with capital needs in excess of $5 million.  Requires the organization to issue taxable bonds in return for a park surcharge.  Prohibits the U.S. from being liable for the security of any such bonds, except that if the surcharge is not imposed for any reason or if such surcharge is reduced or eliminated, the full faith and credit of the United States is pledged to the payment of such bonds and the interest accruing on them. 
Authorizes the Secretary to:  (1) authorize the Superintendent of the park to charge and collect, in addition to the entrance fee, a surcharge of up to $2 for each individual charged the entrance fee; and (2) use such surcharge to amortize the bond issue, to provide for the reasonable costs of administration, and to maintain a sufficient reserve consistent with industry standards.  Requires any funds collected in excess of the amount necessary to amortize the bond issue, pay reasonable administrative

Campaign Information Improvement Act - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to revise requirements for nonpreemptible advertising by broadcast stations.  Revises requirements for the lowest unit charge of a station for the same class and amount of time for the same period to require the lowest charge of the station for the same amount of time for the same time of day and day of week. 
Prohibits a station from preempting a candidate's use of its broadcast time during any period from 30 days before the election until 60 days after the election, unless the circumstances are beyond the control of the station. 
Revises requirements for the free broadcast time obligation for policy debates. 
Revises requirements for the free cable time obligation for policy debates.

SAFE Transitional License Act - Amends the S.A.F.E. Mortgage Licensing Act of 2008 to provide temporary authority for loan originators to continue to originate loans after moving: (1) from one state to another, or (2) from a depository institution to a non-depository institution.

Crime Victims' Bill of Rights Act - Amends the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure to require the court, upon request, to address personally any victim of the offense for which sentence is to be imposed and to afford the individual the opportunity to make a statement and present information in relation to the sentence. 
Amends the Victims of Crime Act of 1984 to require the court, upon request, to provide the victim with an opportunity to be heard in camera, in the penultimate sentence, with respect to the victim's rights. 
Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to require a State, in order not to reduce the funds available for the program by 25 percent, to:  (1) notify a victim of the availability of such separation while waiting for a courtroom appearance; (2) provide such victim such separation; (3) provide the earliest possible notice of the scheduling of each court proceeding or parole hearing that the witness is required or entitled to attend; and (4) address personally any victim of the offense for which sentence is to be imposed and afford the individual the opportunity to make a statement and present information in relation to the sentence. 
Directs the Attorney General to assure that Federal prosecutors and

Requires a copy of a warrant or subpoena to be served on the subscriber or customer of the remote computing service before or at the same time the warrant or subpoena is served on the service provider.
Allows the subscriber or customer a meaningful opportunity to challenge a subpoena.
Makes such provisions applicable to remote computing services and Internet Web sites operated by such entities.
Makes such provisions inapplicable to remote computing services and Internet Web sites operated by non-governmental entities.
Makes such provisions inapplicable to remote computing services and Internet Web sites operated by third parties.
Makes such provisions inapplicable to remote computing services and Internet Web sites if the disclosure is: (1) necessary to initiate, provide, bill, or collect for such service or for access to or use of such Internet Web site; (2) necessary to protect the rights or property of the service or Internet Web site provider; (3) made at the request of the subscriber or customer; (4) made with the subscriber's or customer's affirmative consent; or (5) required by law.
Makes such provisions inapplicable to remote computing services and Internet Web sites if the aggregate customer or subscriber information has been removed from the information disclosed.
Prohibits such service providers from terminating the provision of such service or access to or use

Strengthening Homeland Security, Intelligence, and Essential Law Enforcement Departments Act of 2011 or SHIELD Act of 2011 - Requires, in the event that the total public debt reaches the public debt limit, specified priority payments on obligations incurred by the U.S. government to be made.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, during a period of lapsed appropriations for the Armed Forces, to make available to the Secretary of Defense (and the Secretary of Homeland Security, if applicable) amounts in the Treasury necessary to continue to provide pay and allowances (without interruption) to members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard, including their reserves, who perform active service during the period of lapsed appropriations.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, during a period of lapsed appropriations for a federal agency that employs critical law enforcement officers, to make available to the agency head amounts in the Treasury necessary to continue to provide pay and allowances (without interruption) to such officers during the period of lapsed appropriations. Defines "critical law enforcement officer" as an employee who: (1) has statutory authority to make arrests or apprehensions; (2) is authorized by the agency to carry firearms; and (3) whose duties

Prohibits a product from bearing a label suggesting that it was made in America unless:  (1) the product has been registered with the Department of Commerce; and (2) at least 60 percent of the product was manufactured in the United States and final assembly took place in the United States. 
Requires a person to register with the Department any product on which there is or will be affixed a label suggesting that the product was made in America. 
Establishes penalties for fraudulent use of such labels. 
Amends the Tariff Act of 1930 to require that if an article of foreign origin is required to be marked with a foreign content mark, and the article is assembled from parts that are the product of one or more foreign countries that are not the country of origin, then the article or container shall be marked in such manner as to indicate, or accompanied by such written, printed, or graphic matter that indicates, in English to the ultimate purchaser in the United States the proportion of the customs value of such article that is accounted for by the parts from each such foreign country. 
Requires any product manufactured in the United States and assembled from parts that are the product of a foreign country to:  (1) disclose the country of origin of

District of Columbia Land Use Notification Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 to require the Administrator of the General Services Administration (GSA) to provide notice to the Mayor of the District of Columbia, the Chair of the Council of the District of Columbia, and the Chair of the Advisory Neighborhood Commission in whose neighborhood the property is located before carrying out any activity that affects real property located in the District of Columbia that affects real property located in the District. 
Authorizes the Administrator to waive such requirement if it would jeopardize the public safety or national security interests of the United States. 
Requires a covered agency to provide notice to the individuals described above and give them the opportunity to present comments before carrying out any activity that affects real property located in the District. 
Authorizes a covered agency to waive such requirement if compliance would jeopardize U.S.   security interests, but only if the agency:  (1) certifies such finding and the reasons for it to the individuals and to Congress; and (2) provides such individuals with notice and opportunity to present comments. 
Prohibits any event from being held at the William H. G. Fitzgerald Tennis Center at Rock Creek Park without the prior approval

Security Enhancement and Jobs Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS), within 120 days after receipt of an application submitted by an airport operator, to approve or deny the application and provide the airport with a list of qualified private screening companies, unless the Secretary determines that the approval would compromise security, detrimentally affect the efficiency or effectiveness of the screening of passengers or property at the airport, or otherwise adversely affect the mission of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

Directs the Secretary to reconsider any application for the screening of passengers and property that: (1) was submitted by the operator of an airport pursuant to this Act; (2) was pending for final decision by the Secretary as of January 1, 2011; and (3) has not been approved by the Secretary on or before such date of enactment.

Fair American Corporate Tax Act or FACT Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) reduce the top marginal rate on corporate income by 3% for income exceeding $75,000; (2) reduce the alternative minimum tax rate by 3% for income exceeding $75,000; and (3) limit the amount of tax withheld from payments made by persons to members of the same foreign controlled group of entities (a controlled group as defined by this Act) as a deduction to the foreign parent corporation.

Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Improvement Act of 2011 - Amends the Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Act of 2004 to redefine the term "Alaska Natural Gas Transportation Project" to mean: (1) any natural gas pipeline system that carries Alaska natural gas to the border between Alaska and Canada that is authorized under the Alaska Natural Gas Transportation Act of 1976 or specified statutory authority, and (2) any pipeline segment that the Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Regulatory Commission finds could feasibly be incorporated into and serve as an integrated segment of such system.

Directs the Attorney General to establish the National Task Force on Violence against Women.  Directs the task force to develop a uniform Federal, State, and local law enforcement strategy to protect women against violent crime, to punish violent criminals, and to enhance the rights of violent crime victims. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to transfer certain naval vessels to:  (1) the Government of Brazil; (2) the Government of the Dominican Republic; (3) the Government of Ecuador; (4) the Government of Egypt; (5) the Government of Greece; (6) the Government of Mexico; (7) the Government of Poland; (8) the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States (Taiwan); (9) the Government of Thailand; and (10) the Government of Turkey. 
Expresses the sense of the Congress that:  (1) the President should transfer to the Government of the Philippines certain excess defense articles; and (2) the United States should not oppose the transfer of F-5 aircraft by a third country to the Government of the Philippines.

Volunteer Firefighter and EMS Support Act of 2008 - Amends the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish a program to provide funds to a state or local government, non-profit firefighter association, or governmental or nongovernmental emergency medical services organization that carries out a volunteer firefighter incentive program.

Directs the Secretary to pay such government, association, or organization an amount equal to the total amount of expenditures of funds not received from the federal government made by such government, association, or organization for such fiscal year to carry out the volunteer firefighter incentive program.

Preventing Illegal Radio Abuse Through Enforcement Act or the PIRATE Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to subject any person who willfully and knowingly does or causes or suffers to be done any pirate radio broadcasting (i.e., transmitting on spectrum frequencies between 535 to 1705 kHz or 87.7 to 108 MHz without a Federal Communications Commission license) to a fine of up to $2 million. A person who willfully and knowingly violates such provisions or any rule, regulation, restriction, or condition relating to pirate radio broadcasting shall be subject to a fine of up to $100,000 for each day during which such offense occurs. A person who knowingly and intentionally facilitates pirate radio broadcasting shall be subject to a fine of up to $2 million. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) shall: (1) publish a database of all licensed radio stations operating in the AM and FM bands, and (2) revise its rules to issue a "Notice of Apparent Liability" directly without issuing a "Notice of Unlicensed Operations."  The FCC shall assign enforcement personnel to focus specific and sustained attention on the elimination of pirate radio broadcasting within the

Skills Connection Act - Directs the Secretary of Labor to create a publicly available, easily navigable, and searchable database that contains: (1) a registry of industry-recognized credentials that are consistent with the Secretary's established industry competency models and are consistently updated through third party validation to reflect changing industry competencies; (2) a skills database that lists identified skills that are required for employment in the manufacturing sector, as well as skills developed through service in the Armed Forces; and (3) a jobs bank that enables job seekers to enter basic information about their skills, experience, and credentials, as well as to browse job listings submitted by employers that match those qualifications.

Requires the database to be publicly available and searchable on the Secretary's website.

Supporting America's Protective Security Advisor Act of 2007 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) a Protective Security Advisor Program Office, which shall be the lead office for DHS critical infrastructure protection activities.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to develop a plan for the assignment and distribution of protective security advisors that takes into account baseline requirements and anticipated growth after the enactment of this Act.

Civil Rights Commission Act of 1998 - Extends the term of the Civil Rights Commission (CRC) and authorizes appropriations. 
Revises the term of office for the Staff Director. 
Requires the CRC to:  (1) implement the U.S. General Accounting Office recommendations regarding revision of CRC Administrative Instructions and structural regulations to reflect the current agency structure; and (2) establish a management information system to enhance the oversight and project efficiency of the CRC. 
Requires the CRC to:  (1) report to the Congress on the enforcement of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990; (2) report on the crisis of young African-American males; (3) report on fair employment law enforcement; and (4) develop and carry out a study on the civil rights implications of regulatory obstacles confronting minority entrepreneurs. 
Requires each CRC advisory committee to be designed to conduct fact finding activities and develop findings or recommendations for the CRC.

Workers' Political Rights Act - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to make requirements for contributions and expenditures by labor organizations political committees inapplicable to labor organizations unless they meet specified requirements, including: (1) providing written notification to all employees within the labor organization's bargaining unit or units and new employees within 30 days after commencement of their employment informing such employees that they cannot be obligated to pay, through union dues or any other mandatory payment to a labor organization, for the political activities of such organization; (2) prohibiting requiring an employee actually to join any labor organization but allowing an employee to elect instead to pay an agency fee to the labor organization; (3) limiting the amount of such an agency fee to the employee's pro rata share of the cost of the labor organization's exclusive representation services to the employee's collective bargaining unit; (4) entitling an employee who elects to be a full member of the labor organization and pay membership dues to a reduction of the employee's pro rata share of those dues by the employee's pro rata share of the labor organization's total spending for political activities; and (5) requiring an annual examination by an independent certified public accountant of financial statements supplied by the labor organization att

Telecommunications Trust Act of 1998 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to terminate the requirement for contributions by interstate telephone service providers to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for universal service support funds in the Treasury.  Authorizes the FCC to continue to distribute any balances of such contributions that remain unallocated on the date specified, but the funds appropriated for universal service support shall constitute the exclusive source of funds for the provision of any type of Federal universal service support.  Authorizes appropriations for FY 1999 and each of the five succeeding fiscal years.  Allows appropriations for any fiscal year that are available to carry out universal service support provisions to be made available for obligation by the recipient on the basis of an academic or school year differing from such fiscal year.  Requires any funds from such appropriations during any fiscal year which are not obligated and expended prior to the beginning of the fiscal year succeeding the fiscal year for which such funds were appropriated to remain available for obligation and expenditure during such succeeding fiscal year. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish in the Treasury the Telecommunications Trust Fund consisting of such amounts as may be appropriated or credited pursuant to this Act.  Requires amounts in the Fund to be transferred to the Advanced Telecommunications

Directs the Secretary of Education to pay to Fort Lewis College in the state of Colorado, for each fiscal year beginning in FY2011, the tuition charges for Indian students who are not residents of Colorado and who are enrolled in Fort Lewis College for the academic year ending before the beginning of such fiscal year. Limits the amount paid to Fort Lewis College for each fiscal year under this Act to the tuition charges for Indian students who were not residents of Colorado and who were enrolled in Fort Lewis College for the 2010-2011 academic year.

Treats any amounts received under this Act as a reimbursement from Colorado to Fort Lewis College for complying with the requirement of the Act of April 4, 1910, to admit Indian students free of charge of tuition.

Rebuilding Equity Act of 2013 - Directs the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to establish a voluntary program for borrowers who qualify for the Home Affordable Refinance Program and whose subject property has a loan-to-value ratio of at least 105% to refinance from a loan with an original term of 30 years to one with a term of 20 years or less. Requires the program to pay $1,000 toward the closing costs associated with applying for and receiving the refinancing when the borrower agrees to refinance into a fully amortizing loan with a term of not longer than 20 years.  Directs the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) to adjust the amount of the portion of the closing costs that each enterprise will pay under the program, based on economic conditions generally affecting the mortgage and housing markets, and for each of the next two 12-month periods, upon the expiration of the 12-month period that begins on the enactment of this Act.  Requires the program to terminate three years after its establishment.

Rural Broadband Access Enhancement Act - Amends the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 to revise eligibility requirements for rural broadband loans and loan guarantees.

Requires the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to take steps to reduce the paperwork required of applicants.

Requires the Secretary to conduct outreach designed to inform the population of areas in which there is no or limited broadband service of the program.

Prohibits the Secretary from approving a loan or loan guarantee application for the provision of new broadband service to an eligible rural community in which the service is provided by three or more entities.

Eliminates a limitation on eligibility based on the number of subscriber lines.

Prohibits more than 10% of the amounts made available for each fiscal year for loans or loan guarantees from being used to provide such loans or loan guarantees to entities with more than 10% of the telephone subscriber lines installed in the aggregate in the United States.

Prohibits more than 40% of such amounts from being used to provide such loans or loan guarantees to entities with not less than 2% and not more than 10% of such lines.

Limits the term of loans and loan guarantees to 35 years.

Security Clearance Family Review Act This bill amends federal law regarding presidential security clearances to prohibit the Department of Defense (DOD) from granting eligibility for access to classified information to a relative of the President for purposes of federal employment unless a favorable determination is submitted to the head of DOD.  If the President determines that a relative of the President requires access to classified information for federal employment, the President shall submit a letter to the Director of the Office of Government Ethics requesting a determination regarding the relative's suitability for such access. The Director shall conduct a review to determine whether the applicable relative has any ongoing and substantial commercial relationships with state-owned or privately owned foreign enterprises or financial institutions and, if so, whether the relative is ineligible for access to security clearance because of such relationships.

Waives the core township requirement for certain land for specified Federal land located within specified sections of the Copper River Meridian, Alaska. 
Authorizes Cape Fox to select and receive conveyance of specified surface estate of Tongass National Forest land located outside the exterior selection boundary of Cape Fox.  Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to Cape Fox and Sealaska Corporation the subsurface estate to the land.

This bill designates the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, Missouri, and the Old Courthouse on the grounds of the Jefferson National Expansion Memorial as national historic landmarks.  The bill authorizes the Department of the Interior to take the following actions to ensure the protections of the National Historic Preservation Act:   enter into agreements with the Jefferson National Expansion Memorial Trust to plan and develop the St. Louis riverfront between Eads and Poplar Street bridges, the Memorial grounds including the interstate highway and roadways now traversing them, Luther Ely Smith Square, and the Old Courthouse as a single project area and to facilitate the planning, construction, and operation of a cultural facility on federal land within the boundary of the Memorial; transfer one or more portions of the Memorial grounds to the administrative jurisdiction of the Trust and enter into agreements with the Trust to assist in the implementation of the Final General Management Plan and Record of Decision; and enter into agreements with the Trust for such other facilities and services provided in the design competitions in furtherance of the purposes of this Act, including completing the project of designing the Gateway Arch and constructing the Old Courthouse in St. Louis in time for the 50th anniversary of the Arch's completion in 2015.

Department of Defense Office of the Victim Advocate Act of 2004 - Establishes in the Office of the Secretary of Defense an Office of the Victim Advocate to: (1) coordinate programs and activities of the military departments to the extent that they relate to victims of sexual misconduct or interpersonal violence which, in the case of a member of the armed forces, is carried out by another member or a family member or intimate partner; and (2) serve as the program manager for the victim advocates and the victim service specialists in the Department of Defense.Authorizes appropriations.

Amends the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act to repeal the ownership of cultural items by the federal government based on the land on which they are discovered. 
Requires that any person or entity that disposes of or controls a cultural item on federal land comply with the requirements of this Act. 
Requires that cultural items excavated or discovered on federal land after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under the provisions of this Act, be:  (1) recorded according to generally accepted scientific standards; (2) under the control of the agency having primary management authority for the land on which the cultural item was excavated or discovered until 90 days after the publication in the Federal Register of a notice setting out a general description of the item, its estimated age, and the general area of discovery; and (3) subject to the study provisions of this Act. 
Limits the authorization for study to those items for which no lineal descendants have been identified. 
Revises provisions regarding the study and recording of human remains and associated funerary objects and of all other cultural items.

Transparency and Accountability of Failed Exchanges Act This bill amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require a state that is awarded an exchange establishment grant and terminates the operation of the exchange to submit to Congress and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) an audit of the use of grant and return funds.  HHS shall return to the state any property acquired with grant funds and report on the provision of such property to the state.  HHS may dispose of any such property through a public auction for cash and for not less than its fair market value or lease or hire it.  The bill prohibits the subchapter IV (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act from preemposing any state enforcement action of alleged fraud, waste, and abuse of funds issued pursuant to the bill. States that terminate or transfer their exchange shall refer all current and future matters involving fraud, waste, and abuse of funds issued pursuant to the bill to the Department of Justice.

Transnational Criminal Organization Illicit Spotter Prevention and Elimination Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to impose criminal penalties for knowingly transmitting, by any means, to another person the location, movement, or activities of any federal, state, local, or tribal law enforcement agency with the intent to further a federal crime relating to U.S. immigration, customs, controlled substances, agriculture, monetary instruments, or other border controls.

Imposes criminal penalties for knowingly and without lawful authorization destroying, altering, or damaging any fence, barrier, sensor, camera, or other physical or electronic device deployed by the federal government to control the border or a port of entry or otherwise seeking to construct, excavate, or make any structure intended to defeat, circumvent, or evade any such device.

Amends the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act to prohibit carrying or using a firearm during and in relation to an alien smuggling crime.

Amends the Federal criminal code to: (1) set forth provisions regarding the statute of limitations for violations of this Act; and (2) make provisions regarding the prohibition of carrying or using a firearm during and in relation to an alien smuggling crime.

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a 20-year recovery period for the depreciation of qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property.  "Qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" is defined as any roof system: (1) placed in service above-conditioned or semi-heated on an eligible commercial building, (2) having a slope of equal to or less than 2:12, (3) which replaces an existing roof system, and (4) which includes specified insulation and a primary roof covering, as long as the property is located in a climate zone other than climate zones 6, 7, or 8.  The bill also requires the depreciation of such property to be determined using the alternative depreciation method, which provides for a nonrecognition of depreciation of certain business assets.

Nye County Higher Education Campus Conveyance Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the University and Community College System of Nevada (UCS), without consideration, all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to specified federal land in Nevada for use as a campus for the Nye County Nevada Higher Education Campus. Conditions such conveyance on the Chancellor of the University system agreeing to: (1) pay any administrative costs associated with the conveyance, including the cost of any environmental, wildlife, cultural, or historical resources studies; (2) use the federal land for educational and recreational purposes; (3) release and indemnify the United States from any claims or liabilities which may arise from uses that are carried out on the federal land by the United States or any person; (4) erect at the College an appropriate and centrally located monument that acknowledges the conveyance of the federal land for the purpose of furthering the higher education of citizens in Nevada; and (5) assist the Bureau of Land Management in providing information to the students of the College and the Nevada citizens on public land in Nevada and the role of the Bureau of Land Management in managing, preserving, and protecting such public land. Allows the University system to use the land conveyed for

Protect Marriage from the Courts Act of 2015 This bill prohibits a federal court or the Supreme Court from having jurisdiction to adjudicate or enforce any claim pertaining to the validity, under the U.S. Constitution, of a state law, administrative or judicial decision, that: (1) defines marriage as limited to the union of one man and one woman, or (2) refuses state recognition of or allows the state to refuse recognition of same-sex marriages performed and licensed in other states.

Fairness for Working Americans Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the refundability of the child tax credit; and (2) treat a foreign corporation acquiring a majority ownership interest in a domestic corporation as a domestic corporation for purposes of the lower 80 percent ownership limit on the expatriated corporation's tax liability.

Higher Education Savings Plan Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the ten percent penalty for premature distributions from annuity contracts certain qualified higher education expense distributions.
Grants a Federal charter to the National Academy of Inventors (a nonprofit organization organized under the laws of Florida).

Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid program to adopt a streamlined screening and enrollment process for providers and suppliers of medical or other items or services furnished to a child for which state Medicaid payment is available. A provider or supplier is eligible for such a process if the state has determined there is a limited risk of fraud, waste, or abuse in determining the level of screening to be conducted.

Public Library Innovation Space Act This bill amends the Museum and Library Services Act to authorize appropriations through FY2022 for the public library makerspace grant program.  The bill directs the National Museum of the City of Honolulu, for FY2018, to award competitive grants to eligible partnerships to establish makerspaces at public libraries. An eligible partnership is a partnership that includes a public library and: (1) an economic development corporation, (2) a local government, (3) a state government, (4) an elementary or secondary school, (5) a museum, (6) an institution of higher education, (7) a nonprofit organization, (8) a corporation, or (9) other entities identified by the Department of the Interior.  A makerspace is a facility that is open to the public and provides individuals with access to: (1) tools, technology, and educational resources that are designed to enable such individuals to create physical goods, including prototypes; and (2) educational opportunities, including vocational training and assistance with early-stage business ventures.

Rural Equity Payment Index Reform Act of 2003 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to establish a floor for the work geographic index used in the calculation of the physician fee schedule.

Campaign Sunlight Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to direct the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to establish and operate a website, to be known as the Campaign Accountability Site, through which members of the public may view the contents of political advertisements.

Requires the sponsor of a political advertisement to submit the contents of the advertisement to the FEC in such format as the FEC may require to enable it to be included on the website. Requires the sponsor to include the full contents of any source references cited in the advertisement. Sets forth a deadline for submission.

Veterans Justice Outreach Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out a program to support veterans in contact with the criminal justice system by discouraging unnecessary criminalization of mental illness and other nonviolent crimes.  The VA shall establish coordinators to provide outreach under such program.

Higher Education Family Opportunity Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a deduction for the qualified postsecondary tuition and related expenses paid or incurred by such individual.  Sets forth the allowable deduction amount for each taxable year.
Grants a Federal charter to the Black Veterans of America (a nonprofit corporation organized under the laws of Minnesota).

Anti-Pyramid Scheme Act of 2016 This bill prohibits establishing, operating, promoting, or causing to be promoted a pyramid promotional scheme.  A violation of this bill shall be treated as an unfair or deceptive act or practice in or affecting commerce under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Medical Savings Account Availability Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the monthly limit on the number of medical savings accounts that an individual employee may have. Makes such accounts available to all employees, not just those of small employers and self-employed individuals. Increases the amount of the tax deduction for contributions to medical savings accounts. Allows both employers and employees to contribute to medical savings accounts. Reduces the amount of the tax deduction for high deductible health plans. Allows medical savings accounts to be offered under cafeteria plans.

International Peacekeeping Reform Act of 1997 - Prohibits the availability of funds made available to the Department of State under the account "Contributions for International Peacekeeping Activities" or any other funds made available to the Department under any law to pay for assessed or voluntary contributions to United Nations (UN) peacekeeping activities unless:  (1) with respect to such peacekeeping operation the President certifies to the appropriate congressional committees that the UN Peacekeeping operation meets specified requirements; and (2) the President has notified such committees of the intent to support the establishment of the peacekeeping operation at least 15 days before any vote in the Security Council to establish, expand, or modify such operation.  Provides that if the President determines that an emergency exists which prevented submission of such a 15-day advance notification and that the proposed action is in the U.S. national security interests, the notification shall be provided in a timely manner but no later than 48 hours after the vote by the Security Council. 
Requires the President to determine and certify to the Congress that such UN Peacekeeping operation meets specified requirements, including that:  (1) it involves an international conflict in which hostilities have ceased and all significant parties to the conflict agree to the imposition
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer an income-based credit ($3,000 maximum) for certain child disability education and training expenses.

Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to recognize Alexander Creek, Incorporated (a Group Corporation located within Seward Meridian, Alaska), as an eligible Native village. Requires it to file amendments to its corporate charter and governing business documents to convert it to a Village Corporation.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to commence negotiations with Alexander Creek to fairly and equitably settle any aboriginal land claims and any other claims that it has against the United States. Requires the Secretary to enter into an agreement with it relating to such claims within a specified time frame. Provides that any funds to be provided for it under such agreement shall be available subject to appropriations. Requires the Secretary to carry out such agreement in accordance with this Act and other existing authorities, in coordination with the Administrator of General Services, with respect to property to be transferred to Alexander Creek pursuant to such agreement.

Requires: (1) Alexander Creek to notify each member of the Village Corporation recognized under this Act that it shall cease to receive benefits from Cook Inlet Region Incorporated as at-large shareholders and that all future resource payments from the Region shall be made to the Village Corporation; and (2) the Region to be considered a State and a State agency under existing authorities.

Rural Broadband Enhancement Act - Amends the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to direct the Rural Utilities Service of the Department of Agriculture to make loans or other extensions of credit to provide funds for the construction, improvement, or acquisition of facilities and equipment (including consumer equipment) for the provision of broadband service in eligible rural communities.

Requires the Rural Utilities Service to identify eligible entities (i.e., non-federal public or private entities, including an incorporated or limited liability entity, cooperative, non-profit organization, or limited dividend or mutual association) that submit a plan for a project meeting certain requirements.

Defines "broadband service" as any technology identified by the Rural Utilities Service as having the capacity to transmit data so as to enable a subscriber to such service to originate and receive high-quality voice, data, graphics, or video.

Requires the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to review and recommend modifications of rate-of-data transmission criteria for purposes of the identification of technologies.

Requires a project meeting the requirements of this Act to be determined to have the capability to: (1) deliver broadband service; and (2) make access to broadband service generally available throughout an eligible rural community.
